summary: Analytic adic geometry required for diamonds, planned at declaration granularity on the carriers of AdicSpacesPartII and within the RS-05 narrowing. A0 and A2 are supplier contracts: they identify, clause by clause, the completed tensor products, uniformisation, analytic pullbacks and analytic loci of AdicSpacesPartII R0, and its separated, proper, smooth and étale geometry, analytification and formal models (R0–R2, F0), on the same carriers, adding the relative polydisc and torus, smooth morphisms by ball charts, and the dimension theory of adic spaces with its estimates. A1 builds the finite étale and étale geometry of analytic adic spaces in Kedlaya–Liu's generality (finite étale algebras over complete Tate pairs, strongly sheafy pairs, étale morphisms by local description and their comparison with Huber's), the étale and finite étale sites with geometric points, strict localisations and the Galois category, Scholze's pro-étale site with the erratum's corrected coverings, and the Yoneda-adic presentations used in ECD §15. A3 proves the nonnoetherian affinoid étale approximation ECD 6.4(iv) by analytic algebra: pseudocoherent modules after Kedlaya–Liu II, a Zariski closed embedding of an affinoid étale object into a relative ball (which ECD uses without constructing), its conormal and Jacobian description, the characteristic-p specialisations of Fargues–Scholze IV.4.13–IV.4.19, quantitative perturbation lemmas and the finite-stage approximation through PerfectoidSpaces P5, without diamonds or six operations. A4 builds the finite étale torsor tower of ECD 15.3 and proves its uniform completion perfectoid, with the perfectoid cover presentation; the Spd, representability and étale-site conclusions of ECD 15.4–15.6 are DiamondsAndVStacks D6's. Sources are public (ECD v4, Fargues–Scholze v4, Kedlaya–Liu I and II, Scholze's 2013 paper with its erratum, the Berkeley lectures, Hansen–Kedlaya, de Jong–van der Put) and every excerpt was checked against the text read; Huber's 1996 book is cited only through excerpts reviewed decompositions verified. Every stage is source-decomposed: all its targets are realised by nodes; the anchor's Layers 0–5 and the inputs owned by other roadmaps are requests, and unread proof inputs are gaps.

nodes.title: A0 supplier contract: the completed tensor product of AdicSpacesPartII R0 is the pushout of complete Huber pairs, with its topology, plus ring and affinoid fibre products
nodes.statement: Let f : (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) and g : (A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺) be morphisms of complete Hausdorff Huber pairs (Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.Hom`) whose ring homomorphisms are adic (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-ring-homomorphism; this holds automatically when A is a Tate ring). Let D = (D, D⁺) = B ⊗̂_A C, with inl : (B, B⁺) → D and inr : (C, C⁺) → D, be the completed tensor product of AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product. Declaration: the square (f, g, inl, inr) is a pushout (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.IsPushout`) in the category of complete Hausdorff Huber pairs with Tau Ceti's morphisms of Huber pairs. This pushout is the object AdicEtaleGeometry A0 specifies, on the same carriers: (i) topology — D is the Hausdorff completion of B ⊗_A C for the group topology with fundamental system of neighbourhoods {Iⁿ·F : n ≥ 0}, where F is the image of B₀ ⊗_{A₀} C₀ for rings of definition A₀ ⊆ A⁺, B₀ ⊆ B⁺, C₀ ⊆ C⁺ with f(A₀) ⊆ B₀, g(A₀) ⊆ C₀ and I is an ideal of definition of A₀ generating ideals of definition of B₀ and C₀; (F, I·F) is a pair of definition, and the topology does not depend on these choices; (ii) plus ring — D⁺ is the closure in D of the integral closure, in B ⊗_A C, of the image of B⁺ ⊗_{A⁺} C⁺; it equals the closure in D of the integral closure in D of that image, which is Kedlaya–Liu's plus ring of the coproduct of adic Banach rings and Scholze's D⁺; (iii) universal property — for every complete Hausdorff Huber pair (R, R⁺) and morphisms φ : (B, B⁺) → (R, R⁺), ψ : (C, C⁺) → (R, R⁺) with φ ∘ f = ψ ∘ g there is exactly one morphism χ : D → (R, R⁺) with χ ∘ inl = φ and χ ∘ inr = ψ, and φ, ψ need not be adic; (iv) geometry — if (A, A⁺), (B, B⁺), (C, C⁺) and D are sheafy, then Spa D with Spa(inl), Spa(inr) is the fibre product Spa B ×_{Spa A} Spa C in the category of adic spaces (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-fibre-product); its globalisation to adic spaces under Huber's hypotheses is AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-products-existence. Boundaries: D is not uniformised (the uniform variant is AdicEtaleGeometry:A0/uniformization-contract); sheafiness of D is a hypothesis of (iv), supplied when B is of noetherian type and g is topologically of finite type (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-noetherian-stability) and never inferred from the formula; for perfectoid (A, B, C) over a perfectoid field, perfectoidness and sheafiness of D, and hence the existence of perfectoid fibre products, are the theorem PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces, which applies this node and is not part of it; no fibre product of arbitrary adic spaces is asserted. Lean name: `Huber.Pair.completedTensor.isPushout`.
hypotheses: f, g morphisms of complete Hausdorff Huber pairs with adic ring homomorphisms (automatic over a Tate base).
(R, R⁺) ranges over complete Hausdorff Huber pairs; φ, ψ are arbitrary morphisms of Huber pairs.
(iv) assumes sheafiness of all four pairs; nothing is claimed without it.
proofSteps: Topology (i): the carrier and its topology are those of AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product (common choice of rings of definition, ring topology by Bourbaki's criterion, pair of definition (F, I·F), independence of the choices), recorded in its API `Huber.Pair.completedTensor.pairOfDefinition`; the completion is Tau Ceti `IsHuberRing.completion` of B ⊗_A C. This is word for word the A0 carrier 'topology on a tensor product of compatible complete Huber pairs from rings of definition and ideals of definition, its separated completion'.

Plus ring (ii): R0 defines D⁺ as the closure of E⁺, the integral closure in E = B ⊗_A C of the image P of B⁺ ⊗_{A⁺} C⁺. Let J be the integral closure of P in D. The image of E⁺ lies in J, so D⁺ ⊆ closure(J). Conversely D⁺ is a ring of integral elements of D (completion of Huber pairs, anchor Layer 0.3, as used in R0), so it is integrally closed in D and closed (an open subgroup), and it contains P; hence J ⊆ D⁺ and closure(J) ⊆ D⁺. So D⁺ = closure(J), which is Kedlaya–Liu's 'completion of the integral closure of B⁺ ⊗_{A⁺} C⁺ in D' and Scholze's D⁺ (Proposition 6.18).

Universal property (iii): AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product-universal-property applies to (R, R⁺) because R⁺, a ring of integral elements, is open (hence closed) and integrally closed; commutativity inl ∘ f = inr ∘ g is R0's API `inl_comp`. Existence and uniqueness of χ for every cocone is the colimit property of the pushout cocone, i.e. Mathlib `CategoryTheory.IsPushout` in the category whose objects are complete Hausdorff Huber pairs and whose morphisms are Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.Hom`.

Geometry (iv): AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-fibre-product (morphisms from an adic space into Spa of a complete sheafy pair are morphisms of pairs into its global sections, then (iii)); the gluing to non-affinoid spaces is AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-products-existence (Huber 1996, Proposition 1.2.2).

Boundaries: AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-noetherian-stability supplies sheafiness only for noetherian type (its acceptance records that no sheafiness is asserted beyond), and AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniform-completed-tensor-product shows that D need not be uniform; PerfectoidSpaces P2 applies (i)–(iii) to perfectoid pairs and proves perfectoidness separately.
acceptance: Scalar extension of a Tate algebra (A0 test): for a complete extension L/K of nonarchimedean fields, (K⟨T⟩, K°⟨T⟩) ⊗̂_{(K, K°)} (L, L°) ≅ (L⟨T⟩, L°⟨T⟩) through AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-restricted-power-series (b), and Spa(L⟨T⟩, L°⟨T⟩) = Spa(K⟨T⟩, K°⟨T⟩) ×_{Spa(K, K°)} Spa(L, L°) is the closed unit disc over L.
Polydisc: (K⟨T⟩, K°⟨T⟩) ⊗̂_{(K, K°)} (K⟨S⟩, K°⟨S⟩) ≅ (K⟨T, S⟩, K°⟨T, S⟩) and its Spa is the product of two closed discs (Hübner, Example 9.3).
Plus ring is not the image: for L = ℚ_p(√p), (L, O_L) ⊗̂_{ℚ_p} (L, O_L) ≅ (L × L, O_L × O_L); the idempotent (1, 0) lies in the plus ring but not in the image of O_L ⊗_{ℤ_p} O_L.

Perfectoid scalar extension after P2 (A0 test): for a perfectoid field K, the perfectoid affinoid K-algebra K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ and a perfectoid complete extension L/K, PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces identifies Spa K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ ×_{Spa K} Spa L with Spa of this node's pair K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ ⊗̂_K L = L⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩; the perfectoidness and sheafiness used there are P2's and are not consequences of this node.

Non-example: for ℤ_p → ℤ_p⟦X⟧ ((p, X)-adic, not adic) and ℤ_p → ℚ_p there is no Huber topology on ℤ_p⟦X⟧ ⊗_{ℤ_p} ℚ_p making both maps continuous with ℤ_p⟦X⟧ open (Morel, Example II.3.2.2); the fibre product Spa ℤ_p⟦X⟧ ×_{Spa ℤ_p} Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p) is the open unit disc over ℚ_p, which is not affinoid (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-product-along-finite-type).

nodes.title: Uniformization supplied separately: the uniform completed tensor product is the pushout among uniform complete Tate pairs
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺), (B, B⁺), (C, C⁺) be complete Hausdorff Huber pairs with A a Tate ring and f : (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺), g : (A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺) morphisms of Huber pairs (so f, g are adic and B, C are Tate). Let B ⊗̂ᵘ_A C = (B ⊗̂_A C)^u with inlᵘ = ι ∘ inl, inrᵘ = ι ∘ inr be the uniform completed tensor product of AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniform-completed-tensor-product, where ι : B ⊗̂_A C → (B ⊗̂_A C)^u is the uniformization morphism of AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniformization. Declaration: the square (f, g, inlᵘ, inrᵘ) is a pushout (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.IsPushout`) in the full subcategory of complete Hausdorff Huber pairs (R, R⁺) with R a uniform Tate ring (R° bounded). Moreover ι is the unit of the uniformization adjunction at B ⊗̂_A C, Spa(ι) is a homeomorphism identifying rational subsets, and ι is an isomorphism exactly when B ⊗̂_A C is uniform. This realises A0's clause 'in the cases in which uniformization is necessary, construct it and prove its universal property separately; a separated completion need not be uniform': the completed tensor product of AdicEtaleGeometry:A0/supplier-contract-fibre-products is not uniformised, ℂ_p ⊗̂_{ℚ_p} ℂ_p is a complete separated tensor product that is not uniform, and uniformization is applied only where a consumer works among uniform pairs. No sheafiness of B ⊗̂ᵘ_A C and no fibre-product property of its adic spectrum is asserted. Lean name: `Huber.Pair.uniformCompletedTensor.isPushout`.
hypotheses: A a Tate ring; (A, A⁺), (B, B⁺), (C, C⁺) complete Hausdorff.
The pushout is taken among complete Hausdorff uniform Tate Huber pairs, not among all complete Huber pairs.
proofSteps: Pushout: AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniform-completed-tensor-product (b): given φ, ψ into a complete Hausdorff uniform (R, R⁺) agreeing on A, AdicEtaleGeometry:A0/supplier-contract-fibre-products gives a unique χ₀ : B ⊗̂_A C → (R, R⁺), and the universal property of the uniformization (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniformization (c), API `lift`, `hom_ext`) factors χ₀ uniquely through ι; this is the colimit property of the cocone (inlᵘ, inrᵘ).
Unit of the adjunction: AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniformization (c) states that uniformization is left adjoint to the inclusion of complete Hausdorff uniform Tate pairs, with unit ι.
Adic spectra: AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniformization (d) and R0/spectral-topology-cont-eq: Spa(ι) is a homeomorphism matching rational subsets.
Isomorphism criterion and non-example: AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniform-completed-tensor-product (d) (API `fromCompletedTensor_isIso_iff`); ℂ_p ⊗̂_{ℚ_p} ℂ_p is not uniform (Kedlaya–Liu, Remark 2.8.5).
acceptance: K⟨T⟩ ⊗̂ᵘ_K K⟨S⟩ ≅ K⟨T, S⟩ and ι is an isomorphism (the completed tensor product is already uniform).
ℂ_p ⊗̂_{ℚ_p} ℂ_p → ℂ_p ⊗̂ᵘ_{ℚ_p} ℂ_p is not an isomorphism: the separated completion is not uniform.
For a finite Galois extension L/K of complete nonarchimedean fields, L ⊗̂ᵘ_K L ≅ ∏_{σ ∈ Gal(L/K)} L via x ⊗ y ↦ (xσ(y))_σ.

Why A0's fibre products are not uniformised: a topologically split injection stays split after completed base change but may lose the splitting after uniform completion (Hansen–Kedlaya, Remark 7.2), which AdicSpacesPartII:R5 uses for sousperfectoid base change.

nodes.title: Tracking rings of definition, pseudouniformisers and plus rings through the completed tensor product
nodes.statement: Let f : (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺), g : (A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺) be morphisms of complete Hausdorff Huber pairs with adic ring homomorphisms and D = (D, D⁺) = B ⊗̂_A C (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product). (a) Rings and ideals of definition: the topological ring D and the maps inl, inr depend only on the topological rings A, B, C and the ring maps f, g, not on the rings of definition, the ideal of definition or the plus rings used to build the topology; if ϖ is a pseudouniformiser of A, B or C (Tau Ceti `IsPseudoUniformizer`), its image in D is a pseudouniformiser of D. (b) Independence of A⁺: D⁺ is the closure in D of the integral closure of the subring generated by inl(B⁺) ∪ inr(C⁺); in particular D⁺ does not change when A⁺ is replaced by another ring of integral elements A'⁺ with f(A'⁺) ⊆ B⁺ and g(A'⁺) ⊆ C⁺. (c) Change of plus rings (declaration): let B'⁺ ⊇ B⁺ and C'⁺ ⊇ C⁺ be rings of integral elements of B and C and D'⁺ the plus ring of D for (B'⁺, C'⁺). Then D⁺ ⊆ D'⁺, the identity of D is a morphism of Huber pairs (D, D⁺) → (D, D'⁺), and Spa(D, D'⁺) = Spa(inl)⁻¹(Spa(B, B'⁺)) ∩ Spa(inr)⁻¹(Spa(C, C'⁺)) as subsets of Spa(D, D⁺). When all pairs involved are sheafy this is the open subspace Spa(B, B'⁺) ×_{Spa(A, A⁺)} Spa(C, C'⁺) of Spa(B, B⁺) ×_{Spa(A, A⁺)} Spa(C, C⁺). Lean name: `Huber.Pair.completedTensor.spa_plus_eq_inter_preimage`.
hypotheses: f, g morphisms of complete Hausdorff Huber pairs with adic ring homomorphisms.
(c): B'⁺, C'⁺ rings of integral elements containing B⁺, C⁺.
proofSteps: (a) Independence of the definition data is the step 'independence of choices' of AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product (for two admissible choices take a third inside both; the neighbourhood bases are mutually cofinal), recorded in its API `pairOfDefinition`; the plus rings enter the construction only through the choice of rings of definition inside them, which does not change the topology. Pseudouniformisers: a topologically nilpotent unit maps to a topologically nilpotent unit under the continuous ring maps inl ∘ f, inl, inr (R0 API `completedTensor.isTateRing`).

(b) The image of B⁺ ⊗_{A⁺} C⁺ in B ⊗_A C is the additive subgroup spanned by the products (b ⊗ 1)(1 ⊗ c), b ∈ B⁺, c ∈ C⁺, i.e. the subring generated by the images of B⁺ and C⁺; it does not involve A⁺. R0's plus ring is the closure of its integral closure (R0 API `plus_eq`).

(c) The generating subring, its integral closure and the closure grow with (B⁺, C⁺), so D⁺ ⊆ D'⁺; the identity is continuous, so it is a morphism of pairs. Tau Ceti `spa_antitone` gives Spa(D, D'⁺) ⊆ Spa(D, D⁺). For v ∈ Spa(D, D⁺): v ≤ 1 on D'⁺ iff v ≤ 1 on the subring generated by inl(B'⁺) ∪ inr(C'⁺), because the locus {v ≤ 1} is an integrally closed subring (Tau Ceti `spa_integralClosure`) and is open, hence closed, for continuous v; and v ≤ 1 on that subring iff v ∘ inl ≤ 1 on B'⁺ and v ∘ inr ≤ 1 on C'⁺, i.e. iff Spa(inl)(v) ∈ Spa(B, B'⁺) and Spa(inr)(v) ∈ Spa(C, C'⁺) (Tau Ceti `Pair.Hom.spaComap`).

Geometric reading: Spa(B, B'⁺) ⊆ Spa(B, B⁺) is an open subspace when (B, B'⁺) is sheafy, and the preimages of open subspaces under the projections of a fibre product form the fibre product of the open subspaces (AdicEtaleGeometry:A0/supplier-contract-fibre-products (iv) and the universal property of open subspaces, anchor Layer 5.1).
acceptance: Independence of A⁺: let K be a complete rank-one field whose residue field carries a nontrivial valuation ring (for instance the completion of ℚ_p(t) for the Gauss norm, residue field 𝔽_p(t)) and K⁺ ⊊ K° the preimage of 𝔽_p[t]_(t); then (K⟨T⟩, K°⟨T⟩) ⊗̂_{(K, K⁺)} (K⟨S⟩, K°⟨S⟩) and the same over (K, K°) are both (K⟨T, S⟩, K°⟨T, S⟩).

Change of plus ring: with the same K, the completed tensor product (K, K⁺) ⊗̂_{(K, K⁺)} (K, K⁺) is (K, K⁺), whose spectrum has two points (the rank-one point and the rank-two point); replacing the second factor by (K, K°) gives (K, K°), and Spa(K, K°) is the single rank-one point, which is Spa(inr)⁻¹(Spa(K, K°)).
Pseudouniformiser: p is a pseudouniformiser of ℚ_p⟨T⟩ ⊗̂_{ℚ_p} ℚ_p⟨S⟩ = ℚ_p⟨T, S⟩.

nodes.title: Pullback along a rational open immersion is restriction, computed by the completed tensor product with the rational localisation
nodes.statement: (a) Let g : Y → X be a morphism of adic spaces (anchor Layer 5) and U ⊆ X an open subspace. Then the open subspace g⁻¹(U) ⊆ Y, with g| : g⁻¹(U) → U and the inclusion g⁻¹(U) → Y, is a fibre product Y ×_X U in the category of adic spaces; no hypothesis on g is needed. (b) Declaration: let φ : (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) be a morphism of complete Hausdorff Huber pairs with adic ring homomorphism (automatic if A is Tate), T ⊆ A finite with T·A open, s ∈ A, and A⟨T/s⟩ the rational localisation (Tau Ceti `completionLocalization`, anchor Layer 3.1). Then Spa(φ)⁻¹(R(T/s)) = R(φ(T)/φ(s)) is a rational subset of Spa(B, B⁺), and the morphism B ⊗̂_A A⟨T/s⟩ → B⟨φ(T)/φ(s)⟩ induced (AdicEtaleGeometry:A0/supplier-contract-fibre-products) by B → B⟨φ(T)/φ(s)⟩ and the map A⟨T/s⟩ → B⟨φ(T)/φ(s)⟩ extending φ is an isomorphism of complete Huber pairs over (B, B⁺). (c) Consequently, if (A, A⁺) and (B, B⁺) are sheafy, Spa(B ⊗̂_A A⟨T/s⟩) = Spa(B, B⁺) ×_{Spa(A, A⁺)} R(T/s) = R(φ(T)/φ(s)), and this pair is sheafy: sheafiness is inherited from Spa(B, B⁺), not deduced from the formula. (d) Without adicness (b) fails: for ℤ_p → ℤ_p⟦X⟧ ((p, X)-adic) and the rational subset R(p/p) = Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p) of Spa(ℤ_p, ℤ_p), the preimage in Spa ℤ_p⟦X⟧ is the open unit disc over ℚ_p, which is not quasi-compact and hence not rational, and the completed tensor product is not defined; the fibre product is still the open subspace of (a). Lean name: `Huber.Pair.completedTensor.rationalLocalizationIso`.
hypotheses: (a): g arbitrary, U open.
(b): φ a morphism of complete Hausdorff Huber pairs with adic ring homomorphism; T·A open.
(c): sheafiness of (A, A⁺) and (B, B⁺).
proofSteps: (a) Universal property of open subspaces (anchor Layer 5.1): a morphism h : Z → Y factors through the open subspace g⁻¹(U) iff g(h(Z)) ⊆ U, and then uniquely; a pair (h : Z → Y, k : Z → U) with g ∘ h = ι_U ∘ k therefore factors uniquely through g⁻¹(U).

(b) Preimage: Tau Ceti `Pair.Hom.spaComap_preimage_rationalSubset` gives Spa(φ)⁻¹(R(T/s)) = R(φ(T)/φ(s)) as sets; since φ is adic, φ(T)·B is open (Wedhorn Lemma 7.46(3), as in AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-rational-localisation (1)), so this is a rational subset in Huber's sense.

(b) Isomorphism: A → A⟨T/s⟩ is topologically of finite type, hence adic (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/topologically-finite-type-is-adic), so B ⊗̂_A A⟨T/s⟩ is defined. For a complete Hausdorff Huber pair (R, R⁺), morphisms B ⊗̂_A A⟨T/s⟩ → (R, R⁺) are pairs (β : B → R, α : A⟨T/s⟩ → R) agreeing on A (AdicEtaleGeometry:A0/supplier-contract-fibre-products (iii)); by the universal property of rational localisation (Tau Ceti `existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_of_forall_comap_mem_rationalSubset`, Wedhorn Lemma 8.1) α exists, uniquely, iff Spa(R) maps into R(T/s) under Spa(β ∘ φ), i.e. iff Spa(β) lands in R(φ(T)/φ(s)); by the same universal property for B these β are the morphisms B⟨φ(T)/φ(s)⟩ → (R, R⁺). Both pairs represent the same functor and the comparison morphism is the one of the statement, so it is an isomorphism (Yoneda). This is the case C = A⟨T/s⟩, V = Spa C, W = R(T/s), U = R(φ(T)/φ(s)) of AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-rational-localisation (2), in which p_B⁻¹(U) is all of Spa D.

(c) Spa(B⟨φ(T)/φ(s)⟩) → Spa(B, B⁺) is a homeomorphism onto R(φ(T)/φ(s)) matching rational subsets (Tau Ceti `spaLocalizationHomeomorph`), and the structure presheaf of B⟨φ(T)/φ(s)⟩ is the restriction of that of B (anchor Layer 3.3), so sheafiness is inherited; with (a) and (b) this identifies the fibre product.
(d) AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-product-along-finite-type (acceptance): the fibre product is the increasing union of the rational subsets {|X|ᵐ ≤ |p| ≠ 0}, the open unit disc.
acceptance: Rational pullback (A0 test): for Y = Spa(ℚ_p⟨S⟩, ℤ_p⟨S⟩) → X = Spa(ℚ_p⟨T⟩, ℤ_p⟨T⟩), T ↦ S², and U = {|T| ≤ |p|} = R((T, p)/p): g⁻¹(U) = R((S², p)/p) = {|S²| ≤ |p|} and ℚ_p⟨S⟩ ⊗̂_{ℚ_p⟨T⟩} ℚ_p⟨T⟩⟨T/p⟩ ≅ ℚ_p⟨S⟩⟨S²/p⟩.
PerfectoidSpaces P8's formula A⟨f/h⟩ = A ⊗̂_B B⟨f/h⟩ for a continuous B → A of Tate rings and a rational localisation B⟨f/h⟩ is (b) with (A, B) in the roles of (B, A).
Non-adic base (d): Spa ℤ_p⟦X⟧ ×_{Spa ℤ_p} Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p) = ⋃_n R(Xⁿ/p) is the open unit disc over ℚ_p (Hübner, Example 9.4; Scholze–Weinstein, Lecture 4).

nodes.title: Pullback along a finite étale map is computed by the uncompleted tensor product
nodes.statement: Let φ : (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) be a finite morphism of complete Hausdorff Tate Huber pairs (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-huber-pair-hom) whose ring homomorphism is étale (Mathlib `Algebra.Etale A B`), so that B is a finite étale A-algebra with its natural A-module topology and B⁺ is the integral closure of A⁺ in B; and let ψ : (A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺) be a morphism to a complete Hausdorff Tate Huber pair. Declaration: (i) B is a finite projective A-module, and the canonical map B ⊗_A C → B ⊗̂_A C, from the algebraic tensor product with its natural C-module topology to the completed tensor product of AdicEtaleGeometry:A0/supplier-contract-fibre-products, is an isomorphism of topological rings. Further: (ii) the plus ring of B ⊗̂_A C is the integral closure of the image of C⁺ in B ⊗_A C; (iii) C → B ⊗_A C is finite étale (Mathlib `Algebra.Etale.baseChange`) and (C, C⁺) → (B ⊗_A C, (B ⊗_A C)⁺) is a finite morphism of complete Tate Huber pairs; (iv) if (B ⊗_A C, (B ⊗_A C)⁺) is sheafy — for instance if C is strongly noetherian, since then B ⊗_A C is finite over C and strongly noetherian (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-algebra-over-affinoid (v)) — then Spa(B ⊗_A C) = Spa(B, B⁺) ×_{Spa(A, A⁺)} Spa(C, C⁺) in adic spaces; (v) for f₁, …, f_n, g ∈ A generating the unit ideal, Spa(φ)⁻¹(R(f/g)) = R(φ(f)/φ(g)) with coordinate ring B ⊗_A A⟨f/g⟩ (no completion). Sheafiness of B ⊗_A C is not asserted for a general sheafy C: it is not known whether a finite étale algebra over a sheafy Tate ring is sheafy (Kedlaya–Liu, Remark 8.2.18). The sousperfectoid and perfectoid cases are theorems of AdicSpacesPartII R5 and PerfectoidSpaces P3, and the non-sheafy case is handled by the generalized adic presentations of AdicEtaleGeometry A1. Lean name: `Huber.Pair.completedTensor.finiteEtaleEquivTensor`.
hypotheses: φ finite (R0) with étale ring map; A, C complete Hausdorff Tate.
(iv) assumes sheafiness of the base change (automatic for C strongly noetherian).
proofSteps: Projectivity: `Algebra.Etale A B` gives `Algebra.Smooth A B`, hence flatness (Mathlib `Algebra.Smooth.flat`); B is a finitely presented A-algebra and a finite A-module, hence a finitely presented A-module (Mathlib `Module.FinitePresentation.of_finite_of_finitePresentation`), hence projective (Mathlib `Module.Flat.projective_of_finitePresentation`).

(i) AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-algebra-tensor-complete (i) and (ii), projective case: the tensor topology on B ⊗_A C is the natural C-module topology, B ⊗_A C is a direct summand of a finite free C-module, hence complete and Hausdorff, so the completion map is an isomorphism.

(ii) R0's plus ring is the closure of the integral closure of the image of B⁺ ⊗_{A⁺} C⁺. B⁺ is integral over A⁺ (R0/finite-huber-pair-hom, API `isIntegral_plus`), so that image is integral over the image of C⁺ and the two integral closures agree; the integral closure of C⁺ in the finite C-algebra B ⊗_A C is open (R0/finite-algebra-tensor-complete (ii)), hence closed.
(iii) Mathlib `Algebra.Etale.baseChange` and `Module.Finite.base_change`; the finite morphism of pairs is AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-algebra-tensor-complete (ii).
(iv) AdicEtaleGeometry:A0/supplier-contract-fibre-products (iv); the strongly noetherian case is AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-algebra-over-affinoid (v).
(v) AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-algebra-tensor-complete (iii) (projective case) combined with AdicEtaleGeometry:A0/rational-pullback-comparison (b).
acceptance: A finite étale algebra (A0 test): for p odd, A = ℚ_p⟨T^{±1}⟩ (the unit circle |T| = 1) and B = A[S]/(S² − T), which is finite étale because 2S is a unit; over the rational subset U = {|T − 1| ≤ |p|} the element T has a square root (the binomial series for (1 + (T − 1))^{1/2} converges), so B ⊗_A A⟨(T − 1)/p⟩ ≅ A⟨(T − 1)/p⟩ × A⟨(T − 1)/p⟩ without completion and Spa(B) ×_{Spa A} U is two disjoint copies of U.
ℚ_p(√p) ⊗_{ℚ_p} ℚ_p(√p) ≅ ℚ_p(√p) × ℚ_p(√p) is already complete, and the plus ring is ℤ_p[√p] × ℤ_p[√p], the integral closure of ℤ_p[√p] in the product.

Kummer cover: for n invertible in a complete nonarchimedean field K, the pullback of the finite étale Spa K⟨S^{±1}⟩ → Spa K⟨T^{±1}⟩, T ↦ Sⁿ, along a classical point Spa(L, L°) → Spa K⟨T^{±1}⟩ with T ↦ t is Spa(L[S]/(Sⁿ − t)).

nodes.title: Chart independence: every affinoid chart of the glued fibre product is the completed tensor product of the charts below it
nodes.statement: Let f : X → S and g : Y → S be morphisms of adic spaces satisfying the hypotheses of AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-products-existence, with g adic, and let Z = X ×_S Y with projections p, q. Let W = Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ S, U = Spa(C, C⁺) ⊆ f⁻¹(W) and V = Spa(B, B⁺) ⊆ g⁻¹(W) be open affinoids with complete Hausdorff pairs such that C ⊗̂_A B is sheafy (for instance B stably sheafy and A → C topologically of finite type, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-restricted-power-series). Declaration: the open subspace p⁻¹(U) ∩ q⁻¹(V) of Z, with p, q, is canonically isomorphic over U and V to Spa(C ⊗̂_A B) with Spa(inl), Spa(inr) (AdicEtaleGeometry:A0/supplier-contract-fibre-products). The isomorphism does not depend on the affinoid cover used to construct Z, and for rational U' ⊆ U, V' ⊆ V, W' ⊆ W with f(U') ⊆ W' ⊇ g(V') it restricts to the isomorphism O(U') ⊗̂_{O(W')} O(V') ≅ O(p⁻¹(U') ∩ q⁻¹(V')) of AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-rational-localisation. In particular any two gluings of Z from affinoid charts are canonically isomorphic, compatibly with all charts. Lean name: `AdicSpace.pullbackAffinoidChartIso`.
hypotheses: The hypotheses of AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-products-existence with g adic.

The chosen charts have C ⊗̂_A B sheafy; an affinoid morphism of weakly finite type need not have a topologically-finite-type ring map (Wedhorn Remark 8.52), so the chart condition is stated on the rings.
proofSteps: Open subspaces of a fibre product are fibre products: a pair of morphisms T → U, T → V agreeing over W is a pair T → X, T → Y agreeing over S with images in U and V, hence factors uniquely through Z with image in p⁻¹(U) ∩ q⁻¹(V) (universal property of open subspaces, anchor Layer 5.1); so p⁻¹(U) ∩ q⁻¹(V) = U ×_W V.

Spa(C ⊗̂_A B) is also U ×_W V (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-fibre-product, using the sheafiness hypothesis); two fibre products are uniquely isomorphic compatibly with the projections (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.IsPullback`, uniqueness of limits), which gives the canonical isomorphism and its independence of the gluing data.

Compatibility with rational restriction: for U', V', W' rational, both sides restrict to fibre products U' ×_{W'} V', and AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-rational-localisation (2)–(3) identifies Spa(O(U') ⊗̂_{O(W')} O(V')) with the rational subset p⁻¹(U') ∩ q⁻¹(V') of Spa(C ⊗̂_A B); uniqueness of isomorphisms of fibre products gives the compatibility.

Gluing independence: the construction of Z in AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-products-existence glues such charts (Wedhorn proof of Theorem 8.56(i)); any other admissible cover yields charts related to these by the previous two steps.
acceptance: For X = Y = Spa(ℚ_p⟨T⟩) over S = Spa ℚ_p, with the covers X = {|T| ≤ |p|} ∪ {|p| ≤ |T|} and the trivial cover, the chart over {|T| ≤ |p|} × Y is Spa(ℚ_p⟨T/p⟩ ⊗̂_{ℚ_p} ℚ_p⟨S⟩) = Spa(ℚ_p⟨T, S⟩⟨T/p⟩), the rational subset {|T| ≤ |p|} of the closed bidisc, whichever cover is used.

nodes.title: Associativity, symmetry and unit isomorphisms of fibre products, and their affinoid formulas
nodes.statement: Let S be an adic space and X → S, Y → S, Z → S morphisms locally of finite type, with S, X, Y, Z covered by open affinoids whose rings are complete and stably sheafy (for instance all locally noetherian). Then all iterated fibre products of X, Y, Z over S exist (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-products-existence (a); local finite type and stable sheafiness pass to base changes and composites, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/base-change-stability), and the canonical isomorphisms (X ×_S Y) ×_S Z ≅ X ×_S (Y ×_S Z) (Mathlib `pullbackAssoc`), X ×_S Y ≅ Y ×_S X (Mathlib `pullbackSymmetry`) and X ×_S S ≅ X (Mathlib `IsPullback.of_id_snd`) are the unique isomorphisms compatible with the projections, so they satisfy every coherence identity between composites of them (pentagon and hexagon type identities) by uniqueness of morphisms into a limit. Declaration: on affinoid charts S ⊇ Spa(A, A⁺), with Spa(C, C⁺), Spa(B, B⁺), Spa(E, E⁺) above it and all structure maps adic, the associativity isomorphism is Spa of the ring isomorphism (C ⊗̂_A B) ⊗̂_A E ≅ C ⊗̂_A (B ⊗̂_A E) compatible with the three coprojections, obtained by pasting the pushout squares of AdicEtaleGeometry:A0/supplier-contract-fibre-products (Mathlib `IsPushout.paste_horiz`); the symmetry is Spa of `Huber.Pair.completedTensor.comm` and the unit is Spa of B ⊗̂_A (A, A⁺) ≅ (B, B⁺) for complete B (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product). Lean name: `Huber.Pair.completedTensor.assoc`.
hypotheses: X → S, Y → S, Z → S locally of finite type; all spaces covered by complete stably sheafy affinoids.
On affinoid charts all structure maps adic (automatic over an analytic base).
proofSteps: Existence of the iterated fibre products: R0/fibre-products-existence (a) for X → S, then R0/base-change-stability (i) (the projection X ×_S Y → Y is locally of finite type) and the stable sheafiness of its pieces (R0/fibre-products-existence, 'Stability') for (X ×_S Y) ×_S Z = (X ×_S Y) ×_Y (Y ×_S Z); similarly on the other side.

Coherence: in any category, given the pullbacks, Mathlib's `pullbackAssoc`, `pullbackSymmetry` and the unit isomorphism from `IsPullback.of_id_snd` are characterised by their compatibility with the projections; two morphisms into a limit that agree after all projections are equal, which yields the coherence identities.

Affinoid formula: by Mathlib `IsPushout.paste_horiz`, pasting the pushout squares for (C, B) over A and for (C ⊗̂_A B, E) over A along inl gives a pushout square for (C, B ⊗̂_A E), so the two iterated completed tensor products are canonically isomorphic, compatibly with the coprojections; applying Spa and AdicEtaleGeometry:A0/fibre-product-affinoid-chart-comparison identifies it with Mathlib's associator on the chart.
Symmetry and unit: R0 API `completedTensor.comm` and the R0 unit test (for g = id, B ⊗̂_A A ≅ B̂ = B), with the same chart comparison.
acceptance: For S = Spa K and three closed discs, both iterated fibre products are Spa K⟨T, S, R⟩, and the associator is the identity of K⟨T, S, R⟩ under the evident identifications.

Transitivity of base change: for the closed unit disc D over ℚ_p and an embedding ℚ_p(√p) ⊆ ℂ_p, (D ×_{Spa ℚ_p} Spa ℚ_p(√p)) ×_{Spa ℚ_p(√p)} Spa ℂ_p ≅ D ×_{Spa ℚ_p} Spa ℂ_p = Spa(ℂ_p⟨T⟩, O_{ℂ_p}⟨T⟩) (the pasting of two pullback squares; on rings R0's API `completedTensor.cancelBaseChange`).

nodes.title: The analytic locus X_a of an adic space: open adic subspace, Tate charts, and restriction of adic morphisms
nodes.statement: Let X be an adic space (anchor Layer 5). A point x ∈ X is analytic if it has an open neighbourhood U such that O_X(U) contains a topologically nilpotent unit, equivalently if its support in some (every) open affinoid neighbourhood Spa(A, A⁺) is not an open ideal (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-morphism; Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.IsAnalyticPoint`). The set X_a of analytic points is open. The analytic locus `AdicSpace.analyticLocus X` is the open adic subspace of X on X_a, with its open immersion ι_X : X_a → X; X is analytic (`AdicSpace.IsAnalytic X`) if X_a = X. Properties: (a) for an open subspace U ⊆ X, U_a = X_a ∩ U; (b) for X = Spa(A, A⁺) with A complete, |X_a| is Tau Ceti's `spaAnalytic A⁺`; it is quasi-compact, and for a pair of definition (A₀, I) and generators G = {g₁, …, g_r} of I it is the union of the rational subsets R(G/gᵢ), whose coordinate rings A⟨G/gᵢ⟩ are Tate rings (Tate charts); X_a = X if A is Tate, and X_a = ∅ iff the Hausdorff quotient of A is discrete; (c) X_a is analytic, and every morphism from an adic space to an analytic adic space is adic; (d) restriction: a morphism f : Y → X is adic iff f(Y_a) ⊆ X_a (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-iff-analytic-locus), and then there is a unique f_a : Y_a → X_a with ι_X ∘ f_a = f ∘ ι_Y, functorially in f; (e) universal property: for an analytic adic space T, a morphism T → X factors through ι_X iff it is adic, and then uniquely; (f) base change: if Y ×_X Z exists (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-products-existence) and Z → X is adic, then (Y ×_X Z)_a = p⁻¹(Y_a) = Y_a ×_X Z for the projection p. Conventions: non-Tate Huber pairs such as Witt vector rings and A_inf are allowed at the input; the constructions of AdicSpacesPartII R0 (completed tensor products, fibre products) are applied to their analytic loci through the Tate charts of (b), on which every morphism is adic. For an adic space over Spa(ℤ_p, ℤ_p) with adic structure morphism, X_a is the preimage of Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p); in general (Spa ℤ_p⟦T⟧, Spa A_inf) it is larger and contains analytic points of characteristic p. Lean name: `AdicSpace.analyticLocus`.
hypotheses: X an adic space (anchor Layer 5); (b) additionally X = Spa(A, A⁺) with A complete.
(d)–(f) concern morphisms of adic spaces; (f) needs the fibre product to exist.
proofSteps: Analytic points and openness: AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-morphism defines analytic points of adic spaces; on an affinoid X_a is Tau Ceti `spaAnalytic`, open by `isOpen_val_preimage_spaAnalytic` (it is the union of the loci where an element of the extended ideal of definition does not vanish); analyticity is local (Wedhorn Remark 8.37(2)), so X_a is open in X and U_a = X_a ∩ U, which is (a).

The open subspace: the anchor's Layer 5.1 makes every open subset of an adic space an open adic subspace with an open immersion; this gives analyticLocus and ι_X. A point of X_a is analytic in X_a because analyticity is local, so X_a is analytic.

(b) Tau Ceti `isCompact_val_preimage_spaAnalytic` (quasi-compactness), `spaAnalytic_eq_biUnion_rationalSubset` (the cover by R(G/gᵢ)), `isTateRing_completion_locTopology_of_mem_generators` (the charts are Tate), `spaAnalytic_eq_spa_of_isTateRing` (the Tate case) and `spaAnalytic_eq_empty_iff_discrete_separationQuotient` (the empty case, Wedhorn Proposition 7.49(2)).

(c)–(d) AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-iff-analytic-locus (ii): f is adic iff f(Y_a) ⊆ X_a, and every morphism into an analytic space is adic; the factorisation f_a is the universal property of the open subspace X_a (anchor Layer 5.1), unique because ι_X is a monomorphism; functoriality from uniqueness.
(e) For analytic T, T_a = T, so by (d) a morphism g : T → X is adic iff g(T) ⊆ X_a iff g factors through ι_X.

(f) If Z → X is adic, the projection p : Y ×_X Z → Y is adic (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/base-change-stability (v)); adic morphisms map analytic points to analytic points and every morphism maps non-analytic points to non-analytic points (R0/adic-iff-analytic-locus (iii)), so a point w is analytic iff p(w) is; hence (Y ×_X Z)_a = p⁻¹(Y_a), which is the fibre product Y_a ×_X Z by AdicEtaleGeometry:A0/rational-pullback-comparison (a).

nodes.title: Strongly sheafy Tate rings and locally strongly sheafy analytic adic spaces
nodes.statement: Let A be a complete Hausdorff Tate ring (Tau Ceti `Huber.IsTateRing A`; every Huber ring in this stage is complete and Hausdorff). For n ≥ 0 write A⟨T_1, …, T_n⟩ for Tau Ceti's completed restricted power-series ring `Huber.restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion n A`, again a complete Tate ring. A is strongly sheafy (`Huber.IsStronglySheafy A`) if A⟨T_1, …, T_n⟩ is sheafy for every n ≥ 0, sheafy meaning the anchor's `Huber.IsSheafyRing` (Wedhorn Definition 8.26: the structure presheaf of Spa(R, R⁺) is a sheaf for every ring of integral elements R⁺) (Hansen–Kedlaya Definition 4.1). A Huber pair (A, A⁺) is strongly sheafy when A is. An analytic adic space X (anchor Layer 5, every point analytic) is locally strongly sheafy (`AdicSpace.IsLocallyStronglySheafy X`) if every x ∈ X has an open affinoid neighbourhood Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ X with A a complete strongly sheafy Tate ring. Stability properties that are part of the definition package: (a) A strongly sheafy implies A sheafy (n = 0) and A⟨S_1, …, S_m⟩ strongly sheafy; (b) every rational localisation of a strongly sheafy ring is strongly sheafy; (c) if A is sheafy and Spa(A, A⁺) has a finite rational covering by strongly sheafy rings, then A is strongly sheafy; consequently, on a locally strongly sheafy X every open affinoid Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ X has A strongly sheafy, and every open subspace of X is locally strongly sheafy; (d) finite étale A-algebras are strongly sheafy (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-strongly-sheafy). Examples: complete strongly noetherian Tate rings (in particular affinoid algebras over a complete nonarchimedean field), complete Tate rings with a noetherian ring of definition, and complete Tate rings that are stably sheafy in the anchor's sense (`Huber.IsStablySheafyRing`: each A⟨T_1, …, T_n⟩ is topologically of finite type over A); hence locally noetherian analytic adic spaces (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space) are locally strongly sheafy. Perfectoid and sousperfectoid Tate rings belong to the class as well (their Tate algebras are sousperfectoid, hence stably uniform and sheafy); that membership is proved where those rings are constructed (PerfectoidSpaces and AdicSpacesPartII:R5 consume this node), not here. Non-example: a uniform Tate ring that is not sheafy (Buzzard–Verberkmoes, Mihara) is not strongly sheafy. Sheafiness of A alone is not known to give (d) (Kedlaya–Liu Remark 8.2.18); this is why the class is introduced.
hypotheses: A complete Hausdorff Tate ring; A⟨T_1, …, T_n⟩ is Tau Ceti's completed restricted power-series ring.
Sheafiness is the anchor's ring-level notion `Huber.IsSheafyRing` (quantified over rings of integral elements).
X analytic: its affinoid charts can be chosen with Tate coordinate rings (anchor analytic locus).
proofSteps: Define `Huber.IsStronglySheafy A` as the Prop-valued class ∀ n, `Huber.IsSheafyRing (Huber.restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion n A)` (anchor Layer 3.4 carrier, requested); `AdicSpace.IsLocallyStronglySheafy X` is the existence of an open affinoid cover with strongly sheafy charts.
(a) n = 0 gives sheafiness since A is complete; A⟨S⟩⟨T⟩ = A⟨S, T⟩ (iterated completed restricted power series, tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion).

(b) Hansen–Kedlaya Theorem 4.2: A is strongly sheafy iff for every n the map A⟨T_1, …, T_n⟩ → H⁰(X_n, O) is an isomorphism and H^i(X_n, O) = 0 for i > 0 (cohomology of the sheafified structure presheaf on X_n = Spa(A⟨T⟩, A⁺⟨T⟩), mathlib:CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H; the forward direction is the Čech acyclicity of sheafy pairs, AdicSpacesPartII:R3/sheafy-cech-acyclicity). Hansen–Kedlaya Lemma 4.3(b): these conditions pass from A to A⟨f⟩ and A⟨f⁻¹⟩ (exact sequence 0 → O → O → j_*O_V → 0 for multiplication by T_{n+1} − f resp. 1 − fT_{n+1}). Every rational localisation is an iterate A⟨f⁻¹⟩⟨f_1, …, f_n⟩ (proof of Hansen–Kedlaya Theorem 4.2).

(c) Hansen–Kedlaya Corollary 4.5, the vanishing of higher Čech cohomology of the covering coming from the sheafiness of A (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/sheafy-cech-acyclicity). For an open affinoid V ⊆ X and x ∈ V: choose a strongly sheafy chart Spa(A_i, A_i⁺) ∋ x, a rational subset U of V with x ∈ U ⊆ V ∩ Spa(A_i, A_i⁺), and a rational subset R of Spa(A_i, A_i⁺) with x ∈ R ⊆ U; the functions defining R restrict to O_X(U) and still generate the unit ideal, so R is rational in U, hence in V (rational subsets of rational subsets are rational, anchor Layer 2), and R is strongly sheafy by (b). Finitely many such R cover the quasi-compact V.

Examples: strongly noetherian Tate rings have strongly noetherian Tate algebras (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsStronglyNoetherian), which are sheafy by the anchor's Layer 4.1; a Tate ring with a noetherian ring of definition is strongly noetherian (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/noetherian-type-huber-ring); stably sheafy rings: A⟨T_1, …, T_n⟩ is topologically of finite type over A. Analytic charts of a locally noetherian adic space are strongly noetherian Tate (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/noetherian-type-huber-ring).
Non-example: Hansen–Kedlaya §1 and Remark 3.19 record uniform Tate rings which are not sheafy; for them the condition already fails at n = 0.
acceptance: K⟨T_1, …, T_m⟩ for a complete nonarchimedean field K is strongly sheafy (strongly noetherian).
A rational localisation of a strongly sheafy ring is strongly sheafy, and every open affinoid of a locally strongly sheafy space has a strongly sheafy coordinate ring.
The uniform non-sheafy Tate rings of Buzzard–Verberkmoes and Mihara are not strongly sheafy.

nodes.title: The complete Huber pair of a finite étale algebra over a complete Tate pair
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a complete Tate Huber pair (Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair` on a complete Hausdorff `Huber.IsTateRing` A) and let B be a finite étale A-algebra (Mathlib `Algebra.Etale A B` and `Module.Finite A B`; an object of `CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale A`). Construct the complete Tate Huber pair (B, B⁺) := `Huber.Pair.finiteEtale A⁺ B` and the morphism ι: (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺). (i) Topology: B is a finite projective A-module, and B carries the natural A-module topology (Mathlib `moduleTopology A B`); for any presentation B ⊕ Q ≅ Aⁿ it is both the subspace and the quotient topology from Aⁿ (Kedlaya–Liu Lemma 2.2.12). With it B is a complete Hausdorff topological ring, ι is continuous, every A-linear map from B to a topological A-module is continuous, and B is a Tate ring: if b_1, …, b_m generate B as an A-module, ϖ ∈ A⁺ is a pseudouniformiser and A₀ ⊆ A⁺ a ring of definition, then for N ≫ 0 the ϖ^N b_j are integral over A₀, B₀ := A₀[ϖ^N b_1, …, ϖ^N b_m] is a ring of definition with ideal of definition ϖB₀, and ι(ϖ) is a pseudouniformiser of B. (ii) Plus ring: B⁺ := the integral closure of ι(A⁺) in B; it is a ring of integral elements. (iii) ι is a finite morphism of complete Huber pairs (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-huber-pair-hom); it induces the continuous map Spa(ι): Spa(B, B⁺) → Spa(A, A⁺) (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.spaComap`), whose fibre over x has at most rank_x(B) points; Spa(ι) is surjective when B is faithfully flat over A. (iv) Universal property: for every complete Huber pair (D, D⁺) with a morphism χ: (A, A⁺) → (D, D⁺), the morphisms of Huber pairs (B, B⁺) → (D, D⁺) under (A, A⁺) are exactly the A-algebra homomorphisms B → D; so B ↦ (B, B⁺) is a fully faithful functor from finite étale A-algebras to complete Huber pairs under (A, A⁺). (v) Base change and rational restriction: for every morphism (A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺) of complete Tate pairs, C ⊗_A B is finite étale over C, its natural C-module topology is the tensor-product topology, the canonical map C ⊗_A B → C ⊗̂_A B to the completed tensor product (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product) is a topological isomorphism, and `Huber.Pair.finiteEtale C⁺ (C ⊗_A B)` is the completed tensor product of pairs (plus ring the integral closure of the image of C⁺ ⊗ B⁺); for a rational subset U = R(f/g) of Spa(A, A⁺), Spa(ι)⁻¹(U) is the rational subset R(ι(f)/ι(g)) and O(U) ⊗_A B ≅ B⟨ι(f)/ι(g)⟩ as topological rings, compatibly with plus rings. (vi) Comparison: if A is strongly noetherian or has a noetherian ring of definition, (B, B⁺) is the pair `Huber.Pair.finiteAlgebra` of AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-algebra-over-affinoid, and Spa(B, B⁺) → Spa(A, A⁺) is finite and étale in Huber's sense (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-etale-algebra-comparison, Huber 1.6.6(ii)). Sheafiness of (B, B⁺) is not part of this construction: it holds when A is strongly sheafy (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-strongly-sheafy) and is not known for A merely sheafy (Kedlaya–Liu Remark 8.2.18). The comparison FÉt(A) ≃ FÉt(A^u) with the uniformisation belongs to AdicEtaleGeometry:A4.
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) a complete Hausdorff Tate Huber pair; no sheafiness or noetherian hypothesis.
B finite étale over A as a ring (finite, flat, finitely presented, unramified); topology = natural module topology.
B⁺ is the integral closure of the image of A⁺, never B° (the two differ when A⁺ ≠ A°).
proofSteps: B is finite projective over A: étale gives flat and finitely presented (mathlib:Algebra.Etale), and a finite, finitely presented flat module is projective (Kedlaya–Liu §1.2, Definition 1.2.1 discussion).

Topology: Kedlaya–Liu Lemma 2.2.12 (subspace = quotient topology for B ⊕ Q ≅ Aⁿ, independent of choices); B is closed in Aⁿ, hence Hausdorff and complete (tauceti:TauCeti.completeSpace_moduleTopology); it is the module topology (mathlib:moduleTopology, tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.isModuleTopology), so A-linear maps out of B, in particular multiplication by elements and the multiplication map written in a finite free presentation, are continuous (mathlib:IsModuleTopology.continuous_of_linearMap).

Tate structure: ϖ^N b_j integral over A₀ for N ≫ 0 (scale the coefficients of an integral equation of b_j into A₀); B₀ is the image of A₀^m under the open quotient map A^m → B, hence open; ϖB₀-adic topology on B₀ is the subspace topology; ι(ϖ) is a topologically nilpotent unit.

Plus ring: the subring generated by ι(A⁺) and B₀ is open and consists of power-bounded elements, so its integral closure is a ring of integral elements (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.isRingOfIntegralElements_integralClosure); it equals the integral closure of ι(A⁺) because B₀ is integral over ι(A₀) ⊆ ι(A⁺) (mathlib:integralClosure).

(iii) A → B module-finite and A⁺ → B⁺ integral: finite morphism (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-huber-pair-hom); Spa(ι) is tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spaComap, continuous by tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.continuous_spaComap. Fibre over x: points of Spa(B, B⁺) over x are continuous valuations on the finite étale k(x)^-algebra B ⊗_A k(x)^ (a product of finite separable field extensions) extending x and bounded by 1 on B⁺; each factor carries at most one extension per point of its fibre and, when B is faithfully flat, B ⊗ k(x)^ ≠ 0 and the valuation ring of x extends to a factor (extension of valuation rings); the extension is continuous and is ≤ 1 on B⁺ because valuation rings are integrally closed (compare Kedlaya–Liu Lemma 2.3.14 for the Gel'fand spectrum).
(iv) Continuity of an A-algebra map B → D is automatic by the module topology (step 2), and it carries B⁺ into D⁺ because D⁺ is integrally closed in D and contains χ(A⁺).

(v) AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-algebra-tensor-complete (ii)–(iii) in the finite projective case (no completion needed), mathlib:Algebra.Etale.baseChange for étaleness, integral closure of the image of C⁺ = integral closure of the image of C⁺ ⊗ B⁺ since B⁺ is integral over A⁺; rational preimages: tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spaComap_preimage_rationalSubset; the pullback along a rational localisation is computed by the uncompleted tensor product as recorded in AdicEtaleGeometry:A0/finite-etale-pullback-comparison.

(vi) Both pairs carry the natural module topology and the integral-closure plus ring (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-algebra-over-affinoid); Huber-étaleness is AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-etale-algebra-comparison.
acceptance: For a complete nonarchimedean field K with open valuation subring K⁺ and a finite separable extension L/K, the pair is (L, L⁺) with L⁺ the integral closure of K⁺ in L; for K⁺ = O_K this is (L, O_L).

nodes.title: Finite étale algebras over strongly sheafy Tate rings are strongly sheafy
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a complete Tate Huber pair with A strongly sheafy (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strongly-sheafy-huber-pair) and let B be a finite étale A-algebra with its pair (B, B⁺) = `Huber.Pair.finiteEtale A⁺ B` (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra). Then B is strongly sheafy; in particular (B, B⁺) is sheafy and Spa(B, B⁺) is an affinoid adic space. The proof passes through two statements recorded here: (i) B is locally monogenic over Spa(A, A⁺): there are a finite rational covering {U_k} of Spa(A, A⁺) and monic polynomials P_k ∈ O(U_k)[T] with invertible discriminant such that B ⊗_A O(U_k) ≅ O(U_k)[T]/(P_k) (= O(U_k)⟨T⟩/(P_k)); (ii) (Hansen–Kedlaya Corollary 4.7) a finite, flat, locally free, locally monogenic extension of a strongly sheafy ring is strongly sheafy. Special cases with direct proofs: if A is strongly noetherian, so is B (B⟨T_1, …, T_n⟩ = B ⊗_A A⟨T_1, …, T_n⟩ is finite over a noetherian ring); if A has a noetherian ring of definition A₀, B has the noetherian ring of definition B₀ of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra (i). Boundary: for A only sheafy, sheafiness of B is not known (Kedlaya–Liu Remark 8.2.18); for A stably uniform, B is uniform but not known to be stably uniform (Hansen–Kedlaya Definition 3.13).
hypotheses: A complete Tate and strongly sheafy; B finite étale over A as a ring.
Locally monogenic is meant locally on Spa(A, A⁺) (rational localisations), as in Hansen–Kedlaya's proof of Corollary 4.7.
proofSteps: Residue fields are infinite: for a prime 𝔭 = supp(x), x ∈ Spa(A, A⁺), and a pseudouniformiser ϖ, no power ϖ^N is ≡ 1 mod 𝔭, since 1 − ϖ^N is a unit of the complete ring A; so κ(𝔭) contains elements of infinite multiplicative order.
Primitive elements: B ⊗_A κ(𝔭) is a finite étale algebra over the infinite field κ(𝔭), hence generated by one element whose minimal polynomial is separable; lift it to b ∈ B.

Spreading out: let r be the rank of B at 𝔭 and φ: A^r → B, e_i ↦ b^{i−1}; the finitely generated A-module coker φ vanishes at 𝔭 (Nakayama), so some g ∈ Ann(coker φ) has g ∉ 𝔭, i.e. g(x) ≠ 0; x lies in the rational subset U = {|ϖ^N| ≤ |g|} for N ≫ 0 (continuity of x), on which g is a unit; there φ ⊗ O(U) is a surjection between finite projective O(U)-modules of rank r, hence an isomorphism (mathlib:Module.Projective), and B ⊗_A O(U) ≅ O(U)[T]/(χ_b) for the characteristic polynomial χ_b of multiplication by b (Cayley–Hamilton), whose discriminant is a unit because B is étale. No completion is needed (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra (v)). Quasi-compactness of Spa(A, A⁺) gives (i).

Hansen–Kedlaya Corollary 4.7 on each U_k: O(U_k) is strongly sheafy (rational localisation, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strongly-sheafy-huber-pair (b)), and B_k := O(U_k)[T]/(P_k) is strongly sheafy by the exact sequence 0 → O → O → j_*Õ_V → 0 on Spa(O(U_k)⟨T_1, …, T_{n+1}⟩) given by multiplication by P(T_{n+1}) and Hansen–Kedlaya Theorem 4.2.

Globalise: the preimages of the U_k form a rational covering of Spa(B, B⁺) (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra (v)); B → H⁰(Spa(B, B⁺), O) is an isomorphism and the higher Čech cohomology of this covering vanishes, because the Čech complex is that of the covering {U_k} of the sheafy Spa(A, A⁺) (Čech-acyclic by AdicSpacesPartII:R3/sheafy-cech-acyclicity) tensored with the flat A-module B; conclude by the locality clause (c) of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strongly-sheafy-huber-pair (Hansen–Kedlaya Corollary 4.5).
Special cases: tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsStronglyNoetherian for B⟨T⟩ = B ⊗_A A⟨T⟩ finite over A⟨T⟩; B₀ finite over the noetherian A₀.
acceptance: The Kummer algebra B = K⟨T, T⁻¹⟩[S]/(S² − T) over the annulus is strongly sheafy; indeed B ≅ K⟨S, S⁻¹⟩ is strongly noetherian.
For B = Aⁿ the conclusion is the stability of strong sheafiness under finite products.

Applied with A perfectoid or sousperfectoid (downstream: PerfectoidSpaces, AdicSpacesPartII:R5), it recovers sheafiness of finite étale covers of such affinoids once those rings are shown to be strongly sheafy.

nodes.title: Rational coverings are effective descent morphisms for finite étale algebras
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a complete Tate Huber pair (no sheafiness assumed) and {U_i}_{i=1}^n a finite rational covering of Spa(A, A⁺), with rational localisations A_i = O(U_i) and A_{ij} = O(U_i ∩ U_j), A_{ijk} = O(U_i ∩ U_j ∩ U_k). Then A → A_1 × ⋯ × A_n is an effective descent morphism for finite étale algebras (Kedlaya–Liu Theorem 2.6.9): the functor sending B ∈ FÉt(A) to ((B ⊗_A A_i)_i, canonical isomorphisms over the A_{ij}) is an equivalence onto the category of descent data (B_i ∈ FÉt(A_i), φ_{ij}: B_i ⊗_{A_i} A_{ij} ≅ B_j ⊗_{A_j} A_{ij} satisfying the cocycle condition over the A_{ijk}). All tensor products are uncompleted, the algebras being finite projective (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra (v)); the equivalence is compatible with the plus rings of the associated pairs. Every rational covering has a finite rational subcovering, so the statement covers all rational coverings.
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) complete Tate; {U_i} a finite rational covering.
Descent data are taken in finite étale algebras with uncompleted tensor products.
proofSteps: Choose an affinoid system (A_α, A_α⁺) with completed direct limit (A, A⁺) (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/affinoid-system-approximation); for α large the covering {U_i} is the preimage of a rational covering {U_{α,i}} of Spa(A_α, A_α⁺), and the rational localisations of the A_α form affinoid systems with completed limits A_i, A_{ij}, A_{ijk} (same node, (a)).

By AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-approximation, each B_i descends to some B_{α,i} ∈ FÉt(A_{α,i}), the isomorphisms φ_{ij} descend after enlarging α (full faithfulness of 2-colim_α FÉt(A_{α,ij}) → FÉt(A_{ij})), and the cocycle condition holds after enlarging α again (Kedlaya–Liu proof of Theorem 2.6.9).

At the stage α the ring A_α is a strongly noetherian Tate ring: the underlying finite projective modules glue by Kiehl's theorem on the strongly noetherian affinoid Spa(A_α, A_α⁺) (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/tate-kiehl-affinoid), the algebra structure glues because morphisms of finite modules glue (Spa(A_α, A_α⁺) is sheafy, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/noetherian-rod-sheafy), and the glued algebra B_α is étale: A_α → ∏_i A_{α,i} is faithfully flat for the strongly noetherian Tate ring A_α (tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.faithfullyFlat_pi_toCompletionLoc, Wedhorn Corollary 8.32), B_α ⊗ ∏_i A_{α,i} = ∏_i B_{α,i} is étale, and étaleness descends along faithfully flat maps (mathlib:Algebra.Etale.of_etale_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat).

Set B := B_α ⊗_{A_α} A; then B ⊗_A A_i ≅ B_i compatibly with the φ_{ij} (mathlib:Algebra.Etale.baseChange). Full faithfulness of B ↦ descent datum: a compatible family of A_i-algebra maps is defined at a finite stage and glues there (Kiehl), and two maps agreeing on every U_i agree at a finite stage (full faithfulness in AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-approximation).

The trivial covering {Spa(A, A⁺)} gives the identity equivalence.

nodes.title: Complete Tate pairs are completed direct limits of noetherian affinoid pairs
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a complete Tate Huber pair and ϖ ∈ A⁺ a pseudouniformiser. There is a filtered system (A_α, A_α⁺)_{α ∈ I} of complete Tate Huber pairs with continuous transition maps and compatible continuous maps to (A, A⁺) — an affinoid system in the sense of Kedlaya–Liu Definition 2.6.1 — such that: each A_α is a quotient of a Tate algebra ℤ((z))⟨S_1, …, S_m⟩ (z ↦ ϖ) by a closed ideal, so A_α has the noetherian ring of definition given by the image of ℤ⟦z⟧⟨S_1, …, S_m⟩ and is strongly noetherian (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/noetherian-type-huber-ring), and A_α⁺ is the integral closure of the image of ℤ⟦z⟧⟨S⟩ (Kedlaya–Liu take the image itself; the integral closure has the same adic spectrum, Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.spa_integralClosure`, and still maps into A⁺); colim_α A_α → A has dense image, (A, A⁺) is the completion of (colim_α A_α, colim_α A_α⁺) (Kedlaya–Liu Lemma 2.6.2). Moreover: (a) the restriction map Spa(A, A⁺) → lim_α Spa(A_α, A_α⁺) is a homeomorphism; every rational subset, and every finite rational covering, of Spa(A, A⁺) is the preimage of one of some Spa(A_α, A_α⁺), and then the rational localisations of the A_β (β ≥ α) form an affinoid system whose completed direct limit is the rational localisation of A (Kedlaya–Liu Remark 2.6.3, Lemma 2.6.5, Remark 2.6.7); (b) for a finite étale A_α-algebra B_α, the base changes B_α ⊗_{A_α} A_β (β ≥ α) with their finite étale pairs form an affinoid system with completed direct limit the pair `Huber.Pair.finiteEtale A⁺ (B_α ⊗_{A_α} A)` (no completion needed, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra (v)), and the map Spa(B_α ⊗ A) → Spa(B_α) ×_{Spa(A_α)} Spa(A) of underlying sets is surjective.
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) complete Tate, arbitrary (not necessarily sheafy or noetherian).
The index set I is the set of finite subsets of A⁺; A_α is topologised by the quotient topology of the Tate algebra.
proofSteps: Kedlaya–Liu Lemma 2.6.2: for a finite subset S ⊂ A⁺ let A_S be ℤ((z))⟨S⟩/ker, the kernel of the continuous map to A sending z to ϖ and each variable s to s ∈ S (closed since A is Hausdorff), with the quotient topology, and A_S⁺ the integral closure of the image of ℤ⟦z⟧⟨S⟩; elements of A_S⁺ map into A⁺ because A⁺ is integrally closed (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.isRingOfIntegralElements_integralClosure, tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spa_integralClosure). ℤ⟦z⟧⟨S⟩ is noetherian, so A_S has a noetherian ring of definition.
Colimit and completion: the union of the images of the A_S⁺ is dense in A⁺ because every element of A⁺ lies in some A_S⁺; completing recovers (A, A⁺).

(a) A continuous valuation on A bounded by 1 on A⁺ is the same as a compatible family of such valuations on the A_S (Kedlaya–Liu Remark 2.6.3); rational subsets are defined by finitely many elements, which lie in some A_S (Kedlaya–Liu Remark 2.4.7, Lemma 2.6.5(a)); a finite covering is defined at a stage where all its data are (Kedlaya–Liu Remark 2.6.7).

(b) B_α is finite projective, so completed tensor products with it are uncompleted (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra (v)); surjectivity on points: a point of Spa(B_α) and a point of Spa(A) over the same point of Spa(A_α) come from continuous valuations on the two factors agreeing on A_α, which extend jointly to B_α ⊗_{A_α} A (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/valuation-amalgamation).
acceptance: For A = K a complete nonarchimedean extension of ℚ_p with ϖ = p (so ℤ((z)) maps onto ℚ_p), the A_α are the closed ℚ_p-subalgebras of K topologically generated by finitely many elements of K⁺, and |Spa(K, K⁺)| = lim |Spa(A_α, A_α⁺)|.
A rational subset R(f/g) of Spa(A, A⁺) is the preimage of R(f/g) ⊆ Spa(A_S, A_S⁺) for any S containing ϖ^N f, ϖ^N g with N large.

nodes.title: Finite étale algebras over a complete Tate ring are defined at a finite stage of an affinoid system
nodes.statement: Let (A_α, A_α⁺)_α be an affinoid system with completed direct limit (A, A⁺) (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/affinoid-system-approximation), and A_∞ := colim_α A_α (in rings). Then the base change functors 2-colim_α FÉt(A_α) → FÉt(A_∞) → FÉt(A) are tensor equivalences (Kedlaya–Liu Remark 1.2.9 and Proposition 2.6.8). Concretely: every finite étale A-algebra is B_α ⊗_{A_α} A for some α and B_α ∈ FÉt(A_α); for B_α, B'_α ∈ FÉt(A_α), every A-algebra map B_α ⊗ A → B'_α ⊗ A comes from an A_β-algebra map for some β ≥ α, and two maps agreeing over A agree over some A_β; ranks are preserved. The same holds with (A, A⁺) replaced by any rational localisation, using the induced affinoid systems.
hypotheses: (A_α) an affinoid system of complete Tate pairs (Kedlaya–Liu Definition 2.6.1) with completed direct limit (A, A⁺).
proofSteps: 2-colim_α FÉt(A_α) → FÉt(A_∞) is an equivalence: finite étale algebras are finitely presented, so each is defined at a finite stage, and morphisms and étaleness descend to a finite stage (Kedlaya–Liu Remark 1.2.9, EGA IV 17.7.8).

Full faithfulness of FÉt(A_∞) → FÉt(A): (A_∞, ker α) is a henselian pair for the infimum seminorm α (Kedlaya–Liu Lemma 2.2.3(a)), so FÉt(A_∞) ≃ FÉt(A_∞/ker α) (Kedlaya–Liu Theorem 1.2.8), and idempotents of B ⊗ A lift uniquely (Kedlaya–Liu Lemma 2.2.4(a) and Proposition 1.2.5).

Essential surjectivity: for V ∈ FÉt(A) and a point β of the Gel'fand spectrum M(A), V descends over the Hausdorff localisation colim_α A_{α,β} (Kedlaya–Liu Corollary 2.6.6 and Lemma 2.2.4(b)); by compactness of M(A) there are a stage α and a strong rational covering of Spa(A_α, A_α⁺) over whose members V descends, with isomorphisms on overlaps satisfying the cocycle condition after enlarging α; glue on the noetherian affinoid Spa(A_α, A_α⁺) by Kiehl's theorem (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/tate-kiehl-affinoid; Kedlaya–Liu Theorem 2.5.20(b), Corollary 2.5.19).

The Banach-ring inputs of the last two steps (the Gel'fand spectrum M(A), Hausdorff localisations, Kedlaya–Liu Lemmas 2.2.3–2.2.4 and Corollary 2.6.6) have no nodes in this roadmap or in AdicSpacesPartII; they are recorded as a gap of this node.

nodes.title: Finite étale morphisms of analytic adic spaces by the local algebraic description
nodes.statement: Let f: Y → X be a morphism of analytic adic spaces (anchor Layer 5; every morphism into an analytic adic space is adic, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-morphism). f is finite étale (`AdicSpace.IsFiniteEtale f`) if X has a covering by open affinoid subspaces V = Spa(A, A⁺) such that, for each of them, f⁻¹(V) is affinoid, B := O_Y(f⁻¹(V)) is a finite étale A-algebra via f^♯, and the morphism of Huber pairs (O_X(V), O_X⁺(V)) → (O_Y(f⁻¹V), O_Y⁺(f⁻¹V)) is the morphism (A, A⁺) → `Huber.Pair.finiteEtale A⁺ B` of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra (natural topology on B, plus ring the integral closure of A⁺); equivalently f⁻¹(V) ≅ Spa(B, B⁺) over V with B ∈ FÉt(A) (Kedlaya–Liu Definition 8.2.16, Scholze 2012 Definition 7.1(ii)). The condition is local on the target by definition. Its 'every open affinoid' form (the shape of ECD Definition 6.2(i)) holds over open affinoids with strongly sheafy coordinate ring (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-local-to-global). Conventions: the plus ring is part of the condition (a finite étale ring map with plus ring B° is not finite étale in this sense when A⁺ ≠ A°); f need not be surjective (the empty space over X, and the inclusion of a clopen subspace, are finite étale); on locally noetherian analytic spaces the notion is Huber's 'finite and étale' (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphisms-local-description-and-comparison). The same local condition read in the category of analytic Yoneda-adic spaces (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/generalized-adic-presentation) is Kedlaya–Liu's notion for preadic spaces (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site-generalized).
hypotheses: f a morphism of analytic adic spaces (anchor Layer 5 objects all of whose points are analytic).
The defining cover is part of the existence statement; no particular cover is fixed.
proofSteps: Define `AdicSpace.IsFiniteEtale f` as the existence of an open affinoid cover of X with the stated property; the affinoid model is Spa of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra, which is an adic space when its pair is sheafy (anchor Layer 5 affinoid adic spaces).

Stability under isomorphism and restriction to open subspaces of X: an open subspace is covered by rational subsets of the defining affinoids, and rational restriction of a finite étale pair is finite étale (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra (v)).
acceptance: The fold map X ⊔ X → X is finite étale of degree 2; ∅ → X is finite étale of degree 0.
The Kummer map Spa(K⟨S, S⁻¹⟩) → Spa(K⟨T, T⁻¹⟩), T ↦ S² (char K ≠ 2), is finite étale of degree 2.
The squaring map on the closed unit disc, T ↦ S², is finite but not finite étale (ramified at the origin).

nodes.title: Local-to-global recognition of finite étale morphisms over strongly sheafy affinoids
nodes.statement: Let f: Y → X be a finite étale morphism of analytic adic spaces (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-morphism) and V = Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ X an open affinoid subspace with A strongly sheafy (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strongly-sheafy-huber-pair; automatic when X is locally strongly sheafy). Then: (a) B := O_Y(f⁻¹(V)) is a finite étale A-algebra, f⁻¹(V) is affinoid and f⁻¹(V) ≅ Spa(`Huber.Pair.finiteEtale A⁺ B`) over V; (b) consequently, on a locally strongly sheafy X, f is finite étale iff the preimage of every open affinoid is affinoid and finite étale over it (the form of ECD Definition 6.2(i)), iff this holds over the members of one open cover of X; (c) global sections give an equivalence between finite étale V-spaces and FÉt(A)^op, with quasi-inverse B ↦ Spa(`Huber.Pair.finiteEtale A⁺ B`) (Kedlaya–Liu Lemma 8.2.17(a)); (d) the degree x ↦ dim_{k(x)} (B ⊗_A k(x)) is locally constant on X, and f is surjective iff the degree is everywhere ≥ 1, iff each such B is faithfully flat over A; (e) f is finite in the sense of AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-morphism.
hypotheses: f finite étale; V an open affinoid of X whose coordinate ring A is strongly sheafy.
For V with A merely sheafy, (a) is not claimed: see AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site-generalized for the preadic statement.
proofSteps: Refine: every x ∈ V lies in a rational subset U of V contained in a member W = Spa(A_W, A_W⁺) of the defining cover of f and rational in W (as in AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strongly-sheafy-huber-pair, step (c)); then f⁻¹(U) = Spa(B_W ⊗_{A_W} O(U)) is the rational restriction of a finite étale pair (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra (v)). Quasi-compactness gives a finite rational covering {U_i} of V with f⁻¹(U_i) ≅ Spa(B_i, B_i⁺), B_i ∈ FÉt(O(U_i)).
The identifications of f⁻¹(U_i ∩ U_j) give a descent datum; AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-rational-descent yields B ∈ FÉt(A) with B ⊗_A O(U_i) ≅ B_i compatibly.

B is strongly sheafy (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-strongly-sheafy), so Spa(`Huber.Pair.finiteEtale A⁺ B`) is an affinoid adic space whose restriction over U_i is Spa(B_i, B_i⁺) (rational restriction); the isomorphisms over the U_i agree on overlaps and glue (anchor Layer 5 gluing of morphisms) to f⁻¹(V) ≅ Spa(B, B⁺); B = O_Y(f⁻¹V) by the sheaf property.

(c) Morphisms Spa(B', B'⁺) → Spa(B, B⁺) over V are morphisms of pairs (anchor Layer 5: morphisms into an affinoid adic space are morphisms of pairs of global sections; Kedlaya–Liu Lemma 8.2.9), which are A-algebra maps (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra (iv)); essential surjectivity is (a).

(d) The rank of the finite projective A-module B is locally constant on Spec A; the locus of rank 0 is cut out by an idempotent e, and Spa(eA, eA⁺) is the clopen part of V with empty fibre, nonempty iff eA ≠ 0; surjectivity elsewhere is AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra (iii).
(e) The morphism of pairs is finite (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-huber-pair-hom), so f satisfies the definition of AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-morphism.

For X = X_1 ⊔ X_2 the inclusion X_1 → X is finite étale of degree 1 on X_1 and 0 on X_2, not surjective.

nodes.title: Étale morphisms of analytic adic spaces by the local open-immersion/finite-étale description
nodes.statement: A morphism f: Y → X of analytic adic spaces is étale in A1's sense (`AdicSpace.IsEtaleLocalDescription f`) if every y ∈ Y has an open neighbourhood U ⊆ Y such that f|_U factors as U →^{j} W →^{g} V →^{i} X with j an open immersion, g finite étale (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-morphism) and i an open immersion (Kedlaya–Liu Definition 8.2.16; Scholze 2012 Definition 7.1(iii); ECD Definition 6.2(ii) for perfectoid spaces). Equivalent local form: V can be taken to be a rational subset of an open affinoid of X, W = g⁻¹(V) affinoid with W → V the Spa of a finite étale pair, and U a rational subset of W; that is, locally f is Spa(C, C⁺) ⊆ Spa(B, B⁺) → Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ X with A → B finite étale and B → C a rational localisation (a 'standard affinoid étale' morphism, the form used in ECD 6.4 and 15.6 and in Scholze 2013 Lemma 5.2). Conventions: open immersions and finite étale morphisms are étale; étaleness is local on the source and on the target; no separatedness or quasi-compactness is imposed (two copies of a disc glued along an open subset map étale to the disc); the name distinguishes this notion from Huber's `AdicSpace.Etale` (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/differentials-unramified-smooth-etale), with which it agrees on locally noetherian analytic spaces (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphisms-local-description-and-comparison); Huber's infinitesimal definition is not used on non-noetherian spaces.
hypotheses: f a morphism of analytic adic spaces; no noetherian, sheafiness-of-covers or separatedness hypothesis.
proofSteps: Define `AdicSpace.IsEtaleLocalDescription f` by the existence, around each y, of the factorisation j, g, i.

Standard affinoid form: given y with x = f(y) ∈ V, choose a member V₀ = Spa(A₀, A₀⁺) of a defining cover of g with x ∈ V₀ and g⁻¹(V₀) = Spa(B₀, B₀⁺), then a rational subset R ⊆ V₀ ∩ V with x ∈ R, rational in V₀; g⁻¹(R) = Spa(B₀ ⊗_{A₀} O(R)) (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra (v)); finally a rational subset of g⁻¹(R) containing j(y) and contained in j(U).
Locality on the source is built into the definition; locality on the target: restrict the factorisation to preimages of an open cover of X (open immersions and finite étale maps restrict).
Open immersions: take g = id; finite étale maps: take j, i = id.
acceptance: The inclusion of a rational subset, the fold map X ⊔ X → X and the Kummer map of the annulus are étale.
The inclusion of the origin Spa(K) → Spa(K⟨T⟩) is finite and unramified but not étale.

For K complete nonarchimedean and X = Spa(K⟨T⟩, K°⟨T⟩), the space obtained by gluing two copies of X along the open subset {|p| ≤ |T|} maps étale onto X by the identity on each copy, is not separated over X, and is neither finite étale nor an open immersion.

nodes.title: Comparison of A1's finite étale and étale morphisms with Huber's on locally noetherian analytic adic spaces
nodes.statement: Let X be a locally noetherian analytic adic space (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space; its affinoid charts can be taken to be Spa(A, A⁺) with A a complete strongly noetherian Tate ring) and f: Y → X a morphism of analytic adic spaces. (i) f is finite étale in A1's sense (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-morphism) iff f is finite (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-morphism) and étale in Huber's sense (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/differentials-unramified-smooth-etale: locally of finite presentation with bijective infinitesimal lifting against square-zero thickenings of affinoids). (ii) f is étale in A1's sense (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphism: locally an open immersion, a finite étale morphism and an open immersion) iff f is étale in Huber's sense. (iii) Consequently the category of adic spaces étale over X in A1's sense is Huber's Et/X, with the same morphisms (every X-morphism between them is étale in both senses); since both sites take the jointly surjective families as coverings (Huber §2.1), the étale site of X built on either description is the same (recorded as a compatibility of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site); every A1-étale Y → X enjoys Huber's local properties — standard étale presentations (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-local-structure), flatness and unramifiedness (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-flat-unramified), openness (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/smooth-morphism-open) and local quasi-finiteness (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/unramified-locally-quasi-finite). (iv) If f is étale, Y is again locally noetherian, so (i)–(iii) apply to every object of X_ét. Boundary: the direction 'Huber-étale ⇒ local description' is Huber's Lemma 2.2.8, which enters only through AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-local-open-finite-etale-factorisation (for affinoids over a field through AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-affinoid-finite-etale-embedding, de Jong–van der Put 3.1.4); the gap on Huber's unpublished proof is recorded on that node. No comparison is claimed for non-analytic (e.g. discretely ringed) adic spaces, and on non-noetherian spaces Huber's infinitesimal notion is not used.
hypotheses: X locally noetherian and analytic (so every chart is Spa of a complete strongly noetherian Tate ring).
Huber's Lemma 2.2.8 as imported by AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-local-open-finite-etale-factorisation.
proofSteps: Charts: an analytic chart of noetherian type is a Tate ring, and a Tate ring with a noetherian ring of definition is strongly noetherian (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/noetherian-type-huber-ring).

(i) ⇒: over a defining affinoid V = Spa(A, A⁺) with f⁻¹(V) = Spa(B, B⁺), B ∈ FÉt(A): the pair is R0's `Huber.Pair.finiteAlgebra` (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra (vi)), so f|_V is finite (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-algebra-over-affinoid) and Huber-étale (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-etale-algebra-comparison); finiteness and Huber-étaleness are local on the target (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-morphism, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-smooth-locality). ⇐: AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-morphism gives affinoid preimages finite over the members of a cover, and AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-etale-algebra-comparison identifies them with Spa of finite étale algebras with integral-closure plus rings.

(ii) A1 ⇒ Huber: open immersions are Huber-étale (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/open-embedding-etale), finite étale maps are by (i), composites are (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-smooth-composition), and Huber-étaleness is local on the source (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-smooth-locality). Huber ⇒ A1: AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-local-open-finite-etale-factorisation writes f locally as an open embedding into W followed by a finite Huber-étale W → V ⊆ X; W → V is finite étale in A1's sense by (i).

(iii) Objects agree by (ii); an X-morphism h between étale X-spaces is Huber-étale by Huber's cancellation (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-smooth-cancellation; étale maps are unramified), hence étale in A1's sense by (ii); coverings are the jointly surjective families on both sides (Huber §2.1). Huber's local properties transfer along (ii).

(iv) Y is locally of finite type over X, and its charts are rational subsets of finite étale covers of strongly noetherian Tate affinoids, which are strongly noetherian (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-strongly-sheafy, special case).
acceptance: The Kummer map Spa(K⟨S, S⁻¹⟩) → Spa(K⟨T, T⁻¹⟩), T ↦ S² (char K ≠ 2), is finite étale in both senses.
The inclusion {|T| ≤ |p|} ⊆ Spa(ℚ_p⟨T⟩, ℤ_p⟨T⟩) is étale in both senses and finite in neither.
The analytification of an étale morphism of schemes of finite type over K is étale in both senses (Huber 1.7.3(i), AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-etale-smooth, transported by (ii)).

nodes.title: Base change of finite étale and étale morphisms along morphisms of locally strongly sheafy spaces
nodes.statement: Let f: Y → X be finite étale (resp. étale) (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-morphism, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphism) and g: X' → X any morphism of analytic adic spaces with X' locally strongly sheafy (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strongly-sheafy-huber-pair). Then the fibre product Y' := Y ×_X X' exists in the category of adic spaces, Y' is locally strongly sheafy, and the projection f': Y' → X' is finite étale (resp. étale). Affinoid formula: if V = Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ X is open with f⁻¹(V) = Spa(B, B⁺), B ∈ FÉt(A), and V' = Spa(C, C⁺) ⊆ g⁻¹(V) is an open affinoid, then f'⁻¹(V') = Spa(`Huber.Pair.finiteEtale C⁺ (C ⊗_A B)`), with the uncompleted tensor product and plus ring the integral closure of the image of C⁺ ⊗ B⁺; for a local description U ⊆ W → V ⊆ X of an étale f, the base change over g⁻¹(V) is the open subspace of W ×_V g⁻¹(V) lying over U. Points: the map |Y'| → |Y| ×_{|X|} |X'| is surjective, so jointly surjective families of étale maps pull back to jointly surjective families. The same conclusions hold for an arbitrary analytic X' whenever every algebra C ⊗_A B occurring in the construction is sheafy; without such sheafiness the fibre product is only formed among Yoneda-adic spaces (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site-generalized); fibre products of adic spaces are not asserted to exist in general (Kedlaya–Liu Remark 8.2.5).
hypotheses: f finite étale or étale in A1's sense; g arbitrary (adic, since X is analytic).
X' locally strongly sheafy, or at least every finite étale algebra C ⊗_A B of the construction sheafy.
proofSteps: Affinoid finite étale case: D := C ⊗_A B is finite étale over C (mathlib:Algebra.Etale.baseChange); its pair `Huber.Pair.finiteEtale C⁺ D` is the completed tensor product of pairs without completion (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra (v)) and is strongly sheafy (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-strongly-sheafy), so Spa of it is the fibre product of affinoid adic spaces (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-fibre-product, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product-universal-property); this is the uncompleted-tensor pullback of AdicEtaleGeometry:A0/finite-etale-pullback-comparison.

Global finite étale case: cover X' by strongly sheafy open affinoids V' each mapping into a member V of a defining cover of f; form the affinoid pieces and glue them along the canonical isomorphisms given by their universal properties (anchor Layer 5 gluing); the result satisfies the universal property of the fibre product because it does so locally, and f' is finite étale by construction.

Open immersions: the base change of an open immersion U ⊆ X is the open subspace g⁻¹(U) (AdicEtaleGeometry:A0/rational-pullback-comparison for rational U; anchor Layer 5 in general); the local description of an étale f pulls back piece by piece, and the pieces glue.
Local strong sheafiness of Y': it is covered by rational subsets of the Spa(D, D⁺), which are strongly sheafy (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strongly-sheafy-huber-pair (b)).

Points: for y ∈ Y and x' ∈ X' over the same point of X, reduce to the affinoid finite étale case; the valuations on B and C agree on A and extend jointly to C ⊗_A B (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/valuation-amalgamation; Huber Corollary 1.2.3(d)); the extension is continuous and ≤ 1 on the plus ring, which is integral over the image of C⁺ ⊗ B⁺.

The base change of the rational inclusion {|T| ≤ |p|} ⊆ Spa(K⟨T⟩) along the squaring map T ↦ S² is the rational subset {|S²| ≤ |p|} of Spa(K⟨S⟩).
