nodes.title: Composites of finite étale, resp. étale, morphisms
nodes.statement: Let g: Z → Y and f: Y → X be morphisms of analytic adic spaces with X locally strongly sheafy. (i) If f and g are finite étale, so is f ∘ g: over an open affinoid V = Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ X, (f ∘ g)⁻¹(V) = Spa(C, C⁺) with C finite étale over B = O_Y(f⁻¹V) and hence over A, and C⁺ the integral closure of A⁺ in C. (ii) If f and g are étale, so is f ∘ g. (iii) An étale Y over a locally strongly sheafy X is locally strongly sheafy. The content of (ii) is the local statement: for A strongly sheafy, B ∈ FÉt(A), a rational localisation B → B' and C ∈ FÉt(B'), every point of Spa(C, C⁺) has a neighbourhood that is a rational subset of Spa(D, D⁺) for some D ∈ FÉt(A'), A' a rational localisation of A — 'finite étale after rational after finite étale' is locally 'rational after finite étale after rational' (Kedlaya–Liu Lemma 8.2.17(c)).
hypotheses: X locally strongly sheafy (so that all finite étale pieces are adic affinoids).
(ii) relies on Huber's Lemma 2.2.8 at a noetherian stage (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-local-open-finite-etale-factorisation).
proofSteps: (iii) The charts of Y are rational subsets of Spa of finite étale algebras over strongly sheafy rings (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphism, standard affinoid form), strongly sheafy by AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-strongly-sheafy and AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strongly-sheafy-huber-pair (b).

(i) AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-local-to-global gives f⁻¹(V) = Spa(B, B⁺), B ∈ FÉt(A), B strongly sheafy; applied to g over the affinoid Spa(B, B⁺) it gives g⁻¹ = Spa(C, C⁺), C ∈ FÉt(B); C ∈ FÉt(A) by mathlib:Algebra.Etale.comp and mathlib:Module.Finite.trans; integral closure is transitive (mathlib:integralClosure).

(ii) Reduction: using the standard affinoid form of both maps and shrinking, f ∘ g is locally Spa(C'') ⊆ Spa(C) → Spa(B') ⊆ Spa(B) → Spa(A) ⊆ X with the inner maps finite étale and the inclusions rational; it suffices to treat Spa(C, C⁺) → Spa(A, A⁺) with C ∈ FÉt(B'), B' = B⟨R⟩ rational in B ∈ FÉt(A).

Approximation: choose an affinoid system (A_α) for A (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/affinoid-system-approximation); B, the rational subset R and C descend to B_α ∈ FÉt(A_α), R_α ⊆ Spa(B_α) rational and C_α ∈ FÉt(B_α⟨R_α⟩) for α large (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-approximation applied to (A_α) and to the induced systems), with C = C_α ⊗_{A_α} A.

Noetherian stage: A_α is strongly noetherian, Spa(C_α) → Spa(A_α) is a composite of finite étale maps and a rational inclusion, hence Huber-étale (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphisms-local-description-and-comparison (ii), AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-smooth-composition), hence locally an open immersion into a finite étale cover of a rational subset of Spa(A_α) (same comparison node, direction Huber ⇒ A1, Huber 2.2.8).

Base change back along A_α → A (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-base-change; rational subsets pull back to the rational subsets defined by the same functions): the local factorisations of Spa(C_α) → Spa(A_α) pull back to local factorisations of Spa(C) → Spa(A), and they cover Spa(C) because Spa(C) → Spa(C_α) ×_{Spa A_α} Spa(A) is surjective (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/affinoid-system-approximation (b)).

The composite of the rational inclusion {|S − 1| ≤ |p|} ⊆ Spa(K⟨S, S⁻¹⟩) with the Kummer map S ↦ S² = T is étale; it is an open immersion onto {|T − 1| ≤ |p|}, since |T − 1| = |S − 1||S + 1| = |S − 1| there.

nodes.title: The diagonal of an étale morphism is an open immersion; of a finite étale morphism, open and closed
nodes.statement: Let f: Y → X be an étale morphism of analytic adic spaces with X locally strongly sheafy, so that Y ×_X Y exists (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-base-change). Then the diagonal Δ_f: Y → Y ×_X Y is an open immersion. If f is finite étale, Δ_f is an open and closed immersion: over an open affinoid V = Spa(A, A⁺) with f⁻¹(V) = Spa(B, B⁺), Δ_f is Spa(B, B⁺) ≅ Spa(e(B ⊗_A B)) ⊆ Spa(B ⊗_A B) for the diagonal idempotent e ∈ B ⊗_A B (multiplication sends e to 1, and e kills the kernel of multiplication). Consequences: (a) for étale X-spaces U, W and X-morphisms s, t: U ⇉ W, the equaliser of s and t is the open subspace (s, t)⁻¹(Δ_W) of U, étale over X; so the category of étale X-spaces has equalisers, and for finite étale X-spaces the equaliser is open and closed; (b) every section of an étale morphism is an open immersion, and every section of a finite étale morphism is an open and closed immersion.
hypotheses: f étale (resp. finite étale) in A1's sense; X locally strongly sheafy.
proofSteps: Finite étale case: mathlib:Algebra.FormallyUnramified.iff_exists_tensorProduct gives e ∈ B ⊗_A B with lmul'(e) = 1 (mathlib:Algebra.TensorProduct.lmul') and (1 ⊗ b − b ⊗ 1)e = 0; e is idempotent, B ⊗_A B ≅ e(B ⊗_A B) × (1 − e)(B ⊗_A B), and lmul' restricts to an isomorphism e(B ⊗_A B) ≅ B (Kedlaya–Liu Definition 1.2.2). Both factors are finite étale over A, and idempotents correspond to open and closed subsets of the adic spectrum (Kedlaya–Liu Proposition 2.6.4); Spa(B ⊗_A B) = f⁻¹V ×_V f⁻¹V (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-base-change).

Étale case: locally f|_U is U ⊆ W → V ⊆ X with W → V finite étale; U ×_X U is the open subspace U ×_V U of W ×_V W, and Δ_f|_U is the restriction of Δ_{W/V} to the open U, an open immersion. Δ_f is injective on points, being a section of the first projection, and a local open immersion, hence an open immersion (anchor Layer 5).
(a) (s, t): U → W ×_X W is a morphism and the equaliser is the fibre product with Δ_W; (b) a section σ of f is the base change of Δ_f along (σ ∘ f, id): Y → Y ×_X Y restricted to X ≅ σ(X).

nodes.statement: Let X be a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space and p: Y → X, q: Z → X étale (resp. finite étale) morphisms. Every X-morphism h: Y → Z is étale (resp. finite étale). Equivalently: if q and q ∘ h are étale (resp. finite étale), so is h.

nodes.title: Étale morphisms are open; quasi-compact étale maps factor through their open images
nodes.statement: Let f: Y → X be an étale morphism of analytic adic spaces with X locally strongly sheafy. (i) f is open on underlying spaces. (ii) If Y is quasi-compact, f(Y) is a quasi-compact open subset of X and f factors uniquely as Y → Z → X with Y → Z surjective and étale, Z the quasi-compact open subspace f(Y) and Z → X its inclusion (Kedlaya–Liu Lemma 8.2.17(b)); if moreover X is affinoid, f(Y) is a finite union of rational subsets (de Jong–van der Put Proposition 3.1.7(1)). (iii) A family of étale maps (Y_i → X) is jointly surjective iff the open images cover X; for X quasi-compact finitely many quasi-compact opens V_j ⊆ Y_{i_j} already have images covering X.
hypotheses: X locally strongly sheafy; f étale in A1's sense.
proofSteps: Open immersions are open and composites of open maps are open, so by the local description it suffices to show that Spa(B, B⁺) → Spa(A, A⁺) is open for A strongly sheafy and B ∈ FÉt(A), i.e. that the image of a rational subset W ⊆ Spa(B, B⁺) is open.

Approximation: B = B_α ⊗_{A_α} A and W is the preimage of a rational W_α ⊆ Spa(B_α, B_α⁺) for an affinoid system (A_α) (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/affinoid-system-approximation, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-approximation).

At the noetherian stage Spa(B_α) → Spa(A_α) is finite and Huber-étale (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphisms-local-description-and-comparison (i)), hence open (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/smooth-morphism-open, Huber 1.7.8): its image of W_α is open.

The image of W is the preimage of the image of W_α under Spa(A) → Spa(A_α): '⊆' is clear, and '⊇' follows from the surjectivity of Spa(B) → Spa(B_α) ×_{Spa A_α} Spa(A) on points (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/affinoid-system-approximation (b)).

(ii) Images of quasi-compact sets are quasi-compact; restriction of f to the open subspace f(Y) is étale and surjective; uniqueness because open subspaces are determined by their underlying sets (anchor Layer 5); quasi-compact opens of an affinoid are finite unions of rational subsets (anchor Layer 2). (iii) is formal.

nodes.title: The small étale site of a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space
nodes.statement: Let X be a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strongly-sheafy-huber-pair). The small étale site X_ét consists of: the category Et/X = `AdicSpace.smallEtale X`, the full subcategory of adic spaces over X whose structure morphism is étale in A1's sense (Mathlib `MorphismProperty.Over` of `AdicSpace.IsEtaleLocalDescription` over X, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphism), all X-morphisms being admitted (they are automatically étale, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-cancellation); and the Grothendieck topology `AdicSpace.smallEtaleTopology X` generated by the pretopology of jointly surjective families: (f_i: U_i → U)_i is a covering iff |U| = ∪_i f_i(|U_i|), all points counted, including points of higher rank (Kedlaya–Liu Definition 8.2.19; Huber §2.1; Berkeley Definition 7.5.1(3)). Properties: (i) Et/X has the final object X, fibre products (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-base-change) and equalisers (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-diagonal), hence all finite limits, and its objects are locally strongly sheafy (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-composition (iii)); (ii) the jointly surjective families form a Mathlib `Pretopology` (isomorphisms; stability under base change by the surjectivity of |U ×_V W| → |U| ×_{|V|} |W|; composition); (iii) open subspaces of X are objects and open coverings are coverings, and the inclusion of the analytic site (Mathlib `Opens.grothendieckTopology`) is a continuous functor preserving finite limits, giving the morphism of sites λ_X: X_ét → X_an; (iv) for a morphism g: X' → X of locally strongly sheafy analytic adic spaces, base change U ↦ U ×_X X' is a continuous functor Et/X → Et/X' preserving finite limits, defining a morphism of sites g_ét: X'_ét → X_ét with direct image (g_*F)(U) = F(U ×_X X') (Mathlib `Functor.sheafPushforwardContinuous`) and inverse image g^{-1} (Mathlib `Functor.sheafPullback`), with (h ∘ g)_ét ≅ h_ét ∘ g_ét canonically. On locally noetherian X this is Huber's X_et (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphisms-local-description-and-comparison). For an analytic X that is not locally strongly sheafy, Kedlaya–Liu's site with Yoneda-adic-space objects is AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site-generalized. These are geometric sites: no derived category or cohomology is defined here (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0).
hypotheses: X locally strongly sheafy analytic (so all fibre products of étale X-spaces exist among adic spaces).
Coverings are jointly surjective on all points of the adic spaces, not only on rank-one points.
proofSteps: Category: `MorphismProperty.Over (IsEtaleLocalDescription) ⊤ X` (mathlib:CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.Over); morphisms are all X-morphisms, étale by AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-cancellation.

Finite limits: X is final; fibre products AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-base-change together with AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-composition (the composite U ×_V W → W → X is étale); equalisers AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-diagonal (a).

Pretopology (mathlib:CategoryTheory.Pretopology): isomorphisms are surjective; pullback stability by the surjectivity statement of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-base-change; transitivity because unions of images compose. The topology is `Pretopology.toGrothendieck` (mathlib:CategoryTheory.Pretopology.toGrothendieck).

Analytic site: open immersions are étale (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphism); an open covering is jointly surjective; the functor Opens X → Et/X preserves finite limits (intersections are fibre products), hence is continuous (mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.IsContinuous).

Functoriality: base change preserves étaleness and joint surjectivity (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-base-change) and finite limits (pasting of cartesian squares), so it is continuous and yields mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafPushforwardContinuous and its left adjoint mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafPullback; composition isomorphisms from uniqueness of fibre products.
Comparison with Huber on locally noetherian X: AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphisms-local-description-and-comparison (iii).
acceptance: For X = Spa(K⟨T, T⁻¹⟩) (K ⊇ ℚ_p, p odd) the Kummer covering Spa(K⟨S, S⁻¹⟩) → X is a one-member covering, and the rational covering {|T − 1| ≤ |p|}, {|T − 1| ≥ |p|} is a covering.

For X = Spa(K, K⁺) with K⁺ of rank 2 (points η generic, s closed), the open immersion {η} → X is an object of X_ét whose image contains every rank-one point of X, and the one-member family ({η} → X) is not a covering.
For locally noetherian X the site coincides with Huber's X_et (Huber §2.1).

nodes.title: The small finite étale site
nodes.statement: Let X be a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space. The small finite étale site X_fét consists of the full subcategory `AdicSpace.smallFiniteEtale X` of adic spaces finite étale over X (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-morphism; all X-morphisms, which are finite étale by AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-cancellation) with the topology generated by the jointly surjective families (Kedlaya–Liu Definition 8.2.19). (i) X_fét has finite limits (fibre products by AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-base-change; equalisers are open and closed subspaces by AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-diagonal), finite coproducts (disjoint unions) and an initial object ∅, and the jointly surjective families form a pretopology; (ii) for X = Spa(A, A⁺) affinoid, global sections give an equivalence X_fét ≃ FÉt(A)^op (Mathlib `CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale A`), with quasi-inverse B ↦ Spa(`Huber.Pair.finiteEtale A⁺ B`) (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-local-to-global (c); Kedlaya–Liu Lemma 8.2.17(a)); under it a finite family (B_i) is a covering iff ∏_i B_i is faithfully flat over A; (iii) the inclusion ι: X_fét → X_ét is fully faithful, preserves finite limits and coverings, and so defines a morphism of sites X_ét → X_fét; (iv) for g: X' → X, base change defines a morphism of sites X'_fét → X_fét compatible with (iii); (v) for connected X and a geometric point ξ, the fibre functor makes X_fét a Galois category (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-galois-category).
hypotheses: X locally strongly sheafy analytic.
proofSteps: Category and finite limits: AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-cancellation (morphisms), AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-base-change (fibre products of finite étale maps are finite étale), AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-diagonal (equalisers open and closed, hence finite étale), AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-composition (i) (composites).
Coproducts: a disjoint union of two finite étale X-spaces is finite étale (over an affinoid, B × B' ∈ FÉt(A)).
Pretopology: as for AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site.
Affinoid case: AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-local-to-global (c); joint surjectivity of (Spa B_i) iff the degree of ∏ B_i is everywhere positive iff ∏ B_i is faithfully flat (same node (d)).
Inclusion into X_ét: finite étale maps are étale; ι is fully faithful and preserves fibre products and coverings, hence is continuous (mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.IsContinuous).
acceptance: For a complete nonarchimedean field K and any open valuation subring K⁺, Spa(K, K⁺)_fét ≃ FÉt(K)^op ≃ finite continuous Gal(K^sep/K)-sets, independently of K⁺.
For the annulus X over ℂ_p, the Kummer coverings S^n = T are connected objects of X_fét with automorphism group μ_n.

nodes.title: Étale maps to Spa(C, C⁺) split near the closed point
nodes.statement: Let C be an algebraically closed field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value, C⁺ ⊆ C an open and bounded valuation subring (C°° ⊆ C⁺ ⊆ O_C; C⁺ of any rank ≥ 1) and S = Spa(C, C⁺). (i) |S| is the chain, under specialisation, of the valuation rings between C⁺ and O_C; it has a unique closed point s (corresponding to C⁺), every point specialises to s, and the only open subset containing s is S; S is quasi-compact and connected, and (C, C⁺) is strongly sheafy. (ii) Every finite étale S' → S is isomorphic over S to a finite disjoint union of copies of S: finite étale C-algebras are products C^n (Mathlib `Algebra.FormallyEtale.equivPiOfIsSepClosed`), with plus ring (C⁺)^n. (iii) For every étale morphism g: V → S (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphism) and every v ∈ V with g(v) = s there is a section σ: S → V of g with σ(s) = v, and σ is an open immersion. Hence every jointly surjective family of étale maps to S contains a member with a section. (iv) (Non-example) If C⁺ ≠ O_C, the space V obtained by gluing two copies of S along the open subset S ∖ {s} is étale over S and has two sections, but is not a disjoint union of open subspaces of copies of S: étale S-spaces split near the closed point, not globally. (v) If K is a complete nonarchimedean field that is not algebraically closed and K⁺ ⊆ K is an open valuation subring, a nontrivial finite separable extension L/K with L⁺ the integral closure of K⁺ gives a nonsplit finite étale covering Spa(L, L⁺) → Spa(K, K⁺).
hypotheses: C algebraically closed, complete, nontrivially valued; C⁺ open, bounded, a valuation ring (any rank).
proofSteps: (i) Points of Spa(C, C⁺) are the continuous valuations bounded by 1 on C⁺, i.e. valuation rings V ⊇ C⁺ of C; the overrings of C⁺ are its localisations and form a chain, and continuity excludes the trivial valuation, leaving the V with C⁺ ⊆ V ⊆ O_C; the specialisation order is reverse inclusion; open sets are stable under generisation, so an open set containing the closed point s is everything. (C, C⁺) is strongly sheafy: C⟨T_1, …, T_n⟩ is strongly noetherian (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strongly-sheafy-huber-pair, examples).

(ii) mathlib:Algebra.FormallyEtale.equivPiOfIsSepClosed (C is algebraically closed, hence separably closed, mathlib:IsAlgClosed); the integral closure of C⁺ in C^n is (C⁺)^n; AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-local-to-global identifies finite étale S-spaces with FÉt(C)^op.

(iii) Near v, g is U ⊆ W → S' ⊆ S with W → S' finite étale and U, S' open; s ∈ S' forces S' = S by (i); W ≅ ⊔ copies of S by (ii); the image of v in W lies in one copy S_k and is its closed point; U ∩ S_k is open in S_k and contains its closed point, so S_k ⊆ U by (i); σ: S ≅ S_k ⊆ U ⊆ V is the required section, an open immersion.

(iv) S ∖ {s} = ∪_{a ∈ O_C ∖ C⁺} {|a| ≤ 1} is open and nonempty when C⁺ ≠ O_C; the glued space maps to S by the identity on both copies, a local isomorphism, hence étale; it has two closed points over s, so it is connected but not an open subspace of a copy of S.
(v) Spa(L, L⁺) → Spa(K, K⁺) is finite étale (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra) and has no section, since a section would give a K-algebra map L → K.
acceptance: For C⁺ = O_C, S is a single point and every étale S-space is a disjoint union of copies of S.
For C⁺ of rank 2 (points η, s), the glued space of (iv) has points η, s₁, s₂ and two sections through s₁, s₂.

nodes.title: Geometric points of analytic adic spaces and their fibre functors on the étale site
nodes.statement: Let X be a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space with its étale site X_ét (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site: objects the adic spaces étale over X in A1's local-description sense, coverings the jointly surjective families; on locally noetherian X this is Huber's X_et with its topology, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphisms-local-description-and-comparison). A geometric point of X (`AdicSpace.GeometricPoint X`) is a morphism of adic spaces ξ: Spa(C, C⁺) → X with C an algebraically closed field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value and C⁺ ⊆ C an open and bounded valuation subring of arbitrary rank (rank one, C⁺ = O_C, is a special case, not the definition); its support is x = ξ(s), s the closed point. (a) For every x ∈ X there is a geometric point with support x: with k(x)^ the completed residue field and k(x)^+ its valuation ring, take C the completion of an algebraic closure of k(x)^ and C⁺ a valuation ring of C with C⁺ ∩ k(x)^ = k(x)^+ (extension of valuation rings; C⁺ is then open and bounded). (b) The fibre functor ε_ξ: X_ét → Set, U ↦ Hom_X(Spa(C, C⁺), U) (the lifts of ξ to U), is a point of the site X_ét in Mathlib's sense (`GrothendieckTopology.Point`): its category of elements (the étale neighbourhoods of ξ) is cofiltered and essentially small, and coverings go to jointly surjective families. (c) The stalk of a sheaf F is F_ξ := colim over étale neighbourhoods (U, ū) of F(U) = `Point.sheafFiber`; it is exact and commutes with colimits. (d) Functoriality: for g: X' → X (locally strongly sheafy) and a geometric point ξ' of X', g ∘ ξ' is a geometric point of X and ε_{g∘ξ'} ≅ ε_{ξ'} ∘ g^* for the base change g^* of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site, so (g^{-1}F)_{ξ'} ≅ F_{g∘ξ'} naturally in F. (e) The image of ξ consists of generisations of x (Scholze 2013, footnote to Proposition 3.13). The conservativity of the family (ε_ξ) is AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-enough-points and strict localisations are AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strict-localisation. Higher rank is essential: rank-one geometric points do not detect sheaves supported on points of higher rank (test below; de Jong–van der Put §3.3 for the rigid analytic points).
hypotheses: X locally strongly sheafy analytic; C algebraically closed complete nonarchimedean; C⁺ open bounded valuation subring of any rank.
proofSteps: Structure: `AdicSpace.GeometricPoint X` packages (C, C⁺, [IsAlgClosed C], ξ); the support uses the closed point of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/geometric-point-etale-split (i).

(a) The canonical morphism Spa(k(x)^, k(x)^+) → X of a point (anchor Layer 3 residue fields with their valuations, Layer 5 morphisms from affinoid fields) composed with Spa(C, C⁺) → Spa(k(x)^, k(x)^+); extension of valuation rings along k(x)^ ⊆ C (mathlib:ValuationSubring); C⁺ is open and bounded because it contains C°° and lies in O_C.

(b) Cofiltered: ε_ξ preserves finite limits (Hom out of Spa(C, C⁺) preserves fibre products and equalisers of X_ét, which exist by AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-base-change and AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-diagonal), so its category of elements is cofiltered (as for Mathlib's AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.pointSmallEtale); essentially small because every neighbourhood is dominated by one whose underlying space is an open of a finite étale cover of an affinoid of X. Jointly surjective: given a lift ū: Spa(C, C⁺) → U and a covering (U_i → U), pull back to Spa(C, C⁺) (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-base-change, surjectivity on points gives a member whose pullback meets the closed point) and apply AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/geometric-point-etale-split (iii) to get a section, i.e. a lift to U_i.
(c) mathlib:CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Point.sheafFiber and its exactness properties.

(d) Hom_X(Spa(C, C⁺), U) = Hom_{X'}(Spa(C, C⁺), U ×_X X') by the universal property of the fibre product (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-base-change); the stalk formula follows since g^{-1} is computed by the left Kan extension along a continuous finite-limit-preserving functor (mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafPullback).
(e) Points of Spa(C, C⁺) are generisations of s (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/geometric-point-etale-split (i)) and morphisms preserve specialisation.
acceptance: For X = Spa(K, K⁺) with K⁺ of rank 2 (points η generic, s closed), a geometric point with support s needs C⁺ of rank ≥ 2; every geometric point Spa(C, O_C) → X has support η.
For X = Spa(C, C⁺) and ξ = id, ε_ξ is the global-sections functor, a point by AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/geometric-point-etale-split.
For locally noetherian X, ε_ξ is Huber's fibre functor at ξ (Huber, Chapter 2).

nodes.title: The étale site has enough points: geometric points form a conservative family
nodes.statement: Let X be a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space and, for each x ∈ X, let ξ_x be a geometric point with support x (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site-and-geometric-points). Then the family of points (ε_{ξ_x})_{x ∈ X} of X_ét is conservative (Mathlib `ObjectProperty.IsConservativeFamilyOfPoints`); hence X_ét has enough points (`GrothendieckTopology.HasEnoughPoints`), a morphism of sheaves (of sets, abelian groups, modules) on X_ét is an isomorphism, monomorphism or epimorphism iff it is so on every stalk F_{ξ_x}, and a section of a sheaf over U ∈ X_ét is zero iff its germs at all geometric points of U vanish. The family of rank-one geometric points is not conservative when X has points of higher rank. The classification of all points of the topos (every point is isomorphic to some ε_ξ, Huber Chapter 2) is not part of this node.
hypotheses: X locally strongly sheafy analytic; one geometric point per point of X (any choice).
proofSteps: Mathlib criterion `IsConservativeFamilyOfPoints.mk'` (SGA 4 IV 6.5(a)): it suffices that a sieve S on U ∈ X_ét is covering whenever every lift of every ξ_x to U lifts through some member of S.

Given such S and u ∈ U over x ∈ X: the point (u, s) of |U| ×_{|X|} |Spa(C, C⁺)| lifts to a point t of U ×_X Spa(C, C⁺) (surjectivity, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-base-change); t lies over the closed point s, so the étale map U ×_X Spa(C, C⁺) → Spa(C, C⁺) has a section through t (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/geometric-point-etale-split (iii)), i.e. a lift ū of ξ_x with ū(s) = u.
By hypothesis ū lifts through some V → U in S, so u lies in the image of V; hence the members of S are jointly surjective onto U and S is a covering sieve (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site).
The index family is a set (points of X), giving HasEnoughPoints; the stalkwise criteria follow from Mathlib's `IsConservativeFamilyOfPoints.jointlyReflectIsomorphisms` and its mono/epi variants.

nodes.title: The finite étale site of a connected space is a Galois category; the étale fundamental group
nodes.statement: Let X be a nonempty connected (|X| connected) locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space and ξ: Spa(C, C⁺) → X a geometric point (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site-and-geometric-points). The fibre functor F_ξ: X_fét → FintypeCat, Y ↦ Hom_X(Spa(C, C⁺), Y) — the finite set of components of Y ×_X Spa(C, C⁺), a finite disjoint union of copies of Spa(C, C⁺) (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/geometric-point-etale-split (ii)) — is a fibre functor, and X_fét (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-site) is a Galois category (Mathlib `GaloisCategory`, `PreGaloisCategory.FiberFunctor`). Hence π₁(X, ξ) := Aut(F_ξ) is a profinite group, and F_ξ induces an equivalence of X_fét with finite sets with continuous π₁(X, ξ)-action (Mathlib `PreGaloisCategory.functorToContAction`); for two geometric points the fibre functors are isomorphic, so the groups are isomorphic up to inner automorphism. For X = Spa(K, K⁺), K a complete nonarchimedean field, π₁(X, ξ) ≅ Gal(K^sep/K) for every open valuation subring K⁺.
hypotheses: X nonempty, connected, locally strongly sheafy analytic; ξ any geometric point.
proofSteps: Finite limits and finite coproducts in X_fét: AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-site (i).

Quotients by finite groups: for a finite group G acting on Y ∈ X_fét, Y/G is glued from Spa(B^G) over affinoids Spa(A) ⊆ X with Y|_{Spa A} = Spa(B); B^G is finite étale over A (invariants commute with flat base change to a finite étale cover splitting B, where the statement is about finite G-sets), and formation of B^G commutes with rational localisation (flatness of finite projective modules), so the pieces glue.

Monomorphisms are open and closed immersions (a monomorphism Y → Z in X_fét is finite étale with diagonal an isomorphism, hence of degree ≤ 1: AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-diagonal), so every monomorphism is the inclusion of a direct summand.

F_ξ preserves finite limits and finite coproducts (Hom out of Spa(C, C⁺)), takes values in finite sets and is conservative: a morphism of finite étale X-spaces inducing a bijection on fibres at ξ has degree 1 over the connected X (degrees are locally constant, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-local-to-global (d)), hence is an isomorphism; it preserves quotients by finite groups by the affinoid description.

Galois-category consequences: mathlib:CategoryTheory.GaloisCategory, mathlib:CategoryTheory.PreGaloisCategory.FiberFunctor, mathlib:CategoryTheory.PreGaloisCategory.functorToContAction (an equivalence).
Field case: X_fét ≃ FÉt(K)^op (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-site (ii)), and F_ξ is Hom_K(−, C) = Hom_K(−, K^sep).
acceptance: For X = Spa(K, K⁺), π₁(X, ξ) = Gal(K^sep/K), independently of K⁺.
For X = Spa(C, C⁺) with C algebraically closed, π₁(X, ξ) is trivial.
For the annulus X over ℂ_p, the Kummer coverings S^n = T are connected Galois objects with group μ_n, so π₁(X, ξ) surjects onto lim_n μ_n = ℤ̂(1).

nodes.title: The affinoid étale basis: X is stably adic and sheaves on X_ét are sheaves on the basis
nodes.statement: Let X be a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space. Call an object U → X of X_ét basic if U is affinoid and the composite U → X factors as Spa(D_m) → ⋯ → Spa(D_0) = V ⊆ X with V an open affinoid of X and each Spa(D_{k+1}) → Spa(D_k) either the inclusion of a rational subset or the Spa of a finite étale pair (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra) — composites of rational localisations and finite étale maps (Hansen–Kedlaya proof of Proposition 5.5). Let X_ét^aff ⊆ X_ét be the full subcategory of objects isomorphic to basic ones, with the induced topology. Then: (a) every object of X_ét has a covering (indeed an open covering) by objects of X_ét^aff; (b) every object of X_ét^aff is an affinoid adic space with strongly sheafy coordinate ring; X_ét^aff is closed under finite étale maps and rational subdomain embeddings, and under fibre products in X_ét: it is a stable basis of X_ét, so X is stably adic (Kedlaya–Liu Definition 8.2.19); (c) the inclusion X_ét^aff → X_ét is a dense subsite (Mathlib `Functor.IsDenseSubsite`), so restriction is an equivalence Sh(X_ét, 𝒜) ≃ Sh(X_ét^aff, 𝒜) for every coefficient category 𝒜 for which Mathlib's `IsDenseSubsite.sheafEquiv` applies (sets, abelian groups, modules, rings). For locally noetherian X the objects of X_ét^aff include the affinoids 'rational embedding followed by finite étale followed by rational embedding' of Scholze 2013 Lemma 5.2 and ECD 6.4.
hypotheses: X locally strongly sheafy analytic.
proofSteps: (a) By the standard affinoid form of étale morphisms (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphism), every U ∈ X_ét is covered by open subspaces isomorphic to Spa(C) ⊆ Spa(B) → Spa(A) ⊆ X, which are basic.

(b) Strong sheafiness: induction along the chain, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strongly-sheafy-huber-pair (b) for rational steps and AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-strongly-sheafy for finite étale steps; closure under finite étale maps (a finite étale U' → U with U basic is affinoid, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-local-to-global) and rational embeddings by definition.

Fibre products: for basic U, U' over basic W, U ×_W U' is the preimage in U ×_X U' of Δ_W(W); U ×_X U' is basic (base change of each step: rational localisations base change to rational localisations, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-rational-localisation, finite étale to finite étale, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-base-change), and Δ_W(W) ⊆ W ×_X W is a rational subset by induction along the chain (for a rational step the diagonal is an isomorphism; for a finite étale step it is the open and closed rational subset {|e| ≥ 1} of the diagonal idempotent e, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-diagonal); preimages of rational subsets are rational (tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spaComap_preimage_rationalSubset).

(c) The inclusion is fully faithful (so locally full and faithful) and cover-dense by (a) (mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.IsCoverDense); a sieve on a basic object is covering iff its image is, the topology being induced; mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.IsDenseSubsite and mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.IsDenseSubsite.sheafEquiv give the equivalence.

A sheaf on X_ét is determined by its values on basic objects and their restriction maps (sheafEquiv).

nodes.title: Reduction of étale coverings to rational coverings and finite étale surjections; the étale sheaf criterion
nodes.statement: Let X be a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space and 𝓑 = X_ét^aff the basis of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/basis-comparison. Let P be a property of finite coverings in X_ét of objects of 𝓑 by objects of 𝓑 such that: (a) a covering admitting a refinement with P has P; (b) composites of coverings with P have P; (c) for Y ∈ 𝓑, every rational covering of Y has P; (d) for Y ∈ 𝓑, every surjective finite étale Y' → Y, viewed as a one-member covering, has P. Then every finite covering in X_ét of an object of 𝓑 by objects of 𝓑 has P (Kedlaya–Liu Proposition 8.2.20, after de Jong–van der Put Proposition 3.2.2). Sheaf criterion: a presheaf F of sets (or abelian groups) on X_ét is a sheaf iff (1) for every U ∈ X_ét the restriction of F to the open subspaces of U is a sheaf, and (2) for every surjective finite étale morphism Y' → Y of objects of 𝓑, F(Y) → F(Y') ⇉ F(Y' ×_Y Y') is an equaliser.
hypotheses: X locally strongly sheafy analytic; coverings of basis objects by basis objects are finite (quasi-compactness).
proofSteps: (e) Degree induction: let Z → U be a surjective morphism of basis objects factoring as Z ⊆ V → U with V → U finite étale of maximal degree d and Z ⊆ V open. If d = 1 it is an isomorphism. Otherwise the complement W of the diagonal in V ×_U V is open and closed (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-diagonal) and pr₂: W → V is finite étale of degree d − 1; put Z' = (Z ×_U V) ×_{V ×_U V} W and U' = pr₂(Z'), quasi-compact (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-open-map (ii)); cover U' by finitely many rational U'_i; then {Z'_i → U'_i} has P by induction, {Z → V} ∪ {U'_i → V} by (c), {V → U} by (d), {Z → U} ∪ {Z'_i → U} by (b), and {Z → U} by (a) (Kedlaya–Liu proof of Proposition 8.2.20).

General coverings {Y_i → Y}: refine each Y_i → Y into basic pieces Y_ij ⊆ Z_ij → Y with Z_ij → Y finite étale after a rational step (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/basis-comparison (a)); the images are quasi-compact opens, finite unions of rational U_ijk (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-open-map (ii)); apply (e) to Y_ij ×_Y U_ijk → U_ijk, (c) to {U_ijk → Y}, then (b) and (a).

Sheaf criterion: take P := 'F satisfies the sheaf condition (mathlib:CategoryTheory.Presieve.IsSheafFor) for the covering and for all its base changes along morphisms of 𝓑'; (a), (b) are formal, (c) is (1), (d) is (2) together with stability of surjective finite étale maps under base change (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-base-change). So F|_𝓑 is a sheaf; F agrees with the sheaf on X_ét extending F|_𝓑 (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/basis-comparison (c)) because every U ∈ X_ét has an open covering by basis objects and (1) holds.

The presheaf U ↦ H⁰(U, ℤ/n) of locally constant functions satisfies (1) and (2), recovering the constant sheaf ℤ/n.

nodes.title: The structure sheaves O and O⁺ on the étale site
nodes.statement: Let X be a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space. The presheaves O_{X_ét}: U ↦ O_U(U) and O⁺_{X_ét}: U ↦ O⁺_U(U) on X_ét (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site), with restriction along X-morphisms, are sheaves (of complete topological rings, resp. of rings). For an open subspace U ⊆ X, O_{X_ét}(U) = O_X(U), i.e. λ_{X,*}O_{X_ét} = O_X and λ_{X,*}O⁺_{X_ét} = O⁺_X for λ_X: X_ét → X_an. For a surjective finite étale Spa(B, B⁺) → Spa(A, A⁺) in X_ét, A → B ⇉ B ⊗_A B is an equaliser of topological rings. Only the sheaf property is asserted; the vanishing of higher Čech and sheaf cohomology of O on the basis (Kedlaya–Liu Theorem 8.2.22, Hansen–Kedlaya Proposition 5.8) is cohomological and is owned by AdicSpacesPartII:R3 and ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0.
hypotheses: X locally strongly sheafy analytic.
proofSteps: Sheaf criterion AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-covering-reduction: (1) for U ∈ X_ét, O restricted to the open subspaces of U is the structure sheaf of the adic space U (anchor Layer 3–5); (2) for a surjective finite étale Spa(B) → Spa(A) of basis objects, B is faithfully flat over A (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-local-to-global (d)), Spa(B) ×_{Spa A} Spa(B) = Spa(B ⊗_A B) with no completion (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-base-change), and A is the equaliser of B ⇉ B ⊗_A B (mathlib:CommRingCat.isLimitForkPushoutSelfOfFaithfullyFlat, mathlib:Module.FaithfullyFlat); the topology of A is the subspace topology from B: A → B is universally injective (faithfully flat) with finitely presented cokernel, hence split as a map of A-modules, so A is a closed direct summand of B.

O⁺: f ∈ O(U) lies in O⁺(U) iff |f(y)| ≤ 1 for all y ∈ U; for a covering (U_i → U) every y is the image of some y_i and the valuation at y_i restricts to that at y, so the condition can be checked on the cover.
λ_* O_{X_ét} = O_X: the values on open subspaces are unchanged by definition.
acceptance: For the Kummer covering Y → X of the annulus, O(X) = K⟨T, T⁻¹⟩ is the equaliser of the two maps K⟨S, S⁻¹⟩ ⇉ K⟨S, S⁻¹⟩ × K⟨S, S⁻¹⟩ (Y ×_X Y ≅ Y ⊔ Y, the second map twisted by S ↦ −S).
For X = Spa(K, K⁺) and a finite Galois extension L/K with group G, O(X) = K = L^G.

nodes.title: The étale site of an étale X-space is the slice site: U_ét ≃ X_ét/U
nodes.statement: Let X be a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space and u: U → X an object of X_ét (U is locally strongly sheafy, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-composition (iii)). The functor U_ét → X_ét/U, (V → U) ↦ (V → U → X, with its map to U), is an equivalence of categories, and it identifies the étale topology of U with the topology induced on the slice (Mathlib `GrothendieckTopology.over`): a sieve on V is covering in U_ét iff its image is covering in X_ét. Under this equivalence restriction of sheaves u^{-1}: Sh(X_ét) → Sh(U_ét) is Mathlib's `GrothendieckTopology.overPullback`, (u^{-1}F)(V) = F(V → X), and it agrees with the inverse image along the morphism of sites u_ét of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site; u_*G(W) = G(W ×_X U). The same holds for U ∈ X_fét (U_fét ≃ X_fét/U), and for an open subspace U ⊆ X it restricts to the analytic sites (U_an ≃ X_an/U).
hypotheses: X locally strongly sheafy analytic; u étale (resp. finite étale).
proofSteps: Essential surjectivity: for W → X étale with an X-morphism W → U, W → U is étale (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-cancellation).
Full faithfulness: morphisms over U are the morphisms over X compatible with the maps to U (mathlib:CategoryTheory.Over.iteratedSliceEquiv).
Topologies: coverings are jointly surjective families in both sites, a condition that does not depend on the base (mathlib:CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.over).

Sheaf functors: mathlib:CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.overPullback and the pushforward along the slice inclusion; agreement with u_ét: for V ∈ U_ét, the graph of V → U is a section of the étale projection V ×_X U → V, hence an open subspace of V ×_X U (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-diagonal (b)), which identifies the two restriction functors (base change, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-base-change).
Finite étale and analytic variants: the same argument with AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-site and open subspaces.

For the Kummer covering u: U → X of the annulus and F on X_ét, (u^{-1}F)(U) = F(U).

nodes.title: The strict localisation at a geometric point
nodes.statement: Let X be a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space and ξ: Spa(C, C⁺) → X a geometric point with support x (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site-and-geometric-points). (i) The category N(ξ) of étale neighbourhoods of ξ — pairs (U, ū) with U ∈ X_ét and ū a lift of ξ to U, i.e. the category of elements of the fibre functor ε_ξ — is cofiltered and essentially small. The strict localisation X(ξ) is the cofiltered diagram N(ξ)^op → X_ét, (U, ū) ↦ U, regarded as a pro-object of X_ét ('X(ξ) = lim U'), together with its compatible lift ξ̃ of ξ. (ii) Values: for a presheaf F on X_ét, F(X(ξ)) := colim_{N(ξ)} F(U); for a sheaf this is the stalk F_ξ. Opens of U containing ū(s) give cofinal neighbourhoods (they contain the image of ū, which consists of generisations of ū(s)). (iii) The local rings: O_{X_ét, ξ} := O(X(ξ)) = colim O_U(U) = colim O_{U, ū(s)} and O⁺_{X_ét, ξ} (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-structure-sheaf), with the ring map O_{X_ét, ξ} → C induced by the lifts and the valuation v_ξ pulled back from C⁺. (iv) Underlying space: |X(ξ)| := lim_{N(ξ)} |U|, with the map from |Spa(C, C⁺)| induced by the lifts. (v) Functoriality: g: X' → X and a geometric point ξ' of X' induce N(g ∘ ξ') → N(ξ') by base change, hence X'(ξ') → X(g ∘ ξ') and O_{X_ét, gξ'} → O_{X'_ét, ξ'}. The structure of X(ξ) for analytic X (strictly henselian local ring; X(ξ) is the spectrum of an algebraically closed affinoid field) is AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strict-localisation-analytic.
hypotheses: X locally strongly sheafy analytic; ξ a geometric point (C⁺ of any rank).
proofSteps: (i) N(ξ) is the category of elements of ε_ξ, cofiltered and essentially small (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site-and-geometric-points (b); mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.Elements, mathlib:CategoryTheory.IsCofiltered).

(ii) Definition of the colimit; for sheaves it is `Point.sheafFiber` (mathlib:CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Point.sheafFiber). Cofinality of opens around ū(s): the image of ū consists of generisations of ū(s) (same node, (e)), and open sets are stable under generisation.
(iii) O_{X_ét} is a sheaf (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-structure-sheaf); stalks of the adic spaces U at ū(s) are the colimits over opens (anchor Layer 3), cofinal by (ii).
(iv) Limits of topological spaces over a cofiltered diagram.
(v) Base change of neighbourhoods (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-base-change) and the universal property of the fibre product.
acceptance: For X = Spa(C, C⁺) and ξ = id, (X, id) is an initial object of N(ξ): X(ξ) = X, F(X(ξ)) = F(X) and O_{X_ét, ξ} = C.
For X = Spa(K, K⁺) and ξ given by K ⊆ C, O_{X_ét, ξ} is the separable closure of K in C (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strict-localisation-analytic).

nodes.title: Strict localisations of analytic adic spaces: strictly henselian local rings and algebraically closed affinoid fields
nodes.statement: Let X be a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space, ξ: Spa(C, C⁺) → X a geometric point with support x, and X(ξ) its strict localisation (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strict-localisation). (a) O_{X_ét, ξ} is a strictly henselian local ring: a filtered colimit, along local homomorphisms, of the henselian local rings O_{U, ū(s)}; its residue field κ(ξ) is separably closed, and the closure C_ξ ⊆ C of the image of κ(ξ) is an algebraically closed complete field. (b) With C_ξ⁺ := C⁺ ∩ C_ξ, the map |Spa(C, C⁺)| → |X(ξ)| = lim_{N(ξ)} |U| factors through a homeomorphism |Spa(C_ξ, C_ξ⁺)| ≅ |X(ξ)|: the strict localisation of an analytic adic space is the spectrum of the algebraically closed affinoid field (C_ξ, C_ξ⁺) (Huber, Chapter 2 introduction); in particular F_ξ depends only on x and on the valuation ring C_ξ⁺, and ξ factors through Spa(C_ξ, C_ξ⁺). (c) For X = Spa(K, K⁺) with K a complete nonarchimedean field, O_{X_ét, ξ} is the separable closure K^sep of K in C, X(ξ) = Spa of its completion with C⁺ ∩ (K^sep)^, and the stalk functor on X_ét is F ↦ colim over finite separable L ⊆ K^sep of F(Spa(L, L⁺)), with its continuous Gal(K^sep/K)-action. Clause (b) rests on Huber §2.5, which is not public; its proof below is complete except for the shrinking step recorded as a gap, and no other node of this stage uses (b).
hypotheses: X locally strongly sheafy analytic; ξ a geometric point with support x (C⁺ of any rank).
proofSteps: (a) Local rings: by AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strict-localisation (ii)–(iii), O_{X_ét, ξ} = colim O_{U, ū(s)}; each O_{U, u} is a henselian local ring (Kedlaya–Liu Lemma 2.4.17(a)); the transition maps are local (morphisms of adic spaces induce local maps of stalks, anchor Layer 3–5); a filtered colimit of henselian local rings along local maps is henselian local (mathlib:HenselianLocalRing).

Residue field separably closed: a monic separable polynomial P over κ(ξ) comes from some k(u), u = ū(s); by Kedlaya–Liu Theorem 1.2.8 it gives a finite étale O_{U,u}-algebra with residue algebra k(u)[T]/(P); it spreads out to a finite étale cover U' of an open neighbourhood of u (Kedlaya–Liu Remark 1.2.9; AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra); ū lifts to U' (the pullback of U' to Spa(C, C⁺) splits, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/geometric-point-etale-split), so P has a root in κ(ξ).
C_ξ: the closure of a separably closed subfield of the complete algebraically closed C is algebraically closed (de Jong–van der Put §3.3, citing BGR 3.4.1/6).

(b) Points of X(ξ) over the closed point: every neighbourhood contains the image of ū, which is the image of |Spa(C, C⁺)|; a point of lim |U| is a compatible system of points u_U generising ū(s); the valuations on the O_{U, u_U} assemble to a valuation on O_{X_ét, ξ} bounded by 1 on O⁺_{X_ét, ξ}, i.e. a valuation ring of C_ξ between C_ξ⁺ and O_{C_ξ}; conversely such a valuation ring gives a compatible system. Continuity and the homeomorphism use that the finite étale neighbourhoods realising the finite separable subextensions of κ(ξ)/k(x), shrunk around the chosen point, are cofinal in N(ξ); this shrinking step (the adic, higher-rank form of the 'Key Lemma' of de Jong–van der Put §2 used in their §3.3 cofinality argument) is recorded as a gap.

(c) For X = Spa(K, K⁺), étale X-spaces are locally Spa(L, L⁺)'s rational subsets, the rational subsets of Spa(L, L⁺) containing a point have coordinate ring L (a function bounded by 1 at a point is power-bounded), so O_{X_ét, ξ} = colim L = K^sep; the Galois action comes from the automorphisms of the neighbourhoods Spa(L, L⁺) for L Galois.
acceptance: For X = Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p) and ξ from ℚ_p ⊆ ℂ_p, O_{X_ét, ξ} = ℚ̄_p and X(ξ) = Spa(ℂ_p, O_{ℂ_p}).
For X = Spa(K, K⁺) with K⁺ of rank 2 and ξ supported at the closed point, X(ξ) = Spa(C_ξ, C_ξ⁺) with C_ξ⁺ of rank 2 (two points).

nodes.title: The Kedlaya–Liu étale and finite étale sites of an arbitrary analytic adic space
nodes.statement: Let X be an analytic adic space, not necessarily locally strongly sheafy, regarded as an analytic Yoneda-adic space (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/generalized-adic-presentation: sheaves on complete Huber pairs for the rational topology glued from the sheafified spectra Spa^Y(A, A⁺); on complete Tate pairs these are Kedlaya–Liu's preadic spaces and Scholze–Weinstein's adic spaces; the anchor's adic spaces form a full subcategory, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/adic-spaces-in-yoneda-adic-spaces). For morphisms of analytic Yoneda-adic spaces define finite étale and étale by the local descriptions of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-morphism and AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphism with Spa^Y in place of Spa (Kedlaya–Liu Definition 8.2.16 verbatim), and let X_ét^Y, X_fét^Y be Kedlaya–Liu's small étale and finite étale sites (Definition 8.2.19): objects all étale (resp. finite étale) morphisms Y → X of analytic Yoneda-adic spaces, coverings the set-theoretic (jointly surjective) families. Then: (i) fibre products exist (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/yoneda-adic-fibre-products), the two classes are stable under base change and composition, and the covering families form pretopologies (Kedlaya–Liu Remark 8.2.5, Lemma 8.2.17(c)); (ii) for every complete Tate pair (A, A⁺), sheafy or not, global sections give Spa^Y(A, A⁺)_fét^Y ≃ FÉt(A)^op (Kedlaya–Liu Lemma 8.2.17(a)); (iii) if X is locally strongly sheafy, every object of X_ét^Y is (the image of) an adic space and X_ét^Y ≃ X_ét, X_fét^Y ≃ X_fét (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-site); (iv) geometric points define points of X_ét^Y and form a conservative family, by the proofs of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site-and-geometric-points and AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-enough-points (only Spa(C, C⁺), which is sheafy, is used); (v) this is the site Y_ét, Y_fét of ECD Lemma 15.6 for an analytic adic space Y over ℤ_p, the right-hand side of the comparison Y^◇_ét ≅ Y_ét owned by DiamondsAndVStacks:D6, in the generality ECD Definition 15.5 allows ('adic spaces as defined in [SW13, Section 2.1]').
hypotheses: X analytic; Yoneda-adic spaces, Spa^Y, open immersions, fibre products and |−| as in AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/generalized-adic-presentation and its lemmas.
proofSteps: Definitions: the local conditions make sense for Spa^Y because Spa^Y of a rational localisation is the open subobject over the rational subset (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/yoneda-adic-open-immersions), and Spa^Y of the finite étale pair of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra is defined for every complete Tate A.

(i) Fibre products: AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/yoneda-adic-fibre-products, with the uncompleted tensor product for a finite étale factor (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra (v)); stability and composition: the proofs of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-base-change and AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-composition, which use sheafiness only to stay among adic spaces; the approximation inputs (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/affinoid-system-approximation, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-approximation) are ring-level.

(ii) AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-rational-descent holds for every complete Tate A, and morphisms Spa^Y(B') → Spa^Y(B) over Spa^Y(A) are A-algebra maps B → B' (Yoneda; AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/maps-from-adic-spaces-to-yoneda-affinoids for adic sources).

(iii) Objects over a locally strongly sheafy X are locally Spa^Y of rational localisations of finite étale algebras over strongly sheafy rings, which are sheafy (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-strongly-sheafy), so they lie in the essential image of the adic spaces (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/adic-spaces-in-yoneda-adic-spaces); morphisms agree by full faithfulness.
(iv) The splitting lemma AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/geometric-point-etale-split concerns Spa(C, C⁺) only; the rest of the argument is site-theoretic.
acceptance: For a sheafy complete Tate ring A that is not known to be strongly sheafy and B ∈ FÉt(A), Spa^Y(B, B⁺) → Spa^Y(A, A⁺) is an object of X_fét^Y although Spa(B, B⁺) is not known to be an adic space (Kedlaya–Liu Remark 8.2.18).
For X locally noetherian, X_ét^Y is Huber's X_et.

nodes.title: Étale, finite étale and pro-étale morphisms of pro-objects of X_ét, and the underlying space |U| = lim |U_i|
nodes.statement: Let X is a locally noetherian analytic adic space (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space, every point analytic, so X is locally Spa(A, A⁺) with A a complete strongly noetherian Tate ring), X_ét is its small étale site (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site) and X_fét its finite étale site (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-site). Write pro-X_ét := Pro(X_ét) (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/pro-category-of-finite-t0-spaces, the dual of Mathlib's Ind): its objects are formal cofiltered systems U = (U_i)_{i∈I}, written U = lim U_i, of objects of X_ét indexed by small cofiltered categories I, and Hom(lim_i U_i, lim_j V_j) = lim_j colim_i Hom_X(U_i, V_j) (Scholze 2013, Proposition 3.2). X_ét ⊂ pro-X_ét as constant systems (fully faithful, written c), X is a final object, and cofiltered limits exist in pro-X_ét (a double system is combined into a single one). The underlying space of U is |U| := lim_i |U_i| (limit of topological spaces); it is independent of the presentation and U ↦ |U| is a functor pro-X_ét → Top. A morphism f: U → V of pro-X_ét is: (a) étale (resp. finite étale) if there are a morphism V → V_0 with V_0 ∈ X_ét and an étale (resp. finite étale in the sense of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-morphism) morphism U_0 → V_0 of X_ét with U ≅ U_0 ×_{V_0} V over V; here, for a presentation V = lim_j V_j through which V → V_0 factors, U_0 ×_{V_0} V := lim_j U_0 ×_{V_0} V_j (fibre products in X_ét); (b) surjective if |f| is surjective; (c) pro-étale if there are a small cofiltered category K and an isomorphism U ≅ lim_{k∈K} U_k over V with every U_k → V étale and every transition U_k → U_{k'} finite étale and surjective for k ≥ k' ≥ k_0 (some k_0 ∈ K); such data is a pro-étale presentation. An object U is pro-étale over X if U → X is pro-étale.
hypotheses: X as above (Scholze's standing hypothesis restricted to analytic adic spaces, the case the consumers use).
Size: a Grothendieck universe is fixed; X_ét is locally small, pro-objects are indexed by small cofiltered categories, so pro-X_ét is locally small, and sheaves take values in small sets.
Étale and finite étale morphisms of X_ét are those of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1; every morphism of X_ét is étale by cancellation (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-smooth-cancellation).
proofSteps: pro-X_ét and its Hom formula are the pro-category of D0 applied to X_ét; cofiltered limits exist there (combine double systems).
|U| is well defined: an isomorphism of pro-objects induces compatible maps of the limits, and Top has all limits.

U_0 ×_{V_0} V exists and does not depend on the chosen factorisation up to unique isomorphism: fibre products of étale maps exist in X_ét (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-products-existence), and two factorisations agree after passing to a larger index (Hom(lim V_j, V_0) = colim_j Hom(V_j, V_0)).

nodes.title: Finite-étale towers: transfinite compositions of pullbacks of finite étale surjections (the erratum's corrected covering condition)
nodes.statement: Let X be as in AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-morphism and W ∈ pro-X_ét. A finite-étale tower over W of length λ (an ordinal) is a functor μ ↦ U_μ from the opposite of the well-ordered set {μ : μ < λ} to pro-X_ét over W such that U_0 = W and, for every μ < λ, the canonical morphism U_μ → U_{<μ} := lim_{μ'<μ} U_{μ'} (the limit over the empty set being W) is finite étale and surjective in the sense of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-morphism, i.e. the pullback along some morphism U_{<μ} → V_0 of a finite étale surjective morphism V_0' → V_0 of X_ét. Its composite is lim_{μ<λ} U_μ → W. A morphism t: U → W of pro-X_ét is a finite-étale tower if it is isomorphic over W to the composite of such a tower. Inside pro-X_fét one requires V_0' → V_0 to be a morphism of X_fét; this is the pro-finite-étale tower of Scholze's erratum, item (1). Conventions: a step is allowed at every ordinal, including limit ordinals (Kerz's transfinite compositions); λ ≤ 1 gives isomorphisms and λ = 2 single finite étale surjections. Equivalently (re-indexing by inserting U_{<μ} before U_μ), t is a finite-étale tower iff its opposite lies in the class MorphismProperty.transfiniteCompositions of the opposite of the pullbacks of finite étale surjective morphisms of X_ét, computed in (pro-X_ét)ᵒᵖ with well-order-continuous shapes.

nodes.title: Towers are pro-étale: presentation by finite dependency-closed sets of stages, and the countable case
nodes.statement: Let t: U → W be a finite-étale tower of length λ (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-tower) in pro-X_ét. (a) There are a small directed set K and an isomorphism U ≅ lim_{F∈K} V_F over W in which every V_F → W is finite étale and surjective and every transition V_{F'} → V_F (F ≤ F') is finite étale and surjective; in particular t is pro-étale, and U ∈ X_proét whenever W ∈ X_proét. (b) |t| is surjective with nonempty compact fibres. (c) Conversely, if U = lim_{i∈I} U_i → V is a pro-étale presentation with I countable, then there is i_0 ∈ I with U → U_{i_0} a tower of length ω and U_{i_0} → V étale.
hypotheses: X locally noetherian analytic; W ∈ pro-X_ét arbitrary in (a), (b).
proofSteps: (a) For each μ < λ the morphism U_{<μ} → V_0^{(μ)} classifying the μ-th step has a constant target, so it factors through a finite stage of U_{<μ} (Hom(lim, c V) = colim Hom, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-morphism); record a finite set D(μ) ⊂ μ of earlier stages it depends on. The closure of a finite set of ordinals under D is finite (a finitely branching tree all of whose branches descend in a well-order is finite, by König's lemma). K := finite D-closed subsets of λ, ordered by inclusion, is directed; V_F is the iterated pullback, in increasing order of μ ∈ F, of the finite étale surjections of the steps in F.

Transition maps V_{F'} → V_F are composites of pullbacks of finite étale surjections, hence finite étale surjective (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-etale-composition, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-base-change); lim_F V_F ≅ lim_μ U_μ by comparing the two cofiltered systems. Pro-étaleness of U over X when W ∈ X_proét: AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-composition.
(b) Fibres of |V_F| → |W| are nonempty and finite, so the fibres of the limit are inverse limits of nonempty compact spaces, hence nonempty (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-base-change, proof).

(c) Choose a cofinal sequence i_0 < i_1 < … beyond the threshold of the presentation; U = lim_n U_{i_n} and each U_{i_{n+1}} → U_{i_n} is finite étale surjective; this is the erratum's observation that the case λ = ω needs no change.

nodes.title: Transfinite towers of pullbacks of finite surjections of profinite sets split (the erratum's replacement of Proposition 3.7(i))
nodes.statement: Let f: S → S' be a continuous map of profinite sets written as S = lim_{μ<λ} S_μ with S_0 = S', such that for every μ < λ the map S_μ → S_{<μ} := lim_{μ'<μ} S_{μ'} is the pullback of a surjective map of finite sets along a continuous map S_{<μ} → B_μ. Then f admits a continuous section. Consequently, for X = Spa(C, O_C) with C algebraically closed and O_C of rank one, every finite-étale tower (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-tower) between qc objects of X_proét has a continuous section on underlying spaces; and the printed Proposition 3.7(i) (every continuous open surjection of profinite sets splits) is false and is not used.
hypotheses: λ an arbitrary ordinal; no countability assumption.
proofSteps: Construct compatible continuous sections σ_μ: S' → S_μ by transfinite induction: σ_0 = id; at a step μ, S_μ = S_{<μ} ×_{B_μ} A_μ with A_μ → B_μ surjective finite, choose a set-theoretic section s_μ of A_μ → B_μ and put σ_μ = (σ_{<μ}, s_μ ∘ (S_{<μ} → B_μ) ∘ σ_{<μ}), where σ_{<μ} is the map to the limit induced by (σ_{μ'})_{μ'<μ}.
The σ_μ are compatible, so they define σ: S' → lim S_μ = S; each component is continuous, so σ is continuous and f ∘ σ = id.

For X = Spa(C, O_C): qc objects of X_proét have profinite underlying spaces and finite étale surjections between qc étale X-spaces are, locally on clopen pieces, pullbacks of surjections of finite sets, so the steps of a tower are of the stated form.

nodes.title: Profinite groups are transfinite towers of finite extensions; G → G/G' is a corrected covering of profinite G-sets
nodes.statement: Let G be a profinite group. (a) There are an ordinal λ and closed normal subgroups N_μ (μ < λ) of G, decreasing, with N_0 = G, ⋂_μ N_μ = 1, and N_{<μ}/N_μ finite for every μ < λ, where N_{<μ} := ⋂_{μ'<μ} N_{μ'} (N_{<0} := G); equivalently G = lim_{μ<λ} G_μ with G_0 = 1 and G_μ → G_{<μ} the quotient by a finite normal subgroup. (b) For closed subgroups A ⊂ B of G with A of finite index in B, the G-map G/A → G/B is the pullback of a surjection of finite G-sets. (c) For every closed subgroup G' ⊂ G the map G → G/G' of profinite G-sets is a G-tower, i.e. a covering of the site of profinite G-sets with corrected coverings (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/profinite-g-sets-site); in particular G → pt is a covering.
hypotheses: G profinite; no countability assumption (for G topologically countably generated one may take λ = ω).
proofSteps: (a) Index the open normal subgroups M_μ by the ordinals 1 ≤ μ < λ and put H_μ := G/M_μ, H_0 := 1, so G ⊂ ∏_{μ<λ} H_μ; let G_μ be the image of G in ∏_{μ'≤μ} H_{μ'} and N_μ the kernel of G → G_μ (so N_0 = G); the kernel of G_μ → G_{<μ} embeds in H_μ, hence is finite.
(b) A is open in B, so B ∩ N ⊂ A for an open normal N ⊂ G; then G/B ×_{G/BN} G/AN ≅ G/(B ∩ AN) = G/A, and G/AN → G/BN is a surjection of finite G-sets.

(c) Put T_μ := G/(G' ∩ N_μ); then T_0 = G/G', lim_{μ<λ} T_μ = G (compactness and ⋂ N_μ = 1), T_{<μ} = G/(G' ∩ N_{<μ}), and G' ∩ N_μ has finite index in G' ∩ N_{<μ} (it injects into N_{<μ}/N_μ), so each step is a pullback of a surjection of finite G-sets by (b).
acceptance: G = Z_p: λ = ω, N_n = p^n Z_p, and Z_p → pt is a tower with steps Z/p^{n+1} → Z/p^n.
G = ∏_{i∈I} Z/2 with I uncountable: G → pt is a tower of length card-indexed ordinal with steps Z/2 → pt.

nodes.title: Base change in pro-X_ét along étale, finite étale and pro-étale maps, surjective on underlying spaces (Scholze Lemma 3.10(i))
nodes.statement: Let U, V, W ∈ pro-X_ét with U → V étale (resp. finite étale, resp. pro-étale) and W → V arbitrary. Then U ×_V W exists in pro-X_ét, the projection U ×_V W → W is étale (resp. finite étale, resp. pro-étale), and |U ×_V W| → |U| ×_{|V|} |W| is surjective with nonempty compact fibres. In particular the base change of a surjective étale, finite étale or pro-étale map is surjective, and fibre products commute with cofiltered limits in each variable.
hypotheses: X locally noetherian analytic (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space); pro-X_ét and the morphism classes of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-morphism.
proofSteps: Étale case: U = U_0 ×_{V_0} V; write W = lim W_i with W → V_0 given by compatible W_i → V_0; then U ×_V W = lim_i U_0 ×_{V_0} W_i, and each U_0 ×_{V_0} W_i → W_i is étale (resp. finite étale) by base change in X_ét (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphisms-local-description-and-comparison, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-morphism; fibre products AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-products-existence).

On spaces |U ×_V W| = lim_i |U_0 ×_{V_0} W_i| → lim_i |U_0| ×_{|V_0|} |W_i| = |U| ×_{|V|} |W|; at each finite stage the map is surjective (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-product-points) with finite fibres (étale maps are locally quasi-finite, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/unramified-locally-quasi-finite), and inverse limits of nonempty finite sets are nonempty.
Pro-étale case: with a presentation U = lim U_k, U ×_V W = lim_k U_k ×_V W is a pro-étale presentation over W; fibres are inverse limits of nonempty compact spaces, hence nonempty.

nodes.statement: If U → V → W are étale (resp. finite étale) morphisms of pro-X_ét, then U → W is étale (resp. finite étale): writing V = V_0 ×_{W_0} W and U = U_0 ×_{V_0} V with V_0 → W_0, U_0 → V_0 in X_ét, there is a stage W_i of W with U ≅ U_i ×_{W_i} W for an étale (resp. finite étale) U_i → W_i in X_ét.

nodes.title: Quasi-compact opens of |U| are represented by étale subobjects (Scholze Lemma 3.10(iii))
nodes.statement: Let U ∈ pro-X_ét and W ⊂ |U| a quasi-compact open subset. (a) There is an étale V → U, namely the pullback V = V_i ×_{U_i} U of an open subspace V_i ⊂ U_i at some stage of a presentation U = lim U_i, with |V| → |U| a homeomorphism onto W; if U = lim U_i is a pro-étale presentation, so is the induced presentation V = lim V_i ×_{U_i} U_j. (b) If U ∈ X_proét, then V ∈ X_proét, V → U is a monomorphism, and a morphism V' → U of X_proét factors (uniquely) through V iff |V'| → |U| has image in W. Hence W ↦ V identifies quasi-compact opens of |U| with the subobjects of U they represent, compatibly with finite intersections (fibre products).
hypotheses: X locally noetherian analytic (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space); pro-X_ét and the morphism classes of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-morphism.

For (a) the stage i must be large enough that W is the preimage of a quasi-compact open W_i ⊂ |U_i|; for quasi-compact U this uses that |U| is a cofiltered limit of spectral spaces along spectral maps.

V := V_i ×_{U_i} U is étale over U (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-base-change) with |V| = W; a pro-étale presentation of U restricts to one of V.

(b) If V' → U has image in W, then V' → U_i has image in W_i, so V'_j → U_i factors over V_i for j large (transitions of a pro-étale presentation of V' are surjective for large j), hence V' → U factors over V; uniqueness because open immersions are monomorphisms and pullbacks preserve monomorphisms.

nodes.statement: Let U → V → W be pro-étale morphisms of pro-X_ét with W ∈ X_proét. Then U, V ∈ X_proét and U → W is pro-étale. Moreover, every pro-étale morphism U → V factors as U → U_0 → V with U → U_0 a cofiltered inverse limit of finite étale surjections and U_0 → V étale.

nodes.title: Étale spaces over a locally noetherian analytic adic space locally have finitely many connected components
nodes.statement: Let X be a locally noetherian analytic adic space and Y ∈ X_ét. Every point of Y has an open affinoid neighbourhood Spa(B, B⁺) with B a complete strongly noetherian Tate ring; every such affinoid has finitely many connected components, each open and closed and corresponding to a primitive idempotent of B. In particular every quasi-compact Y ∈ X_ét is a finite disjoint union of connected open and closed subspaces, and Y is locally connected in Scholze's sense.
hypotheses: X locally noetherian analytic; the argument uses sheafiness of strongly noetherian Tate pairs.
proofSteps: Étale morphisms are locally of finite type with local standard étale presentations (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-local-structure), so affinoid opens of Y are Spa(B, B⁺) with B topologically of finite type over a strongly noetherian Tate ring, hence strongly noetherian (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/topologically-finite-type-noetherian-type).

(B, B⁺) is sheafy (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/noetherian-type-stably-sheafy) with O(Spa(B, B⁺)) = B (anchor Layer 3.5 / Layer 4); a decomposition of Spa(B, B⁺) into two open and closed subsets gives an idempotent of B by the sheaf property, and an idempotent e gives the clopen {v(e) = 1}.
B is noetherian, so it has finitely many primitive idempotents; hence finitely many connected components.
acceptance: For Y = X_n in the Kummer tower (connected), there is one component; for Y = X ⊔ X there are two.

sources.excerpt: As a consequence, if Y → X is étale, then locally, Y is connected. This will be used in verifying that the pro-étale site is a site.

nodes.title: An étale map over a finite-étale tower can be rewritten as a tower followed by an étale map
nodes.statement: Let t: U → W be a finite-étale tower (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-tower) and e: A → U an étale morphism of pro-X_ét. Then t ∘ e = e' ∘ t' for a finite-étale tower t': A → B and an étale morphism e': B → W. Consequently every composite of finite-étale towers and étale morphisms (in any order, finitely many) is of the form (étale) ∘ (tower).
hypotheses: X locally noetherian analytic (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space); pro-X_ét and the morphism classes of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-morphism.
proofSteps: Transfinite induction on the length λ of t. λ ≤ 1: t is an isomorphism.
λ = ν + 1: U = U_ν → U_{<ν} is finite étale, so A → U → U_{<ν} is étale (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-etale-composition) and U_{<ν} → W is a tower of length ν; apply the induction hypothesis.

λ a limit ordinal: A = U ×_{E_0} E for some U → E_0 with E_0 ∈ X_ét and E → E_0 étale; since Hom(lim_μ U_μ, c E_0) = colim_μ Hom(U_μ, c E_0), U → E_0 factors through U_{μ_0} with μ_0 < λ. Then A = U ×_{U_{μ_0}} A_{μ_0} with A_{μ_0} := U_{μ_0} ×_{E_0} E; the tail (U_μ)_{μ_0 ≤ μ < λ} is a tower over U_{μ_0} (its partial limits are the U_{<μ}), so A → A_{μ_0} is a tower by base change; A_{μ_0} → U_{μ_0} is étale and U_{μ_0} → W is a tower of length μ_0 + 1 < λ; the induction hypothesis rewrites A_{μ_0} → W as a tower A_{μ_0} → B followed by an étale B → W, and towers compose (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-tower, concatenation).

nodes.title: The corrected covering families form a pretopology on X_proét
nodes.statement: Call a family {f_i: U_i → U}_{i∈I} of morphisms of X_proét a corrected covering if |U| = ⋃_i f_i(|U_i|) and each f_i factors as U_i →^{t_i} W_i →^{e_i} U with t_i a finite-étale tower (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-tower) and e_i étale (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-morphism). Then: (a) the corrected coverings form a Grothendieck pretopology on X_proét (mathlib:CategoryTheory.Pretopology): isomorphisms are coverings, coverings are stable under base change (fibre products exist, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-finite-limits) and under composition; (b) every member of a corrected covering is pro-étale and open; (c) every jointly surjective family of étale morphisms and every finite-étale tower is a corrected covering; (d) every family of pro-étale maps that is a covering in the sense of the printed Definition 3.9 and whose members admit pro-étale presentations indexed by countable categories is a corrected covering; (e) every corrected covering is a covering of the printed Definition 3.9, so the corrected topology is coarser than the printed one, on the same underlying category.
hypotheses: X locally noetherian analytic (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space); pro-X_ét and the morphism classes of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-morphism.

The étale factor e_i and steps pulled back from X_ét are the reading of the erratum's 'similar condition' for Definition 3.9 fixed in this packet (sourceIssues AdicEtaleGeometry/E6, AdicEtaleGeometry/E7).
proofSteps: Isomorphisms: towers of length 1 and identity étale maps.

Base change: étale maps and towers are stable under base change (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-base-change, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-tower), and joint surjectivity is preserved because |U_i ×_U V| → |U_i| ×_{|U|} |V| is surjective.

Composition: for {U_ij → U_i} and {U_i → U} corrected, U_ij → W_ij → U_i → W_i → U; rewrite the middle étale-then-tower W_ij → U_i → W_i as tower-then-étale (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-over-tower-swap), concatenate towers and compose étale maps (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-etale-composition).

(b) towers are pro-étale (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-tower-is-pro-etale), étale maps are pro-étale, composites are pro-étale (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-composition), and pro-étale maps are open (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-maps-open). (d) AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-tower-is-pro-etale (c). (e) by (b).

nodes.title: The pro-étale site X_proét of a locally noetherian analytic adic space, with Scholze's corrected coverings
nodes.statement: Let X is a locally noetherian analytic adic space (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space, every point analytic, so X is locally Spa(A, A⁺) with A a complete strongly noetherian Tate ring), X_ét is its small étale site (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site) and X_fét its finite étale site (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-site). The pro-étale site X_proét is the category of objects U ∈ pro-X_ét that are pro-étale over X (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-morphism), with all morphisms of pro-X_ét between them, equipped with the Grothendieck topology J_proét generated (mathlib:CategoryTheory.Pretopology.toGrothendieck) by the corrected coverings of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/corrected-covers-pretopology: a family {f_i: U_i → U} is a covering iff |U| = ⋃_i f_i(|U_i|) and every f_i factors as U_i → W_i → U, a finite-étale tower U_i = lim_{μ<λ_i} U_{i,μ} → W_i (U_{i,0} = W_i, each U_{i,μ} → lim_{μ'<μ} U_{i,μ'} the pullback of a finite étale surjective morphism of X_ét; AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-tower) followed by an étale morphism W_i → U. A sieve on U is covering iff it contains a corrected covering family. Structure: X is final, X_proét has finite limits computed in pro-X_ét (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-finite-limits), every U has an underlying space |U| = lim |U_i|, quasi-compact opens of |U| are represented by subobjects (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-quasicompact-opens), and all members of coverings are open maps. The correction restricts only the coverings: the underlying category is that of Scholze 2013, Definition 3.9; families of pro-étale maps with countable presentations are coverings exactly as before; J_proét is coarser than the printed topology and strictly coarser as soon as an open surjection of profinite sets without continuous section occurs over a geometric point. No arbitrary open surjection of profinite sets is assumed to split, the deleted Proposition 3.8 and the deleted last sentence of Proposition 3.13 are not used, and the existence of enough points is only the abstract statement for coherent topoi (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/proetale-topos-enough-points). X_proét is not the pro-étale site of a perfectoid space of ECD Definition 8.1(ii) (owned by DiamondsAndVStacks:D2) and not Mathlib's pro-étale topology on schemes.
hypotheses: X locally noetherian analytic (Scholze's hypothesis 'locally noetherian' is needed for Lemma 3.10(vii); the analytic restriction matches the consumers).
Size: a Grothendieck universe is fixed; X_ét is locally small, pro-objects are indexed by small cofiltered categories, so pro-X_ét is locally small, and sheaves take values in small sets.

Reading of the erratum's condition for Definition 3.9 (not displayed in the erratum): an étale factor is allowed (otherwise open covers are excluded; AdicSpacesPartII/E-R4-1) and the steps are finite étale surjections pulled back from X_ét (otherwise the countable case would change); sourceIssues AdicEtaleGeometry/E7.
proofSteps: Underlying category and morphism classes: AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-morphism; stability of X_proét under the constructions used: AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-composition, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-finite-limits.
Topology: the corrected coverings form a pretopology (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/corrected-covers-pretopology); take Pretopology.toGrothendieck.
Comparison with the printed site: every corrected covering is a printed covering and countable presentations give towers of length ω (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-tower-is-pro-etale).
acceptance: For X = Spa(C, O_C) (C algebraically closed, O_C of rank one) quasi-compact objects are profinite sets and J_proét-coverings of a profinite set admit continuous sections locally on a finite partition into clopen subsets.
The Kummer tower over the torus is a covering; an open surjection of profinite sets without section is not.

The higher statements H^i(U, ν^*F) = colim_j H^i(U_j, F) (Scholze Lemma 3.16, i > 0) and Corollary 3.17 are derived-cohomology results owned by ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0 and are not part of this node.

Pass to a finite subcover (quasi-compactness) and combine it into one map V → U, which is a tower followed by an étale map; with a pro-étale presentation V = lim V_l → U, V_l → U is an étale cover for large l and the Čech complex of F̃ for V → U is the filtered colimit of those for V_l → U (F̃(V) = colim F̃(V_l)); this reduces to V → U étale.

For V = V_j ×_{U_j} U étale surjective, V_{j'} → U_{j'} is an étale cover for large j' (the non-surjective locus is a constructible set whose preimage in the limit is empty), and the Čech complex for V → U is the filtered colimit over j' of the Čech complexes for V_{j'} → U_{j'}; exactness in degrees 0 and 1 is the sheaf property of F on X_ét.

nodes.title: The sites G-fsets and G-pfsets of finite and profinite G-sets, with corrected coverings (Scholze Definition 3.4 with the erratum)
nodes.statement: Let G be a profinite group. G-fsets is the category of finite discrete sets with continuous G-action, with coverings the jointly surjective families. G-pfsets is the category of profinite sets with continuous G-action and continuous G-maps; every object is a cofiltered limit of finite G-sets (quotients by open G-invariant equivalence relations), and G-pfsets ≃ Pro(G-fsets). A G-map S_1 → S is G-étale if it is the pullback of a map of finite G-sets along some G-map S → B with B finite, and a G-tower if S_1 = lim_{μ<λ} S_μ with S_0 = S and each S_μ → S_{<μ} := lim_{μ'<μ} S_{μ'} the pullback of a surjection of finite G-sets. A family {f_i: S_i → S} is a (corrected) covering if S = ⋃ f_i(S_i) and each f_i is a G-tower followed by a G-étale map. These coverings form a pretopology; the printed Definition 3.4 (all families of open maps) is replaced by it. For a topological G-module M, F_M(S) := Hom_cont,G(S, M) is a sheaf on G-pfsets. For trivial G, the underlying category is Profinite.
hypotheses: G profinite; the erratum's 'similar condition' for Definition 3.4 is read with the G-étale factor so that a disjoint union is covered by its summands (sourceIssues AdicEtaleGeometry/E6).
Size: a Grothendieck universe is fixed; X_ét is locally small, pro-objects are indexed by small cofiltered categories, so pro-X_ét is locally small, and sheaves take values in small sets.
proofSteps: Pro-description: for S profinite with continuous G-action, the open G-invariant equivalence relations are cofinal among open equivalence relations (compactness of G × S), giving S = lim of finite G-sets.

Pretopology: base change and composition as in AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/corrected-covers-pretopology, with finite G-sets in place of X_ét and the swap argument of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-over-tower-swap (a G-map to a finite G-set factors through a finite stage).

F_M is a sheaf: members of coverings are quotient maps onto their (clopen) images since G-towers are continuous surjections of compact Hausdorff spaces and G-étale maps are clopen-locally disjoint unions of homeomorphisms; continuity and equivariance glue.
acceptance: For G = Z_p, G → pt is a covering (tower with steps Z/p^{n+1} → Z/p^n); for G trivial, {S_1 → S_1 ⊔ S_2, S_2 → S_1 ⊔ S_2} is a covering.

nodes.title: Structure of open surjections of profinite G-sets (Scholze Lemma 3.6)
nodes.statement: Let S → S' be an open surjective map in G-pfsets. Then S = lim_i T_i over S' with T_i = A_i ×_{B_i} S' for surjections A_i → B_i of finite G-sets and surjective G-maps S' → B_i, such that S → T_i is surjective; moreover S = lim A_i and S' = lim B_i. In particular S → S' is a cofiltered limit of pullbacks of surjections of finite G-sets, but (by AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/transfinite-tower-splitting) not necessarily a G-tower.
hypotheses: G profinite; no covering notion is involved.
proofSteps: Write S = lim S_i with S_i finite G-sets; the fibres of S → S_i give finitely many open U_ij ⊂ S whose images U'_ij ⊂ S' are open and cover S'.

Refine: the atoms V'_ij' of the Boolean algebra generated by the U'_ij, their preimages, and the atoms W_ik generated together with the U_ij give finite G-quotients S → A_i, S' → B_i and a surjection A_i → B_i such that S → S' factors surjectively over A_i ×_{B_i} S' → S'.
S is the inverse limit of these, and the last statements follow from the construction.
acceptance: For G = 1 and S = S' × F with F finite, T_i = S for all large i.
The Ribes–Zalesskii open surjection has such a presentation but no section.

nodes.title: Sections over profinite G-sets with free action are exact (Scholze Proposition 3.7(ii), with corrected coverings)
nodes.statement: Let S ∈ G-pfsets have free G-action. Then S ≅ T × G as G-sets for the profinite set T = S/G with trivial action, and the functor F ↦ F(S) from abelian sheaves on G-pfsets (corrected coverings, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/profinite-g-sets-site) to abelian groups is exact.
hypotheses: G profinite; corrected coverings. Proposition 3.7(i) as printed is not used; the splitting comes from the tower structure.
proofSteps: S → S/G is a tower of profinite sets: with the filtration (N_μ) of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/profinite-group-tower, S/N_μ → S/N_{<μ} is a free quotient by the finite group N_{<μ}/N_μ over a profinite base, hence locally on a finite clopen partition a product with that finite group, i.e. the pullback of a surjection of finite sets.
By AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/transfinite-tower-splitting, S → S/G has a continuous section σ, and (t, g) ↦ g·σ(t) is a G-homeomorphism T × G → S.

Exactness: given a surjection F → F' of sheaves and x' ∈ F'(S), there is a finite corrected covering {S_i → S} with lifts on S_i; pulling back along σ: T → S gives a corrected covering {T_i → T} of profinite sets (forgetting G, G-towers and G-étale maps stay towers and étale maps), which has continuous sections on a finite clopen partition (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/transfinite-tower-splitting); extending G-equivariantly via S_i = T_i × G gives a G-equivariant splitting over S and a lift of x'.
acceptance: For G = Z_p and S = G, F ↦ F(G) is exact; this is the input for H^i(pt, F_M) = H^i_cont(Z_p, M) (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0).
