nodes.title: The pro-finite étale site X_profét, with Scholze's corrected coverings (Definition 3.3 with the erratum)
nodes.statement: Let X is a locally noetherian analytic adic space (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space, every point analytic, so X is locally Spa(A, A⁺) with A a complete strongly noetherian Tate ring), X_ét is its small étale site (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site) and X_fét its finite étale site (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-site). X_profét is the category pro-X_fét := Pro(X_fét), a full subcategory of pro-X_ét and of X_proét, with |U| = lim |U_i|. A family {f_i: U_i → U} is a covering if |U| = ⋃ f_i(|U_i|) and each f_i factors as a pro-finite-étale tower U_i → W_i (steps pullbacks of finite étale surjections of X_fét; AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-tower) followed by a morphism W_i → U that is the pullback of a morphism of X_fét along some U → V_0 with V_0 ∈ X_fét. These coverings form a pretopology. The printed Definition 3.3 (families of open morphisms) is replaced by this condition; the erratum states the condition with the tower only, which read literally would exclude the covering of a disjoint union by its summands (sourceIssues AdicEtaleGeometry/E6).
hypotheses: X as stated; the tower steps and the second factor come from X_fét.
Size: a Grothendieck universe is fixed; X_ét is locally small, pro-objects are indexed by small cofiltered categories, so pro-X_ét is locally small, and sheaves take values in small sets.
proofSteps: X_fét ⊂ X_ét is full, so Pro(X_fét) ⊂ Pro(X_ét) is full; objects are pro-étale over X (finite étale surjective transitions after discarding empty summands).

Pretopology: as in AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/corrected-covers-pretopology, with X_fét in place of X_ét (a morphism to a constant object factors through a finite stage; towers and pullbacks of finite étale maps are stable under base change and composition).
acceptance: For X = Spa(K, K⁺), X_profét ≃ Gal(K^sep/K)-pfsets (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/profinite-etale-galois-sets).
The summand inclusions of X ⊔ X form a covering.

The functor Y = lim Y_i ↦ S(Y) := lim_i F_x̄(Y_i) is an equivalence of sites X_profét ≃ π1(X, x̄)-pfsets, for the corrected coverings on both sides (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-finite-etale-site-corrected, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/profinite-g-sets-site).

nodes.title: Open equals pro-étale on X_profét, and the morphism of sites X_proét → X_profét (Scholze Lemma 3.11)
nodes.statement: Let X be locally noetherian analytic. (a) Under the fully faithful inclusion X_profét ⊂ X_proét, a morphism f: U → V of X_profét is open on underlying spaces iff it is pro-étale. (b) The inclusion preserves fibre products and sends coverings of X_profét to coverings of X_proét; hence it defines a morphism of sites X_proét → X_profét. The printed consequence 'the notions of coverings coincide' is not asserted for the corrected coverings and is not used.
hypotheses: X locally noetherian analytic (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space).
proofSteps: (a) Pro-étale maps are open (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-maps-open). Conversely, reduce to X connected and pass to π1-pfsets (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/profinite-etale-galois-sets); an open map of profinite π1-sets is, onto its clopen image, an inverse limit of the maps A_i ×_{B_i} S' → S' (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/open-surjection-profinite-structure), which is a pro-étale presentation.

(b) Fibre products: AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-base-change. Coverings: pro-finite-étale towers are finite-étale towers and pullbacks of morphisms of X_fét are finite étale, so AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-site-corrected accepts them; a covering-preserving functor preserving fibre products is continuous (mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.IsContinuous).
acceptance: For X = Spa(K, O_K) (K p-adic), X_proét = X_profét since étale X-spaces are finite étale, and the morphism of sites is the identity.

sources.excerpt: Under the fully faithful embedding of categories Xprofét ⊂ Xproét , a morphism f : U → V in Xprofét is open if and only if it is pro-étale as a morphism in Xproét . In particular, the notions of coverings coincide, and there is a map of sites Xproét → Xprofét .

nodes.title: Affinoid pro-étale presentations give a generating family of coherent objects; the pro-étale topos is algebraic (Scholze Proposition 3.12(i)–(iii))
nodes.statement: Let X be locally noetherian analytic. (i) If U = lim U_i → X is a pro-étale presentation with all U_i affinoid, then U is a quasi-compact object of X_proét (every covering sieve contains a finite covering family). (ii) Let B_X be the class of such U for which U → X factors through an affinoid open subspace of X; B_X is generating (every object has a covering by members of B_X) and stable under fibre products in X_proét. (iii) Every member of B_X is coherent (quasi-compact and quasi-separated) and Sh(X_proét) is an algebraic topos in the sense of DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/quasicompact-objects-in-a-topos (SGA 4 VI 2.3).
hypotheses: X locally noetherian analytic (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space).
With corrected coverings (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-site-corrected); fewer coverings only make (i) easier.
proofSteps: (i) |U_i| = Spa of a complete Huber pair is spectral (tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spectralSpace_spa_of_pairOfDefinition) and the transitions are spectral, so |U| is spectral, hence quasi-compact (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cofiltered-limits-of-spectral-spaces); members of coverings have open images (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-maps-open), so finitely many cover, and a finite subfamily of a corrected covering whose images cover is a corrected covering.

(ii) Cover U = lim U_i → U_0 → X by the pullbacks of affinoid opens V ⊂ U_0 contained in affinoid opens of X (open immersions: towers of length 1 followed by étale maps); preimages of affinoids under the finite étale transitions are affinoid. Fibre products U ×_V W = lim U_i ×_{V_i} W_i of affinoids over affinoids are affinoid (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-products-existence, local form).
(iii) SGA 4 VI 2.1–2.2 as in Scholze, restricting to B_X: U ×_X U = U ×_{U_0} U for U over the affinoid U_0 is again in B_X, which gives quasi-separatedness.
acceptance: The Kummer tower over the torus is in B_X and coherent.

nodes.title: Quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness in X_proét are detected on underlying spaces (Scholze Proposition 3.12(iv)–(vii))
nodes.statement: Let X be locally noetherian analytic. (iv) U ∈ X_proét is quasi-compact (resp. quasi-separated) iff |U| is. (v) If U → V is an inverse limit of finite étale surjections, U is quasi-compact (resp. quasi-separated) iff V is. (vi) A morphism f: U → V of X_proét is quasi-compact (resp. quasi-separated) iff |f| is. (vii) X_proét is quasi-separated (resp. coherent) iff |X| is. If X is quasi-separated, the full subcategory X_proét^qc of quasi-compact objects with the induced coverings has the same topos as X_proét.
hypotheses: X locally noetherian analytic (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space).
proofSteps: (iv) If |U| is quasi-compact, U is covered by finitely many members of B_X (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/proetale-coherence), hence quasi-compact (SGA 4 VI 1.3); conversely an open cover of |U| induces a covering of U (open immersions from AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-quasicompact-opens). Quasi-separatedness via SGA 4 VI 1.17 and |U_i ×_U U_j| = |U_i| ×_{|U|} |U_j| up to surjection (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-base-change).

(v) SGA 4 VI 2.6 and 1.14(ii) with the coherent members of B_X; the converse by pushing open covers down along the surjective U → V. (vi) from (iii), (iv) and SGA 4 VI 2.6. (vii) from (iii), (iv) and the definitions.
Same topos: quasi-compact objects form a generating family closed under the relevant fibre products when X is quasi-separated (comparison lemma, mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.IsDenseSubsite).
acceptance: For X affinoid, X_proét is coherent; for the open unit disc it is not quasi-compact.

sources.excerpt: (iv) An object U ∈ Xproét is quasicompact, resp. quasiseparated, if and only if |U | is quasicompact, resp. quasiseparated.
sources.match: Proposition 3.12(iv).

sources.excerpt: (vi) A morphism f : U → V of objects in Xproét is quasicompact, resp. quasiseparated, if and only if |f | : |U | → |V | is quasicompact, resp. quasiseparated.
sources.match: Proposition 3.12(vi).

sources.excerpt: (vii) The site Xproét is quasiseparated, resp. coherent, if and only if |X| is quasiseparated, resp. coherent.
sources.match: Proposition 3.12(vii).

sources.excerpt: If X is quasiseparated, one can also consider the subsite Xproétqc ⊂ Xproét consisting of quasicompact objects in Xproét ; the associated topoi are the same.
sources.match: The subsite of quasi-compact objects has the same topos.

nodes.title: The fibre morphisms of topoi i_x: Sh(Y_x,profét) → Sh(X_proét) at points x ∈ X (Scholze Proposition 3.13, first sentence)
nodes.statement: Let X be locally noetherian analytic, x ∈ X, Y_x := Spa(k(x)^, k(x)^+) → X the canonical morphism from the completed residue field pair, x̄ a geometric point over the closed point of Y_x and G_x := π1(Y_x, x̄) ≅ Gal(k(x)^sep/k(x)^) (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-galois-category), so that Y_x,profét ≃ G_x-pfsets (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/profinite-etale-galois-sets). For quasi-compact U = lim U_i ∈ X_proét let Φ_x(U) := lim_i Hom_X(x̄, U_i), a profinite G_x-set. For X quasi-separated, Φ_x: X_proét^qc → G_x-pfsets preserves finite limits and coverings, so it defines a morphism of sites and a morphism of topoi i_x: Sh(G_x-pfsets) → Sh(X_proét) with i_x^*F the sheafification of V ↦ colim_{V → Φ_x(U)} F(U) (U ∈ X_proét^qc); for general X, i_x is defined through any affinoid neighbourhood of x and is independent of it up to canonical isomorphism. The image of Y_x in X is the set of generalisations of x, which can be larger than {x}. The deleted last sentence of Proposition 3.13 (enough points given by profinite covers of geometric points) is not part of this node.
hypotheses: X locally noetherian analytic (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space).
Geometric points as in AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site-and-geometric-points; C⁺ of arbitrary rank.
proofSteps: Hom_X(x̄, U_i) is finite for quasi-compact U_i étale over X (étale maps are locally quasi-finite, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/unramified-locally-quasi-finite), with a continuous G_x-action, so Φ_x(U) is a profinite G_x-set; Φ_x preserves finite limits because Hom_X(x̄, −) does.

Coverings: étale surjective families go to jointly surjective families of G_x-étale maps (geometric points lift along étale surjections, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site-and-geometric-points); finite étale surjective steps go to pullbacks of surjections of finite G_x-sets, so towers go to G_x-towers.

A continuous, finite-limit-preserving functor between sites with finite limits gives a morphism of sites, and X_proét^qc has the topos of X_proét for quasi-separated X (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/proetale-quasicompactness-detection); the pullback formula is the left Kan extension formula (mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafPullback).
acceptance: For X = Spa(K, O_K) with K p-adic and x its point, Φ_x is the equivalence X_proét ≃ G_K-pfsets and i_x is an equivalence of topoi.

nodes.title: The family (i_x^*)_{x∈X} detects zero sheaves (Scholze Proposition 3.13, second sentence)
nodes.statement: Let X be locally noetherian analytic and F an abelian sheaf on X_proét (corrected coverings). If i_x^*F = 0 for every x ∈ X (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/proetale-fibre-morphism-of-topoi), then F = 0. Stalks at geometric points alone do not suffice (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-site-corrected, test ProEtaleSite.test_geometric_stalk_not_conservative), and the functors F ↦ (i_x^*F)(S) are not asserted to be points of the topos.
hypotheses: X locally noetherian analytic (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space).

The printed proof produces a pro-étale surjection V' → U near the fibre over x; for corrected coverings the step that makes it a covering is recorded as a gap (gaps.json, 'Proposition 3.13 conservativity under corrected coverings').
proofSteps: Take U quasi-compact and s ∈ F(U); for x ∈ X the image of s in (i_x^*F)(Φ_x(U)) vanishes, so there are a covering {S'_k → Φ_x(U)} of G_x-pfsets and V_k → U in X_proét^qc with S'_k → Φ_x(V_k) over Φ_x(U) and s|V_k = 0.

Reduce to U, V_k pro-finite-étale over connected X (as in Scholze) and let V'_k ⊂ V_k correspond to the π1(X, x̄)-saturation of the image of S'_k; then V'_k → U is pro-étale with image containing the fibre over x (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-maps-open) and s|V'_k = 0.

Gap: to conclude, the family {V'_k → U} must be refined to a corrected covering of an open neighbourhood of the fibre over x; the printed proof uses that V'_k → U is pro-étale, which suffices only for the printed topology. Granting this step, quasi-compactness of U gives a finite corrected covering on which s vanishes, so s = 0.
acceptance: For X = Spa(K, O_K), i_x^* is an equivalence and the statement is trivial.

sources.excerpt: If for all points x, i∗x F = 0, then F = 0.
sources.match: The conservativity statement of Proposition 3.13.

sources.excerpt: Since S̃ ′ → S̃ is a pro-finite étale cover, Sx̄′ → Sx̄ is an open surjective map, hence so is the map S(V ′ ) = T → S(U ) = Sx̄ . This means that the map V ′ → U is pro-étale.

sources.excerpt: It is not enough to check stalks at geometric points: One has to include the profinite covers of geometric points to get a conservative family.

nodes.title: The pro-étale topos has enough points for abstract reasons (erratum item (2)); the deleted point assertions are not used
nodes.statement: Let X be locally noetherian analytic. If |X| is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, Sh(X_proét) is a coherent topos (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/proetale-quasicompactness-detection (vii)) and therefore has enough points (Deligne's theorem, SGA 4 VI 9.0), i.e. the site satisfies mathlib:CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.HasEnoughPoints; for general X the same holds because X is covered by quasi-compact quasi-separated opens U and Sh(X_proét)/U ≃ Sh(U_proét) (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/proetale-slice). The same applies to G-pfsets. The points are not identified: Scholze's Corollary 3.8 and the last sentence of Proposition 3.13 (enough points given by profinite (G-free) covers of geometric points) are deleted by the erratum and are not used anywhere in this packet.
hypotheses: X locally noetherian analytic (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space).
Deligne's completeness theorem for coherent topoi is requested from DiamondsAndVStacks:D0 (requests.json).
proofSteps: Coherence: AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/proetale-coherence and AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/proetale-quasicompactness-detection.
Deligne's theorem gives a conservative family of points of a coherent topos (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0, requested); a conservative small family of points is HasEnoughPoints.
Local case: coherent opens cover X and localisation along them is compatible with the slice description (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/proetale-slice).
acceptance: For G = 1 and a profinite set T with at least two points, the functor S ↦ C(T, S) on profinite sets is not a point in the sense of mathlib:CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Point: the summand covering {S_1 → S_1 ⊔ S_2, S_2 → S_1 ⊔ S_2} is not sent to a jointly surjective family, since a map T → S_1 ⊔ S_2 meeting both summands factors through neither; this is the misconception about points that the erratum removes.

sources.excerpt: Note however that as both topoi are coherent, they still admit enough points for abstract reasons. These results were not used in the rest of the paper.
sources.match: Both topoi are coherent and have enough points for abstract reasons.

sources.excerpt: In particular, Xproét has enough points, given by profinite covers of geometric points.

nodes.title: The pro-étale site of an étale X-space is the slice site: V_proét ≃ X_proét/V
nodes.statement: Let X be locally noetherian analytic and V ∈ X_ét (so V is a locally noetherian analytic adic space). The functor V_proét → X_proét/c(V), lim V_i ↦ (lim V_i with its map to V), is an equivalence of categories under which the corrected coverings of V_proét correspond to the coverings of the slice topology (mathlib:CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.over of J_proét); hence Sh(V_proét) ≃ Sh(X_proét)/h_V. It is compatible with ν: under the étale slice equivalence V_ét ≃ X_ét/V (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/slice-site), ν_V corresponds to the localisation of ν_X. For V ⊂ X open this is the pro-étale site of an open subspace.
hypotheses: X locally noetherian analytic (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space).
V étale over X; open subspaces are the main case (AdicSpacesPartII:R4/proetale-slice-open-subspace re-exports it on the R0/R1 carriers).
proofSteps: An object W = lim W_k of X_proét with a map to c(V): Hom(lim W_k, c V) = colim_k Hom(W_k, V), so after reindexing all W_k lie over V; each W_k → V is étale by cancellation (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-smooth-cancellation) and the transitions are unchanged, so W ∈ V_proét. Morphisms over V correspond (Hom formula).

Morphism classes agree: a morphism of pro-V_ét is étale (resp. finite étale) in the V-sense iff in the X-sense (pull back E → E_0 of X_ét along V to E ×_X V → E_0 ×_X V of V_ét), and underlying spaces agree; hence towers, étale maps and joint surjectivity agree, so the corrected coverings coincide with the coverings of GrothendieckTopology.over.
Compatibility with ν: on constant objects the equivalence is the étale slice equivalence (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/slice-site).
acceptance: For V = X the equivalence is the identity; for V = X_n in the Kummer tower, (X_n)_proét ≃ X_proét/X_n and X̃ corresponds to the Kummer tower over X_n.

sources.excerpt: Then, we may consider the localized site Xproét /XL of objects with a structure map to XL , and the induced covers. One immediately checks the following result.

nodes.title: Quasi-compact quasi-separated étale spaces over X_{L̂} descend to a finite subextension (the approximation behind Scholze Proposition 3.15)
nodes.statement: Let K be a complete nonarchimedean field with an open valuation subring K⁺, X a quasi-compact quasi-separated adic space locally of finite type over Spa(K, K⁺) (anchor Layer 5.2), L/K a separable algebraic extension with finite subextensions L_i, L_i⁺ and L⁺ the integral closures of K⁺, and X_{L_i} := X ×_{Spa(K,K⁺)} Spa(L_i, L_i⁺), X_{L̂} := X ×_{Spa(K,K⁺)} Spa(L̂, L̂⁺). Then (a) |X_{L̂}| → lim_i |X_{L_i}| is a homeomorphism; (b) for qcqs U_i, U'_i étale over X_{L_i}, Hom_{X_{L̂}}(U_i ×_{X_{L_i}} X_{L̂}, U'_i ×_{X_{L_i}} X_{L̂}) = colim_{j ≥ i} Hom_{X_{L_j}}(U_i ×_{X_{L_i}} X_{L_j}, U'_i ×_{X_{L_i}} X_{L_j}); (c) every qcqs étale X_{L̂}-space is isomorphic to U_i ×_{X_{L_i}} X_{L̂} for some i and some qcqs étale U_i → X_{L_i}. Hence base change is an equivalence 2-colim_i (X_{L_i})_{ét,qcqs} ≃ (X_{L̂})_{ét,qcqs}.
hypotheses: X locally of finite type over Spa(K, K⁺) and qcqs; this is the setting in which X_{L̂} is locally noetherian and Scholze's X_{L,proét} is defined (sourceIssues AdicEtaleGeometry/E8).
proofSteps: (a) Locally X = Spa(A, A⁺); A ⊗̂_K L̂ is the completion of colim_i A ⊗_K L_i, Spa of a completion equals Spa of the ring (Huber 1993, Proposition 3.9), and continuous valuations of a filtered colimit bounded by the colimit plus ring are compatible families; rational subsets are defined at finite level, so the bijection is a homeomorphism.

(b) A morphism g over X_{L̂} is étale and its graph is an open subspace of the fibre product (the diagonal of an étale map is an open embedding, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/infinitesimal-criteria), quasi-compact; by (a) it is the preimage of a quasi-compact open at some finite level; its projection to the source is an isomorphism after base change, hence for large j (surjectivity by quasi-compactness of the open image, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/smooth-morphism-open; injectivity since the diagonal is then surjective); faithfulness similarly.

(c) Locally on the source, an étale map to an affinoid Spa(A_{L̂}) is Spa of A_{L̂}⟨X⟩/(f_1, …, f_n) with f_i ∈ A_{L̂}[X] and invertible Jacobian (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-local-structure (iii)); approximate the coefficients by elements of A ⊗_K L_j (dense) and use stability of standard étale presentations under perturbation (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-presentation-perturbation); rational subsets defined over L̂ are rational subsets defined over some L_j by stability of rational subsets under perturbation (tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.exists_mem_nhds_forall_rationalSubset_eq_of_sub_mem); glue the local descents by (b).
acceptance: X = Spa(Q_p⟨T⟩, Z_p⟨T⟩), L = Q_p(μ_{p^∞}): the Kummer cover T = S^p over X_{L̂} is the base change of the same cover over Q_p.
For X = Spa(K, K°) this is Krasner's lemma: finite separable L̂-algebras come from finite separable L_i-algebras.

nodes.title: Change of base field: X_{L̂,proét} ≃ X_proét/X_L (Scholze Proposition 3.15)
nodes.statement: Let K, K⁺, X, L/K and L_i be as in AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-descent-along-algebraic-extension, with X locally of finite type over Spa(K, K⁺) (not necessarily qcqs). Let X_L := lim_i X_{L_i} ∈ X_proét (a pro-finite-étale object: the X_{L_i} are finite étale over X and the transitions are finite étale surjective). Then there is an equivalence of sites X_{L̂,proét} ≃ X_proét/X_L (slice topology), sending lim_j V_j (V_j qcqs étale over X_{L̂}) to lim_{(i,j)} V_{j,i}, where V_{j,i} → X_{L_i} descends V_j (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-descent-along-algebraic-extension); for L/K finite this is AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/proetale-slice with V = X_L.
hypotheses: X locally of finite type over Spa(K, K⁺): Scholze states the result for locally noetherian X, where X_{L̂} need not be locally noetherian and X_{L,proét} is then undefined (sourceIssues AdicEtaleGeometry/E8).
Coverings on both sides are the corrected ones; the equivalence is checked on the generating family of quasi-compact objects.
proofSteps: Reduce to X qcqs (both sides are local on X, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/proetale-slice) and to quasi-compact objects (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/proetale-coherence).

Functor: descend the stages V_j and the finite étale surjective transitions to some X_{L_i} (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-descent-along-algebraic-extension (b), (c)), giving a pro-étale object over X_L; well defined and fully faithful by (b); essentially surjective because an object W → X_L of X_proét has W_k → X_{L_i} for large i, and base change to X_{L̂} gives V.
Coverings correspond: underlying spaces agree by (a), towers and étale maps descend and base change to towers and étale maps.
acceptance: X = Spa(Q_p⟨T^{±1}⟩, Z_p⟨T^{±1}⟩) and L = Q_p(μ_{p^∞}): X_{L̂,proét} ≃ X_proét/X_L; the Kummer–cyclotomic tower over X_{L̂} is the object X̃ ×_X X_L.

X = Spa(K, K°) with K discretely valued and L = K^sep: on quasi-compact objects X_{L̂,proét} ≃ X_proét/X_{K^sep} ≃ (G_K-pfsets)/G_K ≃ Profinite, matching X_{L̂} = Spa(Ĉ, O_Ĉ) with Ĉ the completed separable closure.

nodes.title: Products U × S with profinite sets in X_proét; an open surjection of profinite sets need not give a covering
nodes.statement: Let X be locally noetherian analytic, U ∈ X_proét and S = lim_j S_j a profinite set (S_j finite discrete). Put S × X := lim_j ⊔_{s∈S_j} X ∈ X_proét (the pullback to X of S viewed in the pro-finite étale site of the base) and U × S := U ×_X (S × X). Then: (a) U × S ∈ X_proét and |U × S| ≅ |U| × S; (b) for quasi-compact V ∈ X_proét, Hom(V, U × S) ≅ Hom(V, U) × C(|V|, S), naturally in V; (c) for S ≠ ∅ the projection U × S → U has a section (choose s ∈ S), so it generates a covering sieve; it is itself a finite-étale tower when S has countably many clopen subsets (length ω) or S = G/G' for a profinite group G (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/profinite-group-tower); (d) for X = Spa(C, O_C) (C algebraically closed, O_C of rank one) and an open continuous surjection f: S → S' of profinite sets without continuous section (Ribes–Zalesskii, Example 5.6.9), U × S → U × S' is pro-étale and surjective, but for U = X the sieve it generates is not a covering of X_proét.
hypotheses: X locally noetherian analytic (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space).
S arbitrary profinite; (d) shows why no splitting of arbitrary open surjections is assumed.
proofSteps: (a) ⊔_{s∈S_j} X is finite étale over X and the transitions for surjective S_j → S_k are finite étale surjective, so S × X is pro-étale over X; U × S exists and is pro-étale (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-base-change, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-composition); |U × S| = lim_j |U| × S_j.

(b) Hom(V, ⊔_{s∈S_j} X) = colim_k Hom_X(V_k, ⊔_{s∈S_j} X) = locally constant maps |V| → S_j, since for quasi-compact V a clopen of |V| = lim |V_k| comes from a finite stage (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cofiltered-limits-of-spectral-spaces); take the limit over j.

(c) A section of a morphism makes the generated sieve maximal. Countable S: S = lim_n S_n with surjective transitions gives a tower of length ω (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-tower-is-pro-etale); S = G/G': AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/profinite-group-tower.

(d) f is pro-étale over X by AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/open-surjection-profinite-structure; if a corrected covering family of S' factored through f, splitting of towers (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/transfinite-tower-splitting) and of étale maps over a finite clopen partition would give a continuous section of f.
acceptance: Scholze, proof of Lemma 5.6: Ṽ ×_V Ṽ ≅ Ṽ × Z_p^n for the Galois cover Ṽ → V with group Z_p^n.

nodes.title: Pro-finite-étale Galois covers are corrected coverings; Ũ ×_U Ũ ≅ Ũ × G and Galois descent of sections
nodes.statement: Let U ∈ X_proét, G a profinite group and Ũ = lim_j Ũ_j → U a pro-finite-étale G-torsor: each Ũ_j → U is finite étale and Galois with group G/N_j for open normal N_j with ⋂ N_j = 1, compatibly. Then (a) Ũ ×_U Ũ ≅ Ũ × G (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/profinite-set-objects) via (x, g) ↦ (x, xg); (b) Ũ → U is a finite-étale tower, hence a covering of X_proét, for every G (not only for countable systems); (c) for every sheaf F on X_proét, F(U) is the equalizer of the two maps F(Ũ) ⇉ F(Ũ × G); if U is quasi-compact quasi-separated and F = ν^*F' for a sheaf F' on X_ét, then F(Ũ × G) = LC(G, F(Ũ)) and F(U) = F(Ũ)^G.

nodes.title: The rational-covering site on the opposite category of complete Huber pairs
nodes.statement: CAff is the category of complete Hausdorff Huber pairs (A, A⁺) (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair on complete Hausdorff Huber rings, A⁺ a ring of integral elements) with morphisms tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom (continuous ring maps carrying A⁺ into B⁺). For (A, A⁺) ∈ CAff and rational subsets U_1, …, U_n (U_k = R(T_k/s_k) with T_k·A open; tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset) covering Spa(A, A⁺), the family of rational localisations (A, A⁺) → (O(U_k), O⁺(U_k)) (anchor Layer 3.1: the completed A⟨T_k/s_k⟩ with the integral closure of the image of A⁺[T_k/s_k]) is a rational covering family of (A, A⁺)ᵒᵖ in CAffᵒᵖ; n = 0 is allowed exactly when Spa(A, A⁺) = ∅, i.e. A = 0. The rational covering families form a coverage on CAffᵒᵖ (mathlib:CategoryTheory.Coverage): for every morphism (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) there is a rational covering family of (B, B⁺) each member of which factors through a member of the given family. J_rat := Coverage.toGrothendieck is the rational topology; a presheaf of sets on CAffᵒᵖ is a J_rat-sheaf iff it satisfies the sheaf condition for all rational covering families (mathlib:CategoryTheory.Presieve.isSheaf_coverage). The presheaf 𝒪: (A, A⁺) ↦ A is represented by (Z[T], Z) (discrete) and satisfies the sheaf condition at the rational covering families of (A, A⁺) and of all its rational localisations iff the structure presheaf of Spa(A, A⁺) is a sheaf of sets on rational covers; for complete Tate pairs this is sheafiness in the anchor's sense (Huber.IsSheafyPair), the topology being automatic by the open mapping theorem (anchor Layer 0.6).
hypotheses: Complete means complete and Hausdorff (anchor convention 3).
Pullbacks of rational subsets along non-adic morphisms need not be rational; the coverage axiom only needs a rational refinement, which exists by quasi-compactness.
Size: CAff is formed from pairs in a fixed universe; sheaves take values in the next universe, where sheafification exists.
proofSteps: Coverage axiom: for φ: (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺), the preimages Spa(φ)⁻¹(U_k) (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.spaComap, continuous) are open and cover Spa(B, B⁺); rational subsets form a basis (tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.isTopologicalBasis_spaRationalFamily) and Spa(B, B⁺) is quasi-compact (spectral: tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spectralSpace_spa_of_pairOfDefinition), so finitely many rational V_l, each inside some preimage, cover Spa(B, B⁺).

B → O_B(V_l) composed with φ sends Spa(O_B(V_l)) into U_k, so it factors uniquely through O_A(U_k) by the universal property of rational localisation (tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_of_isUnit_of_forall_comap_mem_rationalSubset; the plus rings follow by integrality).

Sheaf condition for 𝒪 at (A, A⁺) and its rational localisations is the equalizer condition of the anchor's structure presheaf on rational covers of rational subsets (Spa(O(U)) ≅ U with matching rational subsets, anchor Layer 3.1).
acceptance: The Laurent covering {|T| ≤ |p|}, {|p| ≤ |T|} of Spa(Q_p⟨T⟩, Z_p⟨T⟩) is a rational covering family with members Q_p⟨T/p⟩ and Q_p⟨T, p/T⟩.

nodes.title: Yoneda-adic spaces: generalized adic spaces as sheaves on complete Huber pairs (Scholze–Weinstein pre-adic spaces, Kedlaya–Liu preadic spaces)
nodes.statement: Let CAff and J_rat be as in AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/huber-pair-rational-site. For (A, A⁺) ∈ CAff put Spa^Y(A, A⁺) := the J_rat-sheafification (mathlib:CategoryTheory.presheafToSheaf) of h_{(A,A⁺)} = Hom_CAff((A, A⁺), −). A morphism of sheaves F → Spa^Y(A, A⁺) is an open immersion if there is an open U ⊂ Spa(A, A⁺) with F ≅ colim_{V ⊂ U rational} Spa^Y(O(V), O⁺(V)) over Spa^Y(A, A⁺); a morphism F → G of J_rat-sheaves is an open immersion if its base change along every Spa^Y(A, A⁺) → G is an open immersion in the previous sense. A Yoneda-adic space is a J_rat-sheaf F such that F = colim Spa^Y(A, A⁺) over the category of open immersions Spa^Y(A, A⁺) → F; YAdic is the full subcategory of Sh(CAffᵒᵖ, J_rat) on Yoneda-adic spaces. This is the category of adic spaces of Scholze–Weinstein [SW13, Definition 2.1.5], the pre-adic spaces of the Berkeley Lectures (Definition 3.4.1) and the preadic spaces of Kedlaya–Liu (Definition 8.2.3, on Tate pairs); ECD Definition 15.5 and Lemma 15.6 hold in this generality. The name 'Yoneda-adic' (Berkeley, Appendix to Lecture 3) is used because the anchor's 'pre-adic spaces' (Wedhorn's 𝒱^pre, anchor Layer 3.4) are a different category built from the structure presheaf. Every Yoneda-adic space has an underlying topological space |F| with |Spa^Y(A, A⁺)| = Spa(A, A⁺) (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/yoneda-adic-ind-ringed-description), open immersions into F correspond to open subsets of |F| (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/yoneda-adic-open-immersions), and the anchor's adic spaces form a full subcategory (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/adic-spaces-in-yoneda-adic-spaces). The framework does not assume that any non-sheafy pair is sheafy.
hypotheses: CAff, J_rat as in AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/huber-pair-rational-site; sizes as there.

The construction is needed because sheafiness is not known to be stable under finite étale extension (Kedlaya–Liu, Remark 8.2.18), so Spa of the finite étale algebras used in ECD §15 and in AdicEtaleGeometry:A4 need not be an adic space.
proofSteps: Spa^Y exists because J_rat-sheafification exists (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/huber-pair-rational-site).
Hom(Spa^Y(A, A⁺), G) = G(A, A⁺) for every J_rat-sheaf G: adjunction of sheafification and the Yoneda lemma.
Open immersions and the colimit condition are stable under isomorphism; the full subcategory is replete.
acceptance: Spa^Y(Q_p⟨T⟩, Z_p⟨T⟩) is the image of the closed unit disc; the open unit disc is an open Yoneda-adic subspace that is not affinoid.

nodes.title: Open immersions into Spa^Y(A, A⁺) are the open subsets of Spa(A, A⁺); gluing along rational subsets
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) ∈ CAff. (a) For a rational subset U ⊂ Spa(A, A⁺), the morphism Spa^Y(O(U), O⁺(U)) → Spa^Y(A, A⁺) induced by the rational localisation is an open immersion (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/generalized-adic-presentation) with associated open subset U, and a monomorphism. (b) U ↦ colim_{V ⊂ U rational} Spa^Y(O(V), O⁺(V)) is an order-preserving bijection from open subsets of Spa(A, A⁺) to isomorphism classes of open immersions into Spa^Y(A, A⁺), taking intersections to fibre products and unions to unions. (c) For a rational covering {U_k} of Spa(A, A⁺), Spa^Y(A, A⁺) is the coequalizer of ⊔_{k,l} Spa^Y(O(U_k ∩ U_l)) ⇉ ⊔_k Spa^Y(O(U_k)). (d) Open immersions are monomorphisms and are stable under base change and composition.
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) arbitrary in CAff (sheafiness not assumed).
proofSteps: (a) h_{O(U)} → h_A is a monomorphism of presheaves (a map out of (A, A⁺) factors through O(U) in at most one way, universal property, tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_of_isUnit_of_forall_comap_mem_rationalSubset), and sheafification preserves monomorphisms.

Open-immersion condition: a section of Spa^Y(A, A⁺) over (B, B⁺) is, on a rational covering of (B, B⁺), a morphism φ: A → B'; it factors through O(U) locally iff Spa(φ) lands in U, and the preimage of U is covered by rational subsets V of Spa(B', B'⁺) (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.spaComap_preimage_rationalSubset for adic φ; quasi-compact refinement in general), so the base change is colim over rational V in the preimage of Spa^Y(O(V)).

(b), (c) are Berkeley's observation that open immersions into Spa^Y(A, A⁺) correspond to open subsets of Spa(A, A⁺), together with the sheaf property of J_rat-sheaves for rational coverings (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/huber-pair-rational-site). nodes.title: Yoneda-adic spaces as ind-topologically ringed spaces with valuations; the underlying space |F| (Berkeley Proposition 3.5.3)
nodes.statement: Let (V)_ind be the category of triples (X, 𝒪_X, (|·(x)|)_{x∈X}) with X a topological space, 𝒪_X a sheaf of ind-topological rings (formal filtered colimits "lim" A_i of topological rings; mathlib:CategoryTheory.Ind applied to topological rings) and |·(x)| an equivalence class of continuous valuations on the stalk, with the evident morphisms. For (A, A⁺) ∈ CAff let Spa^ind(A, A⁺) be Spa(A, A⁺) with the sheafification of its structure presheaf in ind-topological rings and the same valuations; a pre-adic space in (V)_ind is an object locally isomorphic to some Spa^ind(A, A⁺). Then X ↦ X^Y, X^Y(A, A⁺) := Hom_{(V)_ind}(Spa^ind(A, A⁺), X), is an equivalence from pre-adic spaces in (V)_ind to Yoneda-adic spaces, with Spa^ind(B, B⁺)^Y ≅ Spa^Y(B, B⁺), matching open immersions. Consequently every Yoneda-adic space F has an underlying topological space |F|, functorial in F, with |Spa^Y(A, A⁺)| = Spa(A, A⁺), open subsets of |F| ↔ open immersions into F, a structure sheaf of ind-topological rings and valuations at points. Sheafifying in topological rings instead (Spa^sh) does not give a fully faithful description of maps between affinoids.

nodes.statement: Let X be an adic space in the anchor's sense (Layer 5: an object of Huber's 𝒱 covered by affinoid adic spaces Spa(B, B⁺) of sheafy complete pairs) and let X^Y := colim Spa^Y(O_X(U), O_X⁺(U)) over the affinoid open subspaces U ⊂ X and their open immersions (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/yoneda-adic-open-immersions). nodes.title: Analytic Yoneda-adic spaces are covered by Tate affinoids and are the preadic spaces of Kedlaya–Liu
nodes.statement: Let F be a Yoneda-adic space. A point x ∈ |F| is analytic if it has an open affinoid neighbourhood Spa^Y(A, A⁺) with A Tate; F is analytic if all its points are (Berkeley Definition 4.3.2). (a) For (A, A⁺) ∈ CAff, x ∈ Spa(A, A⁺) is analytic in this sense iff it is analytic in the anchor's sense (tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.IsAnalyticPoint); in particular the analytic locus of Spa^Y(A, A⁺) is covered by finitely many Spa^Y(O(U_g), O⁺(U_g)) with O(U_g) Tate. (b) Every morphism of Huber pairs out of a Tate (or analytic) Huber ring is adic. (c) Restriction along the inclusion CAff^Tate ⊂ CAff of complete Tate pairs is fully faithful on analytic Yoneda-adic spaces, and identifies them with the Yoneda-adic spaces built on complete Tate pairs, i.e. with Kedlaya–Liu's preadic spaces (complete Tate pairs are the adic Banach rings of Kedlaya–Liu).
hypotheses: Analytic points of Spa(A, A⁺): support not open (anchor Layer 2.3).
proofSteps: (a) Berkeley Proposition 4.3.1(2): an analytic point has a rational neighbourhood with Tate ring of sections; in Tau Ceti the standard cover of the analytic locus by R(G/g) with Tate completed localisations (tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spaAnalytic_eq_biUnion_rationalSubset, tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.isTateRing_completion_locTopology_of_mem_generators).
(b) If ϖ is a topologically nilpotent unit of A then f(ϖ) is one of B, and f(ϖ)ⁿB_0 is an ideal of definition of a ring of definition B_0 (Berkeley Lemma 5.1.2); for analytic A via Proposition 5.1.3.

(c) By (a) an analytic Yoneda-adic space F is the colimit of its open immersions from Spa^Y(A_k, A_k⁺) with A_k Tate, so Hom(F, G) = lim_k G(A_k, A_k⁺) depends only on the restriction of G to complete Tate pairs; conversely a Kedlaya–Liu preadic space (a sheaf on complete Tate pairs, colimit of its affinoids) extends as the same colimit of Spa^Y. Complete Tate rings carry norms defining their topology (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/tate-ring-norm), matching Kedlaya–Liu's adic Banach rings.

T, becomes a topologically nilpotent unit); Spa^Y(Z_p⟦T⟧, Z_p⟦T⟧) itself is not analytic.

nodes.title: Fibre products of analytic Yoneda-adic spaces; affinoid case by completed tensor products
nodes.statement: Analytic Yoneda-adic spaces have fibre products, computed in Sh(CAffᵒᵖ, J_rat), and the fibre product of analytic Yoneda-adic spaces is analytic. For morphisms of complete analytic pairs (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺), (A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺): Spa^Y(B, B⁺) ×_{Spa^Y(A, A⁺)} Spa^Y(C, C⁺) ≅ Spa^Y(B ⊗̂_A C, (B ⊗̂_A C)⁺) for the completed tensor product of AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product, with no sheafiness assumption; |F ×_H G| → |F| ×_{|H|} |G| is surjective. Beyond the analytic case the affinoid formula fails: (Z_p⟦T⟧, Z_p⟦T⟧) ← (Z_p, Z_p) → (Q_p, Z_p) has no pushout of Huber pairs.

proofSteps: Affinoid case: h_B ×_{h_A} h_C = h_{B ⊗̂_A C} on CAff by the universal property of the completed tensor product for adic maps (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product-universal-property; complete pushout, Berkeley Remark 5.1.6), and sheafification preserves finite limits (mathlib:CategoryTheory.presheafToSheaf, finite limits).

Open immersions are stable under base change (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/yoneda-adic-open-immersions (d)); rational subsets of B ⊗̂_A C over rational subsets of B and C are rational with the expected rings (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-rational-localisation), so the fibre product of general analytic Yoneda-adic spaces is covered by affinoid fibre products, hence Yoneda-adic; analytic since B ⊗̂_A C is analytic.

nodes.title: A2 supplier contract: separated, proper and partially proper morphisms of analytic adic spaces and their valuative criteria are AdicSpacesPartII R0's notions
nodes.statement: Let f : X → Y be a quasi-separated morphism of analytic adic spaces (AdicEtaleGeometry:A0/analytic-locus-restriction) which is locally of +weakly finite type (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/plus-weakly-finite-type), with X and Y covered by open affinoids whose rings are complete and stably sheafy (for instance X, Y locally noetherian, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space). These hypotheses make the diagonal Δ_f : X → X ×_Y X and every base change of f along a morphism between such spaces exist (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-products-existence (b); every morphism of analytic adic spaces is adic). With the definitions of AdicSpacesPartII R0: (1) f is separated (Δ_f(|X|) closed) ⇔ Δ_f is a closed embedding ⇔ for every valuation ring (x, A) ∈ X_v and every centre y of (x, A) on Y there is at most one centre z of (x, A) on X with f(z) = y; (2) f is partially proper ⇔ there is exactly one such centre; (3), the declaration: f is proper ⇔ f is quasi-compact and for every (x, A) ∈ X_v and every centre y of (x, A) on Y there is exactly one centre z of (x, A) on X with f(z) = y; (4) closed embeddings and finite morphisms are proper, and separated, universally closed and proper morphisms are stable under composition and under base change between such spaces. These are Huber's notions (Huber 1996, 1.3.1–1.3.10), and AdicEtaleGeometry uses no other: its diagonals, separated, proper and partially proper morphisms and valuative criteria are these, and they are stated only under hypotheses that make X ×_Y X and the base changes exist; outside them (for instance for a perfectoid space over Spa ℚ_p, which is not locally of weakly finite type) no separatedness or properness predicate of adic spaces is defined. They are distinct from the notions for small v-stacks (Scholze–Weinstein, Lecture 17; ECD §§10, 18), whose comparison with these is DiamondsAndVStacks D3/D6's. Lean name: `AdicSpace.IsProper.iff_quasiCompact_and_existsUnique_centre`.
hypotheses: X, Y analytic; f quasi-separated and locally of +weakly finite type.

proofSteps: Existence of X ×_Y X and of base changes: f is locally of weakly finite type (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-type-morphism-classes) and every morphism of analytic adic spaces is adic (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-iff-analytic-locus), so AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-products-existence (b) applies, and its pieces are again covered by stably sheafy affinoids.

(2): AdicSpacesPartII:R0/separated-proper-partially-proper (Huber 1.3.9, with R0/valuative-criterion-specializing, Huber 1.3.8).

(4): AdicSpacesPartII:R0/closed-embedding-proper, R0/finite-morphisms (Huber 1.4.5(ii)), R0/proper-comp and R0/proper-base-change.

nodes.title: The relative closed unit polydisc B^n_X over an adic space
nodes.statement: Let X be an adic space (anchor Layer 5) covered by open affinoids Spa(B, B⁺) with B complete and stably sheafy (for instance X locally noetherian), and n ≥ 0. The relative closed unit polydisc of dimension n is B^n_X := X ×_{Spa(ℤ, ℤ)} Spa(ℤ[T₁, …, Tₙ], ℤ[T₁, …, Tₙ]) (both rings discrete), which exists because Spa(ℤ[T], ℤ[T]) → Spa(ℤ, ℤ) is of finite type (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-products-existence (a)); it comes with the projection π : B^n_X → X and the coordinates T₁, …, Tₙ ∈ O⁺(B^n_X). Properties: (a) charts — over an open affinoid Spa(B, B⁺) ⊆ X, π⁻¹(Spa(B, B⁺)) = Spa(B⟨T₁, …, Tₙ⟩, B⁺⟨T₁, …, Tₙ⟩), where B⟨T⟩ is the completed ring of restricted power series (Tau Ceti `restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion`) and B⁺⟨T⟩ the series with all coefficients in B⁺; B⁺⟨T⟩ is integrally closed in B⟨T⟩, so it is Huber's plus ring and ECD's B^n_Y; (b) universal property — for an adic space Z over X, Hom_X(Z, B^n_X) ≅ O⁺_Z(Z)ⁿ by pulling back T₁, …, Tₙ; (c) base change — B^n_X ×_X X' ≅ B^n_{X'} for X' → X with X' of the same kind, and B^{m+n}_X ≅ B^m_X ×_X B^n_X; (d) π is quasi-compact, separated and smooth with Ω_{B^n_X/X} free on dT₁, …, dTₙ (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/restricted-power-series-smooth), and B^n_X is locally noetherian (resp. analytic) when X is; (e) for X locally noetherian and analytic, B^n_X is the open subspace {|T₁|, …, |Tₙ| ≤ 1} of the relative affine space A^n_ℤ ×_{Spec ℤ} X (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/scheme-fibre-product-analytification). Conventions: the plus ring is B⁺⟨T⟩, not the power-bounded subring B⟨T⟩°: over Spa(K, K⁺) with K⁺ ⊊ K° the fibre is Spa(K⟨T⟩, K⁺⟨T⟩), whereas Tau Ceti's `closedPolydisc` over K uses K⟨T⟩° = K°⟨T⟩; the radius is 1, and polydiscs of radius |ϖ|^{−k} are the rational subsets {|ϖᵏTᵢ| ≤ 1} of the relative affine space. Lean name: `AdicSpace.relativePolydisc`.
hypotheses: X covered by open affinoids with complete stably sheafy rings (so that the fibre product exists as an adic space).
Discrete topology on ℤ[T₁, …, Tₙ] with plus ring ℤ[T₁, …, Tₙ].
proofSteps: Existence: (ℤ, ℤ) → (ℤ[T], ℤ[T]) is a quotient mapping out of ℤ⟨X⟩_{{1},…,{1}} = ℤ[X] (discrete), so Spa(ℤ[T], ℤ[T]) → Spa(ℤ, ℤ) is of finite type (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-type-morphism-classes), and Spa(ℤ[T], ℤ[T]) is an adic space (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/discrete-huber-pair-sheafy); AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-products-existence (a) gives B^n_X.

Charts (a): AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-product-along-finite-type with S = Spa(ℤ, ℤ), weights M_{L,m} = {1} ∪ Lᵐ and 𝔞 = 0: since 1 is a weight and Lᵐ ⊆ B⁺, B⟨T⟩_{M_{L,m}} = B⟨T⟩ with plus ring the integral closure of B⁺⟨T⟩ for every m, so the increasing union is the single affinoid Spa(B⟨T⟩, B⁺⟨T⟩).

Plus ring: B⁺⟨T⟩ = {h ∈ B⟨T⟩ : v(h) ≤ 1 for all v ∈ Spa(B⟨T⟩, B⁺⟨T⟩)}: if a coefficient a_ν of h is not in B⁺ there is v ∈ Spa(B, B⁺) with v(a_ν) > 1 (anchor Layer 2.3, Wedhorn Proposition 7.52(1)); its Gauss extension Σ c_μ T^μ ↦ max_μ v(c_μ) is a continuous valuation bounded by 1 on B⁺⟨T⟩ with value ≥ v(a_ν) > 1 at h. The right-hand side is integrally closed; with Tau Ceti `spa_integralClosure` this shows B⁺⟨T⟩ is the integral closure of itself.

Universal property (b): morphisms Z → Spa(ℤ[T], ℤ[T]) are ring maps ℤ[T] → O_Z(Z) carrying T into O⁺_Z(Z) (Huber 1994 Proposition 2.1(ii), anchor Layer 5; ℤ[T] is complete for the discrete topology), and morphisms into a fibre product are compatible pairs.
(c) Pasting of pullback squares (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.IsPullback.paste_horiz`) and ℤ[T₁..T_m] ⊗ ℤ[T_{m+1}..T_{m+n}] = ℤ[T₁..T_{m+n}].

(d) Smoothness and Ω: AdicSpacesPartII:R0/restricted-power-series-smooth on the charts (Huber 1994's A⟨X⟩ with M_i = {1}); quasi-compact and separated on affinoid charts; noetherian type is preserved by topologically finite type maps (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/topologically-finite-type-noetherian-type); analyticity by AdicEtaleGeometry:A0/analytic-locus-restriction (π is adic on the charts because B → B⟨T⟩ is topologically of finite type).

(e) AdicSpacesPartII:R1/affine-chart-analytification: on a Tate chart Spa(B, B⁺) of the analytic X, with pseudouniformiser ϖ and E = {ϖ}, the charts of A^n ×_{Spec ℤ} Spa(B, B⁺) are Spa(B⟨ϖᵏT⟩, …) (k ≥ 1), and Spa(B⟨T⟩, B⁺⟨T⟩) is the rational subset {|Tᵢ| ≤ 1} of each of them; the identification is canonical because both sides represent Z ↦ {h ∈ O(Z)ⁿ with hᵢ ∈ O⁺(Z)} on affinoid test objects.
acceptance: Over Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p): B¹ = Spa(ℚ_p⟨T⟩, ℤ_p⟨T⟩), the closed unit disc (Scholze–Weinstein, Lecture 4: Spa ℤ[T] × Spa K = Spa K⟨T⟩).
ECD Proposition 24.4 defines B^n_Y for affinoid Y = Spa(A, A⁺) as Spa(A⟨T₁, …, Tₙ⟩, A⁺⟨T₁, …, Tₙ⟩); this construction globalises it.

Consumer instances: the closed embedding Y ↪ B^n_X of ECD 6.4(iv) over affinoid perfectoid X (AdicEtaleGeometry A3, where B^n_X is sousperfectoid by AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-rings), and Huber's relative balls in 1.6.10 and in ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology H1/H4.

nodes.title: The relative torus T^n_X ⊆ B^n_X
nodes.statement: Let X be as in AdicEtaleGeometry:A2/relative-closed-polydisc and n ≥ 0. The relative torus is the open subspace T^n_X := {|T₁ ⋯ Tₙ| ≥ 1} = {|T₁| = … = |Tₙ| = 1} of B^n_X; over an affinoid Spa(B, B⁺) ⊆ X it is the rational subset R(1/(T₁ ⋯ Tₙ)) of Spa(B⟨T⟩, B⁺⟨T⟩), with coordinate ring B⟨T₁^{±1}, …, Tₙ^{±1}⟩ and plus ring B⁺⟨T^{±1}⟩; equivalently T^n_X = X ×_{Spa ℤ} Spa(ℤ[T^{±1}], ℤ[T^{±1}]). Properties: (a) universal property — Hom_X(Z, T^n_X) ≅ ((O⁺_Z(Z))^×)ⁿ, the units of O_Z(Z) that lie in O⁺_Z(Z) with inverse in O⁺_Z(Z); (b) T^n_X → X is smooth (an open subspace of B^n_X), T^n_X ×_X X' ≅ T^n_{X'}, T^{m+n}_X ≅ T^m_X ×_X T^n_X, and T^n_X is a commutative group object over X (coordinatewise multiplication); (c) over Spa(K, K°) it is Scholze's Tⁿ = Spa(K⟨T^{±1}⟩, K°⟨T^{±1}⟩); (d) for a topologically nilpotent unit ϖ of O(X), Tᵢ ↦ 1 + ϖTᵢ identifies B^n_X with the rational subset {|Tᵢ − 1| ≤ |ϖ|} of T^n_X (Scholze 2013, proof of Lemma 5.2, with ϖ = p); (e) B¹_X is covered by T¹_X and its translate {|T − 1| = 1} (ECD, proof of Proposition 24.4). Conventions: T^n_X is the unit polyannulus, not the analytified torus (G_m^n)^{ad} (which is not quasi-compact over a field). Lean name: `AdicSpace.relativeTorus`.
hypotheses: X covered by complete stably sheafy affinoids; for (d), ϖ a topologically nilpotent unit (X analytic, locally).
proofSteps: Rational subset: R(1/(T₁⋯Tₙ)) is a rational subset of each chart (the numerator {1} generates the unit ideal), open with coordinate ring B⟨T⟩⟨1/(T₁⋯Tₙ)⟩ = B⟨T^{±1}⟩ (anchor Layer 3.1; Tau Ceti `spaLocalizationHomeomorph`); on it |T₁⋯Tₙ| ≥ 1 and |Tᵢ| ≤ 1 force |Tᵢ| = 1; the rational subsets glue to the open subspace T^n_X (anchor Layer 5.1).

Universal property (a): a morphism Z → B^n_X is (h^*Tᵢ) ∈ O⁺(Z)ⁿ (AdicEtaleGeometry:A2/relative-closed-polydisc (b)); it factors through T^n_X iff each h^*Tᵢ has |h^*Tᵢ| = 1 everywhere, iff it is a unit whose inverse is in O⁺(Z) (a function with |g| ≥ 1 at every point of an adic space is invertible, anchor Layer 3.3: stalks are local with maximal ideal the support).

(b) Open subspaces of smooth spaces are smooth (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/open-embedding-etale with R0/etale-smooth-composition); base change and products by (a); group law from (a) since units of O⁺ form a group.

(d) The map B⟨T⟩ ← B⟨T^{±1}⟩⟨(T − 1)/ϖ⟩, Tᵢ ↦ 1 + ϖTᵢ, is an isomorphism of complete pairs: (T − 1)/ϖ is power-bounded on {|T − 1| ≤ |ϖ|} and 1 + ϖT is a unit with inverse Σ(−ϖT)ᵏ in B⁺⟨T⟩ (anchor Layer 3.1 universal property of rational localisation).
(e) At a point with |T| < 1, |T − 1| = max(|T|, |1|) = 1, so every point lies in {|T| = 1} or {|T − 1| = 1}.
acceptance: Over K, T¹ = Spa(K⟨T^{±1}⟩, K°⟨T^{±1}⟩) is the unit circle {|T| = 1} of the closed disc.
Scholze 2013, Example 4.4: the tower of Tⁿ with pᵐ-th roots of the coordinates has affinoid perfectoid limit T̃ⁿ; ECD Proposition 24.4 uses the ℤ_p-torsor T̃_{ℂ_p} → T_{ℂ_p}.

nodes.title: Smooth morphisms of analytic adic spaces by local étale charts over relative balls (ECD 24.4)
nodes.statement: Let f : Y' → Y be a morphism of analytic adic spaces with Y covered by open affinoids whose rings are complete and stably sheafy, so that the relative polydiscs B^n_Y exist (AdicEtaleGeometry:A2/relative-closed-polydisc). f is locally étale over a relative ball (`AdicSpace.IsLocallyEtaleOverPolydisc f`) if every y' ∈ Y' has an open neighbourhood U, an integer n ≥ 0 and a morphism g : U → B^n_Y that is étale in the local-description sense of AdicEtaleGeometry A1 (locally an open immersion, a finite étale morphism and an open immersion; AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphisms-local-description-and-comparison), with f|_U = π ∘ g. This is the notion 'smooth' of ECD Proposition 24.4 for analytic adic spaces over Spa ℤ_p, including non-noetherian ones such as spaces étale over a perfectoid or sousperfectoid base. Conventions: the charts are local on the source and n may vary with y'; étale is A1's local description, which on locally noetherian spaces is Huber's étale (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-local-open-finite-etale-factorisation); on locally noetherian analytic spaces the class equals Huber's smooth morphisms (AdicEtaleGeometry:A2/smooth-local-ball-charts), and on general bases Huber's infinitesimal definition is not used. Lean name: `AdicSpace.IsLocallyEtaleOverPolydisc`.
hypotheses: Y analytic and covered by complete stably sheafy affinoids; Y' analytic.
Étale in the local-description sense of AdicEtaleGeometry A1.
proofSteps: Definition by the local condition; the relative polydisc is AdicEtaleGeometry:A2/relative-closed-polydisc and étaleness is AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphisms-local-description-and-comparison.

Stability under composition: if Y'' → Y' has a chart U'' → B^m_{U'} and Y' → Y has a chart U' → B^n_Y, then B^m_{U'} → B^m_{B^n_Y} = B^{m+n}_Y is the base change of an étale map, hence étale (A1), and the composite U'' → B^{m+n}_Y is étale (A1 composition), with B^{m+n}_Y ≅ B^m_Y ×_Y B^n_Y (A2/relative-closed-polydisc (c)).

Stability under base change along Y₁ → Y (with Y₁ of the same kind): charts pull back to étale maps U ×_Y Y₁ → B^n_{Y₁} (A1 base change and A2/relative-closed-polydisc (c)); the fibre products exist because étale maps are locally of finite type over the analytic base (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-products-existence).
acceptance: B^n_Y → Y and T^n_Y → Y are locally étale over a relative ball; étale morphisms are (n = 0).
ECD Proposition 24.4: a separated morphism of analytic adic spaces over Spa ℤ_p that is locally étale over a relative ball has ℓ-cohomologically smooth diamond (DiamondSixOperations S5).

nodes.title: Huber's smooth morphisms are exactly the morphisms locally étale over a relative ball (Huber 1.6.10 globalised)
nodes.statement: Let f : X → S be a morphism of locally noetherian analytic adic spaces (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space, AdicEtaleGeometry:A0/analytic-locus-restriction). Declaration: f is smooth in Huber's sense (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/smooth-morphism) iff f is locally étale over a relative ball (AdicEtaleGeometry:A2/smooth-morphism-ball-charts): every x ∈ X has an open neighbourhood U, n ≥ 0 and an étale g : U → B^n_S (AdicEtaleGeometry:A2/relative-closed-polydisc) with f|_U = π ∘ g. Moreover n equals the rank of the locally free module Ω_{X/S} at x (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/smooth-differentials-locally-free), U can be chosen inside any given neighbourhood of x, and for S = Spa(K, K°) over a complete nonarchimedean field it can be chosen to contain the closure of {x} (Scholze 2013, proof of Lemma 5.2). Composition and base change of smooth morphisms hold on both sides and correspond: AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-smooth-composition and R0's `Smooth.baseChange` on Huber's side, and the API of AdicEtaleGeometry:A2/smooth-morphism-ball-charts on the chart side. This is A2's clause 'smooth morphisms are locally étale over a relative ball' on locally noetherian carriers; the non-noetherian case of ECD 6.4(iv) is AdicEtaleGeometry A3's. nodes.title: Compatible local toric charts for smooth morphisms of smooth rigid spaces
nodes.statement: Let K be a complete nonarchimedean field (nontrivially valued, rank one) with a pseudouniformiser ϖ, and f : X → Y a smooth morphism (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/smooth-morphism) between adic spaces smooth over Spa(K, K°). Let x ∈ X, y = f(x), and let V ⊆ Y be an affinoid open containing the closure of {y} together with an étale map h : V → T^m_K (AdicEtaleGeometry:A2/relative-torus over Spa K) that is a composite of rational embeddings and finite étale maps (such V exist by AdicSpacesPartII:R0/smooth-toric-chart). Declaration: there are an affinoid open U ⊆ f⁻¹(V) containing the closure of {x} in f⁻¹(V), with d the rank of Ω_{X/Y} at x, and an étale map k : U → T^d_V = T^d_K ×_{Spa K} V over V which is a composite of rational embeddings and finite étale maps; consequently (id × h) ∘ k : U → T^d_K ×_{Spa K} T^m_K = T^{d+m}_K is étale, a composite of rational embeddings and finite étale maps, and pr ∘ (id × h) ∘ k = h ∘ f|_U for the coordinate projection pr : T^{d+m}_K → T^m_K. These are compatible local toric charts for f; they exist around every point of X, inside any given neighbourhood, and for Y = Spa K (m = 0) they are the absolute charts of AdicSpacesPartII:R0/smooth-toric-chart. Lean name: `AdicSpace.Smooth.exists_relativeToricChart`.
hypotheses: K complete, rank one; X, Y smooth over Spa(K, K°); f smooth.
V affinoid containing the closure of y with a toric chart h of the stated form.
proofSteps: Relative ball chart: f⁻¹(V) → V is smooth over the Tate affinoid V; AdicEtaleGeometry:A2/smooth-local-ball-charts (from AdicSpacesPartII:R0/smooth-local-structure) gives an open U₀ ∋ x containing the closure M of {x} in f⁻¹(V), with d = rank Ω_{X/Y} at x, and an étale g : U₀ → B^d_V.

Finite étale factorisation: B^d_V is affinoid of finite type over Spa(K, K°); with N the closure of g(x), there is a rational W ⊆ B^d_V containing N such that g⁻¹(W) → W factors as an open embedding g⁻¹(W) → Z followed by a finite étale Z → W (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-local-open-finite-etale-factorisation and R0/etale-affinoid-finite-etale-embedding, with the closure refinement used by Scholze in the proof of Lemma 5.2). Choose an open U ⊆ g⁻¹(W) containing M and rational in Z; it is then rational in g⁻¹(W) and affinoid (a rational subset of a rational subset is rational, anchor Layer 2.2).

Ball into torus: embed B^d_V into T^d_V as the rational subset {|Tᵢ − 1| ≤ |ϖ|} (AdicEtaleGeometry:A2/relative-torus (d)); then k : U → T^d_V is the composite of the rational embedding U ⊆ Z, the finite étale Z → W and the rational embeddings W ⊆ B^d_V ⊆ T^d_V.

Product with h: id × h : T^d_K ×_{Spa K} V → T^d_K ×_{Spa K} T^m_K is the base change of h along T^d_K → Spa K; base changes of rational embeddings are rational embeddings (AdicEtaleGeometry:A0/rational-pullback-comparison) and of finite étale maps are finite étale (AdicEtaleGeometry:A0/finite-etale-pullback-comparison, strongly noetherian case), so (id × h) ∘ k is a composite of rational embeddings and finite étale maps, hence étale (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-smooth-composition, R0/open-embedding-etale).
Compatibility with f: the projection T^d_V → V composed with k is f|_U by construction of g, and projections of fibre products commute with id × h.
acceptance: For the coordinate projection X = Tⁿ_K → Y = T^{n−d}_K, V = Y and h = id, the chart k is the identity: this is the reduction step of Scholze 2013, Proposition 8.5.
For f = π : B¹_V → V the chart is B¹_V ≅ {|T − 1| ≤ |ϖ|} ⊆ T¹_V.

nodes.title: Dimension, pure dimension and relative dimension of adic spaces (Huber 1.8.1)
nodes.statement: Let X be an adic space (anchor Layer 5); its underlying space is locally spectral, hence sober and T0. The dimension of X is dim X := topologicalKrullDim |X| ∈ ℕ∞ ∪ {⊥} (Mathlib `topologicalKrullDim`: the supremum of the lengths of chains of irreducible closed subsets), which is the supremum of the lengths d of chains of specializations x₀ ≻ x₁ ≻ ⋯ ≻ x_d of pairwise distinct points of X (Huber 1996, Definition 1.8.1, as stated in Zavyalov, Definition 3.1); dim ∅ = ⊥. X is of pure dimension d if every nonempty open subset of X has dimension d. For a morphism f : X → Y of analytic adic spaces, the relative dimension is dim f := sup_{y ∈ Y} dim f⁻¹(y), where f⁻¹(y) ⊆ X carries the subspace topology, and f is of relative pure dimension d if every nonempty fibre f⁻¹(y) is of pure dimension d. Conventions: the dimension is that of the topological space, not the Krull dimension of a ring of functions — Spa(K, K⁺) for a complete rank-one field K and a valuation ring K⁺ ⊆ K° of rank r has dimension r − 1 while K has Krull dimension 0; the fibre is the subspace f⁻¹(y), and its comparison with the adic fibre over rank-one points is AdicEtaleGeometry:A2/relative-dimension-rank-one-fibres. This topological relative dimension is distinct from R0's rank of Ω_{X/Y} (API `AdicSpace.Smooth.relativeDimension`); they agree for smooth morphisms by AdicEtaleGeometry:A2/smooth-pure-relative-dimension. Lean name: `AdicSpace.dim`.
hypotheses: X an adic space; for dim f, f a morphism of analytic adic spaces.
proofSteps: dim X is Mathlib's `topologicalKrullDim` of the underlying space; for a sober T0 space, irreducible closed subsets are the closures of unique points (Mathlib `QuasiSober`, `genericPoint`), and Z ⊊ Z' for irreducible closed sets iff the generic point of Z is a proper specialization of that of Z', so chains of irreducible closed subsets correspond to chains of specializations of distinct points (Huber's definition).
Invariance and monotonicity from Mathlib: `IsHomeomorph.topologicalKrullDim_eq` and `Topology.IsInducing.topologicalKrullDim_le` (subspaces, in particular open subspaces and fibres).
Spa(K, K⁺): its points are the valuation rings between K⁺ and K°, totally ordered by specialization, and there are r of them for K⁺ of rank r (Hübner §2), so the longest chain has length r − 1.
acceptance: dim Spa(K, K°) = 0; dim Spa(K⟨T⟩, K°⟨T⟩) = 1 (the Gauss point specializes to rank-two points, and no chain is longer); the closed unit polydisc of dimension n has dimension n.
ECD Lemma 21.6: dim f ≤ dim.trg f for maps of analytic adic spaces.

nodes.title: Smooth morphisms of rank-d differentials have relative pure dimension d
nodes.statement: Let S be a locally noetherian analytic adic space and f : X → S a smooth morphism (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/smooth-morphism) whose module of continuous differentials Ω_{X/S} is locally free of constant rank d (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/smooth-differentials-locally-free). Then f is of relative pure dimension d (AdicEtaleGeometry:A2/dimension-of-adic-spaces). In particular étale morphisms are of relative pure dimension 0, B^n_S → S and T^n_S → S are of relative pure dimension n, and an adic space X smooth over Spa(K, K°) with Ω_X locally free of rank d is of pure dimension d, which for a rigid space means dim O_{X,x} = d at every classical point (Zavyalov, Lemma 3.3). Lean name: `AdicSpace.Smooth.isPureRelDim`.
hypotheses: S locally noetherian analytic; f smooth with Ω_{X/S} of constant rank d.
proofSteps: Local charts: AdicEtaleGeometry:A2/smooth-local-ball-charts gives, locally on X, an étale g : U → B^d_S with f|_U = π ∘ g, d being the rank of Ω_{X/S}.
Relative pure dimension is local on X (pure dimension of a fibre is checked on an open cover of it), so it suffices to treat π ∘ g.

Zavyalov, Corollary 3.4: a composite of an étale map to D^d_S and the projection is of relative pure dimension d. proofSteps: Reduction to affinoids: X and Y are covered by finitely many affinoids with f(Uᵢ) ⊆ Vᵢ and O(Vᵢ) → O(Uᵢ) topologically of finite type, and dim f is the maximum over the pieces.

nodes.title: Relative analytification over an affinoid pair: the affine space is the union of relative polydiscs, on the same carriers
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a complete Huber pair with A a strongly noetherian Tate ring and ϖ ∈ A a pseudouniformiser, S = Spa(A, A⁺), and n ≥ 0. Let (A^n_A)^{ad/S} := A^n_A ×_{Spec A} S be the relative analytification of AdicSpacesPartII:R1/scheme-fibre-product-analytification (for A = K a field, the analytification of AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-functor). Declaration: (A^n_A)^{ad/S} is the increasing union of the rational open subspaces {|ϖᵏT₁|, …, |ϖᵏTₙ| ≤ 1} (k ≥ 1), with charts Spa(A⟨ϖᵏT⟩, A⁺⟨ϖᵏT⟩), and the relative closed polydisc B^n_S of AdicEtaleGeometry:A2/relative-closed-polydisc is canonically the rational open subspace {|T₁|, …, |Tₙ| ≤ 1} of each of them, compatibly with the coordinates Tᵢ and with base change along rational S' ⊆ S; likewise T^n_S (AdicEtaleGeometry:A2/relative-torus) is the open subspace {|Tᵢ| = 1} of (G^n_{m,A})^{ad/S}. Consequently A2's balls and tori are open subspaces of analytifications, and the comparisons of R1 for analytified morphisms (separatedness and properness, AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-separated-proper; étale and smooth, R1/analytification-reflects-etale-smooth; continuous differentials, R1/analytic-kahler-differentials) apply to them on the same carriers; for X smooth of finite type over A, étale charts U → A^n_A analytify to étale charts U^{ad} → (A^n_A)^{ad}, whose restrictions over B^n_S are ball charts in the sense of AdicEtaleGeometry:A2/smooth-local-ball-charts. The étale sites compare through the morphism of sites X^{ad}_ét → X_ét of AdicSpacesPartII:R4/analytification-etale-site. Lean name: `AdicSpace.relativePolydiscIsoAnalyticAffineSpaceChart`.
hypotheses: A strongly noetherian Tate (the hypothesis of R1's relative analytification at an affinoid chart); ϖ a pseudouniformiser.
proofSteps: AdicSpacesPartII:R1/affine-chart-analytification with B = A[T], C = A[T₁, …, Tₙ], E = {ϖ}: the analytification is ⋃_k Spa(A_k, A_k⁺) with A_k = A⟨ϖᵏT⟩ and A_k ⊆ A_h a rational subset {|ϖᵏTᵢ| ≤ 1} for k ≤ h.

Radius one: the rational subset {|Tᵢ| ≤ 1} of Spa(A⟨ϖT⟩, A⁺⟨ϖT⟩) has coordinate ring A⟨T⟩ with plus ring the integral closure of A⁺⟨T⟩, which is A⁺⟨T⟩ (AdicEtaleGeometry:A2/relative-closed-polydisc, plus ring step); this is the chart (a) of B^n_S. Both represent, on affinoid test objects, the morphisms with T ↦ O⁺ (R1 (iii) with the plus-ring condition, and A2/relative-closed-polydisc (b)), so the identification is canonical and compatible with coordinates; base change along rational S' by the same universal property.

nodes.title: Smooth charts form a covering of the étale site of A1
nodes.statement: Let f : X → S be a smooth morphism of locally noetherian analytic adic spaces, and X_ét the small étale site of AdicEtaleGeometry A1 (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site-and-geometric-points), which on these carriers is the site of AdicSpacesPartII:R4/etale-site-on-analytic-carriers. Declaration: the sieve on X generated by the objects U → X of X_ét that admit an étale S-morphism U → B^n_S for some n (ball charts, AdicEtaleGeometry:A2/smooth-local-ball-charts) is a covering sieve of X_ét, and such charts can be chosen with U → X open immersions. Moreover: (i) for every object u : U → X of X_ét, f ∘ u : U → S is smooth and u^*Ω_{X/S} ≅ Ω_{U/S} (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/first-fundamental-sequence with Ω_{U/X} = 0); (ii) for a morphism S' → S of such spaces, the base-change functor X_ét → (X ×_S S')_ét of AdicSpacesPartII:R4/etale-site-functoriality carries ball charts of f to ball charts of its base change; (iii) for S = Spa(K, K°), the objects with a toric chart U → Tⁿ_K that is a composite of rational embeddings and finite étale maps (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/smooth-toric-chart, AdicEtaleGeometry:A2/relative-toric-charts) also generate a covering sieve. These are the compatibilities of A2's smooth charts with A1's site. Lean name: `AdicSpace.Smooth.ballCharts_mem_etaleTopology`.
hypotheses: X, S locally noetherian and analytic; f smooth.
proofSteps: Covering: by AdicEtaleGeometry:A2/smooth-local-ball-charts every point has an open neighbourhood with a ball chart; open immersions are étale (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/open-embedding-etale) and a jointly surjective family of étale maps is a covering of X_ét (AdicSpacesPartII:R4/etale-site-on-analytic-carriers (iii)).

(i) Étale maps are smooth with Ω_{U/X} = 0 (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/infinitesimal-criteria), composites of smooth maps are smooth (R0/etale-smooth-composition), and the first fundamental sequence, left exact for u étale between smooth spaces (R0/differential-criterion-morphism), gives u^*Ω_{X/S} ≅ Ω_{U/S}.

(ii) Base change of ball charts: the chart g : U → B^n_S pulls back to U ×_S S' → B^n_{S'} (AdicEtaleGeometry:A2/relative-closed-polydisc (c)), étale by base change (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphisms-local-description-and-comparison), and the base-change functor on étale sites is AdicSpacesPartII:R4/etale-site-functoriality.
(iii) AdicEtaleGeometry:A2/relative-toric-charts with Y = Spa K: every point has a rational neighbourhood with a toric chart.
acceptance: For X = B¹_K the identity is a ball chart and the cover {|T| = 1} ∪ {|T − 1| = 1} gives toric charts (AdicEtaleGeometry:A2/relative-torus (e)).
Consumer instance: PadicHodgeTheory:P8/vector-bundles-on-analytic-etale-and-proetale-sites and the sheaf Ω¹ on X_ét are computed on such covers.

nodes.title: Huber's generic fibre of a noetherian formal scheme is the analytic locus of its adic space
nodes.statement: Let 𝔛 be a locally noetherian formal scheme (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/locally-noetherian-formal-scheme); it is of type (S) through condition (a) (AdicSpacesPartII:R2/formal-schemes-of-type-S). Let t(𝔛) be Huber's adic space of 𝔛 with π_𝔛 : t(𝔛) → 𝔛 (AdicSpacesPartII:R2/noetherian-formal-scheme-as-adic-space) and d(𝔛) with λ_𝔛 : d(𝔛) → 𝔛 Huber's generic fibre (AdicSpacesPartII:R2/generic-fibre-functor-d). Declaration: there is a canonical isomorphism d(𝔛) ≅ t(𝔛)_a onto the analytic locus of t(𝔛) (AdicEtaleGeometry:A0/analytic-locus-restriction), under which λ_𝔛 = π_𝔛 ∘ ι; it is compatible with open formal subschemes, and for an adic morphism g : 𝔛' → 𝔛 of locally noetherian formal schemes, d(g) = t(g)_a (t(g) is adic by Huber 1994, Proposition 4.2(i)). On 𝔛 = Spf A: d(Spf A) = Spa(A, A)_a, covered by the Tate charts R(G/g) for generators G of an ideal of definition. This is A2's supply of formal schemes and their generic fibres in the scope H1 uses: noetherian formal models (Huber 1996 Example 3.2.11: Spa(A, A)_a), completions of schemes along closed subschemes (AdicSpacesPartII:R2/formal-completion-and-algebraic-comparison, case (α)), and, through the same R2 nodes, the type (S)(b) models (admissible formal schemes over O_K, d(𝔛) = Spa(A[1/ϖ], B) on affines) and microbial valuation rings (d(Spf A) = Spa(K, A)). Lean name: `FormalScheme.genericFibreIsoAnalyticLocus`.
hypotheses: 𝔛 locally noetherian; morphisms adic.
proofSteps: By AdicSpacesPartII:R2/generic-fibre-functor-d (affine formula, case (a)): for A noetherian adic, d(Spf A) = t(Spf A)_a with the restriction of π; the API `FormalScheme.genericFibre_spf_of_isNoetherian` records it.

Globally: both d(𝔛) and t(𝔛)_a satisfy the universal property of Proposition 1.9.1 (R2/generic-fibre-functor-d (c)): an adic space Z with a morphism to 𝔛 satisfying (a) (λ⁻¹(I)·O_Z = O_Z) and (b) factors uniquely through t(𝔛) (R2/noetherian-formal-scheme-as-adic-space); by (a), near every point of Z some element of an ideal of definition of O_𝔛 becomes a unit, so the image points have non-open support and the factorisation lands in the open subspace t(𝔛)_a (AdicEtaleGeometry:A0/analytic-locus-restriction, universal property of open subspaces); conversely t(𝔛)_a satisfies (a) and (b), since on Spa(A, A)_a the Tate charts R(G/g) make g ∈ I invertible. Uniqueness of universal objects gives the isomorphism, compatible with open formal subschemes (both sides restrict to preimages).
Morphisms: t(g) is adic iff g is (Huber 1994 Proposition 4.2(i)); then t(g) restricts to analytic loci (A0 (d)) and d(g) = t(g)_a by the universal property.
Tate charts on d(Spf A): AdicEtaleGeometry:A0/analytic-locus-restriction (b).
acceptance: 𝔛 = Spf ℤ_p⟦T⟧: d(𝔛) = Spa(ℤ_p⟦T⟧)_a = R((p, T)/p) ∪ R((p, T)/T) is quasi-compact and contains characteristic-p points; the Berthelot generic fibre d(𝔛) ×_{Spa ℤ_p} Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p), the open unit disc over ℚ_p, is the part where |p| ≠ 0 and is not quasi-compact (Hübner, Example 8.7).

nodes.title: Pseudocoherent and finite-projective-dimension modules over a commutative ring (Kedlaya–Liu II, Definition 1.1.1)
nodes.statement: Let R be a commutative ring, M an R-module and m ∈ ℕ ∪ {∞}. M is m-pseudocoherent if it admits a resolution ⋯ → P_1 → P_0 → M → 0 by projective R-modules in which P_i is finitely generated for every i ≤ m; M is pseudocoherent if it is ∞-pseudocoherent. M is m-fpd if it admits a resolution 0 → P_m → ⋯ → P_0 → M → 0 by finitely generated projective R-modules of length at most m, and fpd if it is m-fpd for some m. Pinned conventions: m-pseudocoherence is a property of the module only (no topology); 0-pseudocoherent means finitely generated (Mathlib `Module.Finite`) and 1-pseudocoherent means finitely presented (Mathlib `Module.FinitePresentation`); for m ≥ 2 the condition is strictly stronger than finite presentation over non-coherent rings (such as perfectoid rings and their Tate algebras). This is the pseudo-coherence of SGA 6 (Stacks Project Tag 064N), not the notion of Hartshorne's Exercise I.2.11. Every fpd module is pseudocoherent. Lean names: `Module.IsPseudoCoherent R M m`, `Module.IsFPD R M m`.
hypotheses: R commutative; M an arbitrary R-module
m ranges over ℕ ∪ {∞}; the m-fpd condition asks for finitely generated projective terms and length ≤ m
proofSteps: Definition as stated. The characterisations for m = 0, 1: a module is finitely generated iff there is a surjection Rⁿ → M (Mathlib `Module.Finite`), and finitely presented iff moreover the kernel is finitely generated (Mathlib `Module.FinitePresentation`, `Module.FinitePresentation.fg_ker`), which gives the first two terms of a resolution by finite free modules.

Projective resolutions may be replaced by free ones in the degrees ≤ m (add a finitely generated complement Q to Pᵢ and Q to P_{i+1} as well, inductively), so the definition agrees with Stacks Tag 064N for modules.
acceptance: For f ∈ R a non-zero-divisor, R/fR is pseudocoherent and 1-fpd via 0 → R →(×f) R → R/fR → 0 (Kedlaya–Liu II, Remark 1.1.6).
For R = k[x, y₁, y₂, …]/(x·yᵢ : i ≥ 1), the finitely presented module R/xR is not 2-pseudocoherent (see the non-example test).

Without flatness the underived tensor product need not be pseudocoherent: in a non-coherent domain, R/(f) ⊗_R R/(g) = R/(f, g) with both factors 1-fpd can fail to be 2-pseudocoherent; the general statement concerns the derived tensor product.

nodes.title: Two-out-of-three for pseudocoherent and fpd modules (Kedlaya–Liu II, Lemma 1.1.5)
nodes.statement: Let 0 → M₁ → M → M₂ → 0 be a short exact sequence of modules over a commutative ring R and m ≥ 0. (a) If M₁ and M₂ are m-pseudocoherent, so is M. (b) If M₁ is (m−1)-pseudocoherent and M is m-pseudocoherent, then M₂ is m-pseudocoherent. (c) If M is m-pseudocoherent and M₂ is (m+1)-pseudocoherent, then M₁ is m-pseudocoherent. (d) If M₁ and M₂ are m-fpd, so is M. (e) If M₁ is m-fpd and M is (m+1)-fpd, then M₂ is (m+1)-fpd. (f) If M is m-fpd and M₂ is (m+1)-fpd, then M₁ is m-fpd. In particular, if two of M₁, M, M₂ are pseudocoherent (resp. fpd) so is the third, and the pseudocoherent (resp. fpd) modules form an exact subcategory of R-modules closed under extensions, kernels of surjections and cokernels of injections.
hypotheses: R commutative; exactness of 0 → M₁ → M → M₂ → 0
proofSteps: (a), (d): horseshoe lemma — resolutions of M₁ and M₂ by finitely generated projectives combine to a resolution of M with Pᵢ = P'ᵢ ⊕ P''ᵢ (Stacks Tag 064R, 065S).

(b), (c), (e), (f): mapping cone of a lift M₁-resolution → M-resolution, together with Schanuel's lemma to compare kernels of surjections from finitely generated projectives (Stacks Tag 064R for pseudocoherence, Tag 065S for finite projective dimension).
acceptance: For f a non-zero-divisor and M pseudocoherent: fM = ker(M → M/fM) is pseudocoherent, since M/fM = M ⊗ R/fR is pseudocoherent (Kedlaya–Liu II, Remark 1.1.6).

nodes.title: Quotients by weakly regular sequences are fpd, with free conormal module
nodes.statement: Let R be a commutative ring and f₁, …, f_r ∈ R a weakly regular sequence on R (Mathlib `RingTheory.Sequence.IsWeaklyRegular R [f₁, …, f_r]`: each fᵢ is a non-zero-divisor on R/(f₁, …, f_{i−1})). Then the Koszul complex K(f; R) is a resolution of R/(f) by finite free modules of length r; hence R/(f) is r-fpd and pseudocoherent, the ideal (f) is (r−1)-fpd (r ≥ 1), and the conormal module (f)/(f)² is a free R/(f)-module with basis the classes of f₁, …, f_r. Every weakly regular sequence stays weakly regular, with the same conclusions, after any flat base change R → R'.
hypotheses: f₁, …, f_r weakly regular on R (the quotient R/(f) is allowed to be zero)
proofSteps: Induction on r: K(f₁, …, f_r) is the mapping cone of multiplication by f_r on K(f₁, …, f_{r−1}); its homology in positive degrees vanishes because f_r is a non-zero-divisor on H₀ = R/(f₁, …, f_{r−1}) and the higher homology vanishes by induction (Stacks Tag 062F). The case r = 1 is Kedlaya–Liu II, Remark 1.1.6.
Finite projective dimension and pseudocoherence: the Koszul complex has terms ∧ⁱRʳ, finite free; A3/pseudocoherent-two-out-of-three gives the statement for the ideal (f) = ker(R → R/(f)).

Conormal module: for a weakly regular sequence the map (R/(f))ʳ → (f)/(f)², eᵢ ↦ [fᵢ], is an isomorphism (Koszul-regular implies quasi-regular, Stacks Tag 062I); flat base change preserves exactness of the Koszul complex.
acceptance: r = 1: R/fR is 1-fpd for f a non-zero-divisor (Kedlaya–Liu II, Remark 1.1.6).
For a complete Tate ring C, the variables u₁, …, u_N are weakly regular on C⟨u₁, …, u_N⟩, so C = C⟨u⟩/(u) is N-fpd over C⟨u⟩ (used by A3/fs-iv-4-13-regular-sequence).

nodes.title: Natural topology and strictness for finitely generated modules over a complete Tate ring (Kedlaya–Liu II, §1.2)
nodes.statement: Let A be a complete Hausdorff Tate ring (Tau Ceti `IsTateRing`; a pseudouniformiser makes A metrizable, i.e. Kedlaya–Liu's open mapping ring) and M a finitely generated A-module. (a) The natural topology on M — the quotient topology of any surjection Aⁿ → M — is Mathlib's `moduleTopology A M`; it does not depend on the surjection, and every A-linear map from M to a topological A-module is continuous. (b) Open mapping: every continuous surjective A-linear map between complete metrizable topological A-modules is strict (open onto its image); a continuous A-linear map with closed image between complete metrizable modules is strict (Tau Ceti `IsTateRing.isOpenMap`, `IsTateRing.isStrictMap_of_isClosed_range`). (c) If M is Hausdorff for its natural topology then it is complete, and for every exact sequence 0 → K → F → M → 0 with F finite free, K is closed in F. (d) If M is complete for its natural topology and N ⊆ M is a finitely generated submodule, then N is closed in M and complete for its natural topology (Kedlaya–Liu II, Corollary 1.2.11). (e) Finite projective A-modules are complete for their natural topology. (f) A strict exact complex of complete metrizable modules stays strict exact after completion (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/strict-complex-completion-exact). Strictly m-pseudocoherent modules (A3/stably-pseudocoherent-module) are the m-pseudocoherent modules satisfying (c)'s Hausdorff condition.
hypotheses: A complete Hausdorff Tate ring; modules finitely generated for (a), (c)–(e)
for (b), source and target complete metrizable topological A-modules, the source nonarchimedean
proofSteps: (a) Natural topology independence: Kedlaya–Liu II, Definition 1.2.2 and the argument of KL15 Lemma 2.2.6; Mathlib `IsModuleTopology` characterises it and gives continuity of linear maps out of M (`IsModuleTopology.continuous_of_linearMap`).
(b) Tau Ceti `IsTateRing.isOpenMap` (open mapping theorem over a Tate ring, Henkel) and `IsTateRing.isStrictMap_of_isClosed_range`; this is Kedlaya–Liu II, Theorem 1.2.9.
(c) Quotient of a complete metrizable group by a closed subgroup is complete; Hausdorff iff K closed (Kedlaya–Liu II, Remark 1.2.3; Tau Ceti `completeSpace_moduleTopology`).

(d) Kedlaya–Liu's matrix argument: choose generators v of the closure N̂ and w of N with w = Av, A − 1 topologically nilpotent, so A is invertible and N̂ ⊆ N; Tau Ceti `isClosed_of_module_finite_topologicalClosure` gives the same conclusion once the closure is known to be finitely generated.
(e) A finite projective module is a direct summand of a finite free module, hence closed in it by (c).
(f) is AdicSpacesPartII:R0/strict-complex-completion-exact, cited.
acceptance: For A = ℚ_p⟨T⟩ (noetherian), every submodule of a finite module is closed (Tau Ceti `isClosed_of_isNoetherian`); for a non-noetherian perfectoid A a principal ideal fA with f a non-zero-divisor need not be closed (Kedlaya–Liu II, Definition 1.2.13), so (d) cannot be strengthened to arbitrary submodules.
