nodes.title: Strictly and stably pseudocoherent modules over a complete Tate Huber pair (Kedlaya–Liu II, Definitions 1.2.13 and 2.4.1)
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a complete Tate Huber pair (Kedlaya–Liu's adic Banach ring: A complete Hausdorff with a pseudouniformiser ϖ, A⁺ a ring of integral elements). An A-module M is strictly m-pseudocoherent (resp. strictly m-fpd) if it is m-pseudocoherent (resp. m-fpd) (A3/pseudocoherent-module) and complete — in particular Hausdorff — for its natural topology (A3/natural-topology-strict-exactness). M is stably m-pseudocoherent (resp. stably m-fpd) if it is m-pseudocoherent (resp. m-fpd) and for every rational localisation (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) — B = A⟨T/s⟩ the completed localisation at a rational subset R(T/s) ⊆ Spa(A, A⁺) (anchor Layer 3; Tau Ceti `PairOfDefinition.completionLocalization`) — the algebraic tensor product M ⊗_A B is complete for its natural topology as a B-module. 'Stably pseudocoherent' means stably ∞-pseudocoherent. Pinned conventions: tensor products are algebraic, and the definition asks that they already be complete (no completed tensor product is formed); the identity localisation is included, so stably implies strictly; the plus ring enters only through the set of rational subsets; no sheafiness is assumed in the definition. Lean names: `Huber.IsStrictlyPseudoCoherent`, `Huber.IsStablyPseudoCoherent`, `Huber.IsStablyFPD`.
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) complete Tate Huber pair
m ∈ ℕ ∪ {∞}; the natural topology is that of A3/natural-topology-strict-exactness
proofSteps: Definition as stated; the natural topology of M ⊗_A B is the B-module topology (independent of the presentation, A3/natural-topology-strict-exactness).
Stability under base change and extensions needs sheafiness and is proved in A3/rational-localisation-pseudoflat (base change) and A3/pseudocoherent-kiehl-gluing (exactness).
acceptance: Every finite projective A-module is stably pseudocoherent and stably 0-fpd.
Over a strongly noetherian Tate ring every finite module is stably pseudocoherent (Kedlaya–Liu II, remark after Definition 2.4.1).
Kedlaya–Liu II, Example 2.4.2: a quotient A/fA that is strictly but not stably pseudocoherent.

nodes.title: Pseudoflat modules over a complete Tate Huber pair (Kedlaya–Liu II, Definition 2.4.4)
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a complete Tate Huber pair and m ∈ ℕ ∪ {∞}. A topological A-module B is m-pseudoflat if Tor₁^A(P, B) = 0 for every stably m-pseudocoherent A-module P (A3/stably-pseudocoherent-module); pseudoflat means ∞-pseudoflat. Equivalent forms (Kedlaya–Liu II, Remark 2.4.5): Tor₁^A(M, B) = 0 for every strictly m-pseudocoherent M implies m-pseudoflatness; and m-pseudoflatness is equivalent to injectivity of M ⊗_A B → N ⊗_A B for every short exact sequence 0 → M → N → P → 0 with N finite projective and P stably m-pseudocoherent. A complete metrizable A-module B is pro-projective if it carries a filtered family of continuous A-linear projectors πₖ with finite projective images and πₖ(v) → v for all v (Kedlaya–Liu II, Definition 2.4.6). Pinned conventions: Tor is algebraic; only Tor₁ is required (higher Tor need not vanish); 2-pseudoflat implies m-pseudoflat for all m ≥ 2, in particular pseudoflat. Lean names: `Huber.IsPseudoFlat A B m`, `Huber.IsProProjective A B`.
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) complete Tate Huber pair; B a topological A-module (for rational localisations, an A-algebra)
proofSteps: Definition as stated; the equivalences are Kedlaya–Liu II, Remark 2.4.5, from the long exact Tor sequence of 0 → M → N → P → 0.
acceptance: Flat modules are pseudoflat; A⟨T⟩ and A⟨T^{±1}⟩ are pro-projective, hence 2-pseudoflat (A3/restricted-power-series-pro-projective).

nodes.title: Restricted power series and Laurent series are pro-projective; M ⊗_A A⟨T⟩ = M⟨T⟩ (Kedlaya–Liu II, Lemma 2.4.7, Corollaries 2.4.8–2.4.9)
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a complete Tate Huber pair. (a) A⟨T⟩ (Tau Ceti `restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion 1 A`) and A⟨T^{±1}⟩ (restricted Laurent series Σ_{n∈ℤ} aₙTⁿ, aₙ → 0 as |n| → ∞) are pro-projective A-modules (truncation projectors), and pro-projectivity is stable under completed base change. (b) For B pro-projective and M strictly 2-pseudocoherent, M ⊗_A B is complete for its natural topology and Tor₁^A(M, B) = 0; hence every pro-projective module is 2-pseudoflat (A3/pseudoflat-module). (c) For M finitely generated (resp. finitely presented) and complete, the natural maps M ⊗_A A⟨T⟩ → M⟨T⟩ and M ⊗_A A⟨T^{±1}⟩ → M⟨T^{±1}⟩ onto the modules of null sequences are surjective (resp. bijective).
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) complete Tate; in (b) M strictly 2-pseudocoherent; in (c) M complete for its natural topology
proofSteps: (a) πₖ(Σ aₙTⁿ) = Σ_{|n|≤k} aₙTⁿ: continuous projectors with finite free images, converging pointwise.

(b) Kedlaya–Liu's diagram: for 0 → N → Aⁿ → M → 0, compare N ⊗ B → Aⁿ ⊗ B → M ⊗ B → 0 with the completed row 0 → N ⊗̂ B → Aⁿ ⊗̂ B → M ⊗̂ B → 0 (exact because B is pro-projective); the middle map is bijective and the left one surjective since N is finitely generated (A3/natural-topology-strict-exactness (d)); so M ⊗ B = M ⊗̂ B is complete. As M is 2-pseudocoherent, N is finitely presented and the same argument for N gives injectivity on the left, i.e. Tor₁ = 0.
(c) read off from the proof of (b).

nodes.title: Strictness of multiplication by T − f and 1 − fT on Tate algebras over a sheafy pair (Kedlaya–Liu II, Lemma 2.4.10)
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a sheafy complete Tate Huber pair (its structure presheaf on rational subsets is a sheaf; anchor Layers 3–4) and f ∈ A. Let U₁ = {v(f) ≤ 1}, U₂ = {v(f) ≥ 1} be the simple Laurent covering of Spa(A, A⁺) with rational localisations B₁, B₂, B₁₂. Then multiplication by T − f and by 1 − fT are strict injections on A⟨T⟩ and on A⟨T^{±1}⟩ (injective, with closed image, homeomorphisms onto the image). Consequently the ideals (T − f)A⟨T⟩ and (1 − fT)A⟨T⟩ are closed and B₁ = A⟨T⟩/(T − f), B₂ = A⟨T⟩/(1 − fT), B₁₂ = A⟨T^{±1}⟩/(T − f), with no closure needed.
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) complete Tate and sheafy
f ∈ A arbitrary (not assumed power-bounded)
proofSteps: Reduce to A⟨T^{±1}⟩ (A⟨T⟩ → A⟨T^{±1}⟩ is a strict inclusion) and to 1 − fT (T − f = T(1 − fT^{−1})).

Sheafiness gives exactness of 0 → A → B₁ ⊕ B₂ → B₁₂ (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/sheafy-cech-acyclicity) and, by pro-projectivity (A3/restricted-power-series-pro-projective (a)) and the open mapping theorem (A3/natural-topology-strict-exactness (b)), a strict inclusion A⟨T^{±1}⟩ → B₁⟨T^{±1}⟩ ⊕ B₂⟨T^{±1}⟩; so it suffices to treat B₁ and B₂.

On B₁ the element f is power-bounded and 1 − fT is invertible in the Banach ring R of Laurent series bounded as n → ∞ and null as n → −∞, with inverse Σ fⁿTⁿ, so multiplication by it is a homeomorphism of B₁⟨T^{±1}⟩ onto its image; on B₂ write 1 − fT = −fT(1 − f^{−1}T^{−1}) with f^{−1} power-bounded. Injectivity on M⟨T⟩ in general is Kedlaya–Liu II, Remark 1.2.8.

Identification with the rational localisations: B₁ = A⟨T⟩/closure(T − f) and B₂ = A⟨T⟩/closure(1 − fT) (Kedlaya–Liu I, Lemma 2.4.13(a); Tau Ceti `PairOfDefinition.rationalEvalHom_surjective`), and the closures are not needed by the first part.
acceptance: For A = ℚ_p⟨X⟩ and f = X/p: B₁ = ℚ_p⟨X, T⟩/(T − X/p) = ℚ_p⟨X/p⟩.

nodes.title: The three rational localisations of a simple Laurent covering are 2-pseudoflat (Kedlaya–Liu II, Lemmas 2.4.12–2.4.13)
nodes.statement: In the situation of A3/simple-laurent-strict-multiplication ((A, A⁺) sheafy complete Tate, f ∈ A), the maps A → B₂, A → B₁ and A → B₁₂ are 2-pseudoflat (A3/pseudoflat-module). Equivalently: for every exact 0 → M → N → P → 0 with N finite projective and P stably 2-pseudocoherent, the sequences 0 → M ⊗ Bᵢ → N ⊗ Bᵢ → P ⊗ Bᵢ → 0 are exact, and 0 → P → P ⊗ (B₁ ⊕ B₂) → P ⊗ B₁₂ → 0 is exact.
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) sheafy complete Tate; f ∈ A
proofSteps: A → B₂: in the 3 × 3 diagram with rows M ⊗ A⟨T⟩ → N ⊗ A⟨T⟩ → P ⊗ A⟨T⟩ (exact by pro-projectivity, A3/restricted-power-series-pro-projective), columns given by multiplication by 1 − fT (injective on M⟨T⟩ by Kedlaya–Liu II Remark 1.2.8 and identified with M ⊗ A⟨T⟩ by Corollary 2.4.9) with cokernels M ⊗ B₂ (A3/simple-laurent-strict-multiplication), the snake lemma gives injectivity of M ⊗ B₂ → N ⊗ B₂.
B₂ → B₁₂ is 2-pseudoflat by the same argument with f replaced by its inverse in B₂; composing (A3/pseudoflat-module, composition), A → B₁₂ is 2-pseudoflat.

A → B₁: diagram chase in the 3 × 3 diagram whose columns are 0 → X → X ⊗ (B₁ ⊕ B₂) → X ⊗ B₁₂ → 0 for X = M, N, P (exact for N by the glueing square, AdicSpacesPartII:R3/simple-laurent-glueing-square, and for P, M by what precedes); this circumvents the missing direct argument for T − f noted by Kedlaya–Liu.

nodes.title: Reduction of properties of rational inclusions to simple Laurent pieces (Kedlaya–Liu I, Proposition 2.4.24)
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a complete Tate Huber pair and P a property of inclusions V ⊆ U of rational subsets of Spa(A, A⁺) such that (a) P is transitive: P(V ⊆ U) and P(W ⊆ V) imply P(W ⊆ U); (b) P holds for every inclusion V ⊆ U that is a member of a simple Laurent covering of U, i.e. V = {v ∈ U : v(h) ≤ 1} or V = {v ∈ U : v(h) ≥ 1} for some h ∈ O(U). Then P holds for every inclusion of rational subsets.
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) complete Tate (a topologically nilpotent unit z is used)
P transitive and true on simple Laurent pieces
proofSteps: Write U = Spa(B, B⁺) and V = U(f₁, …, fₙ/g). Since g is a unit on V with power-bounded inverse up to a power of z (V rational, O(V) Tate), V ⊆ V₀ := {v ∈ U : v(g z^{−m}) ≥ 1} for m large; V₀ is a simple Laurent piece of U.
Define Vᵢ := {v ∈ V_{i−1} : v(fᵢ g^{−1}) ≤ 1} for i = 1, …, n (g is a unit on V₀); each Vᵢ ⊆ V_{i−1} is a simple Laurent piece and Vₙ = V. Transitivity along V = Vₙ ⊆ ⋯ ⊆ V₀ ⊆ U gives P(V ⊆ U).
The printed proof says V₀ 'is contained in V'; the chain it then uses requires V ⊆ V₀ (recorded in sourceIssues).
acceptance: P(V ⊆ U) := 'O(U) → O(V) is 2-pseudoflat' satisfies (a) and (b) (A3/rational-localisation-pseudoflat).

nodes.title: Rational localisations of sheafy Tate pairs are 2-pseudoflat (Kedlaya–Liu II, Theorem 2.4.15)
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a sheafy complete Tate Huber pair and (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) a rational localisation. Then A → B is 2-pseudoflat (A3/pseudoflat-module). Consequently, for m ∈ {2, ∞} and every stably m-pseudocoherent A-module M, M ⊗_A B is a stably m-pseudocoherent B-module, and M ↦ M ⊗_A B is exact on short exact sequences of stably m-pseudocoherent A-modules.
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) complete Tate and sheafy (so every rational localisation is again sheafy)
m ∈ {2, ∞} for the consequence
proofSteps: Apply A3/rational-inclusion-reduction to P(V ⊆ U) := 'O(U) → O(V) is 2-pseudoflat': transitivity is the composition property of A3/pseudoflat-module (Kedlaya–Liu II, Remark 2.4.5), and simple Laurent pieces are A3/simple-laurent-pseudoflat.

Consequence: for 0 → M' → N → M → 0 with N finite projective, M stably m-pseudocoherent: M' is stably (m−1)-pseudocoherent (A3/pseudocoherent-two-out-of-three plus completeness of kernels), the sequence stays exact after ⊗B, and completeness of (M ⊗ B) ⊗_B C = M ⊗_A C for rational C over B holds by definition; for m ∈ {2, ∞} the (m−1)-pseudocoherence of M' ⊗ B follows inductively (1-pseudocoherence is preserved by any base change).
acceptance: For A strongly noetherian the statement reduces to flatness of rational localisations (Kedlaya–Liu II, Lemma 2.2.6); for A perfectoid, rational localisations are in general not known to be flat (Kedlaya–Liu II, Remark 2.2.8) and this theorem is the substitute.

nodes.title: Tate acyclicity for stably pseudocoherent modules (Kedlaya–Liu II, Theorem 2.5.1)
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a sheafy complete Tate Huber pair, X = Spa(A, A⁺), and M a stably pseudocoherent A-module. Let M̃ be the presheaf on the rational subsets of X with M̃(U) := M ⊗_A O_X(U) (extended to open subsets by limits over rational subsets). Then for every rational U = Spa(B, B⁺) ⊆ X and every finite covering 𝒱 of U by rational subsets, the augmented alternating Čech complex 0 → M ⊗_A B → ∏ M ⊗_A O(V_{i₀}) → ∏ M ⊗_A O(V_{i₀i₁}) → ⋯ is exact. In particular M̃ is a sheaf on the rational subsets with M̃(U) = M ⊗_A B, and Ȟⁱ(U, M̃; 𝒱) = 0 for i > 0.
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) sheafy complete Tate
M stably pseudocoherent

proofSteps: By A3/rational-localisation-pseudoflat, M ⊗_A B is stably pseudocoherent over B, so it suffices to treat U = X.

nodes.title: Finite projective dimension is local on rational coverings for stably pseudocoherent modules (Kedlaya–Liu II, Corollary 2.5.2)
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a sheafy complete Tate Huber pair and M a stably pseudocoherent A-module. If there are m ≥ 0 and a rational covering 𝒱 of Spa(A, A⁺) such that M ⊗_A O(V) is an m-fpd O(V)-module for every V ∈ 𝒱, then M is m-fpd. In particular (m = 0), if every M ⊗_A O(V) is finite projective, M is finite projective.
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) sheafy complete Tate; M stably pseudocoherent; 𝒱 a finite rational covering
proofSteps: m = 0: M̃ is then a vector bundle on Spa(A, A⁺) (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/locally-free-sheaf), so its global sections are finite projective by Kiehl gluing on sheafy Tate affinoids (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/sheafy-tate-acyclicity-and-kiehl-gluing), and they equal M by A3/pseudocoherent-tate-acyclicity.

nodes.title: Pseudocoherent and fpd sheaves of O-modules on adic spaces (Kedlaya–Liu II, Definition 2.5.3)
nodes.statement: Let X be an adic space (anchor Layer 5) covered by affinoid opens Spa(B, B⁺) with (B, B⁺) a sheafy complete Tate Huber pair. A sheaf F of O_X-modules is pseudocoherent (resp. fpd) if X has a covering by such affinoid opens U = Spa(B, B⁺) with F|_U ≅ M̃ for a stably pseudocoherent (resp. stably fpd) B-module M (A3/stably-pseudocoherent-module, A3/pseudocoherent-tate-acyclicity). By A3/rational-localisation-pseudoflat the condition passes to open subspaces and to rational subsets of the chosen affinoids. Pinned conventions: F is a sheaf of O_X-modules on the analytic (not étale) topology; the modules are stably, not merely strictly, pseudocoherent; in AdicEtaleGeometry:A3 the spaces X are rational subsets of relative balls B^N_X over affinoid perfectoid X, which are sousperfectoid (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-rings) and hence sheafy. Lean names: `AdicSpace.IsPseudoCoherentSheaf F`, `AdicSpace.IsFPDSheaf F`.

F a sheaf of O_X-modules

nodes.title: Effective descent of stably pseudocoherent modules along a simple Laurent covering (Kedlaya–Liu II, Lemma 2.5.4)
nodes.statement: In the situation of A3/simple-laurent-strict-multiplication ((A, A⁺) sheafy complete Tate, f ∈ A, simple Laurent covering U₁, U₂ with rings B₁, B₂, B₁₂), the map A → B₁ ⊕ B₂ is an effective descent morphism for stably pseudocoherent modules and for stably fpd modules: every descent datum (M₁, M₂, ψ) with Mᵢ stably pseudocoherent over Bᵢ and ψ: M₁ ⊗ B₁₂ ≅ M₂ ⊗ B₁₂ comes from the stably pseudocoherent A-module M := ker(M₁ ⊕ M₂ → M₁₂), and M ⊗_A Bᵢ ≅ Mᵢ.
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) sheafy complete Tate; f ∈ A
M₁, M₂ stably pseudocoherent (resp. stably fpd) over B₁, B₂
proofSteps: The descent datum defines a sheaf F on X = Spa(A, A⁺), pseudocoherent on U₁, U₂ (A3/pseudocoherent-tate-acyclicity). F is finitely generated by the glueing-square argument (Kedlaya–Liu I, Lemma 2.7.4 = AdicSpacesPartII:R3/glueing-square-finite-surjectivity, on the glueing square of AdicSpacesPartII:R3/simple-laurent-glueing-square), and Ȟ¹({U₁, U₂}, F) = coker(F(U₁) ⊕ F(U₂) → F(U₁₂)) = 0 by the same lemma.

Choose a surjection E → F from a finite free O_X-module; its kernel G is again the sheaf of a descent datum of stably pseudocoherent modules (A3/rational-localisation-pseudoflat, A3/pseudocoherent-two-out-of-three), so 0 → G(X) → E(X) → F(X) → 0 is exact; induction on m shows F(X) is m-pseudocoherent for all m, and it is complete as a closed submodule of F(U₁) ⊕ F(U₂).

Comparison: five lemma in the diagram G(X) ⊗ Bᵢ → E(X) ⊗ Bᵢ → F(X) ⊗ Bᵢ over G(Uᵢ) → E(Uᵢ) → F(Uᵢ) gives F(X) ⊗ Bᵢ ≅ F(Uᵢ); the same diagram over any rational Y gives stability. The fpd case follows from A3/fpd-local-to-global.
acceptance: Finite projective descent data: recovers AdicSpacesPartII:R3/glueing-square-finite-projective-descent on the simple Laurent glueing square.

nodes.title: Kiehl gluing for pseudocoherent sheaves on sheafy Tate affinoids (Kedlaya–Liu II, Theorem 2.5.5 and Corollary 2.5.6)
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a sheafy complete Tate Huber pair and X = Spa(A, A⁺). (a) The global sections functor F ↦ F(X) is an exact equivalence from pseudocoherent (resp. fpd) sheaves of O_X-modules (A3/pseudocoherent-sheaf) to stably pseudocoherent (resp. stably fpd) A-modules, with quasi-inverse M ↦ M̃; in particular every short exact sequence 0 → F' → F → F'' → 0 of pseudocoherent sheaves gives an exact sequence 0 → F'(X) → F(X) → F''(X) → 0 of stably pseudocoherent modules. (b) For every morphism of sheafy complete Tate pairs (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) inducing an open immersion Spa(B, B⁺) → Spa(A, A⁺) (for instance a rational localisation), base extension is an exact functor from stably pseudocoherent (resp. stably fpd) A-modules to stably pseudocoherent (resp. stably fpd) B-modules, M ⊗_A B = M̃(Spa(B, B⁺)), and A → B is pseudoflat.
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) complete Tate and sheafy (in AdicEtaleGeometry:A3: sousperfectoid, for example a rational subset of a relative ball over an affinoid perfectoid space)
proofSteps: (a) Apply Kedlaya–Liu I, Proposition 2.4.20 (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/rational-covering-reduction) to the property 'B → ∏ Cᵢ is an effective descent morphism for stably pseudocoherent modules with exact descent functor' of rational coverings {B → Cᵢ} of rational subsets: locality is A3/pseudocoherent-tate-acyclicity, transitivity is formal, simple Laurent coverings are A3/simple-laurent-pseudocoherent-descent. Exactness of global sections also follows from A3/pseudocoherent-tate-acyclicity.

(b) For 0 → M → N → P → 0 with N finite projective and P stably pseudocoherent, compare M ⊗ B → N ⊗ B → P ⊗ B → 0 with the exact sequence of sections over Y = Spa(B, B⁺) of 0 → M̃ → Ñ → P̃ → 0; the five lemma, applied twice, gives P ⊗_A B ≅ P̃(Y), which is stably pseudocoherent by (a) for Y.
acceptance: (A, A⁺) strongly noetherian Tate: pseudocoherent sheaves are the coherent sheaves and (a) is Kiehl's theorem, AdicSpacesPartII:R3/tate-kiehl-affinoid; finite projective modules: AdicSpacesPartII:R3/sheafy-tate-acyclicity-and-kiehl-gluing.

Application (Fargues–Scholze IV.4.19, char-p form): the ideal sheaf of an affinoid étale Y in a relative ball over an affinoid perfectoid space corresponds to a stably pseudocoherent ideal of A⟨T⟩ (A3/affinoid-etale-zariski-closed-embedding).

nodes.title: Multivariable Newton–Hensel lemma for restricted power series over a complete Tate ring
nodes.statement: Let C be a complete Hausdorff Tate ring with a ring of definition C₀ containing a pseudouniformiser ϖ (Tau Ceti `PairOfDefinition`, `IsPseudoUniformizer`), so that C₀ is ϖ-adically complete and C = C₀[1/ϖ]. Let F = (F₁, …, F_N) with Fᵢ ∈ C₀⟨T₁, …, T_N⟩ (restricted power series with coefficients in C₀, i.e. the ϖ-adic completion of C₀[T]), let t ∈ C₀^N, let J(t) := (∂Fᵢ/∂T_j(t))ᵢⱼ ∈ M_N(C₀), and suppose there are k ≥ 0 and M ∈ M_N(C₀) with M·J(t) = J(t)·M = ϖᵏ·1 and F(t) ∈ ϖ^{2k+1}C₀^N. Then: (a) there is exactly one t* ∈ t + ϖ^{k+1}C₀^N with F(t*) = 0; (b) t* − t ∈ ϖ^{−k}·F(t)·C₀ (componentwise bound |t* − t| ≤ |ϖ|^{−k}|F(t)|), and J(t*) is invertible with ϖᵏJ(t*)^{−1} ∈ M_N(C₀); (c) (functoriality) for every continuous ring homomorphism φ: C → C' of such rings with φ(C₀) ⊆ C'₀, φ(t*) is the solution attached to (φF, φt); (d) (parameters) if F and t depend on further variables — F ∈ C₀⟨S, T⟩^N, t ∈ C₀⟨S⟩^N with the hypotheses in C₀⟨S⟩ — then t* ∈ C₀⟨S⟩^N. Partial derivatives are the termwise ones (Mathlib `MvPowerSeries.pderiv`, which preserves restricted series).
hypotheses: C complete Hausdorff Tate; C₀ a ring of definition containing the pseudouniformiser ϖ
F with coefficients in C₀; t ∈ C₀^N; J(t) invertible with ϖᵏJ(t)^{−1} integral; F(t) ∈ ϖ^{2k+1}C₀^N
proofSteps: Taylor expansion without denominators: F(t + h) = F(t) + J(t)h + Q(t, h) with Q having coefficients in C₀ and lying in the ideal (h)² — the Hasse–Taylor coefficients of a polynomial with coefficients in C₀ lie in C₀ (Mathlib `Polynomial.hasseDeriv` in each variable), and the identity passes to ϖ-adic limits.

Newton iteration t_{n+1} = t_n − ϖ^{−k}M F(t_n): by induction F(t_n) ∈ ϖ^{2k+1+n'}C₀^N with n' → ∞ quadratically and t_{n+1} − t_n ∈ ϖ^{k+1+n'}C₀^N, so (t_n) converges in the ϖ-adically complete C₀^N to t* with F(t*) = 0; J(t*) ≡ J(t) modulo ϖ^{k+1}, so ϖᵏJ(t*)^{−1} = (1 + ϖ(…))^{−1}M is integral.
Uniqueness: if F(s) = 0 with s ∈ t + ϖ^{k+1}C₀^N, then 0 = F(s) − F(t*) = J(t*)(s − t*) + O(|s − t*|²), so |s − t*| ≤ |ϖ|^{−k}|s − t*|² ≤ |ϖ||s − t*|, forcing s = t*.
(c), (d): the iteration commutes with φ and with the parameter ring C₀⟨S⟩, which is again a ring of definition of a complete Tate ring.
acceptance: N = 1, F = T² − a in C₀⟨T⟩ over C = ℚ_p (p odd), t ∈ ℤ_p with t² ≡ a mod p, J(t) = 2t a unit (k = 0): t* is the Hensel square root of a.
F = T − a (N = 1, J = 1, k = 0): t* = a for every t ∈ a + ϖC₀.

nodes.title: Small perturbations of topological generators: automorphisms of A⟨X⟩ and transport of presentations
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a complete Tate Huber pair with pseudouniformiser ϖ and A₀ ⊆ A⁺ a ring of definition containing ϖ. (a) For ε ∈ ϖ·A₀⟨X₁, …, X_n⟩^n the continuous A-algebra endomorphism θ_ε of A⟨X⟩ with θ_ε(X) = X + ε(X) is an automorphism; θ_ε and θ_ε^{−1} preserve A₀⟨X⟩ and A⁺⟨X⟩, and θ_ε^{−1} = θ_{ε'} with ε' ∈ ϖA₀⟨X⟩^n. (b) Let π: (A⟨X⟩, A⁺⟨X⟩) → (C, C⁺) be a quotient mapping of complete Huber pairs over (A, A⁺) (π surjective, C⁺ the integral closure of π(A⁺⟨X⟩); Tau Ceti `Pair.quotient`) and c' ∈ (C⁺)^n with c' − π(X) ∈ ϖ·π(A₀⟨X⟩)^n. Then π' := π ∘ θ_ε, for any lift ε ∈ ϖA₀⟨X⟩^n of c' − π(X), is the continuous A-algebra map with π'(X) = c'; π' is again a quotient mapping, π'(A₀⟨X⟩) = π(A₀⟨X⟩) and π'(A⁺⟨X⟩) = π(A⁺⟨X⟩); and ker π' = θ_ε^{−1}(ker π). (c) If ker π is the closure of (F₁, …, F_r) then ker π' is the closure of (F₁ ∘ θ_ε, …, F_r ∘ θ_ε), and det(∂(F∘θ_ε)/∂X) = (det(∂F/∂X) ∘ θ_ε)·det(1 + ∂ε/∂X), the second factor a unit of A₀⟨X⟩ congruent to 1 modulo ϖ. This is point (3) of Huber's proof of Proposition 1.7.1 ('small perturbations of topological generators define automorphisms') without the noetherian hypothesis recorded there.
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) complete Tate; A₀ ⊆ A⁺ a ring of definition containing ϖ
in (b), π a quotient mapping and c' − π(X) small in the sense stated
proofSteps: (a) θ_ε exists by the universal property of A⟨X⟩ (Tau Ceti `existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_completion_weightedRestrictedSubring`; X + ε ∈ A₀⟨X⟩^n is power-bounded). θ_ε ≡ id modulo ϖA₀⟨X⟩, so it is bijective on the ϖ-adically complete A₀⟨X⟩ (successive approximation), hence an automorphism of A⟨X⟩ = A₀⟨X⟩[1/ϖ]; alternatively its inverse is X ↦ X − ε(X*) with X* the Newton solution of A3/restricted-power-series-newton (k = 0).
(b) π ∘ θ_ε sends X to π(X) + π(ε) = c'. θ_ε is an automorphism preserving A₀⟨X⟩ and A⁺⟨X⟩, so the images and the integral closure are unchanged and ker π' = θ_ε^{−1}(ker π).
(c) θ_ε is a homeomorphism, so it carries closures of ideals to closures of the image ideals; the Jacobian identity is the chain rule for the continuous derivations ∂/∂X_j.
acceptance: X ↦ X + ϖX² is an automorphism of A⟨X⟩ (inverse X ↦ X − ϖX² + 2ϖ²X³ − ⋯); X ↦ ϖX is not (its image misses X), showing why the perturbation must be small relative to π(A₀⟨X⟩) and not merely small.

nodes.title: Standard étale presentations of complete Huber pairs over a complete Tate pair
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a complete Tate Huber pair with pseudouniformiser ϖ and X = Spa(A, A⁺). A standard étale presentation of a complete Huber pair (C, C⁺) over (A, A⁺) is a tuple (N, F, k, π) consisting of N ≥ 0, F = (F₁, …, F_N) ∈ A⁺⟨T₁, …, T_N⟩^N, k ≥ 0 and a morphism of Huber pairs π: (A⟨T⟩, A⁺⟨T⟩) → (C, C⁺) over (A, A⁺) such that (i) π is surjective, ker π is the closure of the ideal (F₁, …, F_N), and C⁺ is the integral closure of π(A⁺⟨T⟩) — so (C, C⁺) is the quotient pair A⟨T⟩/closure((F)) (Tau Ceti `Pair.quotient`); (ii) the Jacobian J_F := det(∂Fᵢ/∂T_j) ∈ A⁺⟨T⟩ (termwise partial derivatives) maps to a unit of C with ϖᵏ·π(J_F)^{−1} ∈ C⁺ (the Jacobian inverse is bounded by |ϖ|^{−k}). The associated affinoid V(F) := Spa(C, C⁺) → B^N_X is the standard étale locus. A presentation is in explicit-inverse form with exponent k' if N = N' + 1, T = (T', S) and F = (F', S·J_{F'} − ϖ^{k'}); then J_F = J_{F'}², |J_{F'}| ≥ |ϖ^{k'}| on V(F), condition (ii) holds with k = 2k', and every presentation can be put in this form (API `withInverse`). Pinned conventions: the number of equations equals the number of variables and all variables have weight 1 (the Tate case of Huber's presentations A⟨X⟩_{T₁,…,T_n}, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-presentation-perturbation); coefficients lie in A⁺ (rescaling by powers of ϖ does not change the ideal); the plus ring is always the integral closure of the image; rational subsets of B^N_X are absorbed by extra variables (A3/standard-presentation-basic-pieces); no sheafiness is part of the definition. Lean name: `Huber.StandardEtalePresentation A A⁺ C C⁺`.
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) complete Tate Huber pair; (C, C⁺) complete Huber pair over it
proofSteps: Definition as stated. The closure in (i) is needed: ideals generated by finitely many elements need not be closed over non-noetherian A (Kedlaya–Liu II, Definition 1.2.13); on tubes it is automatically closed (A3/fs-iv-4-13-regular-sequence).

Explicit-inverse form: given (N, F, k, π), adjoin S with π(S) := ϖᵏπ(J_F)^{−1} ∈ C⁺; the kernel of A⟨T, S⟩ → C is the closure of (F, S·J_F − ϖᵏ) (graph of a bounded function) and the new Jacobian is J_F·J_F.

nodes.title: Rational localisations, finite étale algebras and their composites have standard étale presentations
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a complete Tate Huber pair with pseudouniformiser ϖ. (a) For s₁, …, s_n, t ∈ A⁺ with ϖ^c ∈ {s₁, …, s_n}, the rational localisation (A⟨s/t⟩, A⟨s/t⟩⁺) of R(s/t) (Tau Ceti `completionLocalization`) has the standard étale presentation (n, (tTᵢ − sᵢ), cn, Tᵢ ↦ sᵢ/t) (A3/standard-etale-presentation). (b) If S is a finite étale A-algebra (Mathlib `Algebra.Etale A S` and `Module.Finite A S`) with its natural topology and S⁺ the integral closure of A⁺ in S (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra), then S is complete and (S, S⁺) has a standard étale presentation obtained from any presentation S = A[x₁, …, x_n]/(P₁, …, P_n) with det(∂Pᵢ/∂x_j) invertible in S (Mathlib `Algebra.Etale.iff_isStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension_zero`) by substituting xᵢ = ϖ^{−c}yᵢ with ϖ^cxᵢ ∈ S⁺ and rescaling the equations into A⁺[y]. (c) If (C, C⁺) has a standard étale presentation (N, F, k, π) over (A, A⁺) and (D, D⁺) has one (M, G, l, ρ) over (C, C⁺), then (D, D⁺) has one over (A, A⁺) with N + M variables, equations (F, G̃) for any lift G̃ ∈ A⁺⟨T, U⟩^M of ϖ^{c}G, and Jacobian J_F·J_{G̃}. (d) Consequently, if (C, C⁺) has a standard étale presentation over (A, A⁺) then so does O(V) for every rational subset V ⊆ Spa(C, C⁺), and so does every composite of rational localisations and finite étale maps.
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) complete Tate
(b): S finite étale over A as a ring, with the natural topology
(c): presentations as in A3/standard-etale-presentation
proofSteps: (a) Surjectivity of A⟨T⟩ → A⟨s/t⟩ is Tau Ceti `PairOfDefinition.rationalEvalHom_surjective`; its kernel is the closure of (tTᵢ − sᵢ) and the plus ring is the completed integral closure of the image of A⁺[T] (Kedlaya–Liu I, Lemma 2.4.13(a)); J = tⁿ, and ϖ^c/t ∈ A⟨s/t⟩⁺ because |ϖ^c| ≤ |t| on R(s/t) (Tau Ceti `mem_iff_forall_vle_one`).

(b) S is finite projective, hence complete for its natural topology (A3/natural-topology-strict-exactness (e)). The map A⟨y⟩ → S, y ↦ ϖ^c x, is surjective (its image contains A[x] = S). Let P' be the rescaled equations and C' := A⟨y⟩/closure(P'). The A-algebra map S = A[x]/(P) → C', x ↦ ϖ^{−c}ȳ, is well defined and continuous (linear maps out of the finite module S are continuous, A3/natural-topology-strict-exactness (a)); it is inverse to C' → S on the generators ȳ, so C' ≅ S. Plus rings: S⁺ = int. closure of A⁺ ⊆ int. closure of the image of A⁺⟨y⟩ ⊆ S⁺. Jacobian: det(∂P'/∂y) = unit · det(∂P/∂x)(ϖ^{−c}y).

(c) C⟨U⟩ = C ⊗̂_A A⟨U⟩ = A⟨T, U⟩/closure(F) (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-restricted-power-series (c)); all but finitely many coefficients of G lie in the open subgroup π(A⁺⟨T⟩), and ϖ^cG has all coefficients there for c ≫ 0, so a lift G̃ exists; D = A⟨T, U⟩/closure(F, G̃) since preimages of closed ideals under quotient maps are closed. The Jacobian matrix of (F, G̃) in (T, U) is block lower triangular.
(d) (a) over C, then (c).
acceptance: For (A, A⁺) = (ℚ_p⟨X⟩, ℤ_p⟨X⟩) and ϖ = p, the rational subset {|X| ≤ |p|} = R(X, p / p) has the presentation (2, (pT₁ − X, pT₂ − p), 2) with Jacobian p²; the finite étale ℚ_p⟨X⟩-algebra ℚ_p⟨X⟩[y]/(y² − 1 − pX) (p odd) has the presentation (1, (y² − 1 − pX), 0), whose Jacobian 2y is a unit.

nodes.title: Tubular neighbourhoods of standard étale loci: a nonarchimedean implicit function theorem
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a complete Tate Huber pair with pseudouniformiser ϖ such that every rational localisation of A⟨T₁, …, T_N⟩ is uniform (for instance A sousperfectoid: A⟨T⟩ and its rational localisations are then sousperfectoid, hence uniform), X = Spa(A, A⁺), R ⊆ B^N_X := Spa(A⟨T₁, …, T_N⟩, A⁺⟨T⟩) a rational subset, e = (e₁, …, e_N) ∈ O⁺(R)^N and k ≥ 0, m ≥ 2k + 1. Let Δ := det(∂eᵢ/∂T_j) ∈ O(R) (the derivations ∂/∂T_j of A⟨T⟩ extend uniquely and continuously to the rational localisation O(R)) and let W := R ∩ {|eᵢ| ≤ |ϖ^m| for all i} ∩ {|ϖᵏ| ≤ |Δ|}, a rational subset (the tube of e of radius |ϖ|^m). Put C := O(W)/closure(e·O(W)) with C⁺ the integral closure of the image of O⁺(W), and V(e) ∩ W := Spa(C, C⁺). Then: (a) there is a unique isomorphism of complete Huber pairs over (A, A⁺), Φ: (C⟨u₁, …, u_N⟩, C⁺⟨u⟩) → (O(W), O⁺(W)), such that Φ(uᵢ) = ϖ^{−m}eᵢ and Φ restricted to C is a ring section ρ of the quotient map q: O(W) → C with ρ(q(T)) − T ∈ ϖ^{m−k}O⁺(W)^N; geometrically W ≅ (V(e) ∩ W) ×_X B^N_X(|ϖ|^m) with e corresponding to ϖ^m u; (b) the same holds, with C replaced by C_{W'} := O(W')/closure(e·O(W')), for every rational subset W' ⊆ W (with R replaced by W'); (c) for every rational W' ⊆ W the ideal e·O(W') is closed, O(W')/(e) = C_{W'} = C ⊗̂_{O(W)} O(W'), and V(e) ∩ W' is the rational subset of V(e) ∩ W cut out by the same inequalities.
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) complete Tate with uniform rational localisations of A⟨T⟩ (so O⁺(W') is a ϖ-adically complete ring of definition of O(W') for every rational W'), for instance A sousperfectoid
R rational in B^N_X; e ∈ O⁺(R)^N
on W the Jacobian satisfies |Δ| ≥ |ϖᵏ| (built into W); m ≥ 2k + 1
proofSteps: Section ρ: on W, e(T) ∈ ϖ^mO⁺(W)^N (|eᵢ| ≤ |ϖ^m| pointwise and O⁺(W) = {f : |f| ≤ 1}, Tau Ceti `mem_iff_forall_vle_one`), and J(T) has inverse with ϖᵏJ^{−1} ∈ M_N(O⁺(W)) (adjugate over Δ). A3/restricted-power-series-newton in the ring of definition C₀ = O⁺(W) (bounded by uniformity) gives t* ∈ T + ϖ^{m−k}O⁺(W)^N with e(t*) = 0. The inequalities defining R hold at t* because rational subsets are unchanged by small perturbations of their data (Tau Ceti `exists_mem_nhds_forall_rationalSubset_eq_of_sub_mem`), so T ↦ t* defines a continuous map O(R) → O(W) (universal properties of A⟨T⟩ and of rational localisation: Tau Ceti `existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_completion_weightedRestrictedSubring`, `existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_of_forall_comap_mem_rationalSubset`), which kills e, hence its closure, and induces ρ: C → O(W); q∘ρ = id because Newton's iteration starting from an exact zero is constant (functoriality (c) of the Newton lemma).

Map Ψ: O(W) → C⟨u⟩: in C⟨u⟩ solve e(s) = ϖ^mu by Newton starting at the image T̄ ∈ C^N (parameters, (d) of the Newton lemma): e(T̄) − ϖ^mu = −ϖ^mu is small and J(T̄) has inverse bounded by |ϖ|^{−k}. The inequalities of W hold at s (|e(s)| = |ϖ^mu| ≤ |ϖ^m|; |Δ(s)| = |Δ(T̄)| ≥ |ϖᵏ| by closeness; R by perturbation), so T ↦ s defines Ψ.

Φ := (ρ on C, uᵢ ↦ ϖ^{−m}eᵢ) is defined by the universal property of C⟨u⟩ (eᵢ/ϖ^m ∈ O⁺(W)). Ψ∘Φ = id: on C by uniqueness of Newton solutions near T̄, on u because e(s)/ϖ^m = u. Φ∘Ψ = id: T ↦ the solution of e(x) = e(T) near t*, which is T itself by uniqueness. Both are identities on topological generators (O(W) is generated over A by T and rational coordinates determined by T, as denominators are units), hence identities.

(b) apply (a) to R := W' (its points satisfy the tube inequalities). (c) (u) is closed in C_{W'}⟨u⟩ with quotient C_{W'}; the completed tensor identification is AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-rational-localisation with R0/completed-tensor-restricted-power-series (c) for n = 0.
acceptance: N = 1, R = B¹_X, e = T − a with a ∈ A⁺, k = 0, m = 1: W = {|T − a| ≤ |ϖ|}, C = A and Φ is the translation u ↦ ϖ^{−1}(T − a).
For e with |Δ| = 1 on R (for instance Δ ≡ 1 modulo the ideal of V(e)), k = 0 and the tube {|e| ≤ |ϖ|} ∩ {|Δ − 1| ≤ |ϖ|} is a product V(e) ×_X B^N(|ϖ|).

nodes.title: Stability of standard étale presentations under perturbation (nonnoetherian replacement of Huber 1.7.2)
nodes.statement: Let (N, F, 2k, π) be a standard étale presentation of (C, C⁺) in explicit-inverse form with exponent k (A3/standard-etale-presentation) over a complete Tate pair (A, A⁺) whose Tate algebras have uniform rational localisations (as in A3/tubular-neighbourhood), and put m₀ := 4k + 2. For every G ∈ A⁺⟨T⟩^N with G − F ∈ ϖ^{m₀}A⁺⟨T⟩^N: (a) the quotient pair (C_G, C_G⁺) := A⟨T⟩/closure(G) has the standard étale presentation (N, G, 2k, π_G) (the Jacobian of G is invertible on V(G) with inverse bounded by |ϖ|^{−2k}); (b) V(G) and V(F) both lie in the tube W of F with Jacobian exponent 2k and radius |ϖ|^{4k+1} (A3/tubular-neighbourhood), and there is a unique isomorphism of complete Huber pairs α_{F,G}: (C, C⁺) → (C_G, C_G⁺) over (A, A⁺) with α_{F,G}(π(T)) − π_G(T) ∈ ϖ^{m₀−2k}(C_G⁺)^N; (c) α_{G,F} = α_{F,G}^{−1} (the comparison maps are mutually inverse on the permitted tube, no further shrinking being needed), α_{G,H}∘α_{F,G} = α_{F,H} whenever all three are defined, and α is compatible with base change along morphisms of complete Tate pairs; (d) plus rings correspond: α(C⁺) = C_G⁺. Hence Spa(C_G, C_G⁺) ≅ Spa(C, C⁺) over X, and every property of V(F) over X (étale, sousperfectoid, perfectoid) holds for V(G). If A has a noetherian ring of definition this agrees with AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-presentation-perturbation (Huber 1.7.2).
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) complete Tate with uniform rational localisations of its Tate algebras (for instance sousperfectoid)
presentation in explicit-inverse form F = (F', S·J_{F'} − ϖᵏ)
G ≡ F modulo ϖ^{m₀} coefficientwise, m₀ = 4k + 2
proofSteps: V(G) ⊆ W: at a point of V(G), |F| = |F − G| ≤ |ϖ^{m₀}|; from |S·J_{F'} − ϖᵏ| ≤ |ϖ^{m₀}| < |ϖᵏ| and |S| ≤ 1 one gets |J_{F'}| ≥ |ϖᵏ|, so |J_F| = |J_{F'}|² ≥ |ϖ^{2k}|; so V(G) lies in the tube of F with Jacobian exponent 2k and radius |ϖ|^{4k+1} (note m₀ ≥ 4k + 1 = 2·(2k) + 1). Hence C_G = O(W)/closure(G) (a rational localisation of C_G containing all of Spa(C_G) is an isomorphism, universal property of rational localisation).

Under the tube isomorphism O(W) ≅ C⟨u⟩ (A3/tubular-neighbourhood, F ↦ ϖ^{4k+1}u), G ↦ ϖ^{4k+1}u + δ(u) with δ ∈ ϖ^{m₀}C⁺⟨u⟩^N; the equation u = −ϖ^{−(4k+1)}δ(u) has a unique solution u* ∈ ϖC⁺^N (A3/restricted-power-series-newton, Jacobian ≡ 1 modulo ϖ after dividing by ϖ^{4k+1}), so C⟨u⟩/closure(ϖ^{4k+1}u + δ) ≅ C via u ↦ u*. On V(G) the Jacobian of G satisfies |J_G| = |J_F| ≥ |ϖ^{2k}| since |J_G − J_F| ≤ |ϖ^{m₀}|. This is α_{F,G}^{−1}; α is characterised by closeness of the images of T (uniqueness in the Newton lemma), which gives (c); (a) follows by transporting the Jacobian bound; (d) because α and its inverse are morphisms of pairs (images of A⁺⟨T⟩ correspond).
acceptance: F = (T − a, S − 1) with a ∈ A⁺ (explicit-inverse form with k = 0) and G = (T − a', S − 1) with a − a' ∈ ϖ²A⁺: C = C_G = A and α_{F,G} is the identity of A.
Rational subsets: perturbing s, t in (tT − s) inside ϖ^{m₀} does not change R(s/t) (Tau Ceti `exists_mem_nhds_forall_rationalSubset_eq_of_sub_mem`), consistent with (b).

nodes.title: Standard étale loci over sousperfectoid bases are sousperfectoid affinoids (the étale case of Fargues–Scholze IV.4.17)
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a complete Tate Huber pair with A sousperfectoid (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-ring) and (N, F, k, π) a standard étale presentation (A3/standard-etale-presentation) of (C, C⁺) over (A, A⁺). Then C is sousperfectoid: if W is the tube of F (A3/tubular-neighbourhood), ρ: C → O(W) the section and q: O(W) → C the quotient, and (P̃, ι, σ) a perfectoid frame of the sousperfectoid ring O(W), then (P̃, ι∘ρ, q∘σ) is a perfectoid frame of C. Consequently (C, C⁺) is sheafy and stably uniform, Spa(C, C⁺) is a sousperfectoid affinoid adic space (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-sheafy, R5/sousperfectoid-stably-uniform, R5/sousperfectoid-adic-space), and for every rational U ⊆ Spa(C, C⁺) the ring O(U) is sousperfectoid with a standard étale presentation over (A, A⁺) (A3/standard-presentation-basic-pieces (d)).
hypotheses: A sousperfectoid (for instance perfectoid, or a rational localisation of A'⟨T⟩ with A' perfectoid)
(N, F, k, π) a standard étale presentation
proofSteps: O(W) is sousperfectoid: A⟨T⟩ is (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-rings) and so are its rational localisations (R5/sousperfectoid-rational-localisation).

q is a ring homomorphism with q∘ρ = id, so q is C-linear for the C-module structure on O(W) through ρ, and σ is O(W)-linear; hence σ_C := q∘σ is continuous, C-linear and σ_C∘(ι∘ρ) = q∘ρ = id. P̃ is perfectoid, so (P̃, ι∘ρ, σ_C) is a perfectoid frame.
The remaining statements are the cited R5 results and A3/standard-presentation-basic-pieces.

nodes.title: The equations of a standard étale locus form a regular sequence with closed ideal on its tube (analytic replacement of Fargues–Scholze, Lemma IV.4.13)
nodes.statement: In the situation of A3/tubular-neighbourhood ((A, A⁺) complete Tate, R ⊆ B^N_X rational, e ∈ O⁺(R)^N, tube W), for every rational subset W' ⊆ W: (a) e₁, …, e_N is a weakly regular sequence on O(W') (Mathlib `RingTheory.Sequence.IsWeaklyRegular`) and the Koszul complex K(e; O(W')) is a finite free resolution of O(W')/(e); (b) the ideal e·O(W') is closed and O(W')/(e) ≅ O(V(e) ∩ W'); (c) (e)/(e)² is a free O(V(e) ∩ W')-module with basis the classes of eᵢ; (d) consequently O(W)/(e) is a stably N-fpd, hence stably pseudocoherent, O(W)-module and the ideal (e)·O(W) is stably (N−1)-fpd (A3/stably-pseudocoherent-module). This is the étale case, over any base as in A3/tubular-neighbourhood, of Fargues–Scholze Lemma IV.4.13 (the coordinates of an étale map to a relative ball are regular with closed ideal), whose proof uses the spreading of étale maps — a diamond-level input not used here.
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) and e, W as in A3/tubular-neighbourhood (uniform rational localisations, for instance A sousperfectoid)
W' ranges over rational subsets of W
proofSteps: By A3/tubular-neighbourhood (b), O(W') ≅ C_{W'}⟨u⟩ with e ↦ ϖ^mu; ϖ is a unit, so it suffices to treat u₁, …, u_N on C⟨u⟩ for a complete Tate ring C.

nodes.title: A perfectoid Tate ring of characteristic p is an algebra over a perfectoid field and a completed colimit of p-finite algebras
nodes.statement: Let (R, R⁺) be a perfectoid Tate pair of characteristic p (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras: R a perfect complete Tate ring) and ϖ ∈ R⁺ a pseudouniformiser (Tau Ceti `IsPseudoUniformizer`). Let K := F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^∧ be the t-adic completion of the perfection of F_p((t)), a perfectoid field (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-definition). Then (a) there is a unique continuous ring homomorphism K → R with t^{1/pⁿ} ↦ ϖ^{1/pⁿ} (the unique pⁿ-th roots in the perfect ring R); it is injective when R ≠ 0 and maps K° = F_p[[t^{1/p^∞}]]^∧ into R⁺; so (R, R⁺) is a perfectoid affinoid K-algebra with R⁺ a K°-algebra; (b) consequently (Scholze 2012, Lemma 6.13 = PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-direct-limits-of-p-finite-affinoids) (R, R⁺) is the completion of a filtered colimit of p-finite perfectoid affinoid K-algebras (R_α, R_α⁺), each the completed perfection of a reduced affinoid K-algebra (S_α, S_α⁺) of topologically finite type (Scholze 2012, Definition 6.9); and R⁺/ϖ^M = colim_α colim_r S_α^{+,1/p^r}/ϖ^M for every M, so finitely many elements of R⁺ are approximated modulo ϖ^M by elements of one S_α^{1/p^r} ≅ S_α, again a reduced K-affinoid algebra of topologically finite type (strongly noetherian).
hypotheses: (R, R⁺) perfectoid of characteristic p; ϖ ∈ R⁺ a pseudouniformiser
no base field is assumed: it is constructed
proofSteps: (a) ϖ^{1/pⁿ} ∈ R⁺ exist and are unique (R perfect; R⁺ is integrally closed), and are topologically nilpotent; F_p[t^{1/p^∞}] → R⁺ is continuous for the t-adic topology and extends to the t-adic completion F_p[[t^{1/p^∞}]]^∧ because R⁺ is ϖ-adically complete; inverting t (ϖ is a unit) gives K → R. A ring map from a field to a nonzero ring is injective.

(b) is Scholze 2012, Lemma 6.13(i) (hypothesis: R⁺ a K°-algebra, supplied by (a)), cited as PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-direct-limits-of-p-finite-affinoids; the description modulo ϖ^M comes from its construction (R⁺ the ϖ-adic completion of the colimit, and each R_α⁺ the ϖ-adic completion of colim_Φ S_α⁺), and Frobenius is an isomorphism S_α → S_α^{1/p^r}.
acceptance: R = K itself: the map is the identity; R = K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩: p-finite, the completed perfection of K⟨T⟩.

nodes.title: Jacobian criterion over characteristic-p perfectoid bases: standard étale loci are étale, and affinoid perfectoid over X (Fargues–Scholze IV.4.15(ii) and IV.4.17, characteristic-p étale case)
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a perfectoid Tate pair of characteristic p, X = Spa(A, A⁺), and let (B, B⁺) := (O(Q), O⁺(Q)) for a rational subset Q ⊆ B^m_X (m ≥ 0; m = 0 and Q = X give (B, B⁺) = (A, A⁺)). Let (N, F, k, π) be a standard étale presentation (A3/standard-etale-presentation) of (C, C⁺) over (B, B⁺). Then (a) Spa(C, C⁺) → Spa(B, B⁺) is étale in the local-description sense (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphisms-local-description-and-comparison: every point has an open neighbourhood on which the map factors as an open immersion, a finite étale morphism and an open immersion); (b) if m = 0, then C is a perfectoid Tate ring (C is perfect), Spa(C, C⁺) is an affinoid perfectoid space and Spa(C, C⁺) → X is étale in the sense of ECD Definition 6.2 (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/strongly-etale-morphisms-and-base-change); (c) (Fargues–Scholze IV.4.15(ii), étale case) a morphism g: U → V over X between rational subsets U ⊆ B^n_X and V ⊆ B^n_X such that det(∂gᵢ/∂T_j) is a unit of O(U) with bounded inverse is étale in the local-description sense. No diamond, no ECD 11.30 or 15.6, and no v-descent is used: Fargues–Scholze's proofs of IV.4.15, IV.4.17 rely on ECD Lemma 12.17, on Lemma IV.4.14 (ECD 15.6, 12.17) and on Lemma IV.4.16 (descent to strictly totally disconnected bases), which are replaced by approximation by noetherian (p-finite) bases and Huber's noetherian theory.
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) perfectoid of characteristic p
B = O(Q) for a rational subset Q of a relative ball over X (sousperfectoid, AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-rings)
(N, F, k, π) a standard étale presentation over (B, B⁺); put it in explicit-inverse form first
proofSteps: Base field and noetherian approximation (A3/char-p-perfectoid-base-field): the finitely many coefficients of F (explicit-inverse form) and of the rational data of Q, taken in A⁺ modulo ϖ^{m₀} (m₀ from A3/standard-presentation-perturbation), come from one strongly noetherian K-affinoid algebra S' = S_α^{1/p^r} together with its map S' → A; this gives Q' ⊆ B^m_{Spa S'} and G over O(Q') with image ≡ F modulo ϖ^{m₀}. The same rational data define Q over A (Tau Ceti `exists_mem_nhds_forall_rationalSubset_eq_of_sub_mem`).

Noetherian étaleness: V(G) ⊆ B^N_{Q'} is a standard étale locus over the K-affinoid O(Q'), hence étale over Spa(O(Q')) in Huber's sense (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-local-structure, (ii) ⇒ (i)) and so, over the field K, locally an open immersion into a finite étale cover (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-affinoid-finite-etale-embedding, R0/etale-local-open-finite-etale-factorisation).

Base change: Spa(B, B⁺) is sousperfectoid; the base change of V(G) → Spa O(Q') along Spa(B) → Spa O(Q') exists, is étale in the local-description sense and sousperfectoid (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-etale-base-change); it is Spa of the completed tensor product, which is B⟨T⟩/closure(G_B) with G_B the image of G (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-restricted-power-series (c), R0/affinoid-fibre-product; sheafiness from A3/standard-etale-locus-sousperfectoid).
Perturbation: G_B ≡ F modulo ϖ^{m₀}, so Spa(C, C⁺) ≅ Spa(B⟨T⟩/closure(G_B)) over Spa(B) (A3/standard-presentation-perturbation). This proves (a).

(b) Locally Spa(C) is a rational subset of a finite étale space over a rational subset of the perfectoid X, hence perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/almost-purity-theorem, P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids). C = O(Spa C) (C sheafy, A3/standard-etale-locus-sousperfectoid) embeds into a finite product of perfect rings, so Frobenius is injective; it is surjective because p-th roots are unique locally and glue. A perfect complete Tate ring is perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras). In characteristic p étale maps of perfectoid spaces are strongly étale (P3).
(c) U ≅ V(u − g(T)) ∩ (U ×_X B^n) is a standard étale locus over O(V) in the variables T with Jacobian det(∂g/∂T); apply (a) with base V (B := O(V)).
acceptance: Rational subsets of X and finite étale algebras over rational subsets (A3/standard-presentation-basic-pieces) give étale affinoid perfectoid spaces, as they must (ECD Theorem 6.1(i)).
Non-example: F = T^p − a has J_F = 0 and is not a standard étale presentation; its locus Spa(A⟨T⟩/(T^p − a)) is not étale over X.

nodes.title: Local presentations of a closed subspace from integral cut-offs and graphs; pseudocoherence of its ideal
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a complete Tate Huber pair with A sousperfectoid, X = Spa(A, A⁺), R ⊆ B^N_X a rational subset with coordinates T₁, …, T_N, and (C, C⁺) a complete Huber pair with a standard étale presentation (n, F, k, π_v) over (A, A⁺) in variables v₁, …, v_n (A3/standard-etale-presentation). Let g: Spa(C, C⁺) → R be a morphism over X, i.e. a continuous A-algebra map g*: O(R) → C with g*(O⁺(R)) ⊆ C⁺. Suppose given w₁, …, w_n ∈ O(R) (not necessarily power-bounded), monic polynomials P_l(Z) ∈ O⁺(R)[Z] and M ≥ 1 such that (i) c_l := g*(w_l) satisfies c_l − π_v(v_l) ∈ ϖ·π_v(A₀⟨v⟩) (A₀ ⊆ A⁺ a ring of definition), (ii) g*(P_l(w_l)) ∈ ϖ^{M+1}C⁺ for all l. Put R'' := R ∩ ⋂_l {|P_l(w_l)| ≤ |ϖ^M|} and Q_l := R ∩ {|P_l(w_l)| ≥ |ϖ^M|}. Then: (a) {R''} ∪ {Q_l} is a finite rational covering of R, g factors through R'' and g⁻¹(Q_l) = ∅; (b) w_l ∈ O⁺(R'') for all l; (c) g*: O(R'') → C is a quotient mapping of complete Huber pairs (surjective, C⁺ the integral closure of the image of O⁺(R'')), and for every rational R''' ⊆ R'' the induced O(R''') → O(g⁻¹R''') = C ⊗̂_{O(R'')} O(R''') is again one; (d) C is a stably pseudocoherent O(R'')-module and the kernel of O(R'') → C is a stably pseudocoherent ideal; (e) hence the ideal sheaf I := ker(O_R → g_*O_{Spa C}) is a pseudocoherent sheaf on R (A3/pseudocoherent-sheaf), equal to O_R on each Q_l.
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) complete Tate, A sousperfectoid (so rational subsets of relative balls are sheafy)
(C, C⁺) with a standard étale presentation; g a morphism into R
w, P_l, M as in (i), (ii)
proofSteps: (a) Every valuation satisfies |P_l(w_l)| ≤ |ϖ^M| or ≥ |ϖ^M|, so the sets cover R; they are rational (numerators P_l(w_l), ϖ^M). On Spa(C), |P_l(c_l)| ≤ |ϖ^{M+1}| < |ϖ^M| pointwise.

(b) If |w_l(x)| > 1 at x ∈ R'' then, P_l being monic with coefficients of absolute value ≤ 1, |P_l(w_l)(x)| = |w_l(x)|^{deg P_l} > 1 > |ϖ^M(x)|, a contradiction; so |w_l| ≤ 1 on R'' and w_l ∈ O⁺(R'') (Tau Ceti `mem_iff_forall_vle_one`).

(c) By A3/perturbation-of-generators, v ↦ c is a quotient mapping A⟨v⟩ → C with a transported presentation F̂ = F∘θ; it factors through O(R'') (v ↦ w), so O(R'') → C is surjective with the right plus ring. Rational R''': base change of the quotient along the rational localisation (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-rational-localisation with R0/completed-tensor-restricted-power-series (c)).

(d) Graph: w defines R'' → B^n_X; in P := R'' ×_X B^n_X (coordinates T, v) the graph Γ = V(v − w) lies in the tube {|v − w| ≤ |ϖ|} (Jacobian 1, k = 0), so O(R'') = O(W_Γ)/(v − w) with v − w regular and closed on every rational subset (A3/fs-iv-4-13-regular-sequence) — O(R'') is a stably pseudocoherent O(W_Γ)-module. Inside W_Γ the point set g(Spa C) is V(F̂(v), T − G(v)) where G ∈ A⟨v⟩^N lifts g*(T) along v ↦ c: the graph argument (C → O(W_Γ)/closure(F̂(v), T − G(v)), v ↦ v, and the map back are inverse on the generators T, v) identifies the quotient with C, and this is a standard étale presentation over (A, A⁺) with N + n equations and Jacobian ± det(∂F̂/∂v); so on every rational W' ⊆ W_Γ contained in the tube of that presentation, C ⊗̂ O(W') is a stably fpd O(W')-module (A3/fs-iv-4-13-regular-sequence). Intersecting with Γ = V(v − w) ≅ R'' gives a rational subset R''_t ⊆ R'' containing g(Spa C) on which C ⊗̂ O(R''_t) is pseudocoherent over O(R''_t) = O(W')/(v − w) (A3/pseudocoherent-module API `baseChange_of_isPseudoCoherent_algebra`, Stacks Tag 064Z, since O(W')/(v − w) is pseudocoherent over O(W')), with completeness after rational localisation from (c). The complement R'' ∖ R''_t is covered by the finitely many rational subsets on which one of the tube inequalities fails; they do not meet g(Spa C), and there the ideal is the unit ideal. So the ideal sheaf is pseudocoherent on a finite rational covering of R'', and A3/pseudocoherent-kiehl-gluing gives that C and the kernel of O(R'') → C are stably pseudocoherent O(R'')-modules (A3/pseudocoherent-two-out-of-three).
(e) On R'' by (d) and A3/pseudocoherent-sheaf; on Q_l the sheaf g_*O is zero.
acceptance: Trivial case: C = O(R) and g = id with n = N, w = T, P_l = Z: R'' = R and the ideal is 0.
Application (A3/fs-iv-4-19-zariski-closed-char-p): g*: O(R) → C surjective, w lifts of the presentation variables, P_l monic equations of π_v(v_l) over the image of O⁺(R) (C⁺ is integral over it).

nodes.title: Zariski closed immersions of affinoid étale perfectoid spaces into relative balls (Fargues–Scholze IV.4.19–IV.4.20, perfectoid-base specialisation)
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a perfectoid Tate pair, X = Spa(A, A⁺), Y' ⊆ B^N_X an open subspace which is a finite union of rational subsets (for instance a rational subset or B^N_X itself; Y' is sousperfectoid and smooth over X), Y an affinoid perfectoid space with an étale morphism Y → X (ECD Definition 6.2), and g: Y → Y' a morphism over X. The following are equivalent: (i) Y' is covered by rational subsets V' ⊆ B^N_X such that V := g⁻¹(V') is affinoid and O(V') → O(V) is a quotient mapping (surjective, O⁺(V) the integral closure of the image of O⁺(V')); (ii) for every rational subset V' ⊆ Y' the same holds. If they hold, g is a Zariski closed immersion (Fargues–Scholze Definition IV.4.20), and: (a) the ideal sheaf I_{Y⊂Y'} := ker(O_{Y'} → g_*O_Y) is pseudocoherent (A3/pseudocoherent-sheaf); (b) for every rational V' ⊆ Y', I(V') is a stably pseudocoherent O(V')-module and O(V')/I(V') ≅ O(g⁻¹V') (affine quotient description, with plus ring the integral closure of the image of O⁺(V')); (c) the local generation by N sections with invertible Jacobian near Y is A3/local-equations-near-closed-subspace. The statement holds for perfectoid (A, A⁺) of any characteristic; characteristic p is the case used by AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/affinoid-etale-finite-stage-6-4-iv. Fargues–Scholze prove IV.4.19 for smooth maps of sous-perfectoid spaces using IV.4.15 and IV.4.17 (diamond-dependent) and Kedlaya–Liu's gluing; here only the gluing is used, together with A3/integral-cutoff-graph-presentation.
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) perfectoid; Y' a finite union of rational subsets of B^N_X
Y affinoid perfectoid and étale over X; g an X-morphism
proofSteps: (ii) ⇒ (i) is trivial. (i) ⇒ (a): let V' be a member of the covering and V = g⁻¹(V'). V is affinoid perfectoid and étale over X, so it has a finite rational covering by standard pieces V_β with standard étale presentations over (A, A⁺) (A3/etale-standard-piece-cover). Rational subsets of V are preimages of rational subsets of V' (lift numerators and denominator along the surjection O(V') → O(V)), so V_β = g⁻¹(V'_β) with V'_β ⊆ V' rational, and O(V'_β) → O(V_β) is a quotient mapping. Apply A3/integral-cutoff-graph-presentation with R = V'_β, w = lifts in O(V'_β) of the presentation variables (condition (i) exact) and P_l monic equations of their images over the image of O⁺(V'_β) (exact, O⁺(V_β) being integral over that image): I is pseudocoherent on V'_β. On V' ∖ g(V) — covered by the rational subsets {|a| ≥ |ϖ^j|}, a ∈ ker(O(V') → O(V)), on which a is a unit — I = O. So I is pseudocoherent on Y'.

(a) ⇒ (ii), (b): for rational V' ⊆ Y' (sheafy, sousperfectoid: AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-rings, R5/sousperfectoid-sheafy), 0 → I → O → g_*O_Y → 0 is an exact sequence of pseudocoherent sheaves on V' (g_*O_Y is locally a quotient O(V'_β)/I), so by A3/pseudocoherent-kiehl-gluing its global sections are exact: O(V') → Γ(V', g_*O_Y) = O(g⁻¹V') is surjective with kernel I(V') stably pseudocoherent. The closed subspace Spa(O(V')/I(V'), integral closure) and g⁻¹(V') agree on the rational covering V'_β ∩ V' (both give O(V_β)⊗̂O(V'_β ∩ V'), A3/pseudocoherent-kiehl-gluing (b)), hence g⁻¹(V') is affinoid with that ring; the plus rings agree because both are {f : |f| ≤ 1} on the same space (Tau Ceti `mem_iff_forall_vle_one`).

nodes.title: Affinoid étale perfectoid spaces have standard rational coverings by standard étale pieces
nodes.statement: Let X = Spa(A, A⁺) be an affinoid perfectoid space and f: Y = Spa(B, B⁺) → X an étale morphism (ECD Definition 6.2: locally an open immersion into a space finite étale over an open of X) with Y affinoid perfectoid. Then there are σ₁, …, σ_m ∈ B generating the unit ideal such that every V_j := Y(σ/σ_j) = {|σᵢ| ≤ |σ_j| for all i} is X-isomorphic to a rational subset of an affinoid perfectoid space W_j finite étale over a rational subset U_j ⊆ X (O(W_j) finite étale over O(U_j), O⁺(W_j) the integral closure of O⁺(U_j)). Consequently each (O(V_j), O⁺(V_j)) has a standard étale presentation over (A, A⁺) (A3/standard-presentation-basic-pieces), and so does every rational subset of Y contained in some V_j.
hypotheses: X, Y affinoid perfectoid; f étale in the sense of ECD Definition 6.2
proofSteps: For y ∈ Y choose, by ECD Definition 6.2(ii), opens y ∈ V ⊆ Y, U ⊆ X, an open immersion V → W and a finite étale W → U. Shrink U to a rational U_y ∋ f(y) (rational subsets form a basis); W_y := W ×_U U_y is affinoid perfectoid with O(W_y) finite étale over O(U_y) and plus ring the integral closure (ECD Definition 6.2(i); PerfectoidSpaces:P3/strongly-finite-etale-maps-are-affinoid-over-affinoids).

Choose a rational V'_y of W_y with y ∈ V'_y ⊆ V ∩ W_y, and a rational V''_y of Y with y ∈ V''_y ⊆ V'_y. Then V''_y is cut out in the affinoid V'_y by the restrictions of its defining functions, so it is rational in V'_y, hence in W_y (rational subsets of rational subsets are rational: Kedlaya–Liu I, Lemma 2.4.13(b)).

Refine the covering {V''_y} of Y by a standard rational covering {Y(σ/σ_j)} (Tau Ceti `exists_span_eq_top_forall_rationalSubset_subset_of_isTateRing`); each Y(σ/σ_j) is rational in some V''_y by the same argument.

Presentations: A3/standard-presentation-basic-pieces (a) for U_j, (b) for W_j over U_j (the finite étale algebra with its natural topology, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra), (a) and (c) for V_j.

nodes.title: Local plus-generators on a rational subset are approximated by elements integral over global plus elements and ratios
nodes.statement: Let (B, B⁺) be a complete Tate Huber pair which is stably uniform (for instance perfectoid or sousperfectoid; AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-stably-uniform), σ₁, …, σ_m ∈ B generating the unit ideal, V := Y(σ/σ_j) ⊆ Y = Spa(B, B⁺) and ū ∈ O⁺(V). For every M ≥ 0 there are: finitely many β₁, …, β_r ∈ B⁺; an element z ∈ O⁺(V) with z − ū ∈ ϖ^M O⁺(V); a monic polynomial P(Z) = Z^d + Σ_{e<d} a_e Z^e with P(z) = 0 whose coefficients a_e are polynomials in the ratios σ₁/σ_j, …, σ_m/σ_j with coefficients in ℤ[β₁, …, β_r]; and b ∈ B, s ≥ 0 with b/σ_j^s − z ∈ ϖ^M O⁺(V).
hypotheses: (B, B⁺) complete Tate, stably uniform (O⁺(V) bounded, so {ϖ^M O⁺(V)} is a basis of neighbourhoods of 0)
σ generating the unit ideal
proofSteps: O⁺(V) is the completion of the integral closure of the image of B⁺[T₁, …, T_m] under Tᵢ ↦ σᵢ/σ_j (Kedlaya–Liu I, Lemma 2.4.13(a)); so ū is within ϖ^M O⁺(V) of an element z of that integral closure.
z satisfies a monic equation whose coefficients lie in the image of B⁺[T]; each coefficient is a finite sum of terms β·(σ/σ_j)^ν with β ∈ B⁺; collect the finitely many β.
O(V) is the completion of B[1/σ_j] (Tau Ceti `completionLocalization`), so z is approximated by some b/σ_j^s; closeness in the topology of O(V) is closeness in ϖ^M O⁺(V) by boundedness.
acceptance: B = K⟨X⟩ (K a perfectoid field of characteristic p), σ = (X, ϖ), j = 1, V = {|ϖ| ≤ |X|}: ū = ϖ/X is itself the ratio σ₂/σ₁, with P(Z) = Z − σ₂/σ₁ and r = 0.

nodes.title: An affinoid étale perfectoid space is Zariski closed in a relative ball; its ideal is stably pseudocoherent (the closed embedding asserted in ECD 6.4(iv))
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a perfectoid Tate pair, X = Spa(A, A⁺), and f: Y = Spa(B, B⁺) → X an étale morphism of affinoid perfectoid spaces. Then there are N ≥ 0 and b = (b₁, …, b_N) ∈ (B⁺)^N such that the X-morphism g_b: Y → B^N_X, Tᵢ ↦ bᵢ, is a Zariski closed immersion in the sense of A3/fs-iv-4-19-zariski-closed-char-p with Y' = B^N_X. Equivalently: π_b: A⟨T₁, …, T_N⟩ → B, T ↦ b, is surjective and B⁺ is the integral closure of π_b(A⁺⟨T⟩); the ideal I := ker π_b is a stably pseudocoherent A⟨T⟩-module; the ideal sheaf Ĩ on B^N_X is pseudocoherent; and for every rational V' ⊆ B^N_X, O(V')/I·O(V') ≅ O(g_b⁻¹V') with plus ring the integral closure of the image. Any enlargement b' = (b, b'') with b'' ∈ (B⁺)^{N'} has the same properties.
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) perfectoid (any characteristic); Y affinoid perfectoid; f étale (ECD Definition 6.2)
proofSteps: Standard pieces: σ₁, …, σ_m ∈ B generating the unit ideal with V_j = Y(σ/σ_j) carrying standard étale presentations (n_j, F⁽ʲ⁾, k_j, π_j) over (A, A⁺) (A3/etale-standard-piece-cover); ū⁽ʲ⁾ := π_j(v⁽ʲ⁾) ∈ O⁺(V_j)ⁿʲ.

Choices: aᵢ ∈ B with Σ aᵢσᵢ = 1 and c ≥ 0 with ϖ^c aᵢ, ϖ^c σᵢ ∈ B⁺; a ring of definition A₀ ⊆ A⁺ containing ϖ, and M ≥ 1 with ϖ^{M}O⁺(V_j) ⊆ ϖ·π_j(A₀⟨v⁽ʲ⁾⟩) for all j (possible: the image is open and O⁺(V_j) is bounded); for each j, l, A3/integral-approximation-of-generators gives z_{jl} with z_{jl} − ū_{jl} ∈ ϖ^M O⁺(V_j), a monic P_{jl} with P_{jl}(z_{jl}) = 0 whose coefficients are built from finitely many β's in B⁺ and the ratios σᵢ/σ_j, and b_{jl} ∈ B, s ≥ 0 with b_{jl}/σ_j^{s} − z_{jl} ∈ ϖ^{M+1}O⁺(V_j); choose d with ϖ^d b_{jl} ∈ B⁺. Let b consist of the ϖ^cσᵢ, the ϖ^caᵢ, the β's and the ϖ^d b_{jl}.

Covering of B^N_X: h := Σ T_{ϖ^caᵢ}T_{ϖ^cσᵢ} − ϖ^{2c}; R₀ := {|h| ≥ |ϖ^{2c+1}|} with g⁻¹(R₀) = ∅ (h∘g = 0); S := {|h| ≤ |ϖ^{2c+1}|}, on which the T_{ϖ^cσᵢ} generate the unit ideal; R'_j := S ∩ {|T_{ϖ^cσᵢ}| ≤ |T_{ϖ^cσ_j}| for all i} with g⁻¹(R'_j) = V_j. On R'_j put w_{jl} := T_{ϖ^d b_{jl}}·ϖ^{−d}·(ϖ^c/T_{ϖ^cσ_j})^{s}, so g*(w_{jl}) = b_{jl}/σ_j^s, and let P̃_{jl} be P_{jl} with coefficients lifted to O⁺(R'_j) (β ↦ T_β, σᵢ/σ_j ↦ T_{ϖ^cσᵢ}/T_{ϖ^cσ_j}).

A3/integral-cutoff-graph-presentation on each R'_j (V = V_j, presentation (n_j, F⁽ʲ⁾, …), w_j, P̃_j): conditions (i) (b/σ^s − ū ∈ ϖ^M O⁺(V_j) ⊆ ϖ·π_j(A₀⟨v⟩)) and (ii) (|P_{jl}(b/σ^s)| = |P_{jl}(b/σ^s) − P_{jl}(z)| ≤ |b/σ^s − z| ≤ |ϖ^{M+1}|, the coefficients being power-bounded) hold. It yields rational R''_j ⊇ g(V_j) and Q_{jl} with g⁻¹(Q_{jl}) = ∅ covering R'_j, and quotient mappings O(R''_j) → O(V_j).

The finite rational covering {R₀} ∪ {R''_j} ∪ {Q_{jl}} of B^N_X satisfies A3/fs-iv-4-19-zariski-closed-char-p (i) (on R₀ and Q_{jl} the preimage is empty, Spa(0)); its (ii) for V' = B^N_X and (a), (b) give all claims (B^N_X is sousperfectoid: AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-rings, R5/perfectoid-times-polydisc). Enlargement: the new coordinates are functions of the old ones on Y, and B^{N+N'}_X ⊇ graph ≅ B^N_X.
acceptance: Y = X(s/t) rational with s, t ∈ A⁺: b = (sᵢ/t) works directly, I = closure(tTᵢ − sᵢ).

Y finite étale over X with B = A[x]/(P) and det(∂P/∂x) a unit: b = ϖ^c x works, and I is the closure of the ideal generated by the equations P(ϖ^{−c}T), multiplied by a power of ϖ that puts them into A⁺⟨T⟩.

nodes.title: Conormal description of an affinoid étale closed subspace of a relative ball: I/I² ≅ Ω¹_{B^N_X/X}|_Y
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a perfectoid Tate pair, X = Spa(A, A⁺), U ⊆ B^N_X a finite union of rational subsets, Y affinoid perfectoid étale over X and g: Y → U a Zariski closed immersion (A3/fs-iv-4-19-zariski-closed-char-p). For a rational V' ⊆ U with V := g⁻¹(V') and I := ker(O(V') → O(V)): (a) the continuous differentials vanish, Ω^c_{O(V)/A} = 0 (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/continuous-differentials); (b) the O(V)-linear map δ: I/I² → ⊕_{i=1}^N O(V)·dTᵢ, e ↦ Σᵢ (∂e/∂Tᵢ)|_V dTᵢ, is an isomorphism; in particular I/I² is free of rank N and every basis of it lifts to elements of I whose Jacobian with respect to T is invertible on V. This is ECD's 'Ω¹_{Y/X} = 0 and so I/I² ≅ Ω¹_{B^n_X/X}/I'.
hypotheses: as in A3/fs-iv-4-19-zariski-closed-char-p; V' rational
proofSteps: (a) On each standard piece V_β of V (A3/etale-standard-piece-cover) the presentation matrix of Ω^c is the Jacobian, invertible, so Ω^c_{O(V_β)/A} = 0 (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/continuous-differentials (c)); Ω^c_{O(V)/A} is finitely generated and its base change to the rational covering {V_β} is Ω^c_{O(V_β)/A} = 0 (localisation compatibility of continuous differentials), so it vanishes because maximal ideals of O(V) lift to the covering (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/simple-laurent-glueing-square (c) with Nakayama).

Surjectivity of δ: the conormal sequence I/I² → O(V) ⊗ Ω^c_{O(V')/A} → Ω^c_{O(V)/A} → 0 is exact (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/conormal-sequence) and Ω^c_{O(V')/A} is free on dT₁, …, dT_N (R0/continuous-differentials (c) and rational localisation).

Injectivity and freeness locally: on the pieces R''_β of A3/integral-cutoff-graph-presentation, V is cut out inside the tube W_Γ ⊆ R''_β ×_X B^n_X by the regular sequence (F̂(v), T − G(v)) of length N + n with invertible Jacobian, whose conormal module is free on these classes (A3/fs-iv-4-13-regular-sequence (c)); the conormal sequence of V ⊂ Γ ⊂ W_Γ, with Γ = V(v − w) ≅ R''_β, shows I/I² ⊗ O(V_β) is free of rank N with δ an isomorphism.

Globally: I is stably pseudocoherent (A3/fs-iv-4-19-zariski-closed-char-p (b)), so I/I² = I ⊗ O(V) is a stably pseudocoherent O(V)-module (A3/pseudocoherent-module API `baseChange_of_isPseudoCoherent_algebra`); being locally free it is finite projective (A3/fpd-local-to-global, m = 0), and δ, an isomorphism after base change to a rational covering, is an isomorphism (kernel and cokernel are finitely generated and vanish locally).

nodes.title: The ideal of an affinoid étale Y in a relative ball is generated by N equations with unit Jacobian on a rational neighbourhood of Y
nodes.statement: In the situation of A3/conormal-description (Y affinoid perfectoid étale over the affinoid perfectoid X, g: Y → U ⊆ B^N_X a Zariski closed immersion, V' ⊆ U rational, V = g⁻¹(V'), I = ker(O(V') → O(V))): there are e₁, …, e_N ∈ I with δ(eᵢ) = dTᵢ — so Δ := det(∂eᵢ/∂T_j) is ≡ 1 on V — and a rational subset W ⊆ V' containing g(V) such that e·O(W) is a closed ideal, O(W)/(e) ≅ O(V) compatibly with plus rings, and W lies in the tube of e (A3/tubular-neighbourhood, k = 0). Together with the rational presentation of W this gives a standard étale presentation of (O(V), O⁺(V)) over (A, A⁺) (A3/standard-presentation-basic-pieces (c)). This is ECD's 'I is necessarily generated by n functions in a neighborhood of Y'.
hypotheses: as in A3/conormal-description
proofSteps: Choose eᵢ ∈ I lifting the basis dTᵢ of I/I² (A3/conormal-description). W₀ := V' ∩ {|eᵢ| ≤ |ϖ³| for all i} ∩ {|Δ − 1| ≤ |ϖ|} is a rational tube (|Δ| = 1 on it, k = 0, m = 3) containing g(V). Put C := O(W₀)/closure(e) = O(W₀)/(e) (A3/fs-iv-4-13-regular-sequence) and K := ker(C → O(V)), the image of I.

Since δ is an isomorphism, I = (e) + I², so K = K². I is finitely generated (stably pseudocoherent), hence so is K; a finitely generated idempotent ideal is generated by an idempotent (Mathlib `Ideal.isIdempotentElem_iff_of_fg`): K = εC with ε² = ε, and Spa(C) = V ⊔ V(1 − ε) with V = {ε = 0}.

Lift ε to h ∈ O(W₀) and put W := W₀ ∩ {|h| ≤ |ϖ|}, rational, containing g(V) (ε = 0 there); then O(W)/(e) = C⟨h/ϖ⟩ = C(1 − ε) ≅ O(V) (ε = 1 on the other part, excluded). This replaces Fargues–Scholze's 'closed immersion and étale, hence locally an isomorphism'.
acceptance: Y = X(s/t) embedded in B^n_X by Tᵢ ↦ sᵢ/t, I the closure of (tTᵢ − sᵢ): δ(tTᵢ − sᵢ) = t·dTᵢ, so eᵢ := λ·(tTᵢ − sᵢ) with λ ∈ A⟨T⟩ any lift of t^{−1} ∈ B satisfies δ(eᵢ) = dTᵢ, and the tube W is a rational neighbourhood of the graph of s/t over R(s/t).

nodes.title: Huber's standard étale presentation for affinoid étale maps of affinoid perfectoid spaces (Huber 1.7.1 (i) ⇔ (ii), perfectoid case)
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a perfectoid Tate pair, X = Spa(A, A⁺), and f: Y = Spa(B, B⁺) → X an étale morphism of affinoid perfectoid spaces (ECD Definition 6.2). Then (B, B⁺) admits a standard étale presentation over (A, A⁺) (A3/standard-etale-presentation): B ≅ A⟨T₁, …, T_N⟩/closure(F₁, …, F_N) with det(∂Fᵢ/∂T_j) a unit of B with bounded inverse and B⁺ the integral closure of the image of A⁺⟨T⟩; it can be chosen in explicit-inverse form. Conversely, if A has characteristic p, every standard étale presentation over (A, A⁺) defines an affinoid perfectoid space étale over X (A3/jacobian-criterion-char-p). Hence, in characteristic p: an affinoid perfectoid space Y over X is étale if and only if Y ≅ Spa of a standard étale presentation — the statement of Huber's Proposition 1.7.1 for affinoid perfectoid spaces of characteristic p used in ECD 6.4(iv).
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) perfectoid; f étale with Y affinoid perfectoid
the converse direction: characteristic p
proofSteps: A3/affinoid-etale-zariski-closed-embedding gives g_b: Y → B^N_X Zariski closed with stably pseudocoherent ideal I.
A3/local-equations-near-closed-subspace with V' = B^N_X gives e ∈ I^N with Jacobian ≡ 1 on Y and a rational W ⊇ g_b(Y) with O(W)/(e) ≅ B.

Write W = R(s/t) with s, t ∈ A⁺⟨T⟩ and absorb it by extra variables S with equations tS − s (A3/standard-presentation-basic-pieces (a), (c)): F := (e(T), t(T)S − s(T)), Jacobian Δ·t^{#S}, a unit on Y with bounded inverse. Put it in explicit-inverse form (A3/standard-etale-presentation API `withInverse`).
Converse: A3/jacobian-criterion-char-p (b).

nodes.title: Tilting commutes with cofiltered limits of affinoid perfectoid spaces and identifies the affinoid étale categories
nodes.statement: Let X_i = Spa(R_i, R_i⁺), i ∈ I, be a cofiltered system of affinoid perfectoid spaces with limit X = Spa(R, R⁺) (PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces: R⁺ the ϖ-adic completion of colim R_i⁺ for a compatible pseudouniformiser ϖ, chosen for i ≥ i₀ with compatible p-power roots). Then (a) the tilts X_i^♭ = Spa(R_i^♭, R_i^{♭+}) form a cofiltered system of affinoid perfectoid spaces of characteristic p whose limit is X^♭, i.e. R^{♭+} is the ϖ^♭-adic completion of colim R_i^{♭+} with ϖ^♭ = (ϖ, ϖ^{1/p}, …); (b) tilting gives equivalences (X_i)_{ét,aff} ≃ (X_i^♭)_{ét,aff} and X_{ét,aff} ≃ X^♭_{ét,aff} (affinoid perfectoid spaces étale over the base, ECD Definition 6.2) that commute, up to canonical isomorphism, with the base change functors (X_i)_{ét,aff} → (X_j)_{ét,aff} → X_{ét,aff}. Hence the comparison functor of ECD 6.4(iv) for (X_i) is an equivalence iff the one for (X_i^♭) is.
hypotheses: X_i affinoid perfectoid, cofiltered; the tilting equivalences of PerfectoidSpaces P1–P3 in the generality of perfectoid Tate rings (ECD 3.13, 6.3; see requests)
proofSteps: (a) R^{♭+}/ϖ^♭ ≅ R⁺/ϖ and R_i^{♭+}/ϖ^♭ ≅ R_i⁺/ϖ compatibly (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring); R⁺/ϖ = colim R_i⁺/ϖ (P5 construction); R^{♭+} is ϖ^♭-adically complete and ϖ^♭-torsion free, and so is the completion of colim R_i^{♭+}, and a map between such rings that is an isomorphism modulo ϖ^♭ is an isomorphism. The limit property is PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces for the tilted system.

(b) Tilting induces X_ét ≃ X^♭_ét (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-tilting-and-etale-almost-acyclicity; ECD Theorem 6.3), preserves affinoid perfectoid objects (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-spaces-and-glued-tilting) and commutes with fibre products (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces), hence with base change along X_j → X_i and X → X_i.
acceptance: X_n = {|T| ≤ |p|ⁿ} ⊆ Spa(K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, K°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) with K = ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})^∧ (rational subsets of a perfectoid space, hence affinoid perfectoid): the limit is the origin Spa(K), and the tilted system is {|T^♭| ≤ |t|ⁿ} over K^♭ = F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^∧ with limit Spa(K^♭).

nodes.title: Approximating equations and rational data at a finite stage of a cofiltered limit of affinoid perfectoid spaces
nodes.statement: In the situation of PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces (X = Spa(R, R⁺) = lim X_i, X_i = Spa(R_i, R_i⁺), compatible pseudouniformiser ϖ), write φ_i: R_i → R. (a) For every N ≥ 0, every finite family of elements of R⁺⟨T₁, …, T_N⟩ and every M ≥ 0 there are i and elements of R_i⁺⟨T⟩ whose images agree with the given ones modulo ϖ^M R⁺⟨T⟩; the same holds for the numerators and denominator of a rational subset of B^N_X, and for M large the approximating data define, over X, the same rational subset (Tau Ceti `exists_mem_nhds_forall_rationalSubset_eq_of_sub_mem`). (b) If (N, F_i, k, π_i) is a standard étale presentation of (C_i, C_i⁺) over (R_i, R_i⁺) (A3/standard-etale-presentation) and Y_i := Spa(C_i, C_i⁺) is affinoid perfectoid, then the base change (N, φ_i(F_i), k, ·) is a standard étale presentation of C_i ⊗̂_{R_i} R = R⟨T⟩/closure(φ_i(F_i)), and Y_i ×_{X_i} X = Spa(R⟨T⟩/closure(φ_i(F_i)), integral closure) as perfectoid spaces.
hypotheses: X_i affinoid perfectoid, cofiltered, with limit X (P5)
(b): Y_i affinoid perfectoid (in characteristic p this is automatic, A3/jacobian-criterion-char-p)
proofSteps: (a) R⁺⟨T⟩/ϖ^M = (R⁺/ϖ^M)[T] = colim_i (R_i⁺/ϖ^M)[T], because R⁺ is the ϖ-adic completion of colim R_i⁺ (P5) and polynomial rings commute with filtered colimits; lift finitely many classes to one R_i⁺⟨T⟩. The rational-subset statement is Tau Ceti's perturbation invariance.

(b) C_i ⊗̂_{R_i} R = R⟨T⟩/closure(φ_i(F_i)) with plus ring the integral closure of the image (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-restricted-power-series (c)); the Jacobian condition is preserved by the ring map. Fibre products of affinoid perfectoid spaces are Spa of the completed tensor product (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces); the uniqueness of the plus ring (integral closure of the image) matches both descriptions.

nodes.title: Affinoid étale objects over a cofiltered limit descend to a finite stage (characteristic p)
nodes.statement: Let X_i = Spa(R_i, R_i⁺), i ∈ I, be a cofiltered system of affinoid perfectoid spaces of characteristic p with limit X = Spa(R, R⁺) (PerfectoidSpaces:P5), and Y → X an étale morphism with Y affinoid perfectoid. Then there are i ∈ I and an affinoid perfectoid space Y_i with an étale morphism Y_i → X_i such that Y_i ×_{X_i} X ≅ Y over X. Explicitly: let (N, F, k, π) be a standard étale presentation of O(Y) over R in explicit-inverse form (A3/global-standard-etale-presentation) and m₀ = 4k + 2; choose i and F_i ∈ R_i⁺⟨T⟩^N with φ_i(F_i) ≡ F modulo ϖ^{m₀} (A3/cofiltered-limit-presentation-approximation); then the Jacobian of F_i is invertible on Y_i := V(F_i) (the approximated Jacobian inverse is part of the data), Y_i is affinoid perfectoid and étale over X_i (A3/jacobian-criterion-char-p (b)), and Y_i ×_{X_i} X = V(φ_i(F_i)) ≅ V(F) = Y (A3/cofiltered-limit-presentation-approximation (b), A3/standard-presentation-perturbation). The same holds for every j ≥ i with F_j the image of F_i.

nodes.title: Independence of the finite-stage model from presentations, approximations and indices
nodes.statement: In the situation of A3/finite-stage-approximation-char-p (or of A3/affinoid-etale-finite-stage-6-4-iv in any characteristic): (a) if (Y_i, α) and (Y'_{i'}, α') are two affinoid étale models of Y — Y_i affinoid étale over X_i with α: Y_i ×_{X_i} X ≅ Y, obtained from any standard étale presentations, approximations and indices — then there is j ≥ i, i' and a unique isomorphism β_j: Y_i ×_{X_i} X_j ≅ Y'_{i'} ×_{X_{i'}} X_j over X_j whose base change to X is α'^{−1}∘α; the β_j for larger j are the base changes of β_j; (b) the rule Y ↦ (class of (Y_i, α)) is well defined in the 2-colimit 2-colim_i (X_i)_{ét,aff} and, together with the base change functor, gives mutually quasi-inverse equivalences; (c) the model agrees with the finite-stage descent of Y as a qcqs étale object given by PerfectoidSpaces:P5 (ECD 6.4(ii)): the P5 descent Z_k of Y is isomorphic over some X_j to Y_i ×_{X_i} X_j, and is therefore affinoid for large j.

nodes.title: Comparison of the Zariski closed immersions of A3 with ECD Definition 5.7 and Theorem 5.8 (PerfectoidQuotients Q4)
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a perfectoid Tate pair of characteristic p, X = Spa(A, A⁺), Y = Spa(B, B⁺) affinoid perfectoid étale over X and b ∈ (B⁺)^N as in A3/affinoid-etale-zariski-closed-embedding. Let B^{N,perf}_X := Spa(A⟨T₁^{1/p^∞}, …, T_N^{1/p^∞}⟩, A⁺⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) be the perfectoid relative ball and g^perf: Y → B^{N,perf}_X the map T_i^{1/pⁿ} ↦ b_i^{1/pⁿ}. (a) g^perf is strongly Zariski closed in the sense of ECD Definition 5.7(ii): A⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ → B is surjective (its image contains the image of A⟨T⟩, which is B) and B⁺ is the integral closure of the image of A⁺⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩; in particular g^perf is a Zariski closed immersion (ECD 5.7(i)). (b) Conversely, by ECD Theorem 5.8 (PerfectoidQuotients:Q4/zariski-closed-subsets-are-strongly-zariski-closed), every Zariski closed immersion of an affinoid perfectoid space into an affinoid perfectoid space is strongly Zariski closed; this is the statement relating ECD's notion to Fargues–Scholze's Definition IV.4.20 on perfectoid targets. (c) Boundary: the proof of AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/affinoid-etale-finite-stage-6-4-iv does not use (b) — the closed immersions it needs are into the sousperfectoid ball B^N_X and are constructed as quotient mappings (A3/affinoid-etale-zariski-closed-embedding), and the transfer between characteristics is done on étale categories (A3/tilting-affinoid-etale-and-limits), not on Zariski closed immersions.
