nodes.title: Rings with no nonsplit finite étale covers
nodes.statement: Let R be a commutative ring. A finite étale R-algebra T (Mathlib `Algebra.Etale R T` together with `Module.Finite R T`) is *totally split* if there are finitely many idempotents e₁, …, e_m ∈ R (m ≥ 0, repetitions and zero allowed) and an isomorphism of R-algebras T ≅ ∏_{j=1}^{m} R/(1 − e_j)R. The ring R *has no nonsplit finite étale covers* (Lean: the class `IsFiniteEtaleSplit R`) if every finite étale R-algebra is totally split. Equivalent characterisation: every finite étale R-algebra T that is faithfully flat over R (Mathlib `Module.FaithfullyFlat R T`; for T finite étale this says that the rank of T is ≥ 1 at every prime of R) admits an R-algebra homomorphism T → R. Consequence used in ECD §15: if P ∈ R[X] is monic of degree d ≥ 1 and the class of P′ is a unit of R[X]/(P) (so that (P, 1) is a Mathlib `StandardEtalePair`), then P has a root in R, because R[X]/(P) is étale and free of rank d, hence a faithfully flat finite étale R-algebra. For a field K the condition is equivalent to K being separably closed (Mathlib `IsSepClosed K`). If a ring homomorphism φ : R → R′ induces, by base change, an equivalence between the categories of finite étale algebras, then R has no nonsplit finite étale covers if and only if R′ has none. Pinned conventions: 'split' means totally split over R itself (not after a further faithfully flat extension); the zero algebra is totally split (m = 0); no topology is involved.
hypotheses: R an arbitrary commutative ring; the zero ring is allowed (it has no nonsplit finite étale covers).
proofSteps: Totally split and faithfully flat implies a section: if T ≅ ∏_j R/(1 − e_j)R is faithfully flat then the open and closed sets D(e_j) cover Spec R (a prime outside all of them would have T ⊗ κ(p) = 0); refine them, inside the Boolean algebra of idempotents (mathlib:IsIdempotentElem), to orthogonal idempotents f_j with f_j e_j = f_j and Σ_j f_j = 1; then (r_j)_j ↦ Σ_j f_j r_j is an R-algebra homomorphism T → R.

Sections for faithfully flat algebras imply total splitting, by induction on the maximal rank n of T (T is finite projective, its rank function mathlib:Module.rankAtStalk is locally constant with finitely many values): let e be the idempotent of the locus where the rank is ≥ 1; T × R(1 − e) is a faithfully flat finite étale R-algebra, so it has an R-algebra section, whose e-component is a section σ : T → Re; T being étale, the kernel of σ is generated by an idempotent (the graph of a section of an étale separated morphism is open and closed), so T ≅ Re × T₁ with T₁ finite étale of maximal rank < n; apply the induction hypothesis to T₁.

Root criterion: mathlib:StandardEtalePair with g = 1 and the condition 'P′ invertible modulo P' gives mathlib:Algebra.IsStandardEtale, hence mathlib:Algebra.Etale, for R[X]/(P); mathlib:AdjoinRoot.powerBasis' makes it free of rank d ≥ 1, so faithfully flat; an R-algebra map R[X]/(P) → R is a root of P (mathlib:StandardEtalePair.homEquiv).

Fields: by mathlib:Algebra.Etale.iff_exists_algEquiv_prod an étale K-algebra is a finite product of finite separable field extensions; it is totally split iff every factor is K; so the condition says that K has no proper finite separable extension, which is mathlib:IsSepClosed (via mathlib:IsSepClosed.exists_root for the converse).

Transfer along an equivalence given by base change: idempotents of R are the R-algebra maps R × R → R, so the equivalence identifies idempotents of R and R′; a finite étale T is faithfully flat iff no nonzero idempotent e has Te = 0, so faithful flatness is preserved and reflected, and sections correspond by full faithfulness.
acceptance: IsFiniteEtaleSplit K ↔ IsSepClosed K for every field K; hence the algebraic closures of ℚ_p and 𝔽_p have no nonsplit finite étale covers, while ℚ_p and 𝔽_p do.

The ring of locally constant functions from a profinite set to a separably closed field has no nonsplit finite étale covers (it is a filtered colimit of finite products of that field; use AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/finite-etale-algebras-filtered-colimit).
Over a ring with no nonsplit finite étale covers every monic polynomial P with P′ a unit modulo P has a root; this is the only form in which ECD's proof of Lemma 15.3 uses the hypothesis.

nodes.title: Finite étale G-torsors of commutative rings
nodes.statement: Let G be a finite group, A a commutative ring and B a commutative A-algebra on which G acts by A-algebra automorphisms (Mathlib `MulSemiringAction G B` with `SMulCommClass G A B`). B is a *finite étale G-torsor over A* (Lean: `Algebra.IsFiniteEtaleTorsor G A B`) if B is a finite étale and faithfully flat A-algebra and the Galois map γ : B ⊗_A B → Map(G, B) = ∏_{g ∈ G} B, γ(b ⊗ b′)(g) = b·g(b′), is bijective (geometrically: Spec B → Spec A is a torsor under the constant finite group scheme G). Consequences: B is finite projective of constant rank |G|; A → B is injective and B^G = A (Mathlib `Algebra.IsInvariant A B G`); if A ≠ 0 the action is faithful, so Mathlib's `IsGaloisGroup G A B` holds; more generally γ induces B^{⊗(k+1)} ≅ Map(G^k, B) for k ≥ 0. Constructions: the trivial torsor Map(G, A) with (h·f)(g) = f(gh); the tensor product B ⊗_A B′ of a G-torsor and a G′-torsor is a (G × G′)-torsor; base change along any ring homomorphism A → A′ preserves torsors; if π : G′ → G is surjective and B → B′ is an A-algebra map from a G-torsor to a G′-torsor with g′·ι(b) = ι(π(g′)·b), then B′ is a (ker π)-torsor over B, so ι is faithfully flat and injective. For A = K a field and B a field, B is a G-torsor over K iff B/K is a finite Galois extension and G → Gal(B/K) is an isomorphism. Pinned conventions: G acts on the left; the Galois map is b ⊗ b′ ↦ (b·g(b′))_g; faithful flatness is part of the definition (this excludes B = 0 over A ≠ 0).
hypotheses: G finite; A, B commutative; G acts by A-algebra automorphisms of B.
proofSteps: Rank and projectivity: base change along the faithfully flat A → B turns B into Map(G, B) via γ, which is free of rank |G| over B; finiteness descends (mathlib:Module.Finite.of_finite_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat) and étaleness descends (mathlib:Algebra.Etale.of_etale_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat); the rank is read after base change.

Invariants: A → B is faithfully flat, so A is the equalizer of the two maps B ⇉ B ⊗_A B (faithfully flat descent, mathlib:comonadicExtendScalars); under γ these become b ↦ (b)_g and b ↦ (g(b))_g, so the equalizer is B^G, giving mathlib:Algebra.IsInvariant; if some g ≠ 1 acted trivially, the g- and 1-coordinates of γ would agree on the image, contradicting surjectivity unless B = 0, which faithful flatness excludes for A ≠ 0; this gives mathlib:IsGaloisGroup.
Iterated Galois maps, tensor products and base change: γ is compatible with base change and with tensor products; the iterate B^{⊗(k+1)} ≅ Map(G^k, B) follows by induction from γ.

Morphisms along a surjection π : G′ → G: after the faithfully flat base change A → B′ both B and B′ become trivial torsors Map(G, B′) and Map(G′, B′), and the map becomes pull-back along π up to a translation, which exhibits Map(G′, B′) as a (ker π)-torsor over Map(G, B′); descend along A → B′.
Fields: for B a field, γ bijective means B ⊗_K B ≅ B^{|G|}, i.e. B/K is Galois with |Aut_K(B)| = [B : K] = |G| and G acting faithfully (standard Galois theory).

nodes.title: Henselian pairs are stable under filtered colimits
nodes.statement: Let (R_i, I_i)_{i ∈ I} be a directed system of pairs (I a directed set; ring homomorphisms R_i → R_j carrying I_i into I_j) and R = colim R_i (Mathlib `Ring.DirectLimit`) with I ⊆ R the ideal generated by the images of the I_i (it equals colim I_i). If every (R_i, I_i) is henselian (Mathlib `HenselianRing R_i I_i`), then (R, I) is henselian. In particular, if ϖ ∈ R_{i₀} and every R_i (i ≥ i₀) is henselian along the ideal generated by the image of ϖ, then R is henselian along ϖR. Lean: `Ring.DirectLimit.henselianRing`.
hypotheses: I directed; the transition maps carry I_i into I_j.
proofSteps: Jacobson radical: an element of 1 + I comes from 1 + I_j for some j, which is a unit of R_j because I_j lies in the Jacobson radical of R_j (mathlib:HenselianRing, field jac; mathlib:Ideal.jacobson); its image is a unit of R.

Lifting of simple roots (Mathlib's form of the henselian condition): given f ∈ R[X] monic and a₀ ∈ R with f(a₀) ∈ I and f′(a₀) a unit modulo I, choose j such that f, a₀, an inverse of f′(a₀) modulo I and the witnesses of the two memberships in I all come from R_j (finitely many elements; mathlib:Ring.DirectLimit is a filtered colimit); apply the henselian property of (R_j, I_j) and map the root to R.
acceptance: The ring of integers of an algebraic closure of ℚ_p, a filtered colimit of p-adically complete rings, is henselian along p although it is not p-adically complete.

For a directed system of complete Tate rings A_i, the colimit of their power-bounded subrings A_i° is henselian along a pseudouniformizer coming from the base (used in AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/finite-etale-invariance-along-tower).

nodes.title: Finite étale algebras over a filtered colimit of rings descend to a finite stage
nodes.statement: Let (R_i)_{i ∈ I} be a directed system of commutative rings with colimit R = colim R_i (Mathlib `Ring.DirectLimit`). (a) Every finite étale R-algebra S is isomorphic to S_i ⊗_{R_i} R for some i and some finite étale R_i-algebra S_i. (b) For finite étale R_i-algebras S_i, T_i the natural map colim_{j ≥ i} Hom_{R_j}(S_i ⊗_{R_i} R_j, T_i ⊗_{R_i} R_j) → Hom_R(S_i ⊗_{R_i} R, T_i ⊗_{R_i} R) is bijective. Hence base change is an equivalence of categories 2-colim_i FÉt(R_i) → FÉt(R), compatible with tensor products. Consequently, a finite étale R_i-algebra that becomes faithfully flat, acquires an R-algebra section, or becomes totally split (AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/finite-etale-split-ring) over R already does so over some R_j. Lean: `Ring.DirectLimit.finiteEtaleEquivalence`.
hypotheses: I directed; no finiteness or noetherian hypothesis on the R_i.
proofSteps: Finite étale algebras are finitely presented (mathlib:Algebra.Etale includes finite presentation), so S descends to a finitely presented R_i-algebra S_i and morphisms between finitely presented algebras descend to a finite stage (EGA IV 8.8.2, as quoted in Kedlaya–Liu, Remark 1.2.9).
Finiteness and étaleness of S_i ⊗ R_j hold for j large (EGA IV 17.7.8(ii), loc. cit.).

Faithful flatness: the idempotent of R_i cutting out the rank-zero locus of S_i maps to 0 in R, hence in some R_j; sections and total splittings are finitely many morphisms and equations, hence defined at a finite stage.
acceptance: For R = the algebraic closure of 𝔽_p written as the colimit of the finite fields 𝔽_{p^{n!}}, a finite étale R-algebra (a finite power of R) is defined over some 𝔽_{p^{n!}}.

nodes.title: Every finite étale algebra is split by a finite étale torsor
nodes.statement: Let A be a commutative ring and S a finite étale A-algebra. There are a finite group G and a finite étale G-torsor A → P (AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/finite-etale-galois-torsor) such that S ⊗_A P is totally split over P (AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/finite-etale-split-ring). Explicitly: let n be the maximal rank of S and e_k ∈ A the idempotent of the locus where S has rank k; replace S by S′ := S × ∏_{k<n} (A/(1 − e_k))^{n−k}, finite étale of constant rank n; let δ ∈ S′ ⊗_A S′ be the idempotent with (S′ ⊗_A S′)δ ≅ S′ via multiplication (Mathlib `Algebra.TensorProduct.lmul'`), δ_{ab} (1 ≤ a < b ≤ n) its image in S′^{⊗n} under the (a, b)-th coprojection, ε := ∏_{a<b} (1 − δ_{ab}); then one may take G = S_n (Mathlib `Equiv.Perm (Fin n)`) permuting the tensor factors and P = ε·S′^{⊗n}, the algebra of ordered n-tuples of pairwise distinct points of the fibres of S′. Lean: `Algebra.exists_isFiniteEtaleTorsor_isTotallySplit`.
hypotheses: A arbitrary; S finite étale (finite, flat, finitely presented, unramified).
proofSteps: Constant rank: S is finite projective; its rank function (mathlib:Module.rankAtStalk) is locally constant with finitely many values, giving the idempotents e_k; S′ has constant rank n and S is a direct factor of S′.

Diagonal idempotent: S′ is unramified and finitely presented, so the kernel of multiplication S′ ⊗_A S′ → S′ (mathlib:Algebra.TensorProduct.lmul') is a finitely generated idempotent ideal, hence generated by an idempotent; this gives δ.

Geometric fibres: for every homomorphism A → k to a separably closed field, S′ ⊗ k ≅ k^n and ε cuts out of (S′ ⊗ k)^{⊗n} ≅ k^{Map(n,n)} the factors indexed by injective, hence bijective, maps; so P ⊗ k ≅ k^{S_n} with S_n acting simply transitively.

P is finite étale over A (a direct factor of the finite étale S′^{⊗n}; mathlib:Algebra.Etale.comp, mathlib:Algebra.Etale.baseChange) of constant rank n! ≥ 1, hence faithfully flat; the Galois map P ⊗_A P → Map(S_n, P) is a homomorphism of finite projective P-modules of equal rank that is an isomorphism on every geometric fibre, hence an isomorphism (Nakayama).

The universal frame S′ ⊗_A P → P^n (the a-th coordinate sends s to the image of s in the a-th tensor factor) is likewise an isomorphism on geometric fibres, hence an isomorphism; S ⊗_A P is a direct factor of P^n, hence totally split (API Algebra.IsTotallySplit.quotient_idempotent of AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/finite-etale-split-ring).
acceptance: A = ℚ, S = ℚ(∛2): n = 3 and P is the S₃-torsor ℚ(∛2, ζ₃) (of rank 6 = 3!), the Galois closure.
S = A × A: n = 2 and P ≅ A × A with S₂ exchanging the factors (the trivial torsor).

nodes.title: The cofiltered system of finite étale torsors with no remaining nonsplit finite étale covers (ECD Lemma 15.3, first part)
nodes.statement: Let A be a commutative ring. A *finite étale torsor tower* over A (Lean: the structure `FiniteEtaleTorsorTower A`) consists of a directed set I; for i ∈ I a finite group G_i and an A-algebra A_i with a G_i-action making it a finite étale G_i-torsor over A (AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/finite-etale-galois-torsor); for i ≤ j a surjective homomorphism π_{ij} : G_j → G_i and an A-algebra homomorphism ι_{ij} : A_i → A_j with ι_{ij}(π_{ij}(g)·a) = g·ι_{ij}(a), both functorial in i ≤ j ≤ k (π_{ii} = id, π_{ik} = π_{ij} ∘ π_{jk}, and likewise for ι); such that the direct limit A_∞ := colim_i A_i (Mathlib `Ring.DirectLimit`) has no nonsplit finite étale covers (AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/finite-etale-split-ring). Its group is the profinite group G := lim_i G_i (Mathlib `ProfiniteGrp`), which acts on A_∞ by A-algebra automorphisms with open stabilisers. Construction (Lean: `FiniteEtaleTorsorTower.canonical A`), showing that every ring has a tower: choose a set T of representatives of the isomorphism classes of finite étale A-algebras and, for each S ∈ T, a splitting torsor A → P(S) under a finite group G(S) (AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/splitting-torsor-of-finite-etale-algebra); index by the finite subsets F ⊆ T ordered by inclusion, with G_F := ∏_{S ∈ F} G(S), A_F := ⊗_{S ∈ F} P(S) (tensor product over A; A_∅ = A), π the projections and ι the inclusions of tensor factors. Properties: every finite étale A-algebra becomes totally split over some A_i; A_j is a (ker π_{ij})-torsor over A_i, so all transition maps are injective and faithfully flat; (A_∞)^G = A; and a ⊗ b ↦ (g ↦ a·g(b)) is an isomorphism A_∞ ⊗_A A_∞ ≅ LC(G, A_∞) onto the locally constant maps (Mathlib `LocallyConstant`). Pinned conventions: G_i acts on the left and π_{ij} goes from the larger index to the smaller; no topology is involved (the topological completion is AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/completed-tower-pair).
hypotheses: A an arbitrary commutative ring (the torsor tower is purely algebraic).
proofSteps: The isomorphism classes of finite étale A-algebras form a set (each is a quotient of a polynomial ring in finitely many variables), so T exists.

Levels: a tensor product of torsors is a torsor for the product group (API tensor of AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/finite-etale-galois-torsor); the inclusions of tensor factors are equivariant along the projections of product groups, and the projections are surjective.

Splitting: let C be a finite étale A_∞-algebra. By AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/finite-etale-algebras-filtered-colimit C ≅ C_F ⊗_{A_F} A_∞ with C_F finite étale over A_F, hence over A (mathlib:Algebra.Etale.comp); so C_F ≅ S for some S ∈ T. For F′ = F ∪ {S}, S ⊗_A A_{F′} is totally split (AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/splitting-torsor-of-finite-etale-algebra); C_F ⊗_{A_F} A_{F′} is the quotient of S ⊗_A A_{F′} = C_F ⊗_{A_F} (A_F ⊗_A A_{F′}) by the idempotent of the multiplication map A_F ⊗_A A_{F′} → A_{F′} (a section of an étale algebra), hence totally split; base change to A_∞ keeps it totally split.
Transition maps: API of_surjective of AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/finite-etale-galois-torsor.

Invariants and the pro-torsor isomorphism: pass to the colimit in A_i^{G_i} = A and in the Galois maps A_i ⊗_A A_i ≅ Map(G_i, A_i); the colimit of Map(G_i, A_i) is LC(G, A_∞) (mathlib:LocallyConstant).
acceptance: A = 𝔽_p: the finite fields 𝔽_{p^{n!}} with G = ℤ/n! form a tower (colimit 𝔽̄_p, separably closed), with G = ℤ̂.
The canonical tower exists for every ring, including rings with infinitely many idempotents.

nodes.title: Uniformization of a complete Tate pair does not change its adic spectrum or its finite étale algebras
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a Huber pair (Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair`) with A a complete Hausdorff Tate ring, and let ι : (A, A⁺) → (A^u, A^{u+}) be its uniformization (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniformization: A^u is the separated completion of A for its spectral seminorm, A^{u+} the closure of the image of A⁺). Then: (i) Spa(ι) : Spa(A^u, A^{u+}) → Spa(A, A⁺) is a homeomorphism under which rational subsets correspond (the clause (d) of AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniformization, restated); (ii) base change B ↦ B ⊗_A A^u is an equivalence of categories FÉt(A) → FÉt(A^u) between finite étale algebras, compatible with tensor products; it preserves and reflects faithful flatness and ranks, and induces bijections Hom_A(B, A) ≅ Hom_{A^u}(B ⊗_A A^u, A^u) and between the idempotents of A and of A^u; (iii) for B ∈ FÉt(A) with its Huber pair (B, B⁺) (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra: natural topology, B⁺ the integral closure of A⁺), the pair (B ⊗_A A^u, integral closure of A^{u+}) with its natural topology is uniform and is the uniformization of (B, B⁺); (iv) A has no nonsplit finite étale covers (AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/finite-etale-split-ring) if and only if A^u has none. Lean: `Huber.Pair.uniformization.baseChange_finiteEtale_equivalence` (for (ii); (i), (iii), (iv) are its companion statements `spaComap_homeomorph`, `finiteEtale_uniformization`, `isFiniteEtaleSplit_iff`). Completeness of A is a hypothesis: for the non-complete Tate ring ℚ_p[T] (ring of definition ℤ_p[T], p-adic topology), whose uniformization is ℚ_p⟨T⟩, the finite étale ℚ_p⟨T⟩-algebra ℚ_p⟨T⟩[X]/(X^p − X − T/p) is not the base change of any finite étale ℚ_p[T]-algebra.
hypotheses: A complete Hausdorff Tate ring; A⁺ any ring of integral elements.
Finite étale means finite étale as rings (Mathlib Algebra.Etale and Module.Finite); the topology on B is the natural one.
proofSteps: (i) is AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniformization (d).

(ii): with a norm datum (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/tate-ring-norm) A is a Banach ring in Kedlaya–Liu's sense, and A^u is Kedlaya–Liu's uniformization (Definition 2.8.13), so Kedlaya–Liu Proposition 2.8.16(a) gives the tensor equivalence. Its proof: write (A, A⁺) as the completed direct limit of an affinoid system (A_α) (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/affinoid-system-approximation); the reduced quotients of the A_α with their spectral norms form an affinoid system with completed direct limit A^u, with FÉt unchanged by passing to the reduced quotient (a henselian pair, Kedlaya–Liu Theorem 1.2.8); and AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-approximation (Kedlaya–Liu Proposition 2.6.8) identifies FÉt of both completed limits with the 2-colimits. The same equivalence follows from the topologically henselian comparison: the spectral topology (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-topology) has the ring of definition A° with the ϖ-adic topology; A° is henselian along ϖ because A is complete (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:henselian/henselian-f-adic-rings-and-henselization); and A^u is the completion of A for that topology, so the equivalence FÉt(A) ≅ FÉt(A^u) is the Tate-ring form of the henselian finite étale comparison requested from PerfectoidSpaces:P3.

Faithful flatness, ranks, sections and idempotents: formal consequences of a tensor equivalence that sends A to A^u (API IsFiniteEtaleSplit.of_baseChange_equivalence of AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/finite-etale-split-ring).

(iii): Kedlaya–Liu Proposition 2.8.16(b): the maximal power-multiplicative seminorm on B ⊗_A A^u is equivalent to its natural norm, so B ⊗_A A^u is uniform; it receives (B, B⁺) and is initial among complete uniform targets by the universal property of uniformization (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniformization (c)) and the universal property of the finite algebra (A1).
(iv) is (ii) combined with IsFiniteEtaleSplit.of_baseChange_equivalence.

Non-example: T/p is not in ℚ_p⟨T⟩°, and the discriminant of X^p − X − T/p is ±(pT^{p−1} − (p−1)^{p−1}), a unit of ℚ_p⟨T⟩ but not of ℚ_p[T]; the fibre of the cover over T = 0 is split and over T = p it is the unramified extension of degree p (the reduction X^p − X − 1 is irreducible over 𝔽_p), whereas every finite étale ℚ_p[T]-algebra is L₁[T] × ⋯ × L_r[T] for finite extensions L_j of ℚ_p (the geometric fundamental group of the affine line in characteristic 0 is trivial), whose fibres over ℚ_p-points are all isomorphic.
acceptance: For (A, A⁺) = (ℚ_p⟨T⟩[ε]/(ε²), ℤ_p⟨T⟩ + ε·ℚ_p⟨T⟩) with the product topology, A^u = ℚ_p⟨T⟩ and FÉt(A) ≅ FÉt(ℚ_p⟨T⟩) (a nilpotent thickening).
For A uniform the theorem is trivial (ι is an isomorphism, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniformization (e)).
Completeness cannot be dropped: the ℚ_p[T] example of the statement.

nodes.title: The uniform completion (Â_∞, Â_∞⁺) of a finite étale torsor tower over a complete Tate pair
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a Huber pair with A a complete Hausdorff Tate ring, ϖ ∈ A a pseudouniformizer, and T a finite étale torsor tower over the ring A (AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/finite-etale-torsor-tower) with levels A_i, groups G_i and G = lim G_i. (a) Levels: (A_i, A_i⁺) is the Huber pair of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra (A_i with its natural topology as a finite projective A-module, a complete Tate ring; A_i⁺ the integral closure of A⁺ in A_i); the transition maps ι_{ij} and the action of G_i are morphisms of Huber pairs. (b) Colimit: A_∞ = colim A_i carries the unique ring topology in which A_∞^♮ := colim_i A_i° (a subring, A_i° the power-bounded subring, Tau Ceti `powerBoundedSubring`) is open and carries its ϖ-adic topology; with A_∞⁺ := colim_i A_i⁺ this is a Tate Huber pair (A_∞, A_∞⁺) with ring of definition A_∞^♮, and it is uniform: A_∞° ⊆ ϖ⁻¹A_∞^♮. (c) Completion: the completed tower pair is (Â_∞, Â_∞⁺) := the uniformization (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniformization) of (A_∞, A_∞⁺); since A_∞ is uniform it is the Hausdorff completion (Tau Ceti `IsTateRing.completion`), Â_∞ is a complete uniform Tate ring with ring of definition the ϖ-adic completion of A_∞^♮, and Â_∞⁺ is the closure of the image of colim_i A_i⁺ — this is ECD's 'uniform completion Â_∞ of A_∞' with 'Â_∞⁺ the closure of lim A_i⁺'. (d) G acts on (Â_∞, Â_∞⁺) by automorphisms of Huber pairs over (A, A⁺), continuously (the action map G × Â_∞ → Â_∞ is continuous for the profinite topology of G). (e) Universal property: for every complete Hausdorff Huber pair (B, B⁺) with B° bounded, morphisms of Huber pairs (Â_∞, Â_∞⁺) → (B, B⁺) correspond bijectively to families of morphisms (A_i, A_i⁺) → (B, B⁺) compatible with the ι_{ij}. Lean: `FiniteEtaleTorsorTower.completion T P` for P the Huber pair (A, A⁺). Pinned conventions: the colimit topology is the one of the Berkeley lectures (colim A_i° open and bounded), not the colimit of chosen rings of definition; completeness of A is part of the hypotheses (it is needed for the levels (a) and for AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/finite-etale-invariance-along-tower).
hypotheses: A complete Hausdorff Tate ring with a ring of integral elements A⁺; ϖ ∈ A a pseudouniformizer.
T a finite étale torsor tower over the underlying ring of A.
proofSteps: (a) is AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra applied to the finite étale A-algebras A_i; A-algebra maps between them are continuous for the natural topologies and preserve integral closures of A⁺.

(b) A_∞^♮ is a subring because the ι_{ij} are continuous and so map A_i° into A_j°; it contains ϖ, and A_∞^♮[1/ϖ] = A_∞ because each A_i = A_i°[1/ϖ]. Declaring {ϖ^n A_∞^♮} a basis of neighbourhoods of 0 gives a Tate ring (Tau Ceti `IsTateRing`: ring of definition A_∞^♮, pseudouniformizer ϖ). A_∞⁺ is open (it contains ϖA_∞^♮: ϖ times a power-bounded element of A_i is topologically nilpotent, hence in A_i⁺ by tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.mem_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent_of_isIntegrallyClosedIn) and integrally closed (a colimit of integrally closed subrings). Uniformity: if x ∈ A_∞ is power-bounded then ϖx is topologically nilpotent, so (ϖx)^m ∈ ϖA_∞^♮ for some m and ϖx is integral over A_∞^♮, which is integrally closed in A_∞ (a colimit of the integrally closed A_i° ⊆ A_i); hence ϖx ∈ A_∞^♮.

(c) For a uniform Tate ring the spectral topology is the given one (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-topology (vi)), so the uniformization is the Hausdorff completion; its plus ring is the closure of the image of A_∞⁺ by definition.

(d) Each g ∈ G maps A_∞^♮ onto itself, so G acts by homeomorphisms that extend to Â_∞ and preserve Â_∞⁺; continuity of G × Â_∞ → Â_∞: an element of Â_∞ is within ϖ^n Â_∞^♮ of some x ∈ A_i, which is fixed by the open subgroup ker(G → G_i), and G preserves ϖ^n Â_∞^♮.

(e) A compatible family A_i → B sends A_i° into B° (continuous maps preserve power-boundedness), hence A_∞^♮ into B°, whose ϖ-multiples form a basis of neighbourhoods of 0 since B° is open (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.isOpen_powerBoundedSubring) and bounded; so the induced A_∞ → B is continuous, and it extends uniquely to Â_∞ by the universal property of uniformization (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniformization (c)).
acceptance: For (A, A⁺) = (ℚ_p, ℤ_p) and a tower whose levels are finite Galois extensions of ℚ_p exhausting an algebraic closure (a valid tower, the colimit being separably closed), (Â_∞, Â_∞⁺) = (ℂ_p, 𝒪_{ℂ_p}) and G = Gal(ℚ̄_p/ℚ_p).
For the trivial tower over a complete uniform pair with no nonsplit finite étale covers, (Â_∞, Â_∞⁺) = (A, A⁺).

nodes.title: Finite étale algebras are unchanged along the completed torsor tower
nodes.statement: In the situation of AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/completed-tower-pair ((A, A⁺) complete Tate, T a finite étale torsor tower, (Â_∞, Â_∞⁺) its completion): (i) the base change functors 2-colim_i FÉt(A_i) → FÉt(A_∞) → FÉt(Â_∞) are equivalences of categories, compatible with tensor products, preserving and reflecting faithful flatness; (ii) for k = 1, 2, let C^0(G^k, Â_∞) be the ring of continuous maps G^k → Â_∞ (Mathlib `ContinuousMap`, topology of uniform convergence), which is the completion of colim_i Map(G_i^k, A_i) = LC(G^k, A_∞) for the topology with ring of definition LC(G^k, A_∞^♮); then 2-colim_i FÉt(Map(G_i^k, A_i)) → FÉt(C^0(G^k, Â_∞)) is an equivalence; (iii) Â_∞ has no nonsplit finite étale covers (AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/finite-etale-split-ring). The rings of definition colim_i A_i° and LC(G^k, colim_i A_i°) are henselian along ϖ. Lean: `FiniteEtaleTorsorTower.completion_finiteEtale_equivalence` (with `completion_isFiniteEtaleSplit` for (iii)).
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) complete Hausdorff Tate; T any finite étale torsor tower over A.
proofSteps: Each A_i is a complete Tate ring (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra), so (A_i°, ϖA_i°) is a henselian pair (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:henselian/henselian-f-adic-rings-and-henselization: complete f-adic rings are henselian; A_i° is an open subring of A_i° and ϖA_i° ⊆ A_i°°). In the Tate case this is also direct: A_i° is the directed union of the rings of definition A_{i,0}[b₁, …, b_r], each ϖ-adically complete (Mathlib's instance IsAdicComplete.henselianRing in Mathlib/RingTheory/Henselian.lean), and AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/henselian-pairs-filtered-colimit applies.
colim_i A_i° is henselian along ϖ by AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/henselian-pairs-filtered-colimit.

A_∞ is a Tate ring whose ring of definition colim A_i° is henselian along ϖ, and its completion is Â_∞ (AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/completed-tower-pair (c)); the topologically henselian comparison (Berkeley lectures Theorem 7.4.8; Gabber–Ramero; requested in this generality from PerfectoidSpaces:P3) gives FÉt(A_∞) ≅ FÉt(Â_∞).
2-colim FÉt(A_i) ≅ FÉt(A_∞): AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/finite-etale-algebras-filtered-colimit.

(ii): the same three steps for the directed system R_i = Map(G_i^k, A_i) (finite products of complete Tate rings, power-bounded subring Map(G_i^k, A_i°)); its colimit is LC(G^k, A_∞) and the completion is C^0(G^k, Â_∞), because locally constant maps are dense in continuous maps from a profinite set to a complete ring for the uniform topology.

(iii): A_∞ has no nonsplit finite étale covers (AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/finite-etale-torsor-tower), and (i) is an equivalence given by base change, so API IsFiniteEtaleSplit.of_baseChange_equivalence of AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/finite-etale-split-ring transfers the property.
acceptance: For the ℚ_p tower with Â_∞ = ℂ_p: every finite étale ℂ_p-algebra is split, as it must be (ℂ_p is algebraically closed).

Without completeness of A the lemma fails: over ℚ_p[T] every tower has colimit (ℚ_p-algebra B)[T] with B split, and its completion B̂⟨T⟩ has nonsplit finite étale covers (AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/perfectoid-uniform-completion, acceptance).

nodes.title: Finite étale algebras descend effectively along the completed torsor tower
nodes.statement: In the situation of AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/finite-etale-invariance-along-tower, put C₁ := C^0(G, Â_∞) and C₂ := C^0(G × G, Â_∞), let s, t : Â_∞ → C₁ be s(b)(g) = b and t(b)(g) = g·b, and let d₀, d₁, d₂ : C₁ → C₂ be the face maps (d₀f)(g, h) = g·f(h), (d₁f)(g, h) = f(gh), (d₂f)(g, h) = f(g) (under AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/completed-tower-self-product these are the three coprojections of the uniform completed tensor powers, with b ⊗ b′ ↦ (g ↦ b·g(b′)) and b ⊗ b′ ⊗ b″ ↦ ((g, h) ↦ b·g(b′)·(gh)(b″))). A descent datum on B̂ ∈ FÉt(Â_∞) is an isomorphism of C₁-algebras φ : B̂ ⊗_{Â_∞, s} C₁ ≅ B̂ ⊗_{Â_∞, t} C₁ satisfying the cocycle condition over C₂. Then B ↦ (B ⊗_A Â_∞, canonical φ) is an equivalence from FÉt(A) to the category of finite étale Â_∞-algebras with descent data. Equivalently, FÉt(A) is equivalent to the category of finite étale Â_∞-algebras B̂ with a semilinear action of G extending the action on Â_∞ that is continuous for the natural topology of B̂. Lean: `FiniteEtaleTorsorTower.completion_finiteEtale_descent`.
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) complete Hausdorff Tate; T a finite étale torsor tower over A.
proofSteps: At a finite level, the Galois maps identify Map(G_i, A_i) and Map(G_i², A_i) with A_i ⊗_A A_i and A_i ⊗_A A_i ⊗_A A_i (API iterGaloisMap of AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/finite-etale-galois-torsor), compatibly with the face maps; these systems have colimits LC(G, A_∞), LC(G², A_∞) with completions C₁, C₂.

By AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/finite-etale-invariance-along-tower (i)–(ii), applied compatibly to Â_∞, C₁, C₂, a finite étale Â_∞-algebra with descent datum is the base change of a finite étale A_i-algebra B_i with a descent datum relative to A → A_i, for i large, and morphisms of descent data come from a finite level.

A → A_i is faithfully flat (AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/finite-etale-galois-torsor), so descent data for modules are effective (mathlib:comonadicExtendScalars), the algebra structure descends with them, and the descended algebra is finite (mathlib:Module.Finite.of_finite_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat) and étale (mathlib:Algebra.Etale.of_etale_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat); Kedlaya–Liu Theorems 1.3.4–1.3.5.
Full faithfulness is the same argument for morphisms.
The action form: under C₁ = C^0(G, Â_∞) a descent datum is a family of g-semilinear bijections of B̂ varying continuously with g, and the cocycle condition is the action axiom.
acceptance: For the ℚ_p tower (Â_∞ = ℂ_p, G = Gal(ℚ̄_p/ℚ_p)): finite étale ℚ_p-algebras are equivalent to finite products of ℂ_p with a continuous semilinear G-action permuting the factors (continuity forces the action to factor through a finite quotient on the set of factors), recovering finite étale ℚ_p-algebras as finite G-sets.

nodes.title: Roots of monic polynomials with invertible derivative over a complete Tate ring without nonsplit covers
nodes.statement: Let R be a complete Hausdorff Tate ring with no nonsplit finite étale covers (AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/finite-etale-split-ring), P ∈ R°[X] monic of degree d ≥ 1, B := R[X]/(P) with its natural topology (as a free R-module of rank d with basis 1, x, …, x^{d−1}, x the class of X). Then x is power-bounded in B. If moreover P′(x) = u·(1 − τ) in B with u ∈ R^× and τ ∈ B topologically nilpotent, then B is a finite étale R-algebra (the standard étale algebra of the pair (P, 1), Mathlib `StandardEtalePair`), faithfully flat, and P has a root in R; every root of P in R lies in R°. Lean: `Huber.exists_root_of_derivative_eq_unit_mul_one_sub`.
hypotheses: R complete Hausdorff Tate; P monic with coefficients in R°; d ≥ 1.
proofSteps: B is free with basis 1, …, x^{d−1} (mathlib:AdjoinRoot.powerBasis'), so with the product topology it is a complete Hausdorff Tate ring; x satisfies a monic equation with coefficients in R°, so the powers of x lie in the R°-span of 1, …, x^{d−1}, which is bounded; hence x is power-bounded (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsPowerBounded).

1 − τ is a unit of B (tauceti:IsTopologicallyNilpotent.isUnit_one_sub, B complete nonarchimedean), so P′(x) is a unit of B = R[X]/(P); hence (P, 1) is a mathlib:StandardEtalePair and B is étale (mathlib:Algebra.IsStandardEtale).

B is free of rank d ≥ 1, hence faithfully flat, so it has an R-algebra section (API isFiniteEtaleSplit_iff_exists_section of AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/finite-etale-split-ring), i.e. a root of P (mathlib:StandardEtalePair.homEquiv).
A root r ∈ R of a monic polynomial over R° is power-bounded by the same span argument, so r ∈ R°.

nodes.title: A pseudouniformizer whose p-th power divides p, from a root of x^{p^n} − ϖ₀x − ϖ₀
nodes.statement: Let R be a complete Hausdorff Tate ring in which p is topologically nilpotent and which has no nonsplit finite étale covers, and let ϖ₀ ∈ R be a pseudouniformizer (Tau Ceti `IsPseudoUniformizer`). Choose n ≥ 1 with p^n ∈ ϖ₀R° and p^{n−1} > n (possible: p^n → 0 and ϖ₀R° is open). Then P(X) = X^{p^n} − ϖ₀X − ϖ₀ has a root in R, and every root ϖ satisfies: ϖ ∈ R° is a pseudouniformizer of R; ϖ^{p^n} = ϖ₀(1 + ϖ) with 1 + ϖ ∈ (R°)^×, so ϖ^{p^n} and ϖ₀ divide each other in R°; ϖ^p divides p in R°; and p/ϖ^p is topologically nilpotent. Lean: `Huber.exists_isPseudoUniformizer_pow_dvd_p`.
hypotheses: R complete Hausdorff Tate, p topologically nilpotent, no nonsplit finite étale covers.
proofSteps: In B = R[X]/(P), x is power-bounded (AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/root-of-monic-in-split-tate-ring) and x^{p^n} = ϖ₀(1 + x) ∈ ϖ₀B°, so x is topologically nilpotent.

P′(x) = p^n x^{p^n−1} − ϖ₀ = −ϖ₀(1 − c·x^{p^n−1}) with c = p^n/ϖ₀ ∈ R°; τ = c·x^{p^n−1} is topologically nilpotent (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsPowerBounded.isTopologicallyNilpotent_mul); AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/root-of-monic-in-split-tate-ring gives a root ϖ ∈ R°.

ϖ^{p^n} = ϖ₀(1 + ϖ) ∈ ϖ₀R° shows ϖ topologically nilpotent, so 1 + ϖ is a unit of R° (geometric series, tauceti:IsTopologicallyNilpotent.isUnit_one_add, with R° closed); ϖ is a unit of R because ϖ₀ is.
p^n = ϖ₀c = ϖ^{p^n}w with w ∈ R°; y := p/ϖ^p satisfies y^n = ϖ^{p^n − pn}w with p^n − pn > 0, so y^n and hence y is topologically nilpotent; in particular y ∈ R° and p = ϖ^p·y.
acceptance: R = ℂ_p, ϖ₀ = p, n = 2 (p odd; n = 3 for p = 2): a root ϖ of X^{p²} − pX − p has |ϖ| = |p|^{1/p²}, so |ϖ^p| = |p|^{1/p} and |p/ϖ^p| < 1.
The strict inequality p^{n−1} > n (not ECD's p^{n−1} ≥ n) is what makes p/ϖ^p topologically nilpotent, which the Frobenius step needs (Berkeley lectures, proof of Lemma 10.1.6).

nodes.title: Surjectivity of Frobenius modulo ϖ^p from roots of x^p − ϖ^p x − f
nodes.statement: Let R be a complete Hausdorff Tate ring with no nonsplit finite étale covers and ϖ ∈ R a pseudouniformizer with ϖ^p | p in R° and p/ϖ^p topologically nilpotent. Then for every f ∈ R° there is x ∈ R° with x^p − ϖ^p x = f; consequently Φ : R°/ϖ → R°/ϖ^p, x ↦ x^p (a ring homomorphism since p ∈ ϖ^pR°), is surjective. Lean: `Huber.frobenius_surjective_of_isFiniteEtaleSplit`.
hypotheses: R complete Hausdorff Tate without nonsplit finite étale covers; ϖ^p | p and p/ϖ^p topologically nilpotent.
proofSteps: P(X) = X^p − ϖ^pX − f ∈ R°[X] is monic; in B = R[X]/(P), P′(x) = px^{p−1} − ϖ^p = −ϖ^p(1 − (p/ϖ^p)x^{p−1}); x is power-bounded (AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/root-of-monic-in-split-tate-ring) and p/ϖ^p is topologically nilpotent, so τ = (p/ϖ^p)x^{p−1} is topologically nilpotent (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsPowerBounded.isTopologicallyNilpotent_mul).
AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/root-of-monic-in-split-tate-ring gives a root x₀ ∈ R°, and x₀^p = f + ϖ^p x₀ ≡ f modulo ϖ^pR°.
acceptance: The hypothesis that p/ϖ^p be topologically nilpotent is needed for the étaleness step. Over the perfectoid field K = the completion of ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞}) with ϖ = p^{1/p} (so p/ϖ^p = 1) and f = 1 − p, the polynomial X^p − ϖ^pX − f = X^p − pX + p − 1 has the double root 1 (P(1) = 0 = P′(1)), so K[X]/(P) is not étale; ECD's proof as printed asserts étaleness without this hypothesis (sourceIssues AdicEtaleGeometry/E20).
For R = ℂ_p and ϖ = p^{1/(p+1)}: every element of 𝒪_{ℂ_p} is a p-th power modulo ϖ^p.

nodes.title: The uniform completion of a finite étale torsor tower over a complete Tate ℤ_p-algebra is perfectoid (ECD Lemma 15.3, second part)
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a Huber pair with A a complete Hausdorff Tate ring in which p is topologically nilpotent (a complete Tate ℤ_p-algebra), T a finite étale torsor tower over A (AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/finite-etale-torsor-tower) and (Â_∞, Â_∞⁺) its completed tower pair (AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/completed-tower-pair). Then Â_∞ is a perfectoid Tate ring (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras); explicitly, Â_∞ contains a pseudouniformizer ϖ, a root of X^{p^n} − ϖ₀X − ϖ₀ for any pseudouniformizer ϖ₀ of A and n with p^n ∈ ϖ₀Â_∞° and p^{n−1} > n, such that ϖ^p | p in Â_∞°, p/ϖ^p is topologically nilpotent and Φ : Â_∞°/ϖ → Â_∞°/ϖ^p is bijective. So (Â_∞, Â_∞⁺) is a perfectoid Huber pair with a continuous action of the profinite group G. Completeness of A cannot be omitted: for the non-complete Tate ℤ_p-algebra ℚ_p[T] (ring of definition ℤ_p[T], p-adic topology) every tower has colimit B[T] with B = colim of finite étale ℚ_p-algebras, and the completion B̂⟨T⟩ is not perfectoid (T is not a p-th power modulo ϖ^p at any point), contrary to ECD Lemma 15.3 as stated for all Tate ℤ_p-algebras (sourceIssues AdicEtaleGeometry/E19). Lean: `FiniteEtaleTorsorTower.completion_isPerfectoid`.
hypotheses: A complete Hausdorff Tate ring with p topologically nilpotent; A⁺ any ring of integral elements; T any finite étale torsor tower over A.
proofSteps: Â_∞ is complete, Hausdorff and uniform (AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/completed-tower-pair (c)), and p is topologically nilpotent in Â_∞ (A → Â_∞ is continuous).
Â_∞ has no nonsplit finite étale covers (AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/finite-etale-invariance-along-tower (iii)).
AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/split-tate-ring-is-perfectoid applies; ϖ₀ may be taken in A because a pseudouniformizer of A maps to one of Â_∞.

The non-example: finite étale ℚ_p[T]-algebras are L₁[T] × ⋯ × L_r[T] (the affine line over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 is simply connected), so A_∞ = B[T] with B a colimit of finite étale ℚ_p-algebras; colim A_i° = B°[T], and the completion is B̂⟨T⟩; at a point of Spa(B̂) with completed residue field K, T ∈ K°⟨T⟩ is not a p-th power modulo the maximal ideal of K° (the reduction T is not a p-th power in k[T]).
acceptance: (ℚ_p, ℤ_p): Â_∞ = ℂ_p for the tower of finite Galois extensions, a perfectoid field.

(ℚ_p⟨T⟩, ℤ_p⟨T⟩): Â_∞ is perfectoid and contains, for every pseudouniformizer ϖ as above, compatible approximate p-power roots of T (Frobenius surjective modulo ϖ^p), although ℚ_p⟨T⟩ itself is not perfectoid.

nodes.title: The adic spectrum of a finite étale G-torsor is a G-quotient of the adic spectrum of the torsor
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a Huber pair with A a complete Hausdorff Tate ring, A → B a finite étale G-torsor (AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/finite-etale-galois-torsor) and (B, B⁺) its Huber pair (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra); G acts on (B, B⁺) by automorphisms of Huber pairs over (A, A⁺), hence on Spa(B, B⁺) by (g·y)(b) = y(g⁻¹b). Let q : Spa(B, B⁺) → Spa(A, A⁺) be the induced map (Tau Ceti `spaComap`). Then q is continuous, spectral, open and surjective, its fibres are exactly the G-orbits, and the preimage of the rational subset R(T/s) of Spa(A, A⁺) is the rational subset R(T/s) of Spa(B, B⁺); hence q induces a homeomorphism |Spa(B, B⁺)|/G ≅ |Spa(A, A⁺)| (quotient topology). Lean: `ValuationSpectrum.spaComap_quotientHomeomorph_of_isFiniteEtaleTorsor`.
hypotheses: A complete Hausdorff Tate; B a finite étale G-torsor over A with its natural topology and integral plus ring.
proofSteps: Continuity, equivariance and rational preimages: tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.continuous_spaComap and tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spaComap_preimage_rationalSubset; spectrality follows since preimages of rational (quasi-compact open) subsets are rational.

Surjectivity: B is faithfully flat over A (a torsor), so Spa(B, B⁺) → Spa(A, A⁺) is surjective (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra (iii)). Openness: a faithfully finite étale morphism of adic Banach rings induces an open map of adic spectra (Kedlaya–Liu Lemma 8.2.17(b), as used in the proof of their Lemma 9.1.9).

Fibres are orbits: B ⊗_A B is complete for its natural topology and equals the completed tensor product B ⊗̂_A B (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-algebra-tensor-complete (ii), B being finite projective), and the Galois map identifies it with ∏_{g∈G} B, whose adic spectrum is the disjoint union of |G| copies of Spa(B, B⁺), the g-th copy mapping to Spa(B) × Spa(B) by y ↦ (y, g⁻¹·y). Given y, y′ with q(y) = q(y′), Huber's valuation argument (Huber 1994, proof of Lemma 3.9(i)) produces a point of Spa(B ⊗̂_A B) lying over (y, y′); so y′ = g⁻¹·y for some g.
A continuous open surjection whose fibres are the orbits of a group action induces a homeomorphism from the orbit space.
acceptance: A = ℚ_p, B = ℚ_p(μ_p), G = (ℤ/p)^×: Spa(B, 𝒪_B) and Spa(A, ℤ_p) are points and the fibre is the single orbit.
For the trivial torsor B = Map(G, A), Spa(B) = G × Spa(A) and q is the projection.

nodes.title: The adic spectrum of the completed tower is the limit of the levels and a G-quotient onto Spa(A, A⁺)
nodes.statement: In the situation of AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/completed-tower-pair: (i) the maps Spa(Â_∞, Â_∞⁺) → Spa(A_i, A_i⁺) induce a homeomorphism |Spa(Â_∞, Â_∞⁺)| ≅ lim_i |Spa(A_i, A_i⁺)| of spectral spaces, and every rational subset of Spa(Â_∞, Â_∞⁺) is the preimage of a rational subset of some Spa(A_i, A_i⁺); (ii) q_∞ : Spa(Â_∞, Â_∞⁺) → Spa(A, A⁺) is continuous, spectral, open, surjective and G-equivariant, its fibres are exactly the G-orbits, and it induces a homeomorphism |Spa(Â_∞, Â_∞⁺)|/G ≅ |Spa(A, A⁺)|. Lean: `FiniteEtaleTorsorTower.spa_completion_homeomorph_limit` and `FiniteEtaleTorsorTower.spa_completion_quotientHomeomorph`.
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) complete Hausdorff Tate; T a finite étale torsor tower over A.
proofSteps: Spa(Â_∞, Â_∞⁺) = Spa(A_∞, A_∞⁺), since (Â_∞, Â_∞⁺) is the uniformization (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniformization (d)).

Spa(A_∞, A_∞⁺) → lim Spa(A_i, A_i⁺) is bijective: a valuation on A_∞ is the same as a compatible family of valuations on the A_i (A_∞ is their colimit); it is ≤ 1 on A_∞⁺ = colim A_i⁺ iff each restriction is ≤ 1 on A_i⁺. For a valuation that is ≤ 1 on a plus ring (which contains ϖ times a ring of definition), continuity is equivalent to v(ϖ) being cofinal in its value group; the value group of v is the directed union of those of its restrictions, so v is continuous iff every restriction is; this is Kedlaya–Liu's argument in Remark 2.6.3.
Homeomorphism: a rational subset R(T/s) of A_∞ has T, s in some A_i, so it is the preimage of the rational subset of Spa(A_i); both sides are spectral and the bijection matches quasi-compact opens.

(ii): each Spa(A_i) → Spa(A) is open, surjective with fibres the G_i-orbits (AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/torsor-spa-orbits). Surjectivity of q_∞: an inverse limit of nonempty compact fibres is nonempty. Fibres: if q_∞(x) = q_∞(x′), the sets {g ∈ G : g·x_i = x′_i} (images of x, x′ at level i) are nonempty and closed, decreasing in i, so their intersection is nonempty (G compact). Openness: a basic open is the preimage of a rational U_i ⊆ Spa(A_i), whose image under q_∞ equals the open q_i(U_i) because Spa(Â_∞) → Spa(A_i) is surjective.
acceptance: (ℚ_p, ℤ_p) with Â_∞ = ℂ_p: lim of points is a point and |Spa(ℂ_p, 𝒪_{ℂ_p})|/G = |Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p)|.
No sheafiness of (A, A⁺) is assumed: the identification is one of topological spaces of continuous valuations.

nodes.title: The uniform completed self-product of the completed tower is C^0(G, Â_∞)
nodes.statement: In the situation of AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/completed-tower-pair, for k ≥ 1 let C^0(G^k, Â_∞) be the ring of continuous maps G^k → Â_∞ with the topology of uniform convergence (Mathlib `ContinuousMap`), a complete Hausdorff uniform Tate ring with ring of integral elements C^0(G^k, Â_∞⁺). (i) The isomorphism A_∞ ⊗_A A_∞ ≅ LC(G, A_∞), a ⊗ b ↦ (g ↦ a·g(b)) (API colimTensorEquiv of AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/finite-etale-torsor-tower) induces an isomorphism of Huber pairs from the uniform completed tensor product Â_∞ ⊗̂ᵘ_A Â_∞ (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniform-completed-tensor-product) onto (C^0(G, Â_∞), C^0(G, Â_∞⁺)), carrying inlᵘ and inrᵘ to s(b) = (g ↦ b) and t(b) = (g ↦ g·b); likewise the (k+1)-fold uniform completed tensor power of Â_∞ over A is C^0(G^k, Â_∞). (ii) If p is topologically nilpotent in A, each C^0(G^k, Â_∞) is perfectoid, and |Spa(C^0(G^k, Â_∞), C^0(G^k, Â_∞⁺))| ≅ G^k × |Spa(Â_∞, Â_∞⁺)|; for k = 1 the maps induced by s and t are (g, x) ↦ x and (g, x) ↦ g⁻¹·x. Lean: `FiniteEtaleTorsorTower.uniformCompletedTensor_completion_equiv`.
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) complete Hausdorff Tate; T a finite étale torsor tower over A; for (ii) p topologically nilpotent in A.
proofSteps: Both sides are universal: Â_∞ ⊗̂ᵘ_A Â_∞ is the pushout in complete Hausdorff uniform Tate pairs (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniform-completed-tensor-product (b)), and maps out of Â_∞ into such pairs are maps out of (A_∞, A_∞⁺) (AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/completed-tower-pair (e)); so it is the uniformization of A_∞ ⊗_A A_∞ with its tensor-product topology (ring of definition the image of colim A_i° ⊗ colim A_i°).

Under a ⊗ b ↦ (g ↦ a·g(b)) that image lands in LC(G, colim A_i°). Conversely LC(G, colim A_i°) is generated by colim A_i° and the idempotents of LC(G, ℤ), and idempotents are power-bounded, so it consists of power-bounded elements of A_∞ ⊗_A A_∞; thus the two rings of definition have the same topologically nilpotent elements up to multiplication by ϖ, the spectral topologies agree (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-topology), and the uniformizations agree. The uniformization of LC(G, A_∞) is C^0(G, Â_∞) (uniform limits of locally constant maps).

(ii): C^0(G^k, Â_∞) is complete and uniform (sup norm), ϖ ∈ Â_∞ ⊆ C^0 is a pseudouniformizer with ϖ^p | p, and Frobenius is surjective modulo ϖ^p because a continuous map to Â_∞° is locally constant modulo ϖ^p (AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/perfectoid-uniform-completion gives p-th roots of the finitely many values); so it is perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras). It is the completed colimit over open normal subgroups U of ∏_{G^k/U} Â_∞, whose spectrum is ⊔_{G^k/U} Spa(Â_∞); PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces identifies the spectrum of the completed colimit with lim_U (G^k/U × |Spa(Â_∞)|) = G^k × |Spa(Â_∞)|.
The formulas for s and t: the point (g, x) is the valuation f ↦ |f(g)|_x; pulling back along t gives b ↦ |g·b|_x = (g⁻¹·x)(b).

nodes.title: Perfectoid torsor presentation of a complete Tate ℤ_p-pair: a perfectoid cover and its induced perfectoid equivalence relation
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a Huber pair with A a complete Hausdorff Tate ring in which p is topologically nilpotent. A *perfectoid torsor presentation* of (A, A⁺) (Lean: the structure `Huber.PerfectoidTorsorPresentation P` for P the pair (A, A⁺)) consists of a profinite group G (Mathlib `ProfiniteGrp`), a complete Huber pair (Ã, Ã⁺) with Ã a perfectoid Tate ring (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras), a continuous action of G on (Ã, Ã⁺) by automorphisms of Huber pairs, and a G-invariant morphism of Huber pairs q : (A, A⁺) → (Ã, Ã⁺), such that (a) the map b ⊗ b′ ↦ (g ↦ b·g(b′)) induces an isomorphism of Huber pairs from the uniform completed tensor product Ã ⊗̂ᵘ_A Ã (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniform-completed-tensor-product) onto (C^0(G, Ã), C^0(G, Ã⁺)); (b) Spa(q) : Spa(Ã, Ã⁺) → Spa(A, A⁺) is spectral (in particular quasi-compact), surjective and open, with fibres exactly the G-orbits, so that it induces a homeomorphism |Spa(Ã, Ã⁺)|/G ≅ |Spa(A, A⁺)|. The *perfectoid cover* is X̃ = Spa(Ã, Ã⁺); the *induced perfectoid equivalence relation* is R̃ = Spa(C^0(G, Ã), C^0(G, Ã⁺)) ≅ G × X̃ with the two maps s, t : R̃ ⇉ X̃ induced by b ↦ (g ↦ b) and b ↦ (g ↦ g·b), identity X̃ → R̃ (evaluation at 1) and composition induced by C^0(G, Ã) → C^0(G × G, Ã) — the action groupoid of G on X̃, with all objects affinoid perfectoid. Construction (`Huber.PerfectoidTorsorPresentation.ofTower`): for a finite étale torsor tower T over A (AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/finite-etale-torsor-tower), take G = lim G_i and (Ã, Ã⁺) = (Â_∞, Â_∞⁺) (AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/completed-tower-pair); it is perfectoid by AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/perfectoid-uniform-completion, (a) is AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/completed-tower-self-product and (b) is AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/spa-of-completed-tower; for presentations from towers, finite étale A-algebras are equivalent to finite étale Ã-algebras with descent data over C^0(G, Ã) (AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/finite-etale-effective-descent-along-tower). This is the generalized-affinoid presentation used in ECD §15: (A, A⁺) need not be sheafy, while X̃ and R̃ are affinoid perfectoid. Pinned conventions: R̃ is an equivalence relation only in the category of v-sheaves (DiamondsAndVStacks D6); on underlying sets |R̃| → |X̃| ×_{|Spa A|} |X̃| is surjective but not injective; the quasi-compactness in (b) is part of the definition, and a map that is merely surjective on points is not a presentation.
hypotheses: A complete Hausdorff Tate ring with p topologically nilpotent; A⁺ any ring of integral elements; no sheafiness of (A, A⁺).
proofSteps: Data and axioms for ofTower: AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/completed-tower-pair ((c), (d): the pair and the continuous G-action), AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/perfectoid-uniform-completion (perfectoidness), AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/completed-tower-self-product ((a) and R̃ ≅ G × X̃, R̃ perfectoid), AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/spa-of-completed-tower ((b)); the tower exists for every ring (AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/finite-etale-torsor-tower, canonical).
Groupoid structure: the identities (d₀, d₁, d₂ as in AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/finite-etale-effective-descent-along-tower) are identities of continuous maps G^k → Ã, checked on locally constant maps.
Non-injectivity on points: for (ℚ_p, ℤ_p), |X̃| is a point while |R̃| = G is infinite.
acceptance: Every complete Tate ℤ_p-pair has a perfectoid torsor presentation (ofTower applied to the canonical tower).
For (ℚ_p, ℤ_p): G = Gal(ℚ̄_p/ℚ_p), (Ã, Ã⁺) = (ℂ_p, 𝒪_{ℂ_p}), and (a) is ℂ_p ⊗̂ᵘ_{ℚ_p} ℂ_p ≅ C^0(G, ℂ_p).

nodes.title: ECD 15.1–15.4 as a composite record: the analytic torsor tower is A4's, the Spd, v-sheaf and quotient conclusions are DiamondsAndVStacks D6's
nodes.statement: The results of ECD Lemmas 15.1–15.3 and Proposition 15.4 split by owner as follows. A4's part, which is this node's declaration (Lean: `Huber.Pair.exists_perfectoidTorsorPresentation`, re-exporting `Huber.PerfectoidTorsorPresentation.exists`): for every Huber pair (A, A⁺) with A a complete Hausdorff Tate ring in which p is topologically nilpotent there are a finite étale torsor tower A → A_i under finite groups G_i with no remaining nonsplit finite étale covers (AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/finite-etale-torsor-tower; ECD Lemma 15.3, first part), its uniform completion (Â_∞, Â_∞⁺) with Â_∞⁺ the closure of colim A_i⁺ (AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/completed-tower-pair), which is perfectoid (AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/perfectoid-uniform-completion; ECD Lemma 15.3, second part, with completeness added), carries a continuous action of G = lim G_i with Â_∞ ⊗̂ᵘ_A Â_∞ ≅ C^0(G, Â_∞) (AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/completed-tower-self-product), and satisfies |Spa(Â_∞, Â_∞⁺)| = lim_i |Spa(A_i, A_i⁺)| and |Spa(Â_∞, Â_∞⁺)|/G = |Spa(A, A⁺)| (AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/spa-of-completed-tower; the topological identification in the proof of Proposition 15.4) — together, a perfectoid torsor presentation (AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/perfectoid-cover-presentation). DiamondsAndVStacks D6's part, which consumes the above and is neither stated nor proved in A4: Spd ℤ_p and Spd(A, A⁺) are v-sheaves (Lemma 15.1; DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/spd-of-a-tate-pair, D6/untilt-descent-along-v-covers); Spd of a perfectoid pair is its tilt (Lemma 15.2); Spd(A_i, A_i⁺) → Spd(A, A⁺) is a G_i-torsor of v-sheaves (via Theorem 6.1); Spd(Â_∞, Â_∞⁺) = lim Spd(A_i, A_i⁺) = Spa(Â_∞^♭, Â_∞^{♭+}) → Spd(A, A⁺) is a G-torsor and a universally open qcqs quasi-pro-étale map, Spd(A, A⁺) is a spatial diamond and |Spd(A, A⁺)| = |Spa(A, A⁺)| (Proposition 15.4; DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/spd-is-a-spatial-diamond). For a Tate ℤ_p-algebra A that is not complete, A4's part applies to the completion (Â, Â⁺), whose adic spectrum is that of (A, A⁺); D6 then uses Spd(A, A⁺) = Spd(Â, Â⁺) (continuous maps into perfectoid, hence complete, rings factor through the completion); a torsor tower over the non-complete ring A itself need not have perfectoid uniform completion (sourceIssues AdicEtaleGeometry/E19). No A4 node uses a D6 result.
hypotheses: A complete Hausdorff Tate ring with p topologically nilpotent; for non-complete A the record applies to the completion.
The D6 clauses are recorded for ownership only; A4's prerequisites contain no D6 node, so the stage order A4 → D6 is acyclic.
proofSteps: The A4 declaration is AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/perfectoid-cover-presentation (API exists), assembled from AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/finite-etale-torsor-tower, AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/completed-tower-pair, AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/perfectoid-uniform-completion, AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/completed-tower-self-product and AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/spa-of-completed-tower.

Attribution of the D6 clauses: DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/spd-of-a-tate-pair (Lemma 15.1(ii)), DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/untilt-descent-along-v-covers (Lemma 15.1(i)), DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/spd-is-a-spatial-diamond (Lemma 15.2 and Proposition 15.4), each of which lists AdicEtaleGeometry:A4 among its inputs.
acceptance: Every clause of ECD 15.1–15.4 is attributed to exactly one of A4 and D6.
(ℚ_p, ℤ_p): the A4 data are G = Gal(ℚ̄_p/ℚ_p), Â_∞ = ℂ_p, |Spa(ℂ_p)|/G = |Spa(ℚ_p)|; the D6 conclusion is Spd(ℚ_p, ℤ_p) = Spa(ℂ_p^♭, 𝒪_{ℂ_p^♭})/Gal(ℚ̄_p/ℚ_p).
The record makes no sheafiness assumption on (A, A⁺): the topological identification holds for all complete Tate ℤ_p-pairs.

requests.need: (A) The category of adic spaces (objects of Huber's 𝒱 locally isomorphic to Spa of sheafy Huber pairs), exposed as a category in which Mathlib's IsPullback/HasPullback and IsPushout can be stated; open adic subspaces with the universal property of open immersions (a morphism factors through an open subspace iff its image lies in it, uniquely); morphisms from an adic space T into Spa of a complete sheafy pair (R, R⁺) are the morphisms of pairs (R, R⁺) → (O_T(T), O⁺_T(T)) (Huber 1994 Proposition 2.1(ii)); gluing of adic spaces and of morphisms. These are the carriers of the fibre products, the rational pullback (a), the chart comparison and the analytic locus. (B) The category of adic spaces (objects of Huber's 𝒱 covered by affinoid adic spaces) and its full subcategory of analytic adic spaces, whose affinoid charts can be chosen with complete Tate coordinate rings; open subspaces and open immersions (an open immersion is a morphism that is an isomorphism onto an open subspace; open subspaces are determined by their underlying sets); gluing of adic spaces and of morphisms along open covers; the identification of morphisms X → Spa(A, A⁺) from an adic space X into an affinoid adic space with continuous ring maps A → O_X(X) carrying A⁺ into O⁺_X(X) (Huber 1994 Proposition 2.1(ii), Kedlaya–Liu Lemma 8.2.9); and the canonical morphism Spa(k(x)^, k(x)^+) → X attached to a point x. (C) (a) The category of adic spaces (objects of Huber's 𝒱 covered by affinoid adic spaces Spa(A, A⁺) of sheafy complete pairs), open adic subspaces and open immersions, restriction to open subsets, and gluing of adic spaces and of morphisms along open immersions (Layer 5.1, 5.3), as the carriers of X_ét, X_proét and of the functor ι into Yoneda-adic spaces; (b) Huber 1994 Proposition 2.1(ii) / Wedhorn Proposition 8.25: for an adic space X and a sheafy complete pair (A, A⁺), morphisms X → Spa(A, A⁺) correspond to morphisms of pairs (A, A⁺) → (O_X(X), O_X⁺(X)); (c) morphisms locally of finite type (Layer 5.2), for spaces locally of finite type over Spa(K, K⁺) and their base change to finite and completed algebraic field extensions. (D) The category of adic spaces with open subspaces (universal property of open immersions), gluing of spaces and morphisms, and morphisms from an adic space into Spa of a complete sheafy pair described by morphisms of pairs into its global sections (Huber 1994 Proposition 2.1(ii)): used for B^n_X and T^n_X, their universal properties, and the analytic-locus description of generic fibres. (E) Adic spaces as objects with structure sheaves O_X, O_X⁺ and their sheaves of O_X-modules; open subspaces; the adic space Spa(A, A⁺) of a sheafy pair; morphisms from an adic space into Spa(A, A⁺) correspond to morphisms of pairs into (O_X(X), O_X⁺(X)). A3 defines pseudocoherent sheaves of O_X-modules and Zariski closed immersions on these carriers.

(A) The rational localisation O(U) = (A⟨T/s⟩, integral closure of A⁺[T/s]) of a Huber pair as a complete Huber pair with its universal property among complete Huber pairs and Spa(O(U)) ≅ U matching rational subsets (Tau Ceti has the ring-level pieces `completionLocalization`, `existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_of_forall_comap_mem_rationalSubset`, `spaLocalizationHomeomorph`); the structure presheaf of Spa(A⟨T/s⟩) is the restriction of that of Spa(A, A⁺), so rational subsets of sheafy pairs are sheafy; and Huber's category 𝒱 of v-ringed spaces (Layer 3.4), in which PerfectoidSpaces:P8/categorical-quotient forms quotients. (B) The structure presheaves O, O⁺ on Spa(A, A⁺) with values in complete Hausdorff topological rings; stalks O_{X,x} as local rings with the valuation of x on the residue field and the completed residue field (k(x)^, k(x)^+); local homomorphisms of stalks induced by morphisms; and the sheafiness predicates Huber.IsSheafyPair, Huber.IsSheafyRing (Wedhorn Definition 8.26, quantified over rings of integral elements) and Huber.IsStablySheafyRing with their implications (Layer 3.4). (C) The rational localisation (O(U), O⁺(U)) of a complete Huber pair at a rational subset U as a complete Huber pair, with Spa(O(U), O⁺(U)) ≅ U matching rational subsets and the topological universal property among complete Huber pairs (Layer 3.1); the structure presheaf with its values O(U) on rational subsets, the stalk valuations, and the sheaf criterion on rational coverings of rational subsets (Layers 3.3, 3.5); the predicate Huber.IsSheafyPair (Layer 3.4). Used for the rational site on complete Huber pairs, the open immersions of Yoneda-adic spaces and the ind-ringed description. (D) Rational localisation O(U) as a complete Huber pair with its universal property among complete Huber pairs (for T^n_X = R(1/(T₁⋯Tₙ)) and the embedding B^n ≅ {|Tᵢ − 1| ≤ |ϖ|}), and locality of stalks (a function with |g| ≥ 1 at every point is a unit). (E) For a complete Hausdorff Tate Huber pair (A, A⁺): the structure presheaf O on the rational subsets of Spa(A, A⁺), identified with the completed rational localisations A⟨T/s⟩ (Tau Ceti `completionLocalization`, `presentationLimitPresheaf`), with its restriction maps and plus-ring presheaf O⁺; and the predicate 'sheafy' (O is a sheaf for finite rational coverings of rational subsets), stable under passage to rational subsets. A3 states Kedlaya–Liu's pseudocoherent theory over sheafy pairs in these terms.

(A) Completion of Huber pairs: for a Huber pair (E, E⁺), the closure of the image of E⁺ in the Hausdorff completion Ê is a ring of integral elements of Ê, and Spa(Ê, Ê⁺) → Spa(E, E⁺) is a homeomorphism matching rational subsets (Wedhorn Lemma 7.47, Proposition 7.48); used to identify the plus ring of the completed tensor product with Kedlaya–Liu's and Scholze's. (B) The open mapping theorem for complete Tate rings (Layer 0.6), used to see that a bijective restriction map A → Ȟ⁰ on a rational covering of a complete Tate pair is a topological isomorphism, so that sheafiness of sets for 𝒪 on complete Tate pairs coincides with Huber.IsSheafyPair.

(A) Sheafiness (Huber.IsSheafyRing) of every complete strongly noetherian Tate ring, with exactness of the augmented Čech complexes of finite rational coverings (Layer 4.1); used to show that strongly noetherian Tate rings are strongly sheafy. (B) Sheafiness of complete strongly noetherian Tate pairs (Layer 4.1: Huber.IsSheafyPair and Čech exactness for finite rational coverings of rational subsets), so that O(Spa(B, B⁺)) = B and idempotents of B correspond to open and closed subsets of Spa(B, B⁺) for the affinoid pieces of étale spaces over locally noetherian analytic adic spaces, and so that the structure presheaf 𝒪 on complete Huber pairs satisfies the sheaf condition at such pairs. (C) Sheafiness in the cases A3 uses, at the level of pairs: stably uniform complete Tate pairs are sheafy with Čech-acyclic O on rational coverings (Buzzard–Verberkmoes, Kedlaya–Liu I Theorem 2.4.23). A3 reaches it through AdicSpacesPartII:R3/sheafy-cech-acyclicity and R5/sousperfectoid-sheafy, whose own anchor requests cover the carrier.

(A) Rational-subset calculus on Spa(A, A⁺): a rational subset of a rational subset U of Spa(A, A⁺) (defined by functions of O(U)) is a rational subset of Spa(A, A⁺); rational subsets form a basis closed under finite intersections; every quasi-compact open subset of Spa(A, A⁺) is a finite union of rational subsets. (B) Spectrality of Spa(A, A⁺) and the rational basis with open numerator ideals (present in the pinned tree as TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spectralSpace_spa_of_pairOfDefinition and isTopologicalBasis_spaRationalFamily), and analytic points of Spa(A, A⁺) (Layer 2.3: support not open; TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.IsAnalyticPoint, spaAnalytic): the stage-level import recorded for the orchestrator. (C) Wedhorn Proposition 7.52(1) for complete Huber pairs, A⁺ = {a ∈ A : v(a) ≤ 1 for all v ∈ Spa(A, A⁺)} (used to show that A⁺⟨T⟩ is integrally closed in A⟨T⟩), and Wedhorn Proposition 8.2(2): a rational subset of a rational subset is rational (used for toric charts).

Deligne's completeness theorem for coherent topoi (SGA 4 VI, Proposition 9.0): a coherent topos, in particular the topos of sheaves on a site whose quasi-compact quasi-separated objects form a generating family stable under fibre products (an algebraic topos in the sense of DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/quasicompact-objects-in-a-topos with quasi-compact quasi-separated final object), has a small conservative family of points, stated in Mathlib's form CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.HasEnoughPoints for the site; together with its local version for locally coherent topoi. D0 builds the coherent and algebraic topos interfaces; this theorem is the one input A1 needs beyond them.

Spectrality of the valuation and adic spectra (Layer 1.2–1.5 with Layer 2.1: Spv A, Spv(A, I), Cont A and Spa(A, A⁺) are spectral spaces, via pro-constructible subspaces), so that the underlying space of an adic space is locally spectral, hence quasi-sober and T0, and its irreducible closed subsets are closures of unique points; and the description of Spa(K, K⁺) for a complete rank-one field K and a valuation ring K⁺ ⊆ K° as a chain of specialisations indexed by the valuation rings between K⁺ and K°.

(A) The statements of ECD Definition 6.2 and Theorems 6.1, 6.3 over an arbitrary perfectoid Tate ring (no perfectoid base field): the tilting equivalence of étale sites X_ét ≃ X♭_ét for affinoid perfectoid X, preserving affinoid perfectoid objects and compatible with base change along maps of affinoid perfectoid spaces; and Scholze 2012 Proposition 7.6 in that generality (preimages of affinoid perfectoid opens under finite étale maps are affinoid perfectoid, with finite étale ring map and integral-closure plus ring). The nodes PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-tilting-and-etale-almost-acyclicity and P3/strongly-finite-etale-maps-are-affinoid-over-affinoids are stated over a perfectoid field K; ECD 6.4(iv) is stated for all perfectoid Tate rings. (B) State PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation (Sch12 Proposition 7.4, Gabber–Ramero) in the generality of the Berkeley lectures, Theorem 7.4.8, without a base field: for a Tate ring A with a ring of definition A_0 and a pseudouniformizer ϖ ∈ A_0 such that (A_0, ϖA_0) is henselian, base change B ↦ B ⊗_A Â is an equivalence between finite étale A-algebras and finite étale Â-algebras (Â the completion; equivalently, for a ϖ-torsion-free ring R henselian along ϖ, FÉt(R[1/ϖ]) ≅ FÉt(R^∧[1/ϖ])); and the corollary that for a filtered directed system of complete Tate rings A_i, with compatible power-bounded subrings, 2-colim FÉt(A_i) ≅ FÉt(colim A_i) ≅ FÉt of the completion of colim A_i for the topology in which colim A_i° is open and bounded. The node as stated covers flat K°-algebras over a perfectoid field K only; A4 applies it to Tate ℤ_p-algebras with no base field.

Fibre products of affinoid perfectoid spaces over an arbitrary perfectoid Tate ring (no base field), with the affinoid formula Spa(completed tensor product, completed integral closure of the image of the plus rings) and compatibility with tilting. PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces is stated over a perfectoid field K.

The clause of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:henselian/henselian-f-adic-rings-and-henselization (Huber 1996, Lemma 3.1.1 and Definition 3.1.2) that a complete f-adic ring A is henselian, i.e. (B, I) is a henselian pair for every open subring B ⊆ A° and every open ideal I ⊆ A°° of B — in particular (A°, ϖA°) for a complete Tate ring A — kept as a separately citable declaration, with a proof that does not use Huber's non-public book in the Tate case (A° is the directed union of ϖ-adically complete rings of definition; Stacks 0ALJ and 0FWT).

The completed tensor product V ⊗̂_A W of Banach modules over a complete Tate ring A (Banach spaces over a complete nonarchimedean field), the Hausdorff completion of V ⊗_A W for the tensor topology, with its universal property for continuous bilinear maps into Banach modules (proposed node AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-banach-module). A0's fibre-product contract uses it for completed tensor products of modules, and PerfectoidSpaces P8/P9 request it. Stability of unramified, smooth and étale morphisms of adic spaces under base change along any morphism for which R0's fibre product exists, with smoothness of the same relative dimension and Ωᶜ of the base change the pullback of Ωᶜ (proposed node AdicSpacesPartII:R0/smooth-etale-base-change). A2's ball-chart description of smooth morphisms pulls charts back along it.

gaps.title: Sheafiness of finite étale algebras over a general sheafy Tate pair
gaps.detail: Kedlaya–Liu, Remark 8.2.18: it is not known whether a finite étale extension of a sheafy adic Banach algebra is sheafy, or whether a finite étale cover of an adic affinoid space is an adic space. A0/finite-etale-pullback-comparison therefore states the geometric pullback Spa(B ⊗_A C) = Spa B ×_{Spa A} Spa C under the hypothesis that the base change is sheafy; the ring-level statements (i)–(iii), (v) hold unconditionally. Sheafiness is known for C strongly noetherian (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-algebra-over-affinoid (v)), for C sousperfectoid (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-finite-etale, downstream of A0) and for C perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces P3, downstream of A0); for C stably uniform, finite étale extensions are uniform (Kedlaya–Liu Proposition 2.8.16), but stable uniformity of the extension was not verified in the sources read. The general case is handled by the generalized adic presentations of AdicEtaleGeometry A1. This is an open problem in the literature, not a missing reference.

gaps.title: Banach-ring inputs of Kedlaya–Liu Proposition 2.6.8 are not decomposed
gaps.detail: The equivalence FÉt(A) ≃ 2-colim FÉt(A_α) along an affinoid system uses Kedlaya–Liu Lemma 2.2.3 (henselian pair (A_∞, ker α)), Lemma 2.2.4 (idempotent lifting with norms; FÉt of a direct limit with a multiplicative seminorm), Corollary 2.6.6 (Hausdorff localisations) and compactness of the Gel'fand spectrum M(A). Neither this roadmap nor AdicSpacesPartII has nodes for the Gel'fand spectrum or these lemmas; the node records the argument, and these four inputs are open proof obligations. Consumers affected transitively: finite-etale-rational-descent, finite-etale-local-to-global, etale-composition, etale-open-map and everything built on them in the non-noetherian case (on locally noetherian spaces the comparison with Huber avoids them).

A1 uses it for the direction 'Huber-étale ⇒ local description' and, at a noetherian stage of an affinoid system, for composites of étale maps.

gaps.title: Kedlaya–Liu Lemma 8.2.17(b),(c): the reduction to classical affinoid spaces is only sketched in the source
gaps.detail: The source proof is two sentences ('we may use Lemma 2.6.2 and Proposition 2.6.8 to reduce to the case where all of the spaces involved are classical affinoid spaces'). The nodes carry out the reduction (descending the finite étale and rational data to a noetherian stage, applying Huber's theory, base-changing back and using surjectivity of fibre products on points); these steps are this roadmap's, not checked against a written proof.

gaps.title: Huber 1996 §2.5 (geometric points and strict localisations) is not public: the strict-localisation homeomorphism
gaps.detail: Clause (b) of the node (lim over étale neighbourhoods of |U| is |Spa(C_ξ, C_ξ⁺)|) is Huber's statement from the Chapter 2 introduction (recorded only in data/decompositions/AdicEtaleGeometry.json). Its proof needs a shrinking step: finite étale neighbourhoods realising finite separable subextensions of κ(ξ)/k(x), shrunk around the chosen point over x, are cofinal among étale neighbourhoods; with higher-rank valuations the fibre over x of a finite étale neighbourhood may contain several points in one residue-field factor, and the adic form of de Jong–van der Put's 'Key Lemma' needed to separate them is not proved here. No other node depends on clause (b).

gaps.title: Classification of the points of the étale topos (Huber: every fibre functor is some ε_ξ) is not planned
gaps.detail: Only conservativity of the geometric points is proved (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-enough-points). The statement that every point of X~_et is isomorphic to ε_ξ for a geometric point ξ is from Huber's Chapter 2 introduction (proof in §2.5, not public); no consumer of this stage uses it.

gaps.title: Proposition 3.13 conservativity under corrected coverings
gaps.detail: Scholze's proof of 'if i_x^*F = 0 for all x then F = 0' ends with an open surjection T = π1(X, x̄)·S'_x̄ → S_x̄ of profinite π1-sets and concludes that V' → U is pro-étale, hence a covering. With the erratum's corrected coverings a pro-étale surjection need not be a covering (an open surjection of profinite sets need not be of tower form), and the erratum asserts that all results are kept without re-proving this step. Missing input: a refinement of {V'_k → U} by a corrected covering of an open neighbourhood of the fibre over x, e.g. by showing that the induced map from π1(X, x̄) ×^{π1(Y_x, x̄)} S'_x̄ is a G-tower followed by a G-étale map. No consumer node uses the conservativity statement; the fibre morphisms i_x themselves (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/proetale-fibre-morphism-of-topoi) are unaffected.

gaps.title: Ribes–Zalesskii, Profinite Groups, Example 5.6.9 not in the library
gaps.detail: The existence of an open continuous surjection of profinite sets without continuous section is taken from the erratum's citation of [3, Example 5.6.9] (Ribes–Zalesskii, 2nd ed., 2010). The book is not in the scratch library and was not read, so the non-example tests that use such a map rest on the erratum's statement. Next action: obtain Ribes–Zalesskii §5.6 and record the explicit example (an uncountable inverse limit) in the tests.

gaps.title: Huber 1996 §1.8 (dimension theory) is not public
gaps.detail: Huber's Definition 1.8.1 is known through Zavyalov's Definition 3.1 and is formalised in A2/dimension-of-adic-spaces with Mathlib's topologicalKrullDim. The proofs of Corollary 1.8.7 (relative pure dimension on rank-one fibres), Lemma 1.8.6(ii), Example 1.8.9(i) (étale over a d-ball is of pure dimension d), Definition 1.8.4 (dim.tr) and Lemma 1.8.5(i) (dim f ≤ dim.tr f) are not in the library: Zavyalov quotes them without proof, and ECD Lemma 21.6 refers to the proof of 1.8.5(i). Zavyalov's alternative for Corollary 3.4, Bosch, Lectures on formal and rigid geometry (Lecture Notes in Math. 2105, 2014), Propositions 2.2/17 and 4.1/2, is also not in the library. Next action: obtain Bosch's Lectures (Springer) or reconstruct 1.8.6–1.8.7 from Conrad, Irreducible components of rigid spaces, §2 (in the library as for the rigid case.

gaps.title: Closure-containing neighbourhoods in Huber 1.6.10 and 2.2.8 for relative charts
gaps.detail: Scholze (2013, proof of Lemma 5.2) observes that the open subset constructed in Huber's Corollary 1.6.10, and the rational subset of Lemma 2.2.8 'with similar analysis of its proof', may be taken to contain the closure of a point. Huber's proofs are not public (AdicSpacesPartII records the 1.6.10 and 2.2.8 gaps on R0/smooth-local-structure and R0/etale-local-open-finite-etale-factorisation); A2 uses the same refinement over a relative Tate affinoid base, justified by the non-vanishing-of-a-Jacobian description, which is unverified against Huber's text.

gaps.title: Fargues–Scholze Proposition IV.4.13–IV.4.19 in their general form rest on diamond-level inputs; A3 proves only the étale, perfectoid-base (characteristic-p where needed) specialisations
gaps.detail: Read in full (FS arXiv v4, §IV.4.1, pp. 135–141). Diamond-level steps of the printed proofs: IV.4.13 — 'by spreading of étale maps' from the Zariski closed V(T) to a neighbourhood {|T| ≤ |ϖⁿ|}, with no reference (the available spreading statements are ECD Lemma 12.17 for cofiltered limits of small v-sheaves together with ECD Lemma 15.6); IV.4.14 — ECD Lemmas 15.6 and 12.17; IV.4.15(ii) — Huber 1.6.9(iii) on fibres, ECD Lemma 12.17 (twice), Lemma IV.4.14 and Lemma IV.4.16; IV.4.16 — reduction by descent to perfectoid and then strictly totally disconnected bases (the latter exist by ECD §7, whose proofs use ECD 6.4(iv) itself, so this route is circular for A3); IV.4.17 — IV.4.15; IV.4.18 — ECD Lemma 15.6 and Proposition 11.30; IV.4.19 — IV.4.13, IV.4.15, IV.4.17 and Kedlaya–Liu's pseudocoherent gluing. A3 replaces these, in the étale case over perfectoid bases, by the tube theorem (A3/tubular-neighbourhood), noetherian approximation in characteristic p (A3/jacobian-criterion-char-p) and the graph/idempotent arguments (A3/integral-cutoff-graph-presentation, A3/local-equations-near-closed-subspace). Not proved in A3 and not imported: the smooth (positive relative dimension) cases, bases that are merely sous-perfectoid in mixed characteristic, and IV.4.14, IV.4.16, IV.4.18. Consumers needing those (e.g. charts on Bun_G via Theorem IV.4.2) must obtain them from the roadmap owning Fargues–Scholze Chapter IV.

gaps.title: Kedlaya–Liu II, Remark 2.4.3 imports its statements from Kedlaya's lecture notes [90], unread
gaps.detail: Remark 2.4.3 (p. 36) asserts that for a sheafy (A, A⁺) and a strictly pseudocoherent ideal I with (A/I, (A/I)⁺) sheafy, A/I is stably pseudocoherent, citing [90, Theorem 1.2.7], and the converse citing [90, Theorem 1.4.20] ([90] = Kedlaya, Sheaves, stacks, and shtukas, AWS 2017 notes; not in the library). A3 does not use either statement: the quotients it needs are stably fpd by A3/fs-iv-4-13-regular-sequence. The general quotient statement is therefore not part of A3/stably-pseudocoherent-module's API. Next action: read the AWS notes, Lecture 1, Theorems 1.2.7 and 1.4.20.

gaps.title: Open points acknowledged by Kedlaya–Liu II, retained as boundaries
gaps.detail: (1) Remark 2.2.8: whether rational localisations of non-noetherian sheafy rings are flat is unknown; A3 uses only 2-pseudoflatness (A3/rational-localisation-pseudoflat) and never flatness. (2) After Lemma 2.4.12: the direct argument with 1 − fT does not transfer to T − f when f is not a unit; Lemma 2.4.13's diagram chase is used instead (A3/simple-laurent-pseudoflat). (3) Remark 1.1.12: pseudocoherence of Fitting ideals of pseudocoherent modules is unknown; A3 does not use Fitting ideals.

gaps.title: Gabber–Ramero's henselian finite étale comparison is imported, not read
gaps.detail: The equivalence FÉt(A) ≅ FÉt(Â) for a Tate ring whose ring of definition is henselian along a pseudouniformizer is quoted from the Berkeley lectures (Theorem 7.4.8, citing Elkik and Gabber–Ramero, Almost ring theory, Proposition 5.4.53) and from Sch12 Proposition 7.4; neither source proves it, and Gabber–Ramero was not read here. It is requested from PerfectoidSpaces:P3, whose node records the same unread import. For the uniformization of a complete Tate ring, Kedlaya–Liu Proposition 2.8.16(a) gives an independent proof inside Kedlaya–Liu (Proposition 2.6.8 through affinoid systems and Theorem 1.2.8), which was read.

gaps.title: Openness of Spa for faithfully finite étale maps is quoted from Kedlaya–Liu through classical affinoids
gaps.detail: Kedlaya–Liu prove Lemma 8.2.17(b) by reduction (Lemma 2.6.2, Proposition 2.6.8) to classical affinoid algebras and de Jong–van der Put, Proposition 3.1.7; that last input was not read here. For torsors the openness can also be derived from the orbit description and the compactness of G, which is the route A4/spa-of-completed-tower uses at the limit.

sourceIssues.locator: item (1), p. 1, in the three-page erratum (SHA-256 3cfa56b9…): corrected covers of Definition 3.3 (and, by 'a similar condition', of Definition 3.4)
sourceIssues.printed: instead of asking that the morphisms Ui→ U are open, one asks the stronger condition that Ui→ U can be written as an inverse limit Ui = lim←−µ<λUµ→ U of Uµ∈ pro−Xfét, U0 = U, [...] Uµ→ U<µ [...] is the pullback of a finite étale and surjective map inXfét.
sourceIssues.correction: Read as: each covering map U_i → U is such a transfinite tower followed by the pullback of a morphism of X_fét (for Definition 3.4: a G-tower followed by the pullback of a map of finite G-sets). Taken literally, every covering map is surjective, so the summand inclusions of a disjoint union U_1 ⊔ U_2 (open maps, jointly surjective, a covering of the printed Definition 3.3) would not generate a covering sieve.
sourceIssues.reason: A transfinite composition of pullbacks of surjections is surjective on underlying spaces. For X_profét with U = X ⊔ X (finite étale over X), a covering family must then consist of surjective maps, and no surjective map to X ⊔ X factors through one summand; so the sieve generated by the two summand inclusions contains no covering family, and a sheaf F need not satisfy F(X ⊔ X) = F(X) × F(X).

sourceIssues.printed: A similar condition should then also appear in the definition of covers in the pro-étale topology, Definition 3.9, and in the definition of covers in Definition 3.4. We note that for countable limits, the definitions are unchanged.
sourceIssues.correction: For Definition 3.9 the steps U_μ → U_{<μ} must be allowed to be finite étale surjections in the sense of Definition 3.9 (pullbacks of finite étale surjective maps of X_ét), not only pullbacks of maps of X_fét as in the Definition 3.3 condition; and an étale factor must be allowed (AdicSpacesPartII/E-R4-1). With steps from X_fét only, the statement 'for countable limits, the definitions are unchanged' would fail.
sourceIssues.reason: Let X be the closed unit disc over an algebraically closed complete field of characteristic 0, V ⊂ X the annulus {|T| = 1} (an object of X_ét) and U = lim_n V_n → V the Kummer tower T^{1/p^n}. U → X is pro-étale with a countable presentation, so {U → V} is a covering of the printed Definition 3.9. A pullback along V_n → Z of a morphism Y → Z of X_fét is a union of components of the restriction to V_n of a finite étale cover of X; the closed disc over such a field has no nontrivial finite étale covers (Lütkebohmert's p-adic Riemann existence theorem, not read here), so the connected degree-p steps V_{n+1} → V_n are not of that form. Hence the countable case is unchanged only if steps may be finite étale surjections of X_ét.

sourceIssues.correction: Assume A complete (or, more generally, that A has a ring of definition henselian along a pseudouniformizer). For an arbitrary Tate ℤ_p-algebra A apply the lemma to the completion Â: Spa and Spd do not change, and the tower must be taken over Â. The proof's step 'finite étale over R = Â∞, hence a solution' needs FÉt(A∞) ≅ FÉt(Â∞), which holds when A is complete (the ring of definition colim A_i° is then henselian along ϖ) and fails in general.
sourceIssues.reason: ECD §3 defines a Tate ring without completeness. Take A = ℚ_p[T] with ring of definition ℤ_p[T] and the p-adic topology. Finite étale ℚ_p[T]-algebras are products of L[T] for finite extensions L/ℚ_p (the affine line over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 is simply connected), so every tower has A∞ = B[T] with B a colimit of finite étale ℚ_p-algebras; its uniform completion is B̂⟨T⟩, and at any point of Spa(B̂) with completed residue field K the element T ∈ K°⟨T⟩ is not a p-th power modulo the maximal ideal of K°, so Frobenius is not surjective modulo ϖ^p and B̂⟨T⟩ is not perfectoid. Here FÉt(A∞) → FÉt(Â∞) is not essentially surjective: B̂⟨T⟩[X]/(X^p − X − T/p) is finite étale but not split.
